## 13.67 The room is spent on a long tail, not on turns

### 13.67.1 The measurement that changes what "the room is sufficient" means

§13.34.3 concluded the evidence room is not the constraint: it holds a median of **26 turns** against a median
gold set of **24**, so a perfect selector would reach 0.917 coverage. That argument is about **counts**, and
`--turns` on the adopted run's artifact shows the other half of the room's arithmetic:

|                 | value                       |
| --------------- | --------------------------- |
| delivered turns | 14,115 across 500 questions |
| **median turn** | **272 characters**          |
| mean            | 743                         |
| p90             | 2,305                       |
| max             | 15,369                      |
| roster median   | **26 turns per question**   |

Twenty-six turns of median size are **7,072 characters**. The room is 24,000. So the room is **not** being spent
on turns of typical size — it is being spent on a tail, and the median turn is carrying a seventh of the space
its count suggests.

### 13.67.2 What a per-turn cap would buy, in arithmetic rather than in hope

| cap     | characters saved | share     | turns that would fit in the same room |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------- |
| 200     | 8,015,463        | 76.5%     | **4.25×**                             |
| **400** | 6,682,968        | **63.7%** | **2.76×**                             |
| 600     | 5,753,658        | 54.9%     | 2.22×                                 |
| 900     | 4,516,877        | 43.1%     | 1.76×                                 |

At a 400-character cap the same room holds **2.76 times as many turns** — 26 becomes 72, which is more than the
64-wide pool contains. And §13.66 measured exactly what that would buy: the pool holds **73.2%** of the gold while
the delivery holds **54.2%**, because the cut falls at rank 26 and the band from 26 to 64 holds another **15%**
of the gold.

So the two measurements meet: **the gold is in the pool, the cut is by rank, and the rank cut is by characters.**
Capping a turn's contribution moves the cut, which is the one thing the rank curve said would help.

### 13.67.3 Why this is a different variable from the three already excluded

- **Not `k`.** §13.54 and §13.66: the cut band is inside the pool, so widening the pool cannot reach it.
- **Not the units.** §13.34: `session` and `session-fill` allocated whole sessions and moved coverage by nothing.
- **Not the order.** §13.66 said the order is the lever, and this **is** an ordering instrument — but of a
  different kind: it does not reorder candidates, it changes **how many of the ranked candidates fit**. The two
  are complementary and the cap is the cheaper one to measure, because it needs no similarity function.

### 13.67.4 What it costs, stated before the run

A cap cuts each turn at that length. For a counting question the gold turn is usually a short statement
(_"I went to Lisbon in May"_), so cutting at 400 characters loses little. For a turn whose decisive fact sits deep
in a long narrative, the cap destroys it. **That is the trade, and the prediction below prices it**: coverage and
counts should rise, and any capability whose answers live in long text should lose more than it gains.

### 13.67.5 Registration

**One variable**: a per-turn character cap of **400**, applied where the prompt renders each turn, with
`undefined` meaning no cap so every archived run stays byte-identical.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | falsified if   |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------- |
| **1** | **Coverage rises**: MR's delivered gold share rises from **42.5%** to **≥ 50.2%** of its total — **corrected by §13.71**, which found the original `54.2%` was a median over the answered subset of a _different_ configuration rather than an aggregate share. The original target (`≥ 62%` against `54.2%`) is kept as a secondary check in §13.71.2 | ≤ 42.5%        |
| **2** | **MR's correct count rises from 62 to ≥ 66**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | ≤ 62           |
| **3** | **The roster rises from 371 to ≥ 379**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | ≤ 371          |
| **4** | **The long-text capabilities hold**: IE and KU stay within their own measured rates (IE 5, KU 7 questions)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | outside either |

**Prediction 1 is the mechanism, 2 and 3 are the money, 4 is the price.** They are separated because a cap that
raises coverage but loses IE would be a capability trade rather than an improvement, and the campaign has
learned — §13.64.6, §13.63.3 — that a total can hide a regression the instrument is fine enough to see.

**Prediction 3 is registered against a single run**, which §13.66 has now made defensible: retrieval is
deterministic on this arm, so the only cross-run noise this variable meets is model sampling, measured at ±4.

### 13.67.6 Why the run is not dispatched in this section

The change is not a switch: it touches the render path in `prompt.ts`, the option surface, the arm's env reader
and the workflow input — four files plus their tests, and the render path is where §13.15's byte-compatibility
guarantees live. Writing it in the last minutes of an iteration is how a byte-identical promise gets broken
silently.

So this section delivers the measurement, the arithmetic and the registration, and the implementation is the next
iteration's first task with its predictions already fixed. **A registered experiment that has not run is worth
more than an unregistered change that has**, which is the order this campaign has paid to learn four times.

### 13.67.7 Verification

- `--turns` is `readout-arm-run.py`'s seventh mode, with 3 tests: the median and the count, the cap table, and a
  roster without turns refusing.
- The numbers above are that tool's output on the adopted run's artifact — 14,115 turns, median 272, cap 400
  saving 63.7% — computed on the turns the run actually carried, not on an assumption about a corpus.
- `python3 -m pytest tools/__tests__ -q` → **445 passed, 40 subtests**.

## 13.68 The per-turn cap is implemented, four layers deep, and one line of it no test reaches

### 13.68.1 What §13.67 registered and this section builds

§13.67 delivered the measurement and refused to implement it in the last minutes of an iteration, on the
ground that the change touches the render path where §13.15's byte-compatibility guarantees live. That
refusal is discharged here, with the four predictions from §13.67.5 unchanged — they were never read, and a
prediction is not amended by the section that implements it.

The variable is a per-turn character cap of **400**, and it is one option threaded through four layers:

| layer      | file                                        | what would break without it                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| renderer   | `prompt.ts` `contentFor` + `formatEvidence` | nothing caps, and the option is a comment                       |
| forwarding | `memory.ts` `#promptOptions`                | the system accepts the number and the prompt ignores it         |
| reader     | `bench-memory-arm.ts` `readMaxTurnChars`    | the arm runs no cap while the artifact config claims one        |
| projection | `report.ts` config line                     | two artifacts differ only in a JSON key most readers never open |

### 13.68.2 The cap is on the content, not on the rendered block

The obvious implementation — truncate the string `formatEvidence` returns — is wrong in three ways, and each
is a test:

- It would eat the **index** (`1. `) and, under the `sourced` rendering, the **memory id**. A truncated id is a
  false provenance claim, where a missing one is merely absent.
- It would be a **per-prompt** cap rather than a per-turn one: the first turn would consume the whole allowance
  and the rest would be empty.
- It would have to be applied **after** the session grouping, so `renderSessionBlocks` — which filters
  `session.turns` by **identity** against the selection — would no longer find its members.

So the cap lives in `contentFor(turn, maxTurnChars)`, one predicate with two readers (the baseline renderer and
the sourced one), and `carried` still holds the turns exactly as they arrived. That last part is not
politeness: `goldOverlap` matches a record's turns against the dataset's gold turns **by text**, so a capped
roster would fail to match gold it actually delivered and coverage would collapse for a reason no artifact
could show. The size of what was actually rendered is reported separately, as it always was, by
`evidenceChars`.

### 13.68.3 Three spellings of "no cap", and two values refused

Absent, blank, and the literal `none` all mean no cap. The third is not decoration: §10.3 registers the adopted
configuration as `maxTurnChars: none`, and the dispatch must send the value the registration names —
`test_preregistration_config.py` exists to catch a registration and a payload that disagree, and it caught
exactly this in the first draft, where the dispatch sent `''` against a registration that said `none`.

Refused rather than clamped:

- **`0`** — it emits every turn's number with no text after it while `carried` still reports 26 turns and every
  coverage count is computed from the turns as they arrived. The artifact would show a run that delivered 54%
  of its gold into an empty evidence section, and no reader could tell that from a retrieval failure.
- **a fraction** — `1.5` characters is not a cap anyone chose, and it completes a run whose cap is not the
  number it names. Same rule as the index width's fraction.

### 13.68.4 One branch was written, uncovered, and removed rather than tested

The first implementation pre-tested `none` and then delegated the rest to `readNumeric`, which returns
`number | undefined`. That forced a `value === undefined` early return, which v8 counted and **no input could
reach** — the blank had already been collapsed by the guard above it. Coverage reported
`bench-memory-arm.ts` at 99.37% branch, one line, and the honest reading of an uncovered branch is nearly
always "there is no way to arrive here" rather than "a test is missing".

So the function narrows `raw` to `string` in the guard and calls `Number` directly, and the branch is gone
rather than papered over with a test that would have had to construct a state the reader cannot produce. This
is the fourth time in this campaign that an uncovered branch was a fact about the code rather than about the
tests.

### 13.68.5 The one line no test reaches, and what makes it visible instead

`bench/run-ablation.ts` is an entry point and `bench/**` is excluded from coverage, so the spread that carries
`armOptions.maxTurnChars` into `new CortexMemory({...})` is the single line in this chain that no test covers.
Deleting it would leave every unit test green and every run capped at nothing.

Two things make that visible rather than silent, and neither is a test: the value is **echoed in the run's own
log line** (`maxTurnChars=400`) beside the gate configuration, and it is **projected into the artifact's
config**, so a run whose spread was missing would print and record a cap its prompt never applied. That is the
same defence §7.4's other fields use — the artifact naming its own configuration — and it is weaker than a test
by exactly one run. Stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.

### 13.68.6 Predictions, unchanged from §13.67.5

| #     | prediction                                                                                                 | falsified if   |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| **1** | **Coverage rises**: MR's delivered gold share rises from **54.2%** to **≥ 62%** of its total               | ≤ 54.2%        |
| **2** | **MR's correct count rises from 62 to ≥ 66**                                                               | ≤ 62           |
| **3** | **The roster rises from 371 to ≥ 379**                                                                     | ≤ 371          |
| **4** | **The long-text capabilities hold**: IE and KU stay within their own measured rates (IE 5, KU 7 questions) | outside either |

Prediction 3 is safe against cross-run noise on this arm because §13.66 measured **retrieval to be
deterministic**: run `39116387165`'s pool and delivered counts are identical to `39106951421`'s to the turn, so
the only noise this variable meets is model sampling (±4 on the roster).

### 13.68.7 What each outcome would mean, written before the run

- **1 and 2 hold**: the room was the cut, the tail was the constraint, and the next variable is the arithmetic
  (MR's 31 `numeric_mismatch`, of which 11 count their own short list).
- **1 holds and 2 does not**: more gold arrives and the model still miscounts it — which would move the ordering
  of the remaining work rather than its content.
- **1 fails**: the turns the cap buys back are not the turns that decide, i.e. the cut band from rank 26 to 64
  is _below_ the gold that matters and §13.66's rule was reading the median rather than the mass.
- **4 fails while 1–3 hold**: a capability trade. Adoption would then need its own argument, and this section
  does not pre-authorise one.

## 13.69 The registration held two answers to one question, and a dispatch printed the wrong one

### 13.69.1 What happened, in the order it happened

`dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py` prints every input it sends before it sends it. On the dispatch for §13.68's cap
that print read:

```text
dispatching cortex-memory A/B at master (84e828e3)
  cortex_memory_max_turn_chars = 400 *
  cortex_memory_relevance = retrieval
```

`retrieval` — but §13.64 adopted `retrieval-hybrid` nine sections ago, on TR's eighteen recovered declines, and
`docs/PREREGISTRATION-CORTEX-MEMORY-ARM.md`'s §10.3 says so **in its own first bullet**. The run was cancelled
(`39180563526`, 40 seconds in) before it had asked a question, and nothing about §13.68's cap was measured by
it.

### 13.69.2 The mechanism: last-wins over a document that stated one concept twice

§13.64 appended an adoption bullet near the **top** of §10.3 and left §13.17's original bullet near the
**bottom**. After that section the document named `relevanceSignal` twice:

| position | statement                                               |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| top      | `relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid` — adopted by §13.64 |
| bottom   | `relevanceSignal: retrieval` — added by §13.17          |

`test_preregistration_config.py` parsed the block with `found[concept] = value` in a loop, so **last wins** and
the stale bullet won. The dispatch table also said `retrieval`. So the test compared the dispatch against the
stale bullet, found agreement, and passed — for six sections. Every layer of that chain was behaving correctly
except the one thing no layer owned: the document was answering one question twice.

**Nothing published is invalid.** Every dispatch since §13.64 carried `--set cortex_memory_relevance=retrieval-hybrid`
explicitly, so the runs that produced §13.64's and §13.66's numbers ran the adopted ranking. What was wrong was
the **default**, and a default that is wrong is invisible precisely until a dispatch forgets the override — which
is what happened here.

### 13.69.3 The repair, in three parts, each of which alone would be insufficient

1. **The stale bullet is retired**, and its opening line no longer spells a `concept: value` pair. The historical
   argument stays verbatim underneath, because it is still why the signal exists.
2. **A duplicate is now an error** rather than a precedence rule. `parse_block` raises, names the concept and
   prints both values, because the reader's next step is deciding which of the two to retire. A precedence rule
   would have been the wrong repair in either direction: whichever order it chose, the document would still
   contain two answers and a reader would still have to know the rule.
3. **The dispatch table names the adopted value**, with the reason and this section's number beside it.

The guard is a function over **text**, not over the document, and that is the part worth stating: asserting it
against the real §10.3 would pass forever once the duplicate is fixed, and a guard that only ever sees the fixed
input proves nothing about the state it exists to catch. Three tests: a synthetic duplicate is refused with both
values in the message, a clean block parses normally (the control, so the guard is not vacuous), and the real
registration states each concept exactly once.

### 13.69.4 Why the dispatch's own print is what caught it

The table's docstring argues that a value a run depends on should not arrive by accident, and that an absent key
cannot be shown to be wrong. Both arguments are about **omission**. This defect is about **contradiction**, and
the thing that caught it was not an assertion but the habit of printing the payload before sending it — the same
habit that made `cortex_memory_threshold = 0` visible instead of implicit.

So the lesson is narrower than "add more tests": a value printed on every dispatch is a second reader of the
configuration, and a second reader is what finds a document that disagrees with itself. §13.68's own config line
does the same job for the artifact.

### 13.69.5 What this does not change

- §13.64's adoption, §13.66's rank curve and §13.68's cap are unaffected: the first two ran with the override
  sent explicitly, and the third had not run.
- The `retrieval` signal is **not** refuted. It is the pre-§13.64 configuration and stays reachable by
  `--set cortex_memory_relevance=retrieval`, which is what a re-measurement of that comparison would use.
- The dispatch table now sends what §10.3 registers for every concept, and the test that says so can no longer be
  satisfied by a stale second statement.

## 13.70 The window table, so the cap's mechanism is readable and not only its outcome

### 13.70.1 What a coverage number cannot say

§13.68 registered the cap on **coverage** (prediction 1: MR's delivered gold share 54.2% → ≥62%) and on
**money** (prediction 2: MR correct 62 → ≥66). Both are outcomes. A cap can raise either for a reason neither
number names — the room now holds more turns, so a gold turn that used to be cut arrives — or it can raise
nothing because the roster already fitted and the cap only shortened turns that were not the constraint.

The artifact has carried both halves since §13.11 without anyone putting them side by side: `promptChars` (what
the assembled prompt spent) and `turns` (what it held). `--window` prints them together, per capability, as
medians:

| capability | n   | turns    | chars      | chars/turn | budget    |
| ---------- | --- | -------- | ---------- | ---------- | --------- |
| ABS        | 30  | 33.5     | 22,768     | 687        | 94.9%     |
| IE         | 150 | 29.5     | 23,050     | 763        | 96.0%     |
| KU         | 72  | 27.0     | 22,638     | 822        | 94.3%     |
| **MR**     | 121 | **23.0** | **21,657** | **947**    | **90.2%** |
| TR         | 127 | 26.0     | 22,540     | 855        | 93.9%     |
| **TOTAL**  | 500 | **26.0** | **22,406** | **842**    | **93.4%** |

Run `39116387165`, the control this variable is measured against.

### 13.70.2 What the table says that §13.67 could not

§13.67 measured the **delivered turns'** lengths across the whole roster: median 272 characters, p90 2,305. That
is a statement about the corpus. This table is a statement about the **prompts**: the turns that actually reach
the model average **842 characters** in a 24,000-character room, and the room is **93.4% spent**. So the cap is
not acting on a hypothetical tail — it is acting on the population that fills the room, and there is almost no
unused budget for it to compete with.

For MR specifically: 23 turns at 947 characters. Under a 400-character cap the same 21,657 characters hold
**≈ 53** turns, against a pool of 64 and the arm's 256-turn bound.

### 13.70.3 A diagnostic expectation, labelled as one

Before the run is read, and with the four registered predictions unchanged, the window table must show
**MR's median turns rising from 23 toward 50**. That is a **diagnostic expectation, not a prediction**: it does
not participate in accepting or rejecting the variable, it exists so that a run whose coverage moved without its
window moving is visible as a contradiction rather than read as a result. §13.59 wrote the same distinction down
after promoting a variable on a plausible reading.

### 13.70.4 Why medians, and why the per-turn column is a median of ratios

The artifacts are skewed — one question carries a 15,369-character turn and one carries twenty short statements
— so a mean describes a prompt nobody sent. More subtly, the `chars/turn` column is the **median of each
question's own ratio**, not the ratio of the two medians: the second answers "what would a median prompt spend on
a median count", which no single question is, while the first answers "how long is a typical turn in the
prompt", which is the quantity a cap acts on. The first draft used the ratio of medians and the difference was
visible in MR (942 against 947), which is small here and would not have been for a capability with a wider
spread.

### 13.70.5 Verification

- Three tests, red first: the turns-and-characters table, the budget share (a fixture at 21,000 of 24,000 is
  87.5%), and a record without `promptChars` **refusing** with exit 2 rather than counting as a 0% fill — zero
  would read as "this prompt spent none of its budget", which is a measurement rather than an absence.
- `PROMPT_BUDGET_CHARS = 24_000` is a copy of `DEFAULT_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS`, and the copy is safe because that
  constant is asserted in `cortex-memory`'s own tests: a change there fails a test there, and this tool would
  then describe artifacts with the wrong denominator — which the printed share makes visible rather than hides.
- `tools` **451 passed + 42 subtests**; `pnpm check` re-run before the readout is used to accept anything.

### 13.70.6 Status

| Priority      | Item                                                                                                                  | Needs provider |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| **P0**        | Read run `39180819474` (cap 400 on the adopted hybrid baseline) against §13.68.6, with `--window` beside `--coverage` | yes, in flight |
| **P0 (done)** | The window instrument, and the diagnostic expectation it makes checkable                                              | no             |
| **P1**        | MR's 31 `numeric_mismatch`, of which 11 count their own short list                                                    | yes            |
| P1            | The order function, now measurable per selection through `goldRanks`                                                  | yes            |
| P2            | The §13.55 sentence, now redundant, as its own variable                                                               | yes            |
| P3            | `PATH` ordering                                                                                                       | no             |

### 13.70.7 The exposure, measured before the run rather than assumed

A cap is only a variable if it binds, and its cost is only real if the turns it cuts are the ones carrying the
facts. Both are answerable from the control artifact, per **turn** rather than per question:

| capability | carried turns | longer than 400 | share     | characters removed |
| ---------- | ------------- | --------------- | --------- | ------------------ |
| ABS        | 991           | 321             | 32.4%     | 386,719            |
| IE         | 4,639         | 1,555           | 33.5%     | 2,002,633          |
| KU         | 2,097         | 730             | 34.8%     | 960,842            |
| **MR**     | 2,909         | **1,202**       | **41.3%** | **1,609,132**      |
| TR         | 3,479         | 1,301           | 37.4%     | 1,723,642          |
| **TOTAL**  | 14,115        | **5,109**       | **36.2%** | **6,682,968**      |

So the cap binds on **36.2%** of the turns the model currently reads, and on **41.3%** of MR's. Two consequences
stated before the numbers arrive:

- **The variable is not inert by construction.** A cap that touched 2% of turns could not move coverage and a
  null result would say nothing; this one removes 6.68 million characters from the delivered evidence.
- **The cost is not hypothetical either.** Four in ten of MR's turns will lose text, so §13.67.4's stated trade —
  _a turn whose decisive fact sits deep in a long narrative loses it_ — is being tested on a large minority of the
  population rather than on an edge case. Prediction 4 is what keeps that honest: if IE or KU falls outside its
  own measured rate while MR rises, the run has bought coverage with capability, and §13.68.7 says that needs its
  own argument rather than an adoption.

### 13.70.8 An interaction this variable creates, named before the run

The cap does not only move the cut. It also **lengthens the list the enumeration contract asks the model to
write**: MR's window goes from 23 turns to roughly 53, and under `ask: enumerated` every one of them has to be
considered for Step 1. So the same change that puts more gold in the window also makes the counting task harder,
and §13.59 measured that MR's failures are already of that kind — 14 of 27 numeric failures answer exactly the
number of items they listed, 10 of those off by exactly one.

Two consequences, both stated before the numbers:

- **Prediction 1 and prediction 2 can dissociate in a way that is not a failure of either.** Coverage is about
  what arrived; the correct count is about what the model did with it. A run reading _coverage 62%, correct 63_
  would say the window grew and the reader did not improve — which is §13.59's finding restated on a bigger
  window, and would move the next variable to the arithmetic without contradicting anything here.
- **A rise in `numeric_mismatch` is therefore not evidence against the cap.** It is the expected companion of a
  longer list. §13.61's cost accounting made the same distinction when the closing line moved: the cost appeared
  as `numeric_mismatch` and was counted as the price rather than as a refutation.

This is written down now because it is the explanation that would otherwise be available after the fact, and an
explanation available only after the fact is not a measurement.

## 13.71 Prediction 1 was registered against the wrong statistic, and the error is corrected before the result exists

### 13.71.1 What §13.67.5 said, and what the number actually was

Prediction 1 reads: _"**Coverage rises**: MR's delivered gold share rises from **54.2%** to **≥ 62%** of its
total."_

`54.2%` is **not** a delivered gold share. On the control artifact the three candidate numbers are:

| statistic                                                          | value     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------- |
| MR **aggregate** delivered share (`Σcarried / Σtotal`)             | **42.5%** |
| MR median per-question coverage, all 121 questions                 | 44.4%     |
| MR median per-question coverage **among correct answers** (n = 62) | 53.1%     |

The 54.2% is the third statistic, read from run `39083274990` — a **different configuration** (`relevanceSignal:
retrieval`, pre-§13.64) — and it appears in §13.51.2's table as _"MR: correct 54.2% (n= 62)"_. So the
registration
took a **median over the answered subset of one run** and used it as the **aggregate baseline of another**. Three
errors in one number, and every one of them is the class this campaign keeps finding: the instrument read a field
that was not the field the sentence named.

### 13.71.2 Why this has to be fixed now rather than explained later

The run is in flight (`39180819474`, dispatched before this section was written). If it lands at **56%**, the
original prediction is _falsified_ (56 < 62) while the honest reading is **+13.5 points** — a large success
reported as a failure. If it lands at **61%**, the original is falsified by one point while being a near-doubling
of the effect the registration intended. Either way, evaluating the original number would produce a conclusion
about the arithmetic of a wrong baseline rather than about the cap.

Correcting it **before** the artifact exists is the only version of this that is still pre-registration. The
correction is stated with the error, the corrected baseline is measured rather than assumed, and the original
target is retained as a secondary check so that neither form can be quietly forgotten:

|                            | baseline  | target      | meaning                                       |
| -------------------------- | --------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| original (wrong statistic) | 54.2%     | ≥ 62%       | a median-among-correct from another run       |
| **corrected**              | **42.5%** | **≥ 50.2%** | the same **+7.7 points** the original implied |

Both are reported. A run reading between 50.2% and 62% satisfies the corrected prediction and fails the
original; §13.71.4 says how that is to be read — as the corrected form holding, with the original recorded as
mis-specified rather than as a near miss.

### 13.71.3 The geometry `goldRanks` now permits, computed on the control before the result

`goldRanks` records each gold turn's position in the ranked pool, so the delivered share at any window width is
computable **without a model**. On the control artifact, MR's in-pool gold captured by the top _k_ of the pool:

| k                        | 23    | 26    | 40    | 53        | 64    |
| ------------------------ | ----- | ----- | ----- | --------- | ----- |
| MR in-pool gold captured | 44.9% | 48.3% | 60.9% | **67.8%** | 71.9% |

The control's measured aggregate is **42.5%** against **44.9%** at k = 23 — a **−2.4 point** offset between
geometry and measurement, which is what a room of _characters_ rather than _turns_ does: the median MR prompt
holds 23 turns (§13.70.1), the pool's tail is longer than the median, so the room lands near rank 21 or 22 rather
than 23.

At a 400-character cap MR's 21,657 characters hold **≈ 53** turns, so the same offset applied to the k = 53
figure gives an expectation of **≈ 65%**. That is a **diagnostic band, not a prediction** (§13.70.3's rule): it
does not participate in accepting the variable, and its purpose is to make a mismatch legible — a reading near
**50%** would say the room did not grow as the character arithmetic says it should, and the window table is where
that would be visible.

### 13.71.4 How the result will be read, decided now

1. **Prediction 1** is evaluated against the **corrected** form (≥ 50.2%) and reported against both.
2. **Prediction 2** (MR correct 62 → ≥ 66) is unchanged; it was registered on a count, and counts are the one
   thing this campaign has never mis-read.
3. **Prediction 3** (roster 371 → ≥ 379) is unchanged.
4. **Prediction 4** (IE and KU inside their own rates) is unchanged, and it is the price.
5. If the window table shows MR's median turns **did not rise**, the cap did not bind and every coverage reading
   is about something else — that check comes **before** any of the four, because it is a precondition and not a
   result.

### 13.71.5 What this section is not

It is not a redraw. Nothing about the outcome is known: the run has asked some of its questions and none of its
artifact exists. What is being corrected is a **baseline derived from a different statistic on a different
configuration**, discovered by computing the correct statistic on the control while the treatment ran. §4's
no-redraw rule forbids changing a target to fit a result; it cannot require keeping a target computed from the
wrong number, because that would make the registration a record of arithmetic rather than of intent.

The cost is recorded: **five sections** (§13.63, §13.64, §13.66, §13.67, and the docs sections that quote them)
carry the sentence _"the pool holds 73.2% of the gold and the delivery 54.2%"_, and every one of them pairs an
**all-capabilities** pool figure with a **median-among-correct** MR figure. The correct pairing, on the hybrid
control, is **pool 73.2% all-capabilities against delivered 49.8% all-capabilities**, and **MR pool 71.9%
against MR delivered 42.5%**. Both are stated here so the earlier sentences have a correction in the record
rather than a silent successor.

### 13.71.6 Where the corrected statistic is read from, stated so it cannot be confused again

The aggregate share is `--pool`'s **delivered ÷ gold** column, per capability. `--coverage` reports
**per-question medians by band**, which is a different statistic and is the one the wrong baseline was taken
from. So the reading for prediction 1 is:

```text
python3 tools/readout-arm-run.py --pool  <artifact>   # aggregate: MR delivered / MR gold
python3 tools/readout-arm-run.py --coverage <artifact> # medians by band: the shape, not the level
```

Both are printed, and §13.71's correction exists because the second was used to write down a target for the first.
This costs nothing to state and is the only way the sentence "coverage rose" can be checked by a reader who has
the tool rather than the prose.

### 13.71.7 Which readout shows the cap, and which deliberately does not

`--turns` reports the lengths of the **roster's** turns, and §13.68.2 keeps that roster uncapped on purpose — a
truncated roster would fail to match the gold turns it delivered, because `goldOverlap` compares by text. So
`--turns` on a capped run will look **unchanged**, and that is the instrument working rather than the cap
failing.

What changes is `--window`: the turn **count** rises while `promptChars` stays at the budget, which is what
"more turns in the same room" means. A reader who saw `--turns` unchanged and concluded the cap was inert would
be reading the corpus measure and expecting it to describe a prompt.

## 13.72 The cap moved every mechanism it was registered for, and cost thirty IE questions to do it

### 13.72.1 The reading, prediction by prediction

Run `39180819474`, 1h37m43s, `drift` 500/500 with zero answers differing, config line
`relevanceSignal=retrieval-hybrid relevanceTopK=64 relevanceUnits=turn`, and `maxTurnChars=400` in both the log
and the artifact.

| #     | registered                                                   | observed              | verdict                                                 |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **1** | MR's delivered share 42.5% → **≥ 50.2%** (corrected, §13.71) | **72.2%** (2644/3663) | **met**, by 22 points                                   |
| 1′    | the original form: 54.2% → ≥ 62%                             | 72.2%                 | met — but the original baseline was the wrong statistic |
| **2** | MR correct 62 → **≥ 66**                                     | **75**                | **met**, +13                                            |
| **3** | roster 371 → **≥ 379**                                       | **357**               | **falsified**, −14                                      |
| **4** | IE and KU inside their own measured rates (5 / 7)            | IE **−30**, KU −4     | **falsified** on IE, met on KU                          |

The precondition held and must be read first: MR's median turns went **23 → 68** and `promptChars` stayed at
22,149 of 24,000. The cap bound, the window nearly tripled, and the diagnostic band §13.71.3 registered
(≈ 65%) was exceeded for a reason the next paragraph gives.

Per capability, against the control (`39116387165`):

| capability       | control          | cap 400              | Δ       |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | -------------------- | ------- |
| ABS              | 30               | 30                   | 0       |
| IE               | 133              | **103**              | **−30** |
| KU               | 61               | 57                   | −4      |
| **MR**           | 62               | **75**               | **+13** |
| TR               | 85               | **92**               | +7      |
| **roster**       | **371**          | **357**              | **−14** |
| registered delta | +30.45pp         | +26.80pp             | −3.65pp |
| union            | 437/500 = 87.40% | 401/500 = **80.20%** | **−36** |

### 13.72.2 The mechanism worked better than it was predicted to, and the reason is new

§13.71.3's geometry said a room holding ~53 turns would capture ~67.8% of MR's gold, and predicted ≈ 65% after the
offset the control showed. The run delivered **72.2%** — above the pool's own 71.9% ceiling.

It can go above the ceiling because **the room is now wider than the pool**: 68 turns against 64 scored
candidates, so the selection continues past the ranked set into turns the ranking never offered. Fifty-four gold
turns arrived that way across the arm (MR 12, TR 13, ABS 22, KU 7). That was not predicted, and it is only visible
because `goldOverlap` carries `pool` — the field exists for exactly this kind of surprise rather than for the
question it was built for.

### 13.72.3 The price, and its shape: thirty questions that stopped being answered

IE's loss is not diffuse. Of its 150 questions, **30 went `correct → abstention`**, and its declines rose
**15 → 42**. Their median coverage is **100%** — every gold turn was in the window when the model declined.

So the model was given complete evidence and withdrew. This is not the §13.51 "declining with the evidence in
hand" defect returning by accident: IE is on the **flat** route, which never received §13.57's conditional closing
line, so its block still ends with the unconditional _"If the evidence does not contain the answer, reply exactly
INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE."_ Seventy-three turns of mostly-irrelevant text give that sentence more opportunities to be
true, and the model takes them.

The contrast inside one run makes the point better than any aggregate:

|                                           | declines    | coverage among declines | correct       |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------- |
| **MR** (multi-session, conditional close) | 18 → **10** | 21% → **54%**           | 62 → **75**   |
| **IE** (flat, unconditional close)        | 15 → **42** | 43% → **100%**          | 133 → **103** |

**The same intervention moved abstention in opposite directions on two capabilities**, and the difference tracks
the closing line rather than the coverage.

### 13.72.4 The instrument that broke, and it broke correctly

`GoldOverlap.pool` and `--pool` were built on an assumption stated as an invariant: `carried ≤ pool ≤ total`,
because the delivery is a prefix of the ranked pool. With the room wider than the pool, `carried > pool` is a
**legitimate** state — gold delivered from turns the ranking never scored — and the table printed it as a
**negative** "cut by the budget" and called fourteen records a caller defect.

Both were fixed in this iteration, with tests, and the honest reading of the failure is that the invariant was a
property of the _regime_ rather than of the data: it held for every run while the window was smaller than the
pool, and it stopped holding the first time a variable made the window larger. The table now carries both
directions as separate columns clamped at zero, and only `pool > total` / `carried > total` remain defects.

### 13.72.5 The verdict

**Rejected as a global default.** The roster fell 371 → 357, the union fell 87.40% → 80.20%, and the price is
concentrated in one capability at a measured rate of −30 against a cross-draw noise floor of ±2 for IE.

**Not rejected as a mechanism.** Every mechanism prediction was met or exceeded: delivered share +29.7 points,
declines on MR halved, window nearly tripled, `promptChars` unchanged. The cap does exactly what §13.67 said the
room was doing — it is simply not true that every capability wants the same room.

That is the finding worth keeping, and it is the first time in this campaign that a variable has been **accepted
on one capability and rejected on another within a single run**: MR +13 and TR +7 are named transitions
(`numeric_mismatch → correct` 14, `other → correct` 4, `abstention → correct` 6 on MR), and IE's −30 is thirty
named transitions the other way. Neither is noise, and a single switch cannot express both.

### 13.72.6 What this changes about the campaign's picture

- **The evidence room is not one number.** §13.34.3's count argument and §13.67's character argument were both
  right, and both were answering for the arm as a whole. This run says the optimum is per route.
- **Abstention is a function of list length as well as of coverage.** IE declines at 100% coverage, 42 times.
  That is §13.51's question — _why does a model with the evidence decline?_ — answered for a second capability in
  a different direction.
- **MR's remaining gap is now 32, not 49.** Union 107 on MR against a baseline of 102: the feature answers 75
  where the reference answers 102. The cap moved the coverage constraint a long way and left the counting
  constraint where §13.59 found it — `numeric_mismatch` 31, of which 11 count their own short list.

### 13.72.7 Verification and status

- `drift`: 500 of 500 records, 0 answers differing — the read was not through a stale parser (§13.60's rule).
- `--pool` and its three tests were **changed in this iteration** because the run falsified the invariant they
  encoded; `tools` **454 passed + 42 subtests**; one pre-existing fixture was rewritten rather than kept green.
- `pnpm check` is re-run before this section is committed.

| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------- |

| **P0 (done)** | The global cap's reading: 1 and 2 met, 3 and 4 falsified, mechanism confirmed and rejected as a default            | —              |
| **P1**        | MR's 31 `numeric_mismatch`, of which 11 count their own short list — unchanged by the cap, as §13.70.8 predicted   | yes            |

| P3            | `PATH` ordering                                                                                                    | no             |

## 13.73 The next variable is the cap's reach, and it is one variable

### 13.73.1 Why reach rather than a different width

§13.72 measured the cap at one width (400) over every route and found both a large gain and a large loss. The
obvious next question is whether some _other_ width is better for everyone, and the run already answers it: the
loss is not a matter of degree. IE's thirty questions went `correct → abstention` with **100%** coverage — the
evidence was complete and the model withdrew. No smaller cap turns a complete window into a partial one on a
capability whose questions need one turn; it only changes how many distractors surround it. So a sweep would
find a width that is a compromise between two capabilities rather than a setting that is right for both.

The reach is the variable because the two behaviours are on different routes, and the campaign's own pattern for
route-varying behaviour is a reach set: `renderingRoutes` (§12.9) and `askRoutes` (§13) are both explicit lists
of which routes an option reaches, recorded in the artifact, with the untouched routes asserted to be
byte-identical.

### 13.73.2 Which routes, and the evidence for each

| route             | capability whose questions land there | evidence                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **multi-session** | MR                                    | +13 correct, declines 18 → 10, coverage 21% → 54% among declines. The only move in this run far outside any capability's own noise                                                               |
| **temporal**      | TR                                    | +7 correct, declines flat at 25 → 26 while their coverage rose 40% → 62%. Low-risk, plausibly real, and **inside** TR's own 15-question churn — so it is included for its _shape_, not its count |
| flat              | IE                                    | **−30**, all as `correct → abstention` at 100% coverage. Excluded because of this                                                                                                                |
| knowledge-update  | KU                                    | −4, inside its own rate, on a route with its own block. Excluded as the conservative reading of a move the instrument cannot separate from noise                                                 |
| abstention        | ABS                                   | 0 in both runs. Excluded because nothing moved                                                                                                                                                   |

**TR's inclusion is the one judgement in this table**, and the registration says so: its own cross-draw rate is
15 of 127, so +7 is not evidence. What justifies including it is that the temporal route's block also ends with
the conditional close §13.57 introduced, and its declines did not rise while their coverage did — the opposite
of the signature that cost IE thirty questions. If the run contradicts that, the reach is one route and the
finding is narrower than this section's argument.

### 13.73.3 Registration

**One variable**: `maxTurnChars: 400` applied on the multi-session and temporal routes, and on no others.
Everything else is held: `ask: enumerated`, `relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid`, `relevanceTopK: 64`,
`relevanceUnits: turn`, both thresholds `0`, `sourceTrust 0.5`, `promptContract abstention-evidence-blocks`.

| #     | prediction                                                                                    | falsified if |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| **1** | **IE returns**: ≥ **130** of 150 (control 133; the cap run 103; IE's own rate ±2)             | ≤ 129        |
| **2** | **MR keeps the gain**: ≥ **70** (control 62; cap run 75; MR's rate ±4)                        | ≤ 69         |
| **3** | **KU holds**: ≥ **58** (control 61; KU's rate ±7)                                             | ≤ 57         |
| **4** | **TR holds**: ≥ **80** (control 85; cap run 92; TR's rate ±15)                                | ≤ 79         |
| **5** | **the roster rises**: ≥ **378** (control 371, dispatched on §13.66's deterministic retrieval) | ≤ 377        |

Prediction 1 is the **price restored** and prediction 2 is the **mechanism kept**; they are the two that carry the
argument, and 3–5 exist so that a total cannot hide a trade the instrument is fine enough to see — §13.64.6's
rule, and §13.68.6's.

**Not implemented in this section.** §13.67 did the same thing one iteration earlier and it was right for a
reason this run has now demonstrated twice: the change touches `#promptOptions`, which is where a field becomes
inert without anything failing (§13.68.1's third layer), and the route a prompt is built for is not currently an
input to that method. Doing that in the closing minutes of an iteration is how a byte-identity guarantee breaks —
and the byte-identity here is what keeps the three unchanged routes comparable to their own control runs.

### 13.73.4 What each outcome would mean, decided before the run

- **1, 2 and 5 hold**: the reach is the finding, the roster is near 391, and the next variable is MR's
  arithmetic (§13.59's 11 short-list counts) rather than retrieval.
- **2 holds and 1 does not**: the cap's effect is not route-shaped and the scope assumption is wrong; the next
  step is per-capability width rather than per-route reach, which is a different mechanism (a rule inside the
  prompt rather than a reach set).
- **1 holds and 2 does not**: the gain was an artefact of the same flooding that cost IE, and the cap is
  rejected outright.
- **4 fails while 1–3 hold**: TR's +7 was noise, the reach narrows to one route, and the documented finding is
  that only multi-session wants a wider window.

## 13.74 The reach is implemented, and the compiler is what enforces it

### 13.74.1 Six routes, named by argument rather than defaulted

`#promptOptions` used to take no arguments and apply every prompt option to every route. It now takes the
`TurnCapRoute` the caller is building for, and `#prompt` — the shared path for flat, abstention, assistant and
knowledge-update — takes it as a **required fourth parameter**. The two builders that are one route by
construction name theirs inline (`temporal`, `multi-session`).

Required rather than defaulted, and that is the whole mechanism: a seventh route added later cannot compile
without naming itself, so it cannot silently inherit a cap the artifact says reaches two routes. §13.68.5
recorded the one spread in `bench/run-ablation.ts` that no test reaches; this change removes the analogous risk
from the product side by making the omission a type error rather than a missing line.

The six names live in **one** place per package, and in the product they are one declaration:

```ts
export const TURN_CAP_ROUTES = [
  'multi-session',
  'temporal',
  'flat',
  'knowledge-update',
  'abstention',
  'assistant',
] as const;
export type TurnCapRoute = (typeof TURN_CAP_ROUTES)[number];
```

A list **and** a union rather than a union alone, because the names have to exist at runtime to be validated
against a dispatched reach. Deriving the union from the list means a seventh route cannot be added to one form
without the other.

### 13.74.2 Three spellings, and why `none` is not `absent`

| spelling        | meaning      | why it exists                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| absent or `all` | every route  | the shipped state; `all` so a dispatch can send what §10.3 registers           |
| `none`          | no route     | a run that configures a cap it does not apply — a different claim from absence |
| `a,b,c`         | those routes | the experiment                                                                 |

The config line renders all three distinctly (`all` / `none` / `multi-session+temporal`), joined with `+`
because the line already separates fields with commas. A renderer that collapsed `none` into `all` would
describe the one run that did nothing as the one that did everything, and there is a test for exactly that.

An unrecognised route name is **rejected**, and the message lists the six. Accepted-and-ignored is the failure
that matters here: a typo would apply the cap to five routes while the artifact said six, and every number in
the run would be consistent with the claim.

### 13.74.3 The parity guard was missing, and §13.69's new guard caught me in a minute

`bench-memory-arm.ts` has said since §13.35 that `tools/__tests__/test_ask_table_parity.py` "compares the two
key sets by source". It did not: the module existed **only as a `.pyc`**, so the guard had not run since the
source went missing, and the sentence kept asserting an assertion that no longer existed — the same defect the
module was written for, one level up.

It is restored from its own compiled form, with its two original tests and the same regexes, and extended to the
route vocabulary and to `report.ts`'s `TURN_CAP_ROUTE_COUNT`. Then it did its job immediately: the first
version of §10.3's new bullet quoted the pair `(`maxTurnChars: none`, `maxTurnCharsRoutes: all`)` in prose, the
duplicate detector fired on `maxTurnChars` before the commit existed, and the fix was one rephrasing. A guard
that catches its author within a minute of being restored is worth more than one that has never fired.

### 13.74.4 What is registered, and what the run will decide

Registration is §13.73.3's, unchanged: cap 400 on **multi-session + temporal**, five predictions with each
capability's own rate beside its bound. The dispatch overrides two inputs and holds everything else at §10.3.

### 13.74.5 Verification

- **Red first through the product**: three reach tests failed before `#capReaches` existed, and they assert
  **byte equality** of the prompt on every unreached route — not "shorter", not "uncapped text absent", because
  only equality shows the route is comparable to its own control.
- **Red first through the arm**: seven tests failed before the reader existed, including the rejection of a
  mistyped route and the three renderings of the config line.
- **Four pre-existing whole-shape assertions were extended, not relaxed**: the arm's config grew a field, and a
  test that pins the shape has to pin the new member or it stops describing the object.
- `cortex-memory` **368** (+5), `cortex-eval` **1922** (+7), `tools` **459 passed + 44 subtests**, `pnpm check`
  **exit 0**, four coverage dimensions **100%** (`cortex-node` branch 98.64%, §13.47's known gap).
- Byte-identity for archived runs: `maxTurnChars` absent still means no cap anywhere; a cap with no reach still
  reaches all six, which is what §13.68's run measured.

## 13.75 What the window table has to show for the reach to be what the run claims

### 13.75.1 The claim that is easy to assert and hard to check

The registration says the cap reaches **two** routes. The artifact will say so on its config line
(`maxTurnCharsRoutes=multi-session+temporal`), and a config line is a claim about intent — §13.69 exists because
one of those claims was wrong while every assertion passed.

The reach is falsifiable from the artifact without any new instrument, because `--window` reports turns carried
and characters spent **per capability**, and the four uncapped capabilities must reproduce their control:

| capability | route            | expected under the reach                   |
| ---------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| MR         | multi-session    | turns 23 → ~53–68, coverage 42.5% → rising |
| TR         | temporal         | turns 26 → ~53–68, coverage 43.6% → rising |
| IE         | flat             | **unchanged**: 29.5 turns, 23,050 chars    |
| KU         | knowledge-update | **unchanged**: 27.0 turns, 22,638 chars    |
| ABS        | abstention       | **unchanged**: 33.5 turns, 22,768 chars    |

A reach that leaked would show up as a moved turn count on IE, KU or ABS, and would do so **before** any accuracy
number moved — the window is a property of the prompt, not of the model. That makes it the cheapest check in the
run and the first one to perform.

### 13.75.2 The geometry, computed on the control before the result

From the control artifact's `goldRanks`, the in-pool gold captured by the top _k_ of the pool:

| k                       | MR    | TR    |
| ----------------------- | ----- | ----- |
| 23 / 26 (control rooms) | 44.9% | 47.1% |
| 40                      | 60.9% | 57.5% |
| 53                      | 67.8% | 63.8% |
| 64                      | 71.9% | 68.0% |

The control's measured delivered shares are MR **42.5%** and TR **43.6%**, each a couple of points under its
k-figure because the room is characters rather than turns (§13.71.3). At a 400-character cap the same rooms hold
roughly 53 turns, so **MR ≈ 65% and TR ≈ 61%** are the geometry's expectation — again a **diagnostic band, not a
prediction**, and §13.73.3's five predictions are what decide the variable.

### 13.75.3 What this section is for

It exists so that the first thing read from the artifact is the thing that cannot be argued with afterwards: the
window on the four untouched capabilities. If IE's turn count moves, the run has measured something other than
what it registered, and every capability number in it becomes a statement about an unknown configuration — which
is §13.69's failure mode, caught this time before publication rather than after.

## 13.76 The reach is adopted: five predictions met, and the IE collapse reverses

### 13.76.1 The reading

Run `39205060432`, 1h49m29s, `drift` 500/500 with zero answers differing, config line
`maxTurnChars=400 maxTurnCharsRoutes=multi-session+temporal`, everything else at §10.3.

| #     | registered (§13.73.3) | observed | verdict                               |
| ----- | --------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------- |
| **1** | IE ≥ **130** of 150   | **135**  | **met** — and above the control's 133 |
| **2** | MR ≥ **70**           | **72**   | **met**                               |
| **3** | KU ≥ **58**           | **59**   | **met**                               |
| **4** | TR ≥ **80**           | **94**   | **met**, +9 over the control          |
| **5** | roster ≥ **378**      | **389**  | **met**, +18 over the control         |

**Roster 389/500 = 77.80%**, the campaign's best by 14 questions; registered delta **+32.95pp**, also the best;
union **439/500 = 87.80%**, above the previous high of 437.

### 13.76.2 The check that had to come first, and it came out exact

§13.75 registered the reach's cheapest falsifier: the three untouched capabilities must reproduce their control
**to the turn**, because the window is a property of the prompt and not of the model.

| capability | control turns / chars | this run          |           |
| ---------- | --------------------- | ----------------- | --------- |
| IE         | 29.5 / 23,050         | **29.5 / 23,050** | identical |
| KU         | 27.0 / 22,638         | **27.0 / 22,638** | identical |
| ABS        | 33.5 / 22,768         | **33.5 / 22,768** | identical |
| MR         | 23.0 / 21,657         | 68.0 / 22,149     | capped    |
| TR         | 26.0 / 22,540         | 72.0 / 23,112     | capped    |

Three identical windows is the strongest statement available that the reach did what its name says, and it was
made before any accuracy number was read.

### 13.76.3 The reversal, which is stronger evidence than the original effect

§13.72's run capped every route and IE's declines went **15 → 42**, losing thirty questions to
`correct → abstention` at a median coverage of 100%. This run removes the flat route from the reach and IE's
declines go **15 → 13**, with its accuracy **133 → 135**.

|             | control | cap on all six | cap on two |
| ----------- | ------- | -------------- | ---------- |
| IE correct  | 133     | **103**        | **135**    |
| IE declines | 15      | **42**         | **13**     |
| MR correct  | 62      | 75             | **72**     |
| MR declines | 18      | 10             | **11**     |
| TR correct  | 85      | 92             | **94**     |
| TR declines | 25      | 26             | **24**     |
| KU correct  | 61      | 57             | **59**     |
| ABS correct | 30      | 30             | 29         |
| **roster**  | **371** | **357**        | **389**    |

A correlation can be explained by a third variable; a **reversal** of the same quantity in the same direction
twice cannot. The cap on the flat route caused the decline spike, and taking it off removed it.

### 13.76.4 What the two runs of the capped routes now say together

MR and TR have each been measured at this cap twice — once with every route capped, once with two:

|     | control | cap, all routes | cap, two routes |
| --- | ------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| MR  | 62      | 75              | 72              |
| TR  | 85      | 92              | 94              |

Both are above the control in **both** draws, and the two draws bracket each other within their noise. That is
2-of-2 on each route, which is the strongest claim this campaign can make without repetitions on the same
configuration — and it is what adopts TR's inclusion, which §13.73.2 labelled "the one judgement in the table"
and justified on shape rather than on its +7.

### 13.76.5 Adopted, and what the adoption does not claim

**Adopted**: `maxTurnChars: 400` with `maxTurnCharsRoutes: multi-session,temporal`. Both move into §10.3 and into
the dispatch table, so a future run that forgets the reach would be caught by
`test_preregistration_config.py` rather than by a reader.

Not claimed:

- **Not** that the numbers are the _best_ setting. 400 was registered by §13.67 from the turn-length
  distribution and has now been measured twice; nothing here says 300 or 600 is worse.
- **Not** that TR is settled. Its own cross-draw rate is 15 questions of 127, and two draws above the control is
  evidence of a sign, not of a magnitude.
- **Not** that ABS's 30 → 29 is a cost. ABS's prompt is byte-identical to the control's (33.5 turns, 22,768
  characters), so its one lost question is model sampling and nothing else — and the same reading makes IE's
  133 → 135 and KU's 61 → 59 sampling too. The +18 is MR **+10** and TR **+9** with the untouched three at −1
  between them.
- **Not** that the union is the SOTA line. 439/500 = 87.80% is what the two sides together can already do, and it
  belongs to no single system.

### 13.76.6 What this leaves, and in what order

The remaining gap is **50 questions**: MR 35, TR 14, and ABS 1. MR is 70% of it, and MR's failure taxonomy is now
`numeric_mismatch 33`, `abstention 11`, `long_prose 1` — 45 wrong answers of which three quarters are a number
that is not the gold number.

That is §13.59's finding, on the largest window the arm has ever had, and §13.70.8 predicted it in advance: _the
same change that puts more gold in the window also makes the counting task harder, and a rise in
`numeric_mismatch` is the expected companion of a longer list rather than evidence against the cap_. It rose
31 → 33 while coverage rose 42.5% → 72.2%, exactly as registered.

So the next variable is **MR's arithmetic**, and for the first time it is not competing with a retrieval
question: the window holds 72.2% of MR's gold, the pool's own ceiling is 71.9%, and the room now reaches past the
pool. There is nothing left to retrieve that the ranking could find.

## 13.77 "MR's arithmetic" was the wrong name: three explanations tested and three eliminated

### 13.77.1 What §13.76.6 said, and what the measurement says instead

§13.76.6 named the next variable _MR's arithmetic_, reading the taxonomy — `numeric_mismatch 33` of 45 wrong
answers, three quarters of them a number that is not the gold number. `--lists` (this section's instrument) puts
four candidate explanations against the artifact, and **three of them fail**:

| #   | explanation                    | what would have to be true                          | measured                                                                                | verdict        |
| --- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| 1   | **the list is short**          | lists shorter for failures than for correct answers | median **2.0** items in both groups                                                     | **eliminated** |
| 2   | **the cap cut the item away**  | failures carry more truncated turns                 | 39.1% of turns truncated in failures against **40.8%** in correct answers               | **eliminated** |
| 3   | **the room cut the gold turn** | gold turns at rank ≥ room                           | **69 of 72** correct and **31 of 33** numeric failures have **no** excluded gold at all | **eliminated** |
| 4   | **coverage**                   | failures show less of the gold                      | correct **86.8%** median, numeric **70.8%**, abstention **50.0%**                       | **survives**   |

So the model is not miscounting a list it built, the cap is not eating the deciding fact, and the window is not
cutting gold — it is **showing less gold on the questions it fails**, and the list it writes from what it sees is
the same length either way.

### 13.77.2 Why explanation 3 is the surprising one

The cap took MR's window from 23 turns to 68 against a 64-wide pool, so the room is now **larger than the pool**:
every ranked candidate fits, and the selection spills into unscored turns (12 gold turns arrived "beyond the
pool" in §13.76). `goldRanks` makes this checkable per question, and it comes out stronger than expected — for
**100 of 105** MR questions, every gold turn the ranker surfaced is already inside the window.

That means the cut has stopped being the mechanism. The window has absorbed the pool, and the remaining loss is
the **28% of gold the ranker never surfaces at all** (§13.76.1: 1031 of 3663 turns for MR).

### 13.77.3 What `--lists` had to be able to see

Three tests, red first: the list length beside the gold (the row has to carry both numbers, because the finding
is their difference); the distinction between a statement that equals its own list length and one that does not
(§13.59's split, which is what separates "faithful count of a short list" from "aggregation"); and the
truncation share **per outcome**, because a table that reported only list lengths would leave explanation 2
standing. The exclusion-language column exists for the same reason — it is what identified
`3a704032`'s snake plant as a _judgement_ about the date range rather than a missed turn, and it comes out
**2 of 33**, so "the model decided not to count it" is not the general shape either.

### 13.77.4 The one number the campaign still cannot read

`goldRanks` records `-1` for a gold turn the ranking did not surface, and **-1 does not say how far away it
was**. A gold turn at rank 65 of a 64-wide pool is a near miss that a wider pool would fix; one at rank 900 is a
ranking failure that no width reaches. §13.66 answered that question for the _aggregate_ (the median rank of
surfaced-but-cut gold was ≈ 45 against a room of 26); it cannot be asked of the 28% that never surfaced, because
their ranks were never computed.

That is the instrument gap §13.78 closes, and it is the reason the next run is a **diagnostic** rather than a
test of a hypothesis.

## 13.78 Widening the pool is a different experiment now, and its purpose is a rank the campaign has never seen

### 13.78.1 Why this is not §13.54 again

§13.54 dispatched `relevanceTopK: 256` and read it as a refutation: coverage did not rise, MR's declines rose by
4, TR's coverage fell 39.7% → 32.8%. The mechanism was clear in hindsight and is recorded in §13.66: with a
**26-turn room** and a 64-wide pool, the extra 192 candidates could not enter the window at all, so widening the
pool changed nothing except which floor-scored turns happened to occupy the last few slots.

That mechanism is gone. The room now holds **68** turns (§13.76.2) and the pool is **64**, so:

- every ranked candidate fits, and the selection already spills into unscored turns (12 gold turns arrived
  "beyond the pool");
- **the pool has become the cut** — §13.77.2's measurement that 100 of 105 MR questions have no excluded gold
  turn is a statement about the pool's width, not about the room.

So the same input value is a different experiment, and §4's no-redraw rule is about not re-running a hypothesis
that was refuted _under the configuration it was refuted in_. The configuration changed by measurement, not by
argument.

### 13.78.2 What the run is actually for

`goldRanks` records `-1` for a gold turn the ranking never surfaced, and **`-1` is not a distance**. The two
readings it conflates need opposite repairs:

| if the missing gold sits at rank … | the repair is                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| 65–90                              | a wider pool — a knob                |
| 300–900                            | a better ranker — a research problem |

At `k = 64` the artifact cannot tell them apart for the 28% of MR's gold that never surfaces. At `k = 256` every
gold turn up to rank 255 gets a **number**, which means the question "how far away is the gold we cannot reach"
becomes answerable once, for the whole arm, instead of being argued from medians.

### 13.78.3 Registration

**One variable**: `relevanceTopK: 256`, everything else at §10.3 — including the adopted `maxTurnChars: 400` with
`maxTurnCharsRoutes: multi-session,temporal`, `relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid`, and both thresholds at 0.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                                                                             | falsified if |
| ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| **1** | **`never surfaced` falls**: MR's share of gold the ranker does not surface drops from **28.1%** to **≤ 22%**                                                           | > 28.1%      |
| **2** | **Delivery barely moves**: MR's delivered share changes by **≤ 5 points** in either direction (the room holds 68 of 256, so a wider pool mostly re-orders the same 68) | outside ±5   |
| **3** | **The instrument is otherwise inert**: roster within **±6** of 389                                                                                                     | outside      |
| **4** | **The measurement, not a prediction**: the median true rank of the gold turns that `k = 64` could not surface — reported as a number for the first time                | n/a          |

Prediction 1 is the mechanism ("a wider pool surfaces more"), prediction 2 is its **ceiling** and is why this is
not expected to be an accuracy win, 3 is the instrument's neutrality, and 4 is the point of the run.

### 13.78.4 What each outcome would mean

- **1 and 2 hold, and the median rank is 65–90**: the missing gold is a near miss, a wider pool is the lever, and
  §13.54's refutation is narrowed to "a wide pool is useless when the room is narrow" — which is a better
  statement than the one it replaced.
- **1 holds and the median rank is 300+**: the ranker cannot reach its own gold, the pool width is irrelevant, and
  the next variable is the ranker — a research problem, registered separately.
- **1 fails**: the extra 192 candidates are worse than the floor-scored turns they displace, which would say the
  ranking's tail is noise and that 64 is already generous.

### 13.78.5 Cost, stated because it is the one thing that can go wrong

Scoring 256 candidates per question is four times the pairs of 64 (32,000 → 128,000 over the dataset). The index
build is a separate phase from the passes and is bounded by the same 90-minute per-pass ceiling; on the
`39116387165` run the build logged 32,000 pairs in well under a minute, so four times that is still small against
a 100-minute pass. If the build does dominate, the artifact's own timings say so rather than the run failing
silently.

## 13.79 The unreachable gold sits at rank 114, and MR's accuracy is a step function at 85% coverage

### 13.79.1 The reading

Run `39228533156`, 1h43m12s, `drift` 500/500 with zero answers differing, config line
`relevanceTopK=256` with `maxTurnChars=400 maxTurnCharsRoutes=multi-session+temporal`.

| #     | registered (§13.78.3)                       | observed                 | verdict                        |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------ |
| **1** | MR's never-surfaced ≤ **22%**               | **5.0%** (182 of 3663)   | **met**, by 23 points          |
| **2** | MR's delivered share within **±5** of 72.2% | **72.9%** (2670 of 3663) | **met**                        |
| **3** | roster within **±6** of 389                 | **394**                  | **met**                        |
| **4** | the median true rank beyond the old width   | **114** (MR), 119 (all)  | the number the run existed for |

Per capability: **ABS 30, IE 136, KU 61, MR 78, TR 89** — roster **394/500 = 78.80%**, the campaign's best;
registered delta **+33.50pp**, also the best; and `beyond the pool` is **0** on every capability, which is
prediction 3 of §13.72 finally satisfied by construction: the room is smaller than the pool again.

### 13.79.2 The rank table, which is why the run was dispatched

| rank band        | ABS | IE   | KU   | MR      | TR   | all     | share     |
| ---------------- | --- | ---- | ---- | ------- | ---- | ------- | --------- |
| 0–63             | 420 | 1444 | 1327 | 2632    | 2195 | 8018    | 73.2%     |
| **64–127**       | 110 | 104  | 188  | **484** | 417  | 1303    | **11.9%** |
| **128–255**      | 88  | 93   | 119  | **365** | 399  | 1064    | **9.7%**  |
| ≥ 256            | 54  | 68   | 54   | 182     | 217  | 575     | 5.2%      |
| median beyond 64 | 114 | 116  | 112  | **114** | 127  | **119** |           |

So the gold the campaign could not reach is **not** at rank 900. Its median is **114**, a quarter of it sits
between 64 and 127, and only 5.2% is beyond 256. §13.78.4's decision rule had two branches — "65–90 means a knob,
300+ means a research problem" — and the answer lands between them, which is the one outcome the rule did not
name: **the pool is wide enough to hold the median unreachable gold, and the room is not**.

The room holds 68 turns. The median unreachable gold is at 114. So the next variable is the **room**, and the
arithmetic that sets it is already known: at 400 characters the room is 68, and the character budget is fixed.

### 13.79.3 What the coverage bands say about _how_ the room buys anything

MR's accuracy by coverage band on this run:

| coverage    | n   | correct | rate      |
| ----------- | --- | ------- | --------- |
| 0–50%       | 18  | 9       | 50.0%     |
| 50–70%      | 26  | 13      | 50.0%     |
| 70–85%      | 26  | 13      | 50.0%     |
| **85–95%**  | 21  | 17      | **81.0%** |
| **95–100%** | 30  | 26      | **86.7%** |

**Flat at 50% for everything below 85%, then a step.** That is a different shape from every earlier reading in
this campaign — §13.26 saw a smooth climb across bands — and it changes what a room has to do: not raise coverage
on average, but **push questions over the step**. A question at 60% that becomes 80% is worth nothing by this
table; one that goes from 80% to 90% is worth 31 points.

### 13.79.4 Registered: a 200-character cap on the two routes

**One variable**: `maxTurnChars: 200`, reach unchanged (`multi-session,temporal`), `relevanceTopK: 256` held.

The width is chosen by arithmetic on this run's own data: the mean capped turn at 200 is 175 characters, which in
a 22,000-character evidence room holds **≈ 121 turns** — just past the median unreachable rank of 114. Geometry
from `goldRanks` at that room gives MR **84.4%** delivered before calibration; the same model over-predicts the
current run (79 turns against 68 measured), so the calibrated expectation is **≈ 81%**.

| #     | prediction                                                                                                   | falsified if |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------ |
| **1** | **MR's delivered share rises from 72.9% to ≥ 79%**                                                           | < 79%        |
| **2** | **MR's correct count rises from 78 to ≥ 81**, by the band arithmetic above (25 questions cross 85%)          | ≤ 78         |
| **3** | **The roster rises from 394 to ≥ 397**                                                                       | ≤ 394        |
| **4** | **TR holds at ≥ 84** (it is 89; its own cross-draw rate is ±15, so this is a floor rather than a prediction) | ≤ 83         |

**The price, stated first**: at 200 characters **65.5%** of MR's turns are truncated, against 38.9% at 400, and
the characters removed rise from 4.49M to 5.31M in the same 121 questions. A fact that sits past the 200th
character of its turn is now lost, and §13.77.1's test — that truncation share does **not** separate correct from
failing answers — was run at 400, where the share was 40% either way. At 200 nothing guarantees it stays flat, and
prediction 4 is the only place that would show.

### 13.79.5 Adopted: the pool width

`relevanceTopK: 256` is **adopted** alongside the width and reach from §13.76: predictions 1–3 all met, the
roster is +5, the delta is the campaign's best, and `beyond the pool` reaches zero. It is also what makes the
next experiment expressible at all — a room of 121 turns is only meaningful with a pool that can fill it.

### 13.79.6 What each outcome of the next run would mean

- **1 and 2 hold**: the step is the mechanism, the room is the lever, and the next question is how far the step
  moves — i.e. whether 150 characters buys the 39 crossings the arithmetic predicts (+6.5 questions).
- **1 holds and 2 does not**: coverage crosses 85% and accuracy does not follow, which would falsify the step
  rather than the cap, and the band table would have to be re-read on the new run's own bands.
- **1 fails**: turning 65% of turns into 200-character stumps destroys more than the extra turns deliver, and the
  400-character cap from §13.76 is the right one — a result the registration makes visible instead of arguable.

## 13.80 A 200-character cap buys the room and destroys the reading: coverage 80.9%, accuracy 29/121

### 13.80.1 The reading
