The second is why the pool is drawn from the corpus's own golds rather than invented: an invented
string is easy in a way a real but wrong name is not, and a judge that only rejects non-words has not
been measured on the failure that matters.

#### 13.182.2 Two defects the invariants caught on a real artifact, before a token was spent

Both are in `run-40989420944`, and both would have inflated the false-accept rate:

| question | what happened | what it would have cost |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------- |
| `75499fd8` | the answer says "…it would suit a Golden Retriever like Max…" and closes with "Golden Retriever" on its own line. Replacing the **first** occurrence left the gold intact at the end | a correct answer scored as a false accept |
| `3a704032` | gold is `"3"`, and `"34".includes("3")` is true, so a substring-based invariant rejected the case; the first substitution also applied the token pass on top of the gold pass and produced `"344"` | every numeric swap on a count question silently dropped — the family MR is made of — or a case with two uncontrolled variables |

The fixes are a full-occurrence replacement, word-boundary semantics in the invariant, and mutually
exclusive passes. All three are asserted as test cases, not only as code.

#### 13.182.3 Predictions, registered before dispatch

Payload: `tools/judge-audit.mjs` on the `41159983913` artifact, `limit 120`, `deepseek-chat`, one
pass, temperature 0 (the judge's own setting). 120 accepted answers yield up to 360 cases plus 120
control calls; the plan on that artifact emits **167** (59 `number-swap`, 51 `entity-swap`, 57
`cross-gold`), because a gold with no swappable token emits nothing rather than a bogus case.

| prediction | passes when | falsified when |
| ---------- | ----------- | -------------- |
| the gate | false-accept upper bound **> 5%** — the judge does accept wrong answers | ≤ 5%, and this repository's judge is better than the published one by an order of magnitude |
| numbers are the weak kind | `number-swap` accepts more than `entity-swap` | the reverse; then the failure is naming, not arithmetic |
| a wholly wrong gold is caught | `cross-gold` rate ≤ 10% | above, and the judge is not reading the question |
| the judge is reproducible | control ≥ 95% re-accepted | below, and the noise floor dominates every reading the campaign has |
| the rate is larger than the effect | `falseAccept × 121 ≥ 2` questions on MR | below, and the judge is not the binding constraint |

The first and the last are the ones that change how results are reported: if both pass, every
capability comparison from now on is a **paired flip count**, not a difference of accuracies, because
two points of judge error can produce a two-question difference out of nothing.

#### 13.182.4 The gate, and why the threshold is 5%

Exit 1 when the false-accept upper bound exceeds 5%. The number is not borrowed from the false-share
gate for symmetry: the campaign resolves about 1.7 points (two questions of 121), so a judge that
mis-accepts 5% of wrong answers is already larger than the signal it is being used to detect. Above
it, the correct response is not to stop measuring but to **annotate**: every capability reading
becomes judge-limited rather than memory-limited, and the paired design becomes mandatory.

#### 13.182.5 What this does not say

- **Not agreement with a human.** It measures one judge against one family of perturbations. A low
  rate on substitutions does not transfer to answers that are wrong by **omission** — a plausible
  half-answer, which is exactly the shape `§13.96` found in the MR failures.
- **Not the official judge.** `deepseek-chat` with the official templates is this repository's judge,
  not LongMemEval's. The 62.81% figure is a reference point about judges in general, not a
  prediction about this one.
- **Not a correction.** Nothing here adjusts a published accuracy. It prices the instrument; a
  correction would need ground truth the judge does not have.

### 13.183 The identity fix worked, the cost fell, and the variance did not move: `41159983913` against six predictions

The dispatch registered in `§13.177.6` ran to completion (run `41159983913`, `fa51a895`, 2026-10-31,
02:26–04:27 GMT, 61 minutes). Payload verified from the artifact rather than from the dispatch note:
`ask=operands`, `contract=abstention-evidence-blocks`, `review_pass=bare`,
`relevanceSignal=retrieval-hybrid`, `top_k=256`, `units=turn`, `maxPromptChars=96000`, `runs=4`,
`temperature=0`, `threshold=0` — one variable moved from `41144910162`, the id derivation.

#### 13.183.1 Four predictions hold

| prediction | criterion | measured | verdict |
| ---------- | --------- | -------- | ------- |
| row 6, the premise | ≥ 95% of questions carry `promptVariants == 1` | **500/500 = 100%** | **passes** |
| cache share | ≥ 60% of prompt tokens report a cache hit | **38,402,551 / 50,736,848 = 75.69%** | **passes** |
| witness | `commonPrefix` equals the full length on ≥ 95% of passes | `[null, 94,674, 94,674, 94,674]` against a text of **94,674** characters; all four texts byte-identical | **passes** |
| billed cost | `promptTokens × (1 − 0.9 × cacheShare)` ≤ 0.7 × 28.18 M | **16.17 M** against a ceiling of **19.73 M** (0.574× the previous draw) | **passes** |

The witness is the one worth keeping: three comparisons, three full-length prefixes, four identical
texts. Before the fix, a random id inside every prompt made the bytes differ at an offset near the
end, which is exactly what a cache miss looks like and what made the previous draw's cache share
11.2%. It is now 75.69%, and the instrument that says so is in the artifact rather than in a
provider's dashboard.

The cost prediction passing is the interesting arithmetic: `promptTokens` **rose** 1.62× (31.37 M →
50.74 M) because the ceiling doubled to 96,000, and the billed estimate still fell to 0.574× of the
previous draw. Caching is what pays for the extra room — 75.69% of 50.74 M is 38.40 M tokens the
provider did not charge for.

#### 13.183.2 Two predictions fail, and the failure is the result

| prediction | criterion | measured | verdict |
| ---------- | --------- | -------- | ------- |
| accuracy | MR first repetition ≥ 87, and overall within ±2.2 pt of 84.00% | MR first repetition **84**; overall first repetition **83.80%** | **overall passes, MR fails** |
| within-run spread | MR's four passes span ≤ 2 questions | **84, 86, 87, 92 — span 8** | **fails** |

`§13.177.6` said of the last row: *"the one that costs the campaign something if it passes. If four
passes of one request return near-identical answers, `runs: 4` stops measuring model variance."* It did
not pass — and the opposite finding is worth more than the prediction was:

> **The prompts are now byte-identical and the answers are not.** Four passes of the same request, at
> temperature 0, with a witness proving the bytes match to the character, still spread MR across 8
> questions (84–92) and the roster across 10 (417–427 of 500).

So the 2.2-point band `§13.175.5` measured between two dispatches was **not** the random ids. Some of
it is the reader, and no prompt-level fix removes it. That has three consequences the campaign has to
carry:

1. **`runs: 4` still buys something.** It is not a determinism check; it is the only instrument that
   sees this variance, and the per-run bitmaps (`featureCorrectByRun`) are what make it visible.
2. **A single-repetition reading cannot resolve 2 questions.** MR first repetition is 84 and the mean
   is 87.25; the adoption rule that reads the first repetition is therefore reading the low tail of a
   distribution whose width is larger than the effects being chased. `§13.182` registers the judge
   audit for the same reason from the other side.
3. **Per-capability means, not first-pass counts, are the comparable quantity.** MR 87.25 (84–92),
   TR 102.5 (100–105), IE 143 (141–144), KU 60.25 (59–61), ABS 29 (29–29). ABS is the only capability
   whose four passes agree exactly, which is what a calibrated decline path should look like.

#### 13.183.3 What the run does not say

- **Not that 96,000 is the right ceiling.** It says the ceiling is now affordable at 0.574× the
  previous draw's billed estimate. Whether the extra room *earns* anything is a different question:
  the roster first pass moved 83.00% → 83.80%, which is inside the 10-question span measured here and
  is therefore not a difference this design can see.
- **Not that the id fix helped accuracy.** It was not supposed to. Overall is within the registered
  band; MR first repetition is not, and the honest reading of that is the variance above rather than a
  regression.
- **Not that MR is fixed.** MR mean 87.25 against the reference pipeline's 103.75 on the same
  questions. The 96,000 ceiling did not close a 16-question gap, and `§13.182` now asks whether the
  judge can even see 2 of those questions.

### 13.184 The judge accepts 19.4% of answers that are wrong, and it fails on names rather than numbers

The audit registered in `§13.182` ran as GitHub run `41173396348` on the `41159983913` artifact
(`limit 120`, `deepseek-chat`, 160 cases, 280 calls, 3m48s). It fails its gate, and the shape of the
failure is more useful than the rate.

| bucket | accepts | rate | Wilson 95% upper |
| ------ | ------: | ---: | ---------------: |
| all kinds | **31 / 160** | **19.38%** | **26.19%** |
| `number-swap` | 9 / 61 | 14.75% | 25.72% |
| `entity-swap` | **22 / 49** | **44.90%** | 58.69% |
| `cross-gold` | 0 / 50 | 0.00% | 7.14% |
| **control** (unperturbed, re-judged) | **120 / 120** | **100%** | — |

#### 13.184.1 Five predictions, and the one that was falsified is the finding

| prediction | criterion | measured | verdict |
| ---------- | --------- | -------- | ------- |
| the gate | upper bound > 5% | **26.19%** | holds |
| numbers are the weak kind | `number-swap` > `entity-swap` | **14.75% vs 44.90%** — the reverse, by 3× | **falsified** |
| a wholly wrong gold is caught | `cross-gold` ≤ 10% | **0/50 = 0%** (upper 7.14%) | holds |
| the judge is reproducible | control ≥ 95% | **120/120 = 100%** | holds |
| the rate is larger than the effect | `falseAccept × 121 ≥ 2` | **23.5 questions** | holds |

The falsified row is the one to carry forward. Replacing a **name** is three times more likely to be
accepted than replacing a **number**, and replacing the entire answer is never accepted. Read as one
statement about the judge: **it checks that the answer is about the right thing with the right shape,
and does not check that it names the right entity.**

#### 13.184.2 Why that specific failure matters more than 19.4%

A memory system built on extracted atoms has one characteristic error: it retrieves the right sentence
about the wrong person. `§13.182` was written expecting the numeric failure, because the MR capability
is mostly counts. The audit says the opposite, and the consequence is uncomfortable:

> **The judge is blindest exactly where this system is weakest.**

A wrong count is caught three times as often as a wrong name. So an arm that answers "3 concerts"
where the gold is "5" is likely to be marked wrong, while an arm that answers with a fact about the
wrong colleague is likely to be marked right. MR accuracy is therefore inflated preferentially on the
substitution errors, and no aggregate reading can say by how much.

#### 13.184.3 What this does to the campaign's headline comparison

`§14` reports MR at **87.25** (mean of four passes) against the reference pipeline's **103.75** on the
same 121 questions and calls that a 16-question gap. The judge's false-accept rate applied to 121
questions is **23.5 questions**. The instrument's error is larger than the effect it is being used to
report.

That does not mean the gap is zero. It means the gap **cannot be attributed to memory** until the
judge is fixed or the grading is paired, and the honest annotation is:

- MR 87.25 and the 16-question gap are **judge-limited**, not memory-limited.
- The paired comparison (same question, both arms, count flips) is now mandatory rather than
  preferred, because a paired flip is a decision the judge made twice on the same question rather than
  an aggregate that its error can move in one direction.
- The reference pipeline is graded by the same judge, so the 100–105 it scores is inflated by the same
  bias. Which of the two it inflates more is unknown, and that asymmetry is now the largest
  unmeasured quantity in the campaign.

#### 13.184.4 Two things in the design that this reading needed, and one it did not

**Needed:** the control. 120/120 means the judge is perfectly reproducible on these answers, so the
19.4% is not noise and `§13.135`'s 5.0% floor belongs to the reader rather than to the judge. Without
this row, 19.4% could have been read as "the judge is unstable", which is a different problem with a
different fix.

**Needed:** the three kinds. The aggregate 19.4% alone would have supported the false conclusion that
the judge is equally wrong about everything, and the next step would have been "use a better judge".
The split says where to spend the effort instead: an entity check, not a model upgrade.

**Not needed, and recorded as an error:** `§13.182.3` registered the plan as **167** cases (59/51/57),
computed on the previous artifact `40989420944`. The dispatch audited `41159983913` and planned
**160** (61/49/50). Case refusal is per-question, so the count moves with the artifact; the
predictions are about rates and are unaffected. The registration is left as written and the
discrepancy is recorded here — editing a registration after the fact is the one thing that would make
it worth nothing.

#### 13.184.5 The next step this implies, registered now

**Re-grade MR with an entity check, before any further MR experiment.** Concretely: for every MR
question the judge accepted, extract the set of names the gold contains and the set the answer
contains; an accepted answer whose name sets are disjoint from the gold's is a candidate false
accept. That is a deterministic filter over answers already in the artifact, it needs no new calls,
and it prices how much of the 44.9% actually landed on MR rather than on `number-swap`-friendly IE
questions.

Prediction to test, registered before the tool exists: the entity-checked MR accuracy will be **at
most 84/121 first repetition minus 5** — i.e. at least five of the 84 accepted MR answers name
something the gold does not. If it is fewer than five, the 44.9% is concentrated in the capabilities
with more names (IE, TR) and MR's gap stays a memory question.

### 13.185 The entity check reaches two of eighty-four MR golds, and the prediction it falsifies is the finding

`§13.184.5` registered one prediction and one reason for it: if the judge does not check names, then some
of the 84 accepted MR answers should name something the gold does not, so MR after an entity check would
be **at most 79**. The tool is `tools/mr-entity-recheck.mjs`, the predicate is `nameScreen`, and the
reading is `tools/mr-entity-recheck-reading.json`, taken on `41159983913` with no model and no key.

#### 13.185.1 What was counted

| population | rows | `shared-name` | `names-disjoint` | `unnamed-gold` | `unnamed-answer` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| accepted | 84 | 1 | **0** | **82** | 1 |
| rejected | 37 | 0 | 0 | 33 | 4 |

**Candidates 0. Reach 2 of 84.** The prediction is **falsified**, and not because MR is clean.

#### 13.185.2 Why it is falsified, which is worth more than the prediction

82 of the 84 accepted MR golds contain no name at all. They are `2`, `$50`, `20%`, `3 days`, `$5,850`,
`140 hours`, `an hour and a half`, `43`, `$750`. Multi-session reasoning on this dataset is arithmetic
across sessions, so a screen built on *which name appears* cannot be pointed at the capability the
campaign's head-to-head is about.

The consequence is not about MR at all. Across all five capabilities the screen reaches **119 of 419**
accepted answers, and MR contributes **two** of those. So `§13.184`'s 44.90% on `entity-swap` is a
statement about the 119, and the previous iteration's annotation — `19.38% × 121 = 23.5` questions of MR
headroom — had no premise behind the multiplication. The rate is real; its transfer to MR was assumed.

**Withdrawn:** "MR 87.25 is judge-limited, not memory-limited" (`§13.184.4`, `docs/MEASURE-JUDGE-AUDIT.md`,
`03-execution-plan.md` §14.2, `04` §9.132). The audit's own reading stands unchanged; the annotation does
not. What replaces it is `§13.186`, which measures the channel MR does have.

#### 13.185.3 The control, because a screen that fires nowhere would also produce this table

On all five capabilities: accepted `5 of 419` (1.2%) against rejected `5 of 81` (6.2%) — the screen
fires **5.2× more often** on answers the judge rejected than on the ones it accepted, so it detects
something. It is not calibrated, and one of the five accepted candidates is a *correct* abridged answer
(`Screen protectors, phone wallet cases` against a gold about an `iPhone 13 Pro`). The list is for
adjudication, not for subtraction, and every row prints both texts and both name sets so a reader can
check the predicate rather than trust it.

#### 13.185.4 Two defects the real artifact found, neither of which a test wrote

**`Five` was read as a name.** Gold `Five months ago` yields `goldNames: [Five]`, and an answer naming a
city is then `names-disjoint`, so the screen listed a false accept on a question about duration. Number
words are now excluded from `NOT_A_NAME`, beside the months and weekdays `§13.182` had already excluded.
Because `entity-swap` draws its replacement pool from the same function, this also removes nonsense
substitutions from the audit — one fix, two instruments.

**Pronouns made a correct answer a candidate.** `They adopted a Labrador` extracted `They`, which made the
answer's name set non-empty and disjoint from a gold naming Rachel. Pronouns, discourse markers and
sentence-initial function words are excluded, and the case is a test.

**Not needed, and recorded as an error:** a sample of the population, because the count alone could not
distinguish "the answers are clean" from "the screen cannot see them". `--sample N` was added and
`--capability MR --sample 25` is what produced 13.185.2. The first dispatch of the workflow (`41176808751`)
printed a table that took a second dispatch (`41177330482`) and a sample to explain.

### 13.186 MR read without the judge: zero false accepts in eighty answers, and one disagreement in a hundred and one

`§13.185` ends with a channel that cannot see MR. This section registers the one that can, because the
control that made 13.185 worth publishing — reach — is also what says where to look next: MR golds are
numbers.

#### 13.186.1 The instrument

`numericScreen` (`packages/cortex-eval/src/numeric-recheck.ts`) compares the value an answer **commits
to** with the values the gold states. The arm ends its replies with its answer (`$60 / 5 = $12 per mug.
12`), so the last numeric token is that value. Five relations: `agrees`, `agrees-early` (the gold's value
appears, and the answer commits to a different one), `differs`, `gold-unreachable` (a gold with no digits),
`answer-unreachable` (a decline lands here). No model, no key, no credit.

Two things follow from having no judge in the loop: the reading is not the instrument's opinion, and
**false rejects become measurable** — the audit perturbs answers the judge already accepted, so a rejected
answer that was right never enters its sample.

#### 13.186.2 What it reads

| population | rows | `agrees` | `agrees-early` | `differs` | gold unreachable | answer unreachable |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| accepted | 84 | **80** | 0 | **0** | 4 | 0 |
| rejected | 37 | 1 | 0 | 20 | 8 | 8 |

- **False accepts: 0 of 80 readable accepted answers. Wilson 95% upper bound 4.6%.**
- **False rejects: 1** — `92a0aa75`, gold `1,5` (two acceptable values), the answer stated `1`.
- Judge-free accuracy **81/101 (80.2%)**. The judge, on the same 101 rows: **80/101**.

The two instruments disagree on **one MR question out of 101**, and the judge is the one that is wrong.

#### 13.186.3 Why 4.6% settles the question the audit could not

The audit's gate is 5%, and its own bound was 26.19%. On MR's number channel the bound is **4.6%** — under
the gate, and 5.7× smaller than what the audit's overall bound would have licensed. If the judge were as
lenient on MR numbers as the aggregate suggested, 80 readable accepted answers would carry about **21**
false accepts. It carries **0**.

Per capability, the same rule: MR `0/80` (4.6%), TR `1/54` (9.8%), IE `0/43` (8.2%), KU `1/32` (15.7%),
ABS `0/0`, all `2/209` (3.4%). Both false accepts in 209 are outside MR. A judge that misses a swapped
name at 44.90% is not a judge that accepts wrong numbers, and those two statements are only in tension if
the rate is read as a per-answer property — which it never was.

#### 13.186.4 The silent denominator, which is the defect this reading shipped and then fixed

`sourcesFrom` filtered on `typeof question.answer === 'string'`. A **decline** is written without an
`answer` key, so the filter dropped every decline: MR lost **8 of its 121 rows**. Nothing said so, and the
damage was invisible in the numerator — a decline is never correct, so the accepted count was untouched
while the denominator fell from 121 to 113. The workflow's own output (`41177874270`) says 113; the
committed reading says 121, and the difference is this fix.

The repair is not a wider filter, it is the recognition that a decline is a **row with a relation**
(`answer-unreachable` / `unnamed-answer`). Both tools now print `N of M unusable, no verdict`, so the one
thing that can be dropped is a row with no verdict at all, and it is counted.

#### 13.186.5 What changes, and what does not

- **Withdrawn:** MR is judge-limited. The annotation cost 23.5 hypothetical questions; the measurement
  finds 1 actual disagreement.
- **Unchanged:** MR's 84/121, the four-round spread 84/86/87/92, the 16-question gap to the reference arm
  (100–102). The gap is now a **memory** finding on the numeric channel rather than a grading one, which
  makes the `enumerated` / review-pass / session-channel work the right place to spend the next round.
- **Unchanged:** the judge audit's 19.38%. It keeps its own meaning — this judge does not verify names —
  and it can no longer be multiplied by 121. It applies to the 119 accepted answers whose golds state a
  name, 2 of which are MR.
- **New:** a reading whose error is not the judge's. Every capability comparison in this campaign has been
  a comparison of two judge readings; MR now has one that is not.

#### 13.186.6 What it cannot say, each with the class it costs

1. **A wrong answer that keeps the gold's number.** `3 people` against a gold of `3 days` agrees here, and
   the judge accepted it. This bounds the number channel, not the capability.
2. **Units.** `3 days` against `72 hours` differs. The class is small on MR and is not zero.
3. **Scale.** `20%` is 20, so `0.2` differs. A normaliser that guessed the scale would be deciding the
   answer.
4. **Golds with no digits.** `an hour and a half`: 4 of the 84 accepted, 20 of 121 rows. Excluded from the
   rate and counted beside it, because a denominator that absorbed them would make the instrument look
   better the blinder it got.
5. **Other capabilities.** The stated-answer semantics hold where the answer is a value; on TR the same
   rule reads 28.3%, which is not a claim about TR. Only MR is read as an accuracy here.

#### 13.186.7 The next step this implies, registered now

The judge is not what costs MR 16 questions, so the next experiment is a **memory** experiment, and the
candidate already has a mechanism and a prediction on file: `PREREG-MR-SESSION-CHANNEL` (session-granularity
relevance, `MR ≥ 96/121`). Before dispatching it, register one thing this reading makes cheap to check:
**the number screen must be run on the new artifact in the same reading step**, because an MR gain that
moves 121 answers can now be checked for whether it moved them by being right rather than by being
accepted — and if the reference arm's 100–102 contains false accepts of its own, the gap is smaller than
16 and the target of 96 is easier than it looks. That check is `--capability all` on both arms, and it
needs no key.

### 13.187 The gap was never a constant: the masks were read, and the plan's next step was one that had already run

**Registered 2026-10-31, on artifact `41159983913`, with no new dispatch.** Reading
`tools/paired-flip-reading.json`; instrument `packages/cortex-eval/src/paired-flip.ts`;
shell `tools/paired-flip.mjs`; accounting `tools/__tests__/test_paired_flip.py` (8 tests) and
`packages/cortex-eval/src/__tests__/paired-flip.test.ts` (14).

#### 13.187.1 What was never read

`AblationResult.featureCorrectByRun` and `baselineCorrectByRun` are four correctness masks per arm, one
character per dataset question, run-major. The field's own docblock gives the purpose and names the
failure it was added for: a spread *"cannot separate one question flapping four times from four
questions flapping once each"*. It has been in the artifact since that comment was written.

**No tool in this repository read it.** Every capability comparison in the campaign — including the
`15 to 25 questions, paired, in every run` of `PREREG-MR-SESSION-CHANNEL` §1 — subtracted two means.
"Paired" there meant *same run*, and the distinction that matters is *same question*.

#### 13.187.2 The reading

| capability | n | baseline per repetition | feature per repetition | gap per repetition |
| --- | --: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MR | 121 | 105, 104, 104, 102 | 84, 86, 87, 92 | **21, 18, 17, 10** |
| TR | 127 | 84, 83, 83, 83 | 105, 100, 104, 101 | −21, −17, −21, −18 |
| IE | 150 | 1, 1, 1, 1 | 141, 143, 144, 144 | −140, −142, −143, −143 |
| KU | 72 | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 60, 59, 61, 61 | −60, −59, −61, −61 |
| ABS | 30 | 30, 30, 30, 30 | 29, 29, 29, 29 | 1, 1, 1, 1 |

| capability | durable-miss | durable-win | agreed-wrong | contested | flapping (b/f) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| MR | **17** | **4** | 8 | 20 | 3 / 18 |
| TR | 3 | 20 | 13 | 17 | 1 / 17 |
| IE | 0 | 136 | 4 | 9 | 0 / 9 |
| KU | 0 | 58 | 10 | 4 | 0 / 4 |
| ABS | **1** | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 / 0 |

MR's sixteen-question gap is a mean over gaps of 21, 18, 17 and 10, and the number it subtracts is
itself unstable (105, 104, 104, 102). The decomposition is **17 durable misses − 4 durable wins = 13**,
plus 3.5 of flapping asymmetry — from **37 disagreements** (29 and 8) out of 121, with 72 agreed-right
and 8 agreed-wrong.

#### 13.187.3 The ceiling, and the target that was above it

The 84 already contains the four durable wins, so the arithmetic is closed at both ends:

- fix all 17 misses, lose nothing: **101/121 = 83.5%**;
- fix all 17, lose the 4 wins — which is what *resembling the reference arm* means, since those four
  are questions it loses every time: **97/121 = 80.2%**.

`PREREG-MR-SESSION-CHANNEL` §5 registered **96/121**. That number is above the ceiling of the strategy
it named, and it was never reachable by transplanting the reference pipeline. Reaching 96 requires
winning questions the reference arm also loses, i.e. the `agreed-wrong` 8 plus part of the 20 contested.

**This is a withdrawal of a target, not of a measurement.** 96 was a floor set before anyone had read
the pairing, and a floor that no version of the named treatment can clear is not a floor.

#### 13.187.4 The seventeen, and the direction that makes a fix net three

Composition: **off-by-one 6, decline 5, aggregation 4, other 2**, listed by id in
`tools/paired-flip-reading.json` and in `MEASURE-PAIRED-FLIP.md` §4.

Five of the six off-by-one misses are **under-counts** (`3→2`, `4→3`, `4→3`, `23→22`, `2→1`), one is an
**over-count** (`2e6d26dc`, `5→6`), and the aggregation class carries a second over-count (`a9f6b44c`,
`2→4`). A treatment that pushes the arm toward inclusion therefore buys five and may sell two:
**net three, not seven.** That constraint is registered before the experiment so it cannot be read
afterwards as an explanation.

Two of the seventeen name their own missing operand in prose — `edced276` ("the Hawaii trip is
mentioned but no duration is given anywhere in the evidence") and `2b8f3739` ("the third item's total
is not stated") — and the reference arm produces the gold for both. An answer that names its own
missing operand is the most informative failure in the set, because it cannot be a miscount.

#### 13.187.5 Withdrawn: the next step was a registration with a result section

The previous iteration closed by naming

> the next experiment is `PREREG-MR-SESSION-CHANNEL` (session-granularity relevance, `MR ≥ 96/121`)

and wrote the same into `04` §9.134.7 and `03` §14.2. That registration has a `§6 Result`: run
`40498191604`, gate line `relevanceSignal=retrieval-session`, **MR 83/121 = 68.60%** against the
control's 84, P2 refuted by thirteen questions, and §6.2 closing the retrieval-unit axis because the
gold turn reaches the rendered prompt for 500 of 500 questions.

**A registration that has a result section is not a registration**, and the file is in the same
repository as the plan that cited it. The cost is not the arithmetic — the arithmetic was right about
the wrong thing — it is that two documents disagreed and nothing compared them.

#### 13.187.6 Registered now, both cheap and both falsifiable

**A. The ABS defect, which is one question and one route.** `6456829e_abs` is wrong in 4 of 4
repetitions while `reference-pipeline` is right in 4 of 4. Gold `None` (a false premise), answer
`5 tomato plants`: the question asks for **tomatoes and chili peppers** and the reply answers one
operand. `ask: operands` reaches the **`multi-session` route alone** (`prompt.ts`'s reach map says one
route even though its gate admits three), and `classifyQuestionShape` runs only under that ask — so the
abstention route is outside the reach of the one mechanism in this repository that asks a reader whether
every operand of a question is present. The route whose whole job is to notice an unanswerable question
is the route the missing-operand check cannot see.

> **Prediction:** extending the missing-operand check to the abstention route takes ABS to **30/30**
> and leaves MR, IE, KU and TR byte-identical.

**Falsified if** ABS does not reach 30/30, or any other capability moves a single question, or its
prompts move one byte.

**B. The next MR experiment is read on the masks, not on the mean.** This arm's four repetitions span
84 to 92 with `promptVariants == 1` for all 500 questions, so a first-repetition movement under eight
questions is inside the observed range and cannot be attributed to a treatment.

> **Prediction / criterion:** the next MR dispatch must move **at least three of the seventeen named
> durable misses** and lose **at most one durable win**, counted on `featureCorrectByRun`, and its
> report must carry the mask comparison rather than the difference of means.

**Falsified if** the artifact cannot be read at question level, or the treated population does not
intersect the durable set.

**C. One free check the artifact already supports.** Four of the five durable declines have numeric
golds (`5 days`, `20%`, `50`, `1,998`) and one has `7`. `d905b33f` and `c18a7dc8` are two the operands
ask was written for (`§13.166` names both), and both still decline under it.

> **Prediction:** searching the stored `featurePromptTexts` for the gold's own numeral finds it absent
> for at least three of the five.

**Falsified if** all five carry the gold numeral in their prompt — which would move them from
retrieval to reader and make the decline class a reader defect instead.

**D. A silent truncation manufactures a refusal, so the cut needs a marker behind an option.**
The prediction in C is met five of five, and reading the prompts for the reason found a defect rather
than a reader failure. `a4996e51`'s turn ends at exactly `maxTurnChars` with

```
... analyzing engagement metrics. During peak campaign seasons, I increase my work hours
```

and the next turn in the same session asks how to phrase those hours — the corpus confirming the fact was
in the elided tail. `contentFor` → `truncateCodePointSafe` adds **no marker**, so the reader sees a
sentence that stops and the contracts tell it to decline when an operand is missing: **the truncation
manufactures the refusal.**

Two of the other four declines carry a decoy numeral of the gold's own value in an unrelated turn (`20%` on
Zara jeans for a question about a book; `5 days a week` for a question about a parcel), which is why the
check has to be numeral-in-context and why a numeral count would have reported two reader failures.

**Not fixed silently.** `prompt-turn-cap.test.ts` protects *"every archived prompt stays reproducible from
the code"*, so a marker cannot be an edit to `truncateCodePointSafe`. The change is:

1. `PromptOptions.turnCutMarker?: 'none' | 'ellipsis'`, default `'none'` — the current bytes;
2. when `'ellipsis'`, cut to `maxChars - 1`, back off to the last whitespace inside the final 20% of the
   window if one exists, trim the tail, append `…`; total length still `≤ maxChars`;
3. forward it through `CortexMemoryOptions` and `#promptOptions` (`§7.4`: a field the arm can set and the
   prompt can ignore is the side-channel defect);
4. workflow input `turn_cut_marker`, echoed in the artifact's config line;
5. TDD: default-off byte equality against the current prompts; `'ellipsis'` ends a capped turn with `…`
   and never exceeds the cap; a mid-word cut backs off; a surrogate pair is still never split.

> **Prediction:** with `turnCutMarker: 'ellipsis'` and everything else fixed, at least one of the five
> durable declines is answered, and the other four are unchanged — the marker tells the reader the text
> continues, and it cannot tell it what the missing text said.

**Falsified if** no durable decline moves, or more than two move in either direction, or any uncapped
prompt changes one byte (the option must be inert when the cap is absent).

#### 13.187.7 What this does not say

1. `durable` is a property of the code only when the repetitions share a prompt. Here they do
   (`promptVariants` 1 for 500 of 500); on an artifact where it is 4, the verdict would mean "durable
   across four different prompts" and would understate what a fix can reach.
2. `agreed-wrong` is a ceiling of this harness, not of the capability: 8 MR questions may be winnable by
   a different prompt, window or reader. What is ruled out is winning them by resembling the reference arm.
3. The classes come from `tools/mr-failure-census.mjs`'s classifier, read from the gold and the answer,
   and inherit its blindness: a wrong answer that keeps the gold's number is invisible to it.
4. `feature.metrics.correct` is repetition 0 (419 of 419/417/425/427) and no field says so. The tool
   prints that sentence above every number for that reason.

### 13.188 The cut now says so — shipped behind a value, and one thing §13.187.6D got wrong

**Registered 2026-10-31, before the dispatch.** Product change in
`packages/cortex-memory/src/prompt.ts` (`TurnCutMarker`, `cutWithMarker`), forwarded through
`CortexMemoryOptions.turnCutMarker` and `#promptOptions`; arm in
`packages/cortex-eval/src/bench-memory-arm.ts` (`readTurnCap`, `TURN_CUT_MARKERS`); artifact field
`memoryArmConfig.turnCutMarker` and a `turnCutMarker=` term on the config line. Accounting:
`prompt-turn-cut-marker.test.ts` (11), `bench-memory-arm.test.ts` (+10), and
`tools/__tests__/test_ask_table_parity.py` (+3 for the third duplicated table).

#### 13.188.1 The defect, stated as the string the reader received

`a4996e51` is one of MR's **17 durable misses** (§13.187.2). Its decisive turn was **delivered and
then cut** at `maxTurnChars`, and the stored `featurePromptTexts` ends the sentence at
`…I increase my work hours`; the next turn of the same conversation asks how to phrase those hours.
The reader declined.

That is not a reader failure and not a retrieval failure. The turn arrived — every coverage count in
the artifact says so, correctly — and what arrived was a sentence that stops, at a cap whose whole
purpose is to stop mid-text. Every contract in `prompt.ts` instructs the reader to decline when an
operand is not stated, so declining was the *correct* response to a prompt that had silently lost the
operand.

#### 13.188.2 What changed, and the two states that must remain byte-identical

`PromptOptions.turnCutMarker` takes `'none'` (default) or `'ellipsis'`. Under `'ellipsis'` a turn the
cap cut is rendered as: cut at `maxChars - 1`, back off one unit if that lands on a low surrogate, back
off further to a whitespace **only if** the nearest one is inside the last 20% of the window, trim, then
`…`. The marker therefore spends one of the cap's units rather than adding one, so the room the cap
buys is unchanged: the same number of turns fit.

Two inert states are assertions rather than claims, because both are places a marker would lie:

1. **No cap** — there is no cut to mark, so a marker without a cap renders the previous bytes.
2. **A turn shorter than the cap** — no cut happened, so nothing is appended.

And the prompt-level clip in `fitToBudget` is deliberately untouched: it spends the room's last
characters, so a mark there would have to shorten the text by one unit to pay for itself, which is a
different trade from the one registered here.

#### 13.188.3 §13.187.6D named an input this workflow does not have

That block registered *"workflow input `turn_cut_marker`"*. The workflow declares **24** of GitHub's 25
`workflow_dispatch` inputs, and `test_dispatch_inputs.py` **forbids** sitting at the ceiling — a rule
written precisely so the next registration is not blocked by plumbing. So the marker rides on the cap's
own value:

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| blank, or `none` | no cap; every archived run |
| `<width>` | cap at `<width>`, silent cut; every capped run to date |
| `<width>:ellipsis` | cap at `<width>`, the cut prints `…` |
| `<width>:none` | the same state as `<width>`, spelled so a registration can name its control |

The compound syntax exists **only at the dispatch boundary**; the artifact records `maxTurnChars` and
`turnCutMarker` as separate fields, so no reader of an artifact has to parse it back apart. This is also
the truer shape: a marker without a cap marks nothing, so the grammar makes the impossible combination
**unexpressible** instead of guarding against it at runtime — the guard in the arm was written first and
then deleted, because a state no dispatch can produce does not need a test.

#### 13.188.4 The dispatch

Treatment `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars: 400:ellipsis` against the adopted control `400`, every other
input identical, read on the **mask** (`paired-flip.ts`), not on the mean.

**Prediction.** At least one of the five §13.187.4 durable declines is answered; the other four do not
move; every uncapped prompt and every uncut turn is byte-identical.

**Falsified if** none of the five moves (the mark is not enough information), or three or more move in
either direction (the mark is not the variable), or any prompt without a cut changes a byte, or MR moves
by fewer than two questions while the other four capabilities move at all.

#### 13.188.5 Cost, in the unit the cap is stated in

The marker replaces one character of text with `…` per cut turn, so per-turn length is **≤** the cap and
the count of turns delivered is unchanged. The token effect is bounded by the turns that are cut: at a
400-character cap on the MR route, 26 delivered turns with a median of 272 characters means few turns are
cut at all, and a `…` is one or two tokens. This is the rare treatment that spends **nothing** to say
something true.

#### 13.188.6 What this does not claim

1. It does not claim the reader will then answer `a4996e51` correctly — only that it will no longer be
   declining on text that was never shown. The operand may still be beyond the cap.
2. It does not touch the four other durable declines: §13.187 read their evidence as genuinely absent
   (`20%` on Zara jeans for a book question is a decoy numeral, not the answer), so this treatment
   cannot reach them and predicting otherwise would be predicting a retrieval change from a rendering
   one.
3. It says nothing about the ceiling. 101/121 = 83.5% remains the best this class of fix can produce,
   and this is one question of seventeen.

### 13.189 The bill split by the side that spent it — the instrument token work has to start from

**Registered 2026-10-31, as an instrument rather than a treatment.** `packages/cortex-eval/src/usage-by-side.ts`
(`minusUsage`, `residualUsage`, `bothSides`, `traceUsage`), `packages/cortex-eval/src/system-mirror.ts`
(`mirrorMembers`, moved out of the arm so both wrappers share one delegation), artifact field
`usageBySide`, a per-side table in the provider-spend section. Accounting: `usage-by-side.test.ts` (12),
`system-mirror.test.ts` (3).

#### 13.189.1 What the artifact could not say

`llmUsage` is the whole bill and nothing else: on `41159983913` that is **50,736,848 prompt tokens over
5,670 calls**, 38,402,551 of them (75.69%) served from the provider's prefix cache. The one question any
token work has to answer — *which side spent it* — had no field, so a saving on the feature arm was
indistinguishable from a saving on the judge, and a run that halved its window could not be told from one
that halved its retries. §13.84's own budget decision was argued from coverage counts, not from spend.

#### 13.189.2 The split, and why its residual is a definition rather than a tag

The process ledger is global by design (`cortex-ai/src/usage.ts`: replacing it would change the `LLM`
contract or make every caller forward a number it does not want). So the split is taken **around each
answer**: snapshot, call, snapshot, add the delta to that side's accumulator — and the wrap uses
`finally`, because a call that throws has still left the machine and been billed.

What is left after both sides is `residual = total − baseline − feature`, which names the judge, the
phrasing stage and any setup by **construction** rather than by a tag each caller would have to remember.
That makes the closure `baseline + feature + residual === total` true by definition, and the renderer
prints it as a line (`Attribution closes: yes`) so a reader does not have to add three columns.

`minusUsage` refuses a negative rather than clamping: a part larger than its whole means the two
snapshots did not come from one ledger, and a clamped zero would print as a side that spent nothing —
the opposite of what happened. The renderer follows the same rule and says `SPLIT UNAVAILABLE` instead of
printing a table that does not add up.

#### 13.189.3 What it deliberately does not measure

1. **Currency.** Still no rate card in this repository; the columns are tokens.
2. **Embedding calls.** `llmUsage` counts completions through the adapter; the embedding client is a
   different endpoint and is not in this ledger. Stated because "the split closes" is a claim about
   completions only, not about the whole invoice.
3. **Per-question cost.** The accumulator is per side, not per question. A per-question ledger would be a
   second table in the artifact and a second place to drift; the question a saving has to answer is
   "which side", and that is what this answers.

> **Prediction for the next dispatch that carries it:** the feature arm accounts for the large majority
> of prompt tokens (its room is 96,000 characters against the reference pipeline's smaller window), and
> the residual is a two-digit share of the bill rather than a rounding term.

**Falsified if** the feature arm is not the largest of the three parts, or the residual is larger than
the feature arm, or either side reports zero on a run whose total is non-zero.

### 13.190 The abstention rule could only see the question as a whole — `operand-gap`, and the one question it is counted against

**Registered 2026-10-31, before dispatch.** Product: `EvidenceAsk` gains `'operand-gap'`, `ASK_ROUTES` and
`ASK_CHANGES` both `['abstention']`, `ASK_CONTROLS` `'route'`, and one constant —
`OPERAND_GAP_ABSTENTION_INSTRUCTION`, the shipped abstention block with its **closing line replaced**
(`withReplacedClose`). Arm: one row in `ASK_ROUTES`, which is what `readAsk` validates a dispatch against.
Accounting: `prompt-operand-gap.test.ts` (7), `ask-changes.test.ts` 29 → **31** (the data-driven loop picks
the value up, so the reach and the change set are asserted against the registration rather than by this
file), `bench-memory-arm.test.ts` 183 → **184**.

#### 13.190.1 The failure, and the six controls that make it a prompt defect

`6456829e_abs` asks *"How many plants did I initially plant for tomatoes and chili peppers"*. Its gold is a
decline — the evidence states five tomato plants and never mentions chili peppers. The arm answers **`5`**
in every repetition of every archived run: a correct count of **half** the question. The reference pipeline
declines on it. ABS therefore reads 29/30 where the reference arm reads 30/30, run after run.

The population is not one question. Six others in the same thirty have the same shape — one operand carried,
one absent, a gold that says so in almost the same words — and all six decline correctly: `edced276_abs`
(Hawaii and Seattle), `e5ba910e_abs` (headphones and iPad), `gpt4_70e84552_abs` (fence and cows),
`gpt4_c27434e8_abs` (Ferrari and Porsche), `gpt4_fe651585_abs` (Tom and Alex), `80ec1f4f_abs` (museums or
galleries). A mechanism that gets six of seven right is not a capability limit, so the failure is in what
**this** instance's prompt said, and the two readings that survive are the reader's willingness to return a
*number* for a partly-evidenced counting question and the block's own rule.

#### 13.190.2 Why the closing line, and not a sentence above it

The shipped abstention block declines on *"If no evidence supports an answer, reply exactly
`INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`"* — a predicate over the **question**, and a half-answer satisfies it, because
evidence does support an answer to "how many tomato plants". That is what the reader reads, and it is
literally true. The per-part condition is not a qualification of that predicate; it is a different
predicate, so it has to be the rule that decides and not a rule near it.

The placement argument is measured, not asserted: §13.55 inserted its rule **above** the closing line on the
same reasoning (an exception belongs adjacent to the rule it excepts) and run `39035438120` returned the
same delta and, of the 28 MR declines it inherited, 21 declined again — twelve of them holding a non-empty
Step 1 list. `withReplacedClose` exists because of that reading. So `operand-gap` replaces the block's last
line, `Otherwise reply with the answer alone.`, with a rule that carries both halves: *answer alone only
when the evidence supports an answer to **every part** of the question; a question that names several things
is answerable only if the evidence mentions all of them; if a part is missing, or the question asks for a
total over parts where only some are stated, reply exactly the token.*

Everything else in the block is untouched, including the earlier token rule. A question with one absent
operand is still declined for the shipped reason as well as the new one.

#### 13.190.3 What this deliberately does not fix

1. **The retrieval half.** The census on the archived run measures the window as **64 lines naming tomatoes
   and 0 naming chili peppers**: the query expansion fused the two operands into one phrase
   (`["tomatoes and chili peppers", "initially plant", "how many plants"]`), a fused phrase can only be
   satisfied by the operand that exists, and the six sessions it pulled are dense enough to look complete.
   Decomposing the expansion into one phrase per operand is a treatment on a different layer — the paired
   success `gpt4_c27434e8_abs` decomposed (`["Ferrari model", "Porsche 991 Turbo S model"]`) — and one run
   cannot price two layers. §13.104 is the record of what a bundled edit costs the reading.
2. **The wording the reference pipeline also carries.** Its aggregation prompt names the arithmetic taxonomy
   (a sum, a difference, an average, a percentage, an elapsed time, a date). Adding that here would make
   this run two changes — a predicate and a vocabulary — and it is the registered next step if the
   predicate alone does not convert.
3. **The quantity-versus-ordering confound.** `6456829e_abs` is a `how many` question; every one of the six
   controls except `80ec1f4f_abs` is a `which … first` or a total, and none of the seven both decomposes its
   expansion and asks for a count. So a null result here cannot be read as clearing the question-type
   explanation, and it is recorded as a confounder rather than resolved.

#### 13.190.4 The criterion, and why it is one-sided

Reach and change set are the same single route, which no ask before this one manages: the abstention route
is the only route that reads `CONTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS.abstention`, so MR, IE, KU and TR read the shipped block
**by construction**.

**Dispatched as `41188431321`**, load copied field for field from `41185512391` with `ask` the only field
changed (`operands` → `operand-gap`; `maxPromptChars 96000`, `maxTurnChars 400:ellipsis` on
`multi-session,temporal`, `promptContract abstention-evidence-blocks`, `reviewPass bare`, `runs 4`,
`limit 0`, commit `9cd56e8`). That makes the comparison per capability rather than whole-run, and each
line of it is checkable in the two artifacts:

| capability | route | control `41185512391` reads | this run reads | readable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ABS** | abstention | shipped block | shipped block, closing line replaced | **yes — one variable** |
| IE | flat | shipped block | shipped block | yes — prompts must be byte-identical |
| KU | knowledge-update | shipped block | shipped block | yes — prompts must be byte-identical |
| TR | temporal | shipped block | shipped block | yes — prompts must be byte-identical |
| MR | multi-session | `operands` block on 7 derivation questions | shipped block | **no** — two asks, and this registration does not read MR |

The marker does not enter this comparison: `turnCutMarker` rides on the turn cap, the cap's reach in both
runs is `multi-session,temporal`, and the abstention route is outside it — so both runs' ABS prompts are
marker-free and the only difference in them is the line this ask replaces.

That makes ABS's criterion directional: **30 of its 30 golds are declines**, so the only way this treatment
can lose a point is by converting a correct decline into an answer. The prediction is therefore about one
question and not about a headline:

> **Prediction:** `6456829e_abs` declines in the feature arm, in all four repetitions; the other 29 ABS
> questions keep declining; ABS reads **30/30** per repetition; IE, KU and TR read prompts byte-identical to
> `41185512391`'s on every question, which is the reach table checked against an artifact rather than
> against itself; MR is unread here; the added characters are one 60-word line on 30 questions, which is
> below the run's rounding.

**Falsified if** `6456829e_abs` answers again — then the per-part clause is not the variable, the chain's
prose half is wrong, and the next candidate is the retrieval half (§13.190.3 item 1) — or if any ABS
question that declined in the control answers here, or if any of IE, KU and TR shows a single prompt whose
bytes moved, which would mean the reach table is not what the renderer does.

### 13.191 The pair tool read lengths where it should have read digests — and criterion 3 was vacuous for an ask

**Registered 2026-10-31, as an instrument.** `tools/window-pair.mjs` gains `promptIdentity`: a three-state
reading of `promptDigest` across the two artifacts (`digest-equal` / `digest-differs` / `unmeasured`), a
per-capability count, and one line — `length is not identity` — counting the questions whose prompts changed
**bytes at the same length**. The JSON summary gains the four id lists. Accounting: `test_window_pair.py`
13 → **16**, tools 989 → **992**.

#### 13.191.1 Two fields were measured and neither was reported

`promptCharsEqual` was computed in `compare()` and printed nowhere. That is the shape this campaign keeps
finding one level up: a number that exists in the code and not on the page is a number no reading can use, and
it reads as coverage. `promptDigest` had the same history for a different reason — §13.171 built it to answer
"did the prompt move" and, from the day it landed until now, **no tool read it**.

#### 13.191.2 What criterion 3 was actually asserting, and where it is vacuous

Criterion 3 is *"the mechanism is administered on the temporal route and nowhere else"*. Its evidence was the
**delivered turns**: a route whose turns did not reorder was treated as a route whose prompt did not move. For
`13.153`'s window reorder that is exact — the mechanism *is* a reorder. For an instruction-block ask it is
vacuous by construction: an ask changes no turn, so every question reads as untouched, criterion 3 passes, and
it would pass identically on a run where the ask reached all six routes. §13.190 is the first ask whose single
claim is exactly "five routes read the same bytes", so the instrument has to read bytes.

#### 13.191.3 Why `unmeasured` is a state and not a default

An artifact written before §13.171 has no digest. Folding "no digest" into "equal" would report an identity
nobody checked, on the archived runs — which are precisely where a cross-run prompt comparison is most
tempting, because they are the only control artifacts a new dispatch has. The tool prints the count and says
in words that a missing field is not a match.

#### 13.191.4 What the new line is for

`length is not identity` is not a diagnostic of the tool; it is a diagnostic of **every earlier reading**. A
swapped instruction line of the same length was invisible to `promptChars`, and every reach table in this
campaign was asserted against it. On the two artifacts this line will first be pointed at (`41185512391` and
`41188431321`) the expectation is **0**: three of the four capabilities should have identical digests and
identical lengths, and ABS should differ on both, because the replaced closing line is a different length.

**Falsified if** any IE, KU or TR question reports `digest-differs` between those two runs — then the reach
table is not what the renderer does, and §13.190.4's single-variable claim is false for a reason that has
nothing to do with prompt wording. Also falsified if the tool reports `unmeasured` on those two runs, which
would mean the digest is not being written on the path that produces the artifacts.

| §6.1.6's "median answer length"                   |                       **19** |                       **60** |
| — same population, `method='higher'` p90          |                      **715** |                      **513** |
| answers longer than the decline token             | 449 answered · median **30** | 447 answered · median **90** |
| median `rawOutput` length, all 500                |                    **251.5** |                    **236.0** |
| `bareRetry.attempted` → `answered`                |                  **23** → 23 |                    **7** → 7 |
| final replies that are the token and nothing else |      29 of 51, **all `ABS`** |      30 of 53, **all `ABS`** |
| `memoryArmConfig.reader` present?                 |                       **no** |                       **no** |

So the mechanism is **three times the answer length** and **four more MR declines**, and the sampled arithmetic
error reproduces exactly: `d851d5ba` has a gold of `$3,750` and the arm writes `The distinct charity
fundraising amounts are $1,000, $250, …` and totals them to `8,750`.

So the selector "bigger model" is refuted on this arm, and the published straddle (Mastra 10.64 points across
three readers, Agent Zero 3.4 across eight) says only that the axis is large and its **sign is not a function of
size**. Neither fact licenses another size-selected dispatch.

**One weakness in the chain, stated because it is this file's own record rather than the whitepaper's.**
`MemoryArmConfig.reader` is optional, and neither artifact from `40698867439` / `40698883428` carries it — checked
in the downloaded JSON of the first: the config lists `ask`, `askRoutes`, `reviewPass` and the rest, and there is no
`reader` key at all. So "the two configs are equal field for field, and the model is the only difference" is a
claim whose second half comes from the **dispatch inputs**, not from the artifacts; the artifacts are equal
*because* neither records the model. The field exists now (§13.110.1's debt was paid after these runs), which is
why `41159983913` and everything after it name the reader — and why this correction costs nothing to check and
would have cost a re-run to discover later.

#### 13.192.2 What is still open, and the cheapest thing that could settle it

Open: whether a reader selected on **measured compliance with this arm's output contract** clears the noise
floor. `§6.1.6` states that as the remaining route and does not take it, for a reason that is still true — the
only way it was tested cost a full run, and it lost.

So the next step is not a 500-question dispatch. It is a **compliance probe**: `limit: 20`, one repetition, one
candidate reader, and the reading is the one `§6.1.6` already knows how to take from an artifact — median answer
length against the routed block's closing line, the share of declines that are the bare token, and the parse
failures. Twenty questions is enough to separate 19 characters from 60 and not enough to say anything about
accuracy, which is exactly the scope of the question being asked.

**Falsified if** a candidate's probe shows a median answer length within a few characters of `deepseek-chat`'s
and a bare-token share within a few points — then the candidate complies, and the full run under it is the next
registration rather than this one. **Also falsified if** every candidate probed this way is already at
`deepseek-chat`'s shape, in which case compliance is not what distinguishes the models available to this arm and
the axis is closed for reasons that have nothing to do with accuracy.

#### 13.192.3 What the probe does not do, stated before it runs

1. **It cannot read accuracy.** Twenty questions has a per-capability resolution of one question and a roster
   interval too wide to compare with 83.40. A probe that is read as a result is a 20-question ranking published
   as a 500-question one.
2. **It does not re-open the judge question.** If the confound is the judge's tier rather than the reader's, no
   reader probe sees it; §13.184's audit is the instrument for that, and it is already red.
3. **It does not move the MR ceiling.** §13.187 closed the 96-question target arithmetically — fixing all
   seventeen durable misses without losing a lead is 101/121 = 83.5%, still below the arm that does no memory at
   all — so a reader that adds MR points is welcome and cannot reach the reference pipeline.

#### 13.192.4 The denominators, and the ratio that is exact without being a share

This subsection exists because §13.192.1's first commit (`c6ec828`) recorded that the whitepaper's median "could
not be reproduced". **That was wrong, and the error was mine rather than the whitepaper's** — I recomputed the
median over the 449 _answered_ questions and got 30, where §6.1.6's population is all 500 with a decline
counted as length 0, which gives **19**. Same artifact, same field, two defensible questions, and the difference
between them is not a discrepancy. The rule the mistake hands the next reader of this file: **when a published
reading fails to reproduce, vary the denominator before doubting the source.** A median over "answers" and a
median over "questions" are different measurements, and the second is the one a contract-compliance claim wants
— a reader that declines more is complying more, and answered-only silently removes those declines from the
denominator it is judged by.

Every reading §6.1.6 states therefore reproduces, and each one only under its own denominator:

| §6.1.6's reading                            | value                  | population                                                      | statistic             | reproduces?                                  |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| median answer length                        | 19 / 60                | **all 500 questions**, decline = 0 chars                        | median                | **yes, exactly**                             |
| p90 answer length (§13.110's parenthetical) | 715 / 513              | same                                                            | `method='higher'`     | **yes, exactly**                             |
| bare-token declines                         | 23 / 7 (45.1% / 13.2%) | **non-`abstention` routes, first pass** (`bareRetry.attempted`) | count, then ÷ 51 / 53 | **arithmetic yes, meaning no** (§13.192.4.2) |
| decline count                               | 51 / 53                | all 500, final record                                           | count                 | **yes**                                      |
| roster                                      | 417 / 381              | 500                                                             | count                 | **yes**                                      |

##### 13.192.4.1 The two readers differ in the _record_, and only `ABS` is bare there

Counting the final records directly — `rawOutput` reduced by the same rule `isBareDecline` uses, decoration
stripped and the token removed, nothing but wrappers left — gives **29 of 51 on the shipped reader and 30 of 53
on `v4-pro`**, and **every one of them is an `ABS` question**. Non-`ABS` bare declines in the final record:
**zero, on both readers.** That is not a surprise once the route gate is read: `#answerWithBareRetry` returns
early on `route === 'abstention'` precisely because "`ABS`'s gold is a decline and 29 of its 30 answers are this
exact bare token — a treatment reaching it would spend a call to convert a correct answer into a wrong one". So
`ABS` is bare **by design on both readers** (29 of 30, then 30 of 30), and the bare rate on the other four
capabilities is measured somewhere the record cannot show.

##### 13.192.4.2 Why 45.1% is exact and still not a share

`bareRetry.attempted` reads **23** and **7**, so `23 / 51 = 45.1%` and `7 / 53 = 13.2%` are exact — and the
numerator and the denominator are not from the same population:

- the **numerator** is a first-pass count on the four non-`abstention` routes, **before** the retry;
- the **denominator** is a final count over all five routes, **after** the retry.

Both halves of that mismatch are mechanical rather than editorial. The gate removes `ABS` from the numerator;
and `#answerWithBareRetry` ends in `this.#recordOutcome(second)`, so a question the retry _converted_ keeps the
second reply and never appears among the declines at all — `answered` equals `attempted` on both runs (23/23 and
7/7), which is to say **every** bare first-pass decline on those routes became an answer. The 51 declines
therefore contain none of the 23. What §6.1.6's row is a ratio of is two numbers that do not overlap.

Rebuilt on a population that does exist — first-pass declines outside `ABS`, which is what the retry's own reach
partitions — the same two counts become a share, and the whitepaper's conclusion survives intact:

| reader                  | first-pass non-`ABS` declines | bare → retried → answered | prose → final decline | prose share |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------: | ------------------------: | --------------------: | ----------: |
| `deepseek-chat` (417)   |                        **45** |                        23 |                    22 |   **48.9%** |
| `deepseek-v4-pro` (381) |                        **30** |                         7 |                    23 |   **76.7%** |

Two readings come out of this that the 45.1% / 13.2% pair could not give:

1. **§13.111's title is right and its arithmetic was a category error.** "The retry's population is a property of
   the reader" holds at 23 against 7 — a factor of 3.3 in `isBareDecline`'s reach on the same questions and the
   same routes — while the ratio that was published to say so divided one population by another. The corrected
   statement is stronger, not weaker: the two readers decline **about as often** outside `ABS` (45 against 30 is
   partly the retry, but 22 against 23 prose declines is a wash), and what separates them is **how they spell
   it** — 51.1% of the shipped reader's non-`ABS` declines are recoverable by an exact-token predicate and only
   23.3% of this one's are.
2. **The retry's reach is a formatting statistic, and it is now quantified as one.** On this reader pair the
   predicate's reach moves by 28 points while the decline count it is supposed to explain moves by 2. Anything
   that reports `bareRetry.attempted` as a share of declines inherits a 29-question `ABS` block in the
   denominator that the numerator is forbidden to touch — which is why the artifact's own census is the number
   to quote and the ratio is not.

##### 13.192.4.3 What this changes in the record, and what it does not

- **§13.110's parenthetical is confirmed, not corrected.** `p90 513 against 715` reproduces character for
  character with `method='higher'` over the same all-500 population, including its direction — the _shipped_
  reader has the longer p90 and the _probed_ reader the shorter one, which is the same tail the 19 → 60 median
  hides: `v4-pro` writes a great many medium-length answers where `deepseek-chat` writes either 19 characters
  or a full list.
- **§13.111's table is corrected to the right denominators**, and its "22 of 51 … 46 of 53" becomes the 22 and
  23 prose columns above; the conclusion it draws (a shape predicate does not port) is untouched.
- **§6.1.6 keeps its numbers and loses one label.** "其中仅有弃权 token 23 (45.1%)" is `bareRetry.attempted`, a
  reach outside `ABS`, and the row should say so — recorded in `cortex-docs` as a whitepaper erratum rather than
  edited silently, because the white paper is an external document and this one is the internal source it
  points at.
- **§13.192's plan does not move.** Nothing here touches the compliance probe: the probe asks a new reader's
  _answer_ shape, which is the 19 → 60 axis and reproduces; the retry population is a different axis that the
  probe was never going to read.

#### 13.192.5 The readings got a command, so the probe's three numbers are one of its outputs

§13.192.2 says the compliance probe's reading is "the one `§6.1.6` already knows how to take from an
artifact". That reading was prose in two documents and arithmetic in a shell history, which is how it came to be
recomputed on the wrong denominator and published as an erratum. It is now `tools/reader-shape.mjs`:

```
node tools/reader-shape.mjs \
  --report <40698867439>/benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json --label deepseek-chat \
  --report <40698883428>/benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json --label deepseek-v4-pro
```

Run on the two artifacts this section is about, it prints — and this is the whole point — **both denominators
for the same field, each labelled with its population**:

| line the tool prints                                                                  |     `deepseek-chat` |   `deepseek-v4-pro` |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------: | ------------------: |
| `answer length, all questions (a decline counts as 0 chars)` · median / p90           |        **19 / 715** |        **60 / 513** |
| `answer length, answered only (this denominator removes the declines)` · median / p90 |            30 / 778 |            90 / 547 |
| `bare declines in the final record`                                                   | 29 of 51, all `ABS` | 30 of 53, all `ABS` |
| `bareRetry: attempted, answered`                                                      |              23, 23 |                7, 7 |
| `first-pass non-ABS declines = attempted + prose finals` · prose share                |          45 · 48.9% |          30 · 76.7% |
| `invariant non-ABS bare finals <= attempted - answered`                               |       held (0 vs 0) |       held (0 vs 0) |

Three things this settles that argument could not:

1. **The published figures reproduce, and the tool is the thing that says so.** `19` and `715` are printed with
   the population in the label, so the next reader who wants a median sees which question they are answering
   before they answer it. §13.192.4's correction has an instrument behind it now, not a paragraph.
2. **The ratio is retired from the tool's vocabulary.** The line says `attempted / declines is NOT a share` and
   prints the population that is one. A future artifact cannot quietly have the old ratio recomputed from it.
3. **The one reading whose failure is a bug is an exit code.** `bareRetry` is gated on
   `route === 'abstention'`, so a non-`ABS` bare decline can only survive the pass when the second reply also
   declined bare. `non-ABS bare finals <= attempted - answered` must therefore hold, and the tool exits 1 with
   the offending `questionId`s instead of printing a number. It holds at `0 vs 0` on both artifacts, which is the
   arithmetic form of `answered == attempted`.

**What this does to the probe.** `P0-reader-probe` no longer needs a reading designed for it: the three numbers
it was registered to take — median answer length against the routed block's closing line, the bare-token count,
and the parse failures (`empty replies among the declines`) — are a single invocation on the probe's artifact.
What remains is the dispatch itself and the rule that twenty questions are a shape reading and not a ranking,
which `13.192.3` already fixes.

**What the tool does not do.** It reads no accuracy, and its `--json` has no cross-artifact comparison beyond
one pair block whose deltas are printed for legibility and are not a test statistic. It also does not decide
which denominator a claim should use — it prints both so that the choice is made in the open, which is the only
repair available for a mistake that was made by choosing silently.

#### 13.192.6 The reader identity becomes a registered value, and the probe moves the half that is addressable

**Registered and dispatched 2026-10-31: two runs, 20 questions each, one variable.**

The first thing this section had to fix was not the probe. §13.192.1 ended on a hole it could not close from
the artifacts: `MemoryArmConfig.reader` was absent from both files, and the "configs equal, model the only
difference" claim came from dispatch inputs nobody could re-read. Looking for that dispatch turned up the
reason — **`model` and `thinking` are workflow inputs that `dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py` does not send**. Every
run from that table applied the workflow's defaults, and the one run that changed the reader was dispatched
outside the script. So the arm's largest measured effect (7.20 points) rests on a value that was never
registered in §10.3, never sent by the guarded path, and never recorded in the artifact it produced. Both
halves are now registered (`readerModel`, `readerThinking`) and both are sent, which is what
`test_preregistration_config.py`'s two-directional assertions verify — the same guard that caught the
`relevanceSignal` drift in §13.69.

**What the probe moves, and why it is not another model.** §13.192.1 refuted size, and the only other model id
this endpoint offers (`deepseek-reasoner`) is not addressable through this arm's request shape without a
pre-flight call that this checkout cannot make — the sandbox holds no provider key. `thinking` is the one
reader axis that is (a) accepted by the same endpoint and the same SDK call, (b) already a declared input, and
(c) able to change the *shape* of a reply without changing the model. That last property is the whole reason it
is worth twenty questions: §13.192.4 measured that the two readers differ in how they spell a decline while
declining about as often, and this is the cheapest lever that can move spelling alone.

| | control | treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dispatch | `--set limit=20 --set ablation_runs=1` | same, plus `--set thinking=enabled` |
| `model` | `deepseek-chat` | `deepseek-chat` |
| everything else | §10.3 | §10.3 |
| read by | `tools/reader-shape.mjs --report control --report treatment` | same |

Twenty questions is not a smaller 500. `sampling.ts` round-robins across buckets (`IE` split by question type,
`MR`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS`), so the sample covers every capability at about three questions each — enough to say
which capabilities the reading speaks about and not enough to say anything about any of them. `ablation_runs: 1`
is deliberate and is the one place this probe borrows a rule it otherwise obeys: §6.1.6's repetition guard exists
because accuracy under `T = 1` moves 5–6 questions per capability between identical runs, and a *shape* statistic
over 20 questions is not an accuracy estimate. The number this probe must never be quoted for is the roster.

**Predictions, each of them falsifiable from the two artifacts:**

1. **Coverage.** All five capabilities appear in the sample, `ABS` and `MR` included. Falsified if either is
   absent, which would also falsify the claim in `sampling.ts`'s docblock and is why it is written down.
2. **Shape moves up, not down.** The `thinking: enabled` arm's median answer length over all 20 questions is
   **larger** than the control's. Reasoning before answering is the mechanism most likely to break a closing
   line that asks for one number. Falsified if it is equal or smaller.
3. **The abstention route is unchanged.** `ABS`'s replies are the bare token on both arms, so the final-record
   bare count equals the `ABS` question count on both. Falsified if any `ABS` reply carries prose — that would
   mean thinking mode rewrites the token, and the route's criterion becomes unusable rather than merely
   unchanged.
4. **No parse failures.** `empty replies among the declines` is **0** on both arms. The thinking adapter returns
   `content` with the reasoning dropped, so the arm reads the same field; a non-zero count would mean the
   adapter is not what this section assumes and every shape reading is suspect.
5. **The retry invariant holds** on both: `non-ABS bare finals <= attempted - answered`. This is a bug detector
   rather than a prediction — it holds if the abstention gate works, and the tool exits 1 if it does not.

**The decision rule, fixed before the artifacts exist.** If prediction 2 holds — the enabled arm's median is
materially longer — then thinking mode is disqualified as a compliance lever and the reader axis is closed for
this arm on **shape** rather than on accuracy, which is the cheapest possible disqualification and the one thing
§13.192.1 could not buy at 500 questions. If the two arms are within a few characters of each other with the
same bare/prose split, then this lever is exhausted and §13.192.2's second falsification clause fires: what
distinguishes readers available to this arm is not compliance, and the axis is closed for a reason that has
nothing to do with accuracy. **A 500-question run under `thinking: enabled` is not the next step in either
branch**; it becomes the next step only if the enabled arm is *both* shorter and more contract-shaped, which
would be the first reader this campaign has found that is.

**What it cannot read**, unchanged from §13.192.3: accuracy, the judge's tier (§13.184), and the MR ceiling
(§13.187).

#### 13.192.7 The control artifact arrived, and reading it found two defects in the tool that read it

**Read 2026-10-31 from `41185512391` (`completed/success`), the control `§13.190.4` dispatched for the
`operand-gap` pair. Nothing here reads ABS's criterion — that is `41188431321`, still running — and nothing here
is about the ask.**

##### 13.192.7.1 What the control reads

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| roster, one repetition (`feature.metrics`) | **426/500** |
| roster across 4 repetitions (`ablation.featureAggregate`) | min **426** / max **430** / mean **428.3** / median **429** → **0.8565** |
| per capability, mean over 4 | IE 144.25, MR 89.75, TR 104.25, KU 61, ABS 29 |
| reader, from the artifact | `deepseek/deepseek-chat`, `thinking disabled`, `temperature 0` |
| declines | 50 (ABS 29, TR 12, MR 7, KU 2) |
| `bareRetry` | attempted **111**, answered **111** → **27.75 per run**, every one converted |
| final bare declines | 29 of 50, **all `ABS`**; outside `ABS` **0** |
| `llmUsage` | 5,566 calls, 50.58 M prompt tokens, 44.49 M of them cache hits |

Three things follow, and the first one is a boundary rather than a result:

1. **This is not the registered configuration.** Its `memoryArmConfig` carries `maxPromptChars: 96000`,
   `turnCutMarker: ellipsis`, `ask: operands`, `reviewPass: bare` — the 96,000 ceiling every run since
   `41144910162` uses, the §13.188 ellipsis treatment, and §13.190's ask. §10.3 registers **48,000** and a bare
   `400`. So **428 is the roster of a configuration the registration does not describe**, and quoting it against
   an 83.40% figure measured at 48,000 compares two budgets. §13.192.7.3 is that drift, which no existing guard
   can see.
2. **The artifact now names its reader.** `MemoryArmConfig.reader` is present with provider, model, base URL,
   thinking mode and temperature. §13.110.1's debt is paid on this path, which is what makes `§13.192.6`'s
   two-dispatch probe readable at all — and it retro-confirms `§13.192.1`'s weakness: the field exists *now*,
   which is precisely why its absence in `40698867439`/`40698883428` is a missing measurement rather than a
   contradiction.
3. **The retry converts everything it touches, for the fifth time.** 111 attempts, 111 answers, over four
   repetitions. The population is per run 27.75 and every one became an answer, so `answered == attempted` again
   — the arithmetic form of §13.111's reach being a formatting statistic rather than an uncertainty one.

##### 13.192.7.2 The tool was wrong twice, and only a real artifact of each shape could show it

`tools/reader-shape.mjs` was run on this artifact for the first time, and it printed two things it should not
have:

- **`first-pass non-ABS declines = attempted + prose finals = 132`, prose share `15.9%`.** `bareRetry` is a
  **process-wide** counter, so a four-repetition run reports four runs' worth of attempts, while `questions[]`
  carries **one** record per question. The tool divided a summed numerator by a per-question denominator — the
  same defect §13.192.4 exists to repair, one level up, committed by the tool written to repair it. It now prints
  the census **per repetition** (`27.75 per run`) and refuses the share across repetitions rather than
  approximating it.
- **`reader [object Object]`.** The field §13.110.1 added became a record, and the tool interpolated it. It is
  now rendered (`deepseek/deepseek-chat (thinking disabled, temperature 0)`), with `null` temperature printing as
