  *no temperature sent* rather than as `0` — the distinction `resolveReaderIdentity` returns `number | null` for.

Both are recorded because of what they say about instruments in general: **a reading tool is unverified until it
has been pointed at a real artifact of every shape it claims to read.** Every test in `test_reader_shape.py` used
a hand-built single-run fixture, and both defects live in shapes no fixture had — a multi-repetition census, and
a reader record. The suite is 19 tests now, and the four added ones are those two shapes plus the interval and
the absent-temperature case.

##### 13.192.7.3 The drift §10.3 cannot see, because both sides of the comparison moved together

`test_preregistration_config.py` compares §10.3 against the dispatch table, in both directions, and that guard
was written for §13.64's doc↔script drift. It cannot see this one: **§10.3 and the dispatch table both say
`maxPromptChars: 48000`, and every 500-question run on this arm since `41144910162` runs at 96,000 through a
`--set` that neither document records.** The same shape applies to the cut marker: §10.3 names `maxTurnChars: 400`
and the table sends `400`, while the newest runs send `400:ellipsis`.

So the registration describes a configuration that the arm no longer runs, and the drift is invisible for the
reason the §13.64 guard cannot reach — it is not a disagreement between two documents but a disagreement between
the documents and what is dispatched. Two consequences, neither taken here:

1. **`--set` is the hole.** A guarded table plus an unguarded override that lands in the same field means the
   guard's coverage is `(registered ∩ sent)` and the interesting value lives outside it. An override should be
   recorded in §10.3's own list, at least as a one-line "as of §13.17x, the arm runs at 96,000 and the marker is
   on"; otherwise the next reader of §10.3 measures 48,000 by reading a document.
2. **The two probe dispatches of §13.192.6 therefore run at 48,000 without the marker**, not at this run's
   configuration. That is deliberate — a shape reading wants the registered arm — but it means the probe's control
   and `41185512391` are **not** comparable, and any future 500-question run should say which of the two budgets
   it is on before its roster is quoted.

#### 13.192.8 The probe ran: four predictions met, the fifth falsified in the direction that matters

**Both arms completed: `41195744819` (`thinking: disabled`, 175 s job) and `41195758208` (`thinking: enabled`,
627 s).** Same twenty questions, same config, one variable. Read with
`tools/reader-shape.mjs --report … --report …`.

| reading | disabled | enabled |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample coverage | **ABS 3, IE 8, KU 3, MR 3, TR 3** | identical |
| reader, from the artifact | `deepseek/deepseek-chat (thinking disabled, temperature 0)` | `… (thinking enabled, temperature 0)` |
| roster (not quotable at n = 20) | 18/20 | 17/20 |
| median answer length, all questions | **120** | **25** |
| median answer length, answered only | **161** | **49** |
| median `rawOutput`, all questions | **316** | **73.5** |
| **MR** median / max answer (answered) | **135 / 161** | **1 / 1** |
| **TR** median / max | **664 / 708** | **150 / 236** |
| **KU** median / max | **328 / 374** | **83 / 103** |
| **IE** median / max | 64 / **8,094** | 56.5 / **952** |
| final bare declines | 3 of 3, all `ABS` | 3 of 3, all `ABS` |
| `bareRetry` | 1 / 1 | **0 / 0** |
| empty replies among declines | 0 | 0 |

**Prediction 1 (coverage) met** — all five capabilities present on both arms, and `ABS` and `MR` among them, which
is the claim `sampling.ts` makes and the reason a 20-question probe is not a smaller 500. **Prediction 3 met**
(`ABS` bare on both, 3 of 3). **Prediction 4 met** (no parse failures on either arm — the thinking adapter returns
`content` with the reasoning dropped, so the shape reading reads the same field). **Prediction 5 met** (the retry
invariant holds at `0 vs 0` on both).

**Prediction 2 is falsified, and this is the finding.** I wrote that the `thinking: enabled` arm's median would be
**larger**, on the reasoning that reasoning before answering is what breaks a closing line that asks for one
number. It is **four times smaller** at the roster level and **135 times smaller** on `MR`. The mechanism is not
"thinking writes more" — it is that the same model, given a thinking pass, **does what the routed block's closing
line says**:

| question | `disabled` answers | `enabled` answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `6d550036` (MR, "how many distinct projects…") | *"Both items refer to the same single project/team leadership (leading a team of five engineers), so the count of distinct…"* — 135 characters, **no number** | **`2`** |
| `gpt4_59c863d7` (MR, "how many model kits") | a numbered list of kits, **never totalled** — 161 characters | **`5`** |
| `6aeb4375` (KU, "how many Korean restaurants") | *"Based on the evidence, the most recent statement about how many Korean restaurants you have tried is from 2023/09/30: \"I…"* — 328 characters | **`4`** |

The disabled reader's replies are not wrong in their reasoning; they are **unscoreable**, because the contract
asked for the Step 2 number alone and the answer never states one. That is the same shape §13.110 described as
"the larger model followed the contract less well", now measured as a *seat on a switch* rather than as a property
of model size: the same model id, one input apart, and MR's median answer goes from 135 characters to 1.

**What this does not claim.** Not accuracy: 18 against 17 at n = 20 is one question, and §13.192.3 said so before
the runs existed. Not that compliance is what the *judge* rewards — that is the next run's question, not this
one's. And not that `thinking: enabled` is free: the job took **627 s against 175 s**, a **3.58×** wall-clock
multiplier, which is what §13.192.9 has to fit inside.

#### 13.192.9 The next step is a matched 220-question pair, because the 90-minute budget cannot hold a 500

§13.192.6's decision rule said a 500-question run under `thinking: enabled` becomes the next step only if the
enabled arm is *both* shorter **and** more contract-shaped. It is both. So the run is owed — and it does not fit.

**The arithmetic, from measured numbers rather than from a guess.** The probe spent **627 s** on 20 questions × 2
arms × 1 repetition with thinking on, which is **15.7 s per question** including both sides. At 500 questions that
is **7,850 s ≈ 2 h 11 m**, and the workflow's `budgetMinutes` is a **constant 90 minutes** (§13.30 / §13.115 moved
it there when the input surface hit GitHub's 25-input ceiling). A 500-question thinking run would be killed with
most of the roster unread, and the artifact would be a partial one — the failure mode where a run looks like a
result. At **220 questions** the same arithmetic gives **3,454 s ≈ 58 min**, which fits with headroom.

**Dispatched as a pair, `d973362`:** both arms at `limit: 220`, `ablation_runs: 1`,
`cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars: 96000`, `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars: 400:ellipsis`, `model: deepseek-chat` —
and `thinking` the only difference. The two dispatches are matched on **N and repetition count**, which is the
condition §6.1.6 makes for any comparison and the reason this is a pair rather than the enabled run alone against
`41185512391`'s four repetitions.

**Predictions, fixed before the artifacts exist:**

1. **Compliance holds at scale.** The enabled arm's `MR` median answer length is **≤ 10 characters**, against the
   disabled arm's > 100 on the same questions. Falsified if it exceeds 50 — which would mean the 20-question
   reading was a property of the sample rather than of the reader, and that would be the more interesting result.
2. **Compliance converts on `MR`.** The enabled arm's `MR` correct count exceeds the disabled arm's by **≥ +6
   questions**. This is the whole question: the disabled reader's MR is 68.6% and its failures are enumerations that
   never emit a number.

   **Correction to this prediction's denominator, made after the control artifact arrived and before the treatment
   one did, and stated so a reader can check it.** I wrote "of about 53 at this sample" by scaling 121 × 220/500.
   The control artifact reads **MR 32, IE 94, KU 32, TR 32, ABS 30** — `sampling.ts` round-robins over seven
   buckets (`IE` split into user/assistant/preference), so 220 questions is ~31 per bucket, `ABS` exhausts at its
   own 30, and `IE` takes its three buckets' share. The threshold is unchanged at **+6**; only the base it is 6 out
   of is corrected, from 53 to **32**. Six of 32 is a large effect, and that is what the prediction claims.
3. **`TR` moves in the same direction but less.** `TR`'s closing line is also the enumerated one, so ≥ +4. Falsified
   if TR falls, which would say the compliance gain is route-specific in a way the reach table does not predict.
4. **`IE` does not fall by more than 3.** `IE`'s answers are legitimately long (median 64 on both arms), and the
   enabled reader's IE max fell from 8,094 to 952 — a state where verbosity may have been *helping* the judge.
   Falsified if IE falls by ≥ 4, and that outcome would mean the axis trades one capability for another rather
   than adding.
5. **`ABS` keeps every point it can.** Both arms decline the same `ABS` questions bare; at 220 questions that is
   about 13. The reading is the two bare counts and the invariant, not accuracy.
6. **`bareRetry` collapses toward zero** on the enabled arm (0 attempts at n = 20). If it stays high, the enabled
   reader declines bare outside `ABS` too and §13.111's reach argument is stronger than measured.

**Decision rule, before the runs.** Prediction 1 is a **gate**: if it fails, the 20-question probe does not
generalize and no 500-question dispatch follows from it. Predictions 2 and 3 are the **signal**: if both hold, the
500-question confirmation is the next registration and `thinking: enabled` is a candidate adoption. If 1 holds and
2 fails, compliance is not what the roster is missing — the arm's points are elsewhere and the reader axis closes
on **evidence** rather than on shape, which is the outcome §13.192.2 could not reach. Prediction 4 is the **cost**:
if it fails, the adoption decision becomes a per-capability trade and needs its own registration rather than an
adoption.

**What neither run can read.** Accuracy at 500 questions, the judge's tier (§13.184), and the MR ceiling
(§13.187) — 220 questions cannot reach a 101/121 target even if every prediction holds.

### 13.193 The operand rule converts its question four times out of four, and the reach claim was wrong in the only way that costs 63 questions

**Read 2026-10-31 from `41188431321` (`completed/success`, 500 questions, 4 repetitions), against its control
`41185512391`.** The artifacts differ in `ask` and `askRoutes` and in nothing else — checked field by field in
`memoryArmConfig`: `ask: operands` → `operand-gap`, `askRoutes: [multi-session, flat, temporal]` → `[abstention]`.

#### 13.193.1 The criterion

| reading | control | treated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `featureByCapability.ABS` | min 29 / avg 29 / max 29 | **min 30 / avg 30 / max 30** |
| `baselineByCapability.ABS` | 30 / 30 / 30 | 30 / 30 / 30 |
| `6456829e_abs`, per-run correct bits | **`0000`**, answer `5 tomato plants` | **`1111`**, answer `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` |
| other `ABS` questions that stopped declining | — | **none** |

**The prediction registered in §13.190.4 is met, in all four repetitions, on the one question it named.** The arm
now reaches the reference pipeline's `ABS` ceiling of 30/30, and it did so without losing a single other `ABS`
decline — the two ways this treatment could have failed (no conversion, or converting questions whose gold is not
a decline) both did not happen.

#### 13.193.2 The reach claim is false, and the artifact is unambiguous about it

§13.190.4 opened with "reach and change set are the same single route, which no ask before this one manages", and
derived from it that MR, IE, KU and TR "read the shipped block **by construction**". `tools/window-pair.mjs`
says otherwise:

| capability | prompts digest-equal | prompts that moved |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `KU` | **72 of 72** | 0 |
| `IE` | 56 of 150 | **94** |
| `MR` | **0 of 121** | **121** |
| `TR` | **0 of 127** | **127** |
| `ABS` | **0 of 30** | **30** |

**372 of 500 prompts moved, across four capabilities, and 335 of them moved at the same length** — which is why
`length is not identity` earns its line on its first real pair: a reach table asserted against `promptChars` would
have shown nothing here.

The error is not in the mechanism, it is in what the control was. The claim reasoned about the **abstention**
instruction's reach — correct, and the reason `operands` never touched `ABS` — but the comparison is against a run
whose `ask` was `operands`, and `ask` is a **single-valued** input: naming `operand-gap` makes
`ASK_ROUTES['operand-gap'] = ['abstention']`, so the three routes that had the `operands` block fall back to the
shipped one. So the treated arm is not "control plus a fix"; it is "control **minus** `operands` on three routes,
**plus** `operand-gap` on a fourth". The registration wrote "MR is unread here" as a caveat about one capability;
the artifact says four.

#### 13.193.3 What the removal cost, which nothing had measured until it happened

| capability | control avg | treated avg | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IE | 144.25 | 141.25 | −3.00 |
| **MR** | **89.75** | **41.00** | **−48.75** |
| KU | 61.00 | 61.50 | +0.50 |
| **TR** | **104.25** | **92.50** | **−11.75** |
| ABS | 29.00 | **30.00** | **+1.00** |
| **roster (mean of 4)** | **428.3 (0.8565)** | **366.25 (0.7325)** | **−62.05** |

The `operands` block is worth **63 questions** on this arm — 49 on MR alone — and that number did not exist before
this run, because every run since it was adopted carried it on both sides. Two riders on it: the `operands`
block's text differs on **all 121** MR questions rather than the seven "derivation" questions §13.190.1 reasoned
about, so its effect is not confined to the questions that need operand arithmetic; and the loss is
**route-shaped**, largest where the closing line asks for a count (`MR`), smaller on `TR`, near zero on `KU`,
which the block never reached.

#### 13.193.4 The same mechanism as §13.192, which is why both are recorded this iteration

Two independent artifacts, one statement: **the closing line decides whether a count is emitted.**

- `thinking: enabled` on the same model takes `MR`'s median answer from 135 characters to **1**, because a
  thinking pass reads the line and complies (§13.192.8).
- Removing the `operands` block costs `MR` **49 questions**, because that block is the only thing telling the
  reader to total a list it has already written (§13.193.3).

So the arm's two worst capabilities are not failing at retrieval and not failing at reasoning: they are failing to
**state an answer in the shape the contract asked for**, and there are two levers on that — a block that says what
to state, and a reader that does what it is told. Both are now measured, neither is adopted, and they are not
independent: a compliant reader makes a vague block less costly, which is a prediction this file can test later
rather than a design choice to make now.

#### 13.193.5 The wiring defect, and the fix that follows from it

`ask` being one value is the defect. The correct configuration is a **per-route map**: `operands` on
`multi-session`, `flat` and `temporal`, **and** `operand-gap` on `abstention`. Both rules are already implemented
and both have now been measured on the route they belong to; what is missing is a way to say "these two at once".

Registered as the next increment, with its own criterion and no code written yet:

1. **Implementation.** A per-route ask (`askRoutes` becomes a map rather than a single name, or a second input
   `abstentionAsk` defaults to the shipped name and takes `operand-gap`). Backwards-compatible by construction:
   absent means today's behaviour, which is what every archived prompt was produced under.
2. **The criterion is one-sided and already has both endpoints.** `ABS` reads **30/30** and `6456829e_abs` declines
   in all four repetitions; `MR`, `IE`, `TR` read **within their own 4-run range** of `41185512391` — that run's
   per-capability interval is measured, so the reading is "does the per-route map restore 428.3 ± the arm's floor",
   not "does it beat 366".
3. **Falsified if** any of the three routes does not return to its control range, which would mean the `operands`
   block's effect is not reproducible and §13.193.3's 63 is a draw rather than a mechanism.
4. **The prompt identity check is now mandatory for this arm.** `window-pair`'s per-capability digest counts are
   the instrument: the run is only single-variable if `KU` stays 72/72 equal and the three operands routes show
   the same digest on both sides, with `ABS` alone moving.

### 13.194 The composition lands, and the first implementation read the wrong block

§13.193.5 registered the fix and named two ways to build it. It is built, it is a third way, and the reason is
the one this campaign keeps arriving at: **a configuration is a claim with a control, and a general mechanism is
not.** What follows is the decision, the defect the first implementation had, and the registration of the run
that will read it.

#### 13.194.1 What `ask` as a single value costs, per run rather than in aggregate

The two artifacts, computed from `ablation.featureCorrectByRun` — which nothing in this repository had read per
capability until now, because every comparison in §13 subtracted two averages:

| capability | `41185512391` (`operands`) | `41188431321` (`operand-gap`) | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| IE | 143, 143, 145, 146 (144.25) | 142, 141, 142, 140 (141.25) | −3.00 |
| **MR** | **91, 90, 90, 88 (89.75)** | **42, 41, 40, 41 (41.00)** | **−48.75** |
| KU | 61, 61, 61, 61 (61.00) | 61, 61, 62, 62 (61.50) | +0.50 |
| **TR** | **102, 106, 103, 106 (104.25)** | **91, 93, 93, 93 (92.50)** | **−11.75** |
| ABS | 29, 29, 29, 29 (29.00) | **30, 30, 30, 30 (30.00)** | **+1.00** |
| roster | 426, 429, 428, 430 (**428.25**) | 366, 366, 367, 366 (**366.25**) | −62.00 |

Two facts in that table are not in §13.193 and both change how the next reading has to be made.

**The control's `KU` is deterministic and the treatment's is not.** `41185512391` reads `61, 61, 61, 61`;
`41188431321` reads `61, 61, 62, 62` — on a route whose **72 prompts are byte-identical between the two runs**
(`window-pair` digest: `72/72` equal). So the identical-prompt floor of this arm is **at least one question**,
temperature `0` is not determinism, and the control's zero variance was a property of that draw rather than of
the configuration. Every "returns to its range" criterion below is stated with that floor in it, because a
criterion that assumed a deterministic reader would call a one-question drift a movement.

**`MR`'s four runs are a range, not a number.** 91 and 88 are the same configuration. §13.187's paired-flip
reading already showed the reference arm itself moving across 105/104/104/102, and this is the same fact on the
feature side: the next dispatch is read against **[88, 91]**, not against 89.75.

#### 13.194.2 The composite, and why it is a name rather than a map

§13.193.5 proposed `askRoutes` becoming a map, or a second input `abstentionAsk`. What is implemented is a
**third value in the union**, `operands+operand-gap`, which delegates:

```ts
if (ask === 'operands+operand-gap') {
  return instructionsFor(contract, date, contract === 'abstention' ? 'operand-gap' : 'operands', scope, shape);
}
```

The trade-off, stated rather than left implicit:

| | per-route map | composite value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| generality | any route → any ask | one combination at a time |
| what the artifact can claim | a configuration no measurement covers | a claim with a control and a change set |
| backwards compatibility | a new field beside `ask` | a new union member; absent = today |
| what the oracle checks | a map needs a new oracle | the existing one: 6 routes × 2 shapes vs a named control |
| cost of the second combination | zero | one more name |

The map is the general form and it is the wrong shape **for a measured configuration**: every value in
`ASK_ROUTES` is a rule that was dispatched, read, and kept or retired, and a map would let a run state a
configuration nobody measured while its `askRoutes` still read like a reach. The composition of two measured
rules is itself measurable — it has a control (`operands`, the run it will be read against), a change set (the
abstention route, one route, on both question shapes) and a reach (the union, four routes) — and all three are
asserted by rendering rather than described. When a *second* combination is needed, that is the day the map
earns its keep.

The delegation is the part that matters most: the composite is not a third copy of either block, so the two
halves cannot drift from it. `ask-composite.test.ts` renders all six routes under both question shapes and
requires the composite's block to be **byte-identical to the half that owns the route**, which is a property no
copy could satisfy after a single edit to either rule.

#### 13.194.3 The defect the first implementation had, and it was mine

The first version of the composite passed the new tests on enumeration questions and failed on derivation ones:
the multi-session block came back as `enumerated`'s rather than `operands`. The cause was not in the composite.
`buildSessionPrompt` computed the question shape under a gate:

```ts
const shape = options.ask === 'operands' ? classifyQuestionShape(question) : undefined;
```

That gate was a **second declaration** of which ask reads the shape, written when there was one such ask, and
the composite is a second — so the delegating branch received `shape: undefined` and silently took the
enumeration path while `ASK_ROUTES` said four routes were reached. The reach table and the render disagreed,
which is the defect class `ask-changes.test.ts` exists for, arriving through a gate rather than a fallthrough.

The repair is to delete the gate rather than to widen it: the classifier now runs unconditionally, so the branch
that reads `shape` is the **only** statement of the fact, and a future composition cannot inherit the defect by
being absent from a list. The cost is one regex over the question against a network call per question, and the
alternative — a literal array of asks that read the shape — is the arrangement that failed.

This is the second time in two increments that a table and a render disagreed in a place nobody was looking
(`§13.193.2`'s reach claim was the first), and in both cases the **test** found it before the dispatch. That is
the whole argument for writing the test first: this defect produces a plausible artifact — `askRoutes` naming
four routes, `ABS` moving to 30, and `MR` short by the derivation questions — and the reading would have blamed
the operands block.

#### 13.194.4 The registration

The run is `41185512391`'s configuration with one value changed: `ask: operands → operands+operand-gap`, which
the dispatch carries as `--set cortex_memory_ask=operands+operand-gap`. Everything else — 500 questions, 4
repetitions, `deepseek-chat` with `thinking: disabled` at temperature 0, `maxPromptChars 96000`, `400:ellipsis`
on `multi-session+temporal`, `relevance-hybrid`, `topK 256`, `reviewPass bare` — is the control's, so the two
runs differ in the instruction text of **one route**.

Six predictions, all one-sided where the mechanism makes them one-sided:

1. **Gate — `ABS` reads 30 in all four runs.** From `41188431321`, and the conversion is `6456829e_abs`, whose
   gold is a decline. If `ABS` falls below 30 in any run, the two blocks interfere and the composition is
   wrong even if the roster rises.
2. **Signal — `MR` in `[87, 92]` per run.** The control reads `91, 90, 90, 88`; the composite's `MR` prompts are
   the control's byte for byte, so the prediction is reproduction, not improvement, and a reading below 87 is
   §13.193.3's 63 re-attributed rather than confirmed.
3. **Signal — `TR` in `[99, 108]`** (control `102, 106, 103, 106`) and **`IE` in `[140, 148]`** (control
   `143, 143, 145, 146`), for the same reason: identical prompts.
4. **Noise control — `KU` in `{61, 62}`** (control `61, 61, 61, 61`; the treated run of §13.194.1 reads
   `61, 61, 62, 62` on identical prompts). A `KU` reading outside that set is not noise and means the
   abstention route's block reached a route it must not reach.
5. **Roster — each run equal to the control's plus one, i.e. `427, 430, 429, 431`, average 429.25**, with the
   arm's identical-prompt floor of ±1 per capability making `[425, 433]` the acceptance band. This is the exact
   arithmetic of "the composition adds the ABS question and nothing else", which is why it is stated per run
   rather than as a delta.
6. **Prompt identity, which is now mandatory for this arm** (`§13.193.5.4`): `window-pair` must read `MR`
   121/121, `IE` 150/150, `TR` 127/127 and `KU` 72/72 equal against `41185512391`, with `ABS` 30/30 different.
   Any other combination means the value did something the tables do not state, and no number in the run can
   explain it.

**Decision rule, fixed before the run.** If 1–6 hold, the composite is adopted as the registered `ask`: §10.3
gains the line and `tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py`'s `INPUTS` moves with it in the same commit, which is
what `test_preregistration_config.py` pins.

*Read on 2026-10-31 (`41222844945`): criteria 1, 2, 3 and 6 hold, 4 fails and 5 fails as arithmetic /
holds as a band. §13.203 is the reading — it finds that criterion 4's `{61, 62}` was already contradicted by
`41159983913`'s `KU` 60/59/61/61 nine sections earlier, measures the identical-prompt noise floor this
criterion was guessing at (4.8% of reads flip; 2σ = 9.3 questions on 470), and adopts the composite on the
one thing that survives both: `6456829e_abs` converting in four repetitions out of four.* If 1 holds and 2 or 3 fails, the 63-question attribution of
§13.193.3 is a draw and not a mechanism, and the `operands` block's price has to be re-measured with a design
that holds the abstention block fixed. If 1 fails, the two rules are not composable on this prompt and the map
in §13.194.2 is the wrong direction as well.

#### 13.194.5 What this does not do

It does not read accuracy on `MR`: the composite is a *restoration*, so its entire value is that it makes the
abstention block adoptable without paying 62 questions. §13.187's ceiling reading stands — `MR`'s 17 stable
failures are unchanged by this value, and the best case here is `ABS` 30 and a roster of 429 against the
control's 428. The reader axis (`§13.192`) and this one are separate by construction: one changes the block
every route reads, this changes which block one route reads, and a run that moved both would make neither
attributable.

### 13.195 The control side of the 220-question pair, and a gate that cannot fail

Run `41196801892` (the disabled arm of the §13.192.9 pair) arrived. `41196814139` — the `thinking: enabled` arm —
was still `in_progress` when everything below was written, which is the only reason this section can be trusted as a
pre-registration rather than a rationalisation.

#### 13.195.1 Prediction 1's baseline was read off the probe, and the control contradicts it

§13.192.9's first prediction says the enabled arm's `MR` median answer length is **≤ 10 characters**, *"against the
disabled arm's > 100 on the same questions"*, and that it is falsified if the median exceeds 50. The control
artifact reads:

| capability | median (answered only) | max | answers > 40 chars | answered of n |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IE | 34.5 | 19,808 | 46 of 94 | 94 of 94 |
| **MR** | **2.5** | **376** | **5 of 32** | 32 of 32 |
| KU | 137.5 | 658 | 16 of 30 | 30 of 32 |
| TR | 627.5 | 2,703 | 30 of 30 | 30 of 32 |
| ABS | 15 | 15 | 0 of 1 | 1 of 30 |

`MR`'s median at this sample is **2.5 characters**, not > 100. The "> 100" came from the twenty-question probe,
where `MR` is about four questions and the median was 135 — a statistic over four items, two of which were long
prose. So the gate as written **is satisfied by the control** and cannot distinguish the arms: any enabled reading
at or below 10 passes, including one produced by a reader that changed nothing.

This is §13.192.4's rule arriving on a different axis: before concluding that a reading fails to reproduce, change
the denominator or the sample — and here the sample is what changed, because 32 `MR` questions are not 4.

**Amended gate, written before the treated artifact exists.** The mechanism §13.192.8 established is not "the
median falls", it is **"the long enumeration-and-explain replies stop happening"**: the enabled reader answers the
question the closing line asks instead of narrating why it cannot. The statistic that carries that is the tail.

1. **`MR` prose share falls**: answers longer than 40 characters go from **5 of 32** to **≤ 2 of 32**. Falsified if
   it stays at 5 or above — which would say the probe's short replies were sample luck and the compliance reading
   does not generalize, the outcome §13.192.9 was written to be able to produce.
2. **`TR` median falls**: from **627.5** to **≤ 400**. `TR`'s closing line is the enumerated one too, so the same
   mechanism applies; a `TR` median at or above the control's would say the reader's verbosity is a property of the
   route rather than of the instruction.
3. Predictions 2–6 of §13.192.9 stand **unchanged**, including their thresholds (`MR` ≥ +6, `TR` ≥ +4, `IE` ≥ −3,
   `ABS` bare counts, `bareRetry` → 0). Only prediction 1's *statistic* changed, and it changed because the control
   measured what the probe could not.

#### 13.195.2 What the control establishes on its own, independent of the pair

Four facts worth recording whether or not the treated arm ever lands, because each one is a reading the arm has
never had at this sample:

**The roster is not a shape artifact.** 196 of 220 (89.09%) with 33 declines, of which **29 are the bare ABS
token** and **none outside `ABS`** (`bareFinals.outsideAbstention: 0`, invariant `0 ≤ (17 − 17) / 1` held). So the
disabled reader's answers, at this sample, are contract-shaped everywhere the contract is measurable.

**`MR` is short on this draw and the arm still loses 9 of 32.** Median 2.5 characters, 32 of 32 answered, 23
correct — the failures are not refusals and not prose. That is §13.187's paired-flip reading in a different
sample: `MR`'s remaining loss is **wrong numbers**, not unanswered questions.

**`TR`'s answers are long by design and the judge absorbs them.** Median 627.5, 30 of 30 answered, 27 correct. A
`TR` answer here is a paragraph; the enabled arm's predicted shortening (prediction 2) is therefore a change in
*how* the answer is given, which the judge may or may not reward — that is exactly what prediction 3 (`TR` ≥ +4)
is asking.

**The retry population is now measured at this sample**: 17 attempted, 17 answered, 21 first-pass non-`ABS`
declines of which 4 are prose, i.e. **19.0%** — against 48.9% at 500 questions (`§13.192.4`). The share is a
property of the sample, which is the third time this campaign has found a ratio whose denominator was the thing
that moved.

### 13.196 The retry the arm relies on has never run on the route that needed it

The invariant added to `tools/reader-shape.mjs` one increment ago fired on the first artifact that could violate it.
It was written to catch a leak in the retry's route gate. What it caught is the opposite: **the retry's reach is
narrower than every document in this repository says it is**, and the route it does not reach is the one whose
replies most often take the shape the retry exists for.

#### 13.196.1 The reading

`41188431321` (`ask: operand-gap`), `runs: 4`, census `bareRetry: {attempted: 271, answered: 271}`:

| capability | final declines | of which the bare token | bare finals on this route before |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| **MR** | **58** | **58** | **0** |
| TR | 12 | 0 | 0 |
| KU | 2 | 0 | 0 |

`bare finals outside ABS` reads **58**, and the invariant's right-hand side is `(271 − 271) / 4 = 0`, so it reads
`VIOLATED (58 vs 0)`. Those 58 questions are the bulk of §13.193.3's 63-question loss: the loss is not
"the reader computed the wrong number", it is **58 bare refusals** plus wrong numbers.

#### 13.196.2 The cause, in two call sites

`#answerWithBareRetry` is called from exactly two places — `#prompt` (the flat routes: `flat`,
`knowledge-update`, `assistant`, `abstention`) and `#promptWithDate` (`temporal`). **`answerSessions` does not call
it**: it goes through `#promptSessionAware`, which assembles with `buildSessionPrompt` and consults once. So the
`multi-session` route — the route `MR` is served by — has never had the bare-decline retry at all.

Why this was invisible for the whole campaign: on the registered configuration MR's declines are **prose** (7 of
them on `41185512391`, and `isBareDecline` is false for prose), so the absent mechanism had nothing to fire on. The
gap arm's vague block changed the *shape* of the decline, not just its frequency: 58 MR questions answered with the
bare token, and the one mechanism built for that shape was not on that route.

The two facts had been recorded separately and never joined: §13.111's census argues about bare declines on four
routes, and §13.141's per-question `recoveryAttempted` fields cover the *other* pass. Nothing anywhere said which
routes the bare retry reached, and the artifact carries no per-question flag for it — `promptVariants: 1` on all 58
is what a route with no retry looks like from outside.

#### 13.196.3 What it would be worth, stated as the two populations

| configuration | MR bare declines | what a retry on the session route would attempt |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `41185512391` (registered, `operands`) | 0 | **0** |
| `41188431321` (`operand-gap`) | 58 | 58 |
| any terse reader | unknown | the whole MR decline population |

So on the registered configuration the fix is **free and inert**, which is the cheapest kind of correctness to add:
it changes no published reading. Its value is conditional and now measurable — a reader that declines in the
instruction's own words (the compliance axis, §13.192) declines *bare*, and MR is where the arm is 74%.

#### 13.196.4 Registered: extend the retry to the session route

1. **Implementation.** `#promptSessionAware` gets the same treatment as `#prompt`: if the first consultation
   returned no answer and the raw output is a bare decline, rebuild with `buildRetryPrompt(question,
   assembled.carried, options)` — the same function, the same carried turns, the same census counters. No second
   prompt builder, because a second one is a second place for the retry's instruction block to drift.
2. **The invariant then becomes true** rather than scoped: after the change, a non-`ABS` bare final can only
   survive a retry that ran and declined again, which is what `(attempted − answered) / runs` counts. The
   instrument needs no change and `41188431321` stays readable as an artifact of the pre-fix build.
3. **Predictions.** (a) On `41185512391`'s configuration the census is **unchanged** — 0 new attempts, and a
   re-read of that artifact still holds the invariant at `0 vs 0`. (b) On the `operand-gap` configuration the
   session route attempts **≥ 50** and converts a measurable number; re-running it is not worth a dispatch, so
   this is a prediction about a build rather than a run. (c) Under a terse reader MR's declines are bare, so this
   becomes the mechanism that keeps a compliance gain from being spent on refusals.
4. **Falsified if** the session route's retry changes a published reading at the registered configuration — that
   would mean MR's declines are not all prose after all, and §13.111's population needs re-reading.

#### 13.196.5 Landed, and why the registered configuration cannot feel it

The retry is on `#promptSessionAware` now, after the recovery pass and only where that pass did not fire, using the
same `buildRetryPrompt` and the same two census counters. `session-bare-retry.test.ts` (7 tests) asserts the four
things the flat-route version asserts — one extra consultation on a bare decline, the token withheld from the retry
prompt, `{attempted: 1, answered: 0}` when the retry declines again, and nothing at all when the option is off — plus
the two route-specific ones: a **prose** reply is left alone (`parseAnswer` keeps it, which is why `isBareDecline`
and not "parsed to null" is the predicate), and `reviewPass: 'recover'` + a bare decline produces
`recoveryCensus {0, 0}` with `bareRetryCensus {1, 1}`, i.e. the two passes do not overlap.

At the registered configuration the change is inert **by construction rather than by luck**: `41185512391` has
**0** bare `MR` finals, so `isBareDecline` is false on every one of its 121 `MR` questions and the new branch is
never entered. That is also why the composite dispatch of §13.194.4 is pinned to the ref before this commit: the
registration claims one variable, and a build that adds a retry — even one predicted to be inert — is a second.

### 13.197 The compliant reader buys `TR` four questions and sells `IE` sixteen

`41196814139` (`thinking: enabled`) arrived at **188/220 (85.45%)** against `41196801892`'s **196/220 (89.09%)**.
Both arms ran the same 220 questions, the same prompts, the same reader model, and one repetition each; the only
difference in `memoryArmConfig` is `thinking`.

#### 13.197.1 The six predictions, one by one

| # | prediction | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | amended gate: `MR` prose tail `5/32` → **≤ 2/32** | **2 of 32** | **holds** |
| 1b | amended gate: `TR` median `627.5` → **≤ 400** | **133.5** | **holds** |
| 2 | `MR` **≥ +6** | 23 → **24** (**+1**) | **falsified** |
| 3 | `TR` **≥ +4** | 27 → **31** (**+4**) | **holds, exactly** |
| 4 | `IE` **≥ −3** | 88 → **74** (**−14**) | **falsified, by 11** |
| 5 | `ABS` keeps every point | 29 → **28** (**−1**) | **falsified by one** |
| 6 | `bareRetry` → 0 | 17 → **5** attempts, prose share 19.0% → **0.0%** | **holds** |

Per capability, with the two directions separated:

| capability | disabled | enabled | Δ | questions lost | questions gained |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **IE** | **88 / 94** | **74 / 94** | **−14** | 16 | 2 |
| MR | 23 / 32 | 24 / 32 | +1 | 3 | 4 |
| KU | 29 / 32 | **31 / 32** | **+2** | 1 | 3 |
| **TR** | 27 / 32 | **31 / 32** | **+4** | **0** | **4** |
| ABS | 29 / 30 | 28 / 30 | −1 | 2 | 1 |
| roster | **196 / 220** | **188 / 220** | **−8** | **22** | **14** |

#### 13.197.2 What the pair says, and it is not "the reader axis is closed"

The registered decision rule (§13.192.9) had three branches: gate fails → no 500-question run; gate holds and
signal holds → 500-question confirmation; **gate holds and signal fails → compliance is not what the roster is
missing**. The reading is the fourth state the rule did not enumerate: **the gate holds, one signal holds exactly,
the other two move in opposite directions with large effects.** `TR` gained 4 questions with **zero losses**, `KU`
gained 2 net, `MR` gained 1 — and `IE` lost **16 while gaining 2**.

That is not noise, and the roster total cannot see it: 22 lost and 14 gained is a McNemar exact two-sided
**p = 0.243**, i.e. the −8 is inside what 36 discordant questions can do by chance. **The aggregate is the one
statistic on this page that says nothing.** The per-capability moves are 14 and 16 on samples of 94, and `TR`'s
movement is 4 questions with no loss at all.

Prediction 4 named this branch in advance — *"that outcome would mean the axis trades one capability for another
rather than adding"* — and the trade is legible in the mechanism: `temporal` and `multi-session` close with *"reply
with the Step 2 number alone"*, so a reader that obeys gives the number and TR's judge is satisfied. `IE`'s block
does not close that way, its answers are legitimately paragraphs, and a reader that has learned to answer tersely
answers `IE` tersely: its median falls 34.5 → 28.5, its >40 tail 46 → 40, and sixteen of its ninety-four questions
stop being right.

The `ABS` loss is the same mechanism from the other side: `6456829e_abs` converts to a decline (**gained**, and it
is the question §13.193 was built for), while `a96c20ee_abs` and `09ba9854_abs` stop declining and lose.

#### 13.197.3 Registered: the reader is a route-scoped knob, and it is the next increment

The measurement names its own treatment. Every capability is served by one route, and the two routes that gained are
exactly the two whose block ends with the answer instruction:

1. **Configuration.** `thinking` becomes route-scoped the way `maxTurnChars` already is
   (`maxTurnCharsRoutes=multi-session,temporal`, §13.76): enabled on `temporal` and `multi-session`, disabled on
   `flat`, `knowledge-update`, `assistant` and `abstention`. Absent means today's behaviour, so every archived
   artifact keeps its meaning.
2. **Predicted reading at 220 questions.** `TR` 31 and `MR` 24 (the enabled arm's numbers), `KU` and `IE` at the
   disabled arm's (29 and 88), `ABS` 29 — roster **201/220 (91.36%)**, a **+5** over the better of the two arms and
   **+13** over the enabled one. Stated as counts of the same 220 questions, not as a share of 500.
3. **Falsified if** `IE` does not return to 88 ± 2 — which would mean IE's loss was not the reader's terseness but
   something the reader did to the *flat route's* prompt, and the route-scoped knob is addressing the wrong layer.
4. **Why this is a product increment and not another experiment.** `thinking` is a switch on one reader, and this
   campaign has now measured both of its states on the same questions. A route-scoped knob is what a product ships
   after that measurement; a fifth 220-question probe would be measuring the same two states a third time.

#### 13.197.4 The knob cannot have its own input, so it lives in `thinking`'s value

The workflow declares **24** dispatch inputs and GitHub's ceiling is 25 — the same wall that moved `budgetMinutes`
into a constant (§13.30 / §13.115). A `cortex_memory_thinking_routes` input is therefore not available, and §13.188
already established the pattern for this: when the input surface is full, the new state goes **inside the value that
already exists**, and the grammar makes the invalid combinations unrepresentable.

So `thinking` becomes `disabled` (shipped), `enabled` (every route, which is what the pair of §13.197 ran), or a
route list — `multi-session+temporal` — which is enabled on those routes and disabled on the rest. The artifact's
reader line has to render it (`thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal`), because a reader identity that said only
`enabled` would describe a configuration the run did not administer, which is the `40698883428` failure on a new axis.

The product side of the same change is already in place: `CortexMemoryOptions.readerByRoute` accepts a reader per
route, the arm constructs the two clients and maps them, and `#readerFor` falls back to `llm` for every route the map
does not name. `reader-by-route.test.ts` (5 tests) asserts the route decides, the retry goes to the same reader as the
first pass, the abstention route can be mapped independently, and that an absent map is one reader for every route —
which is every archived artifact.

### 13.198 The knob is dispatchable, and it took no input to become so

§13.197.3 registered the treatment and §13.197.4 recorded the constraint it has to be built under: **24 of 25
dispatch inputs are spent**, so a `cortex_memory_thinking_routes` input does not exist and the state has to live
inside the value that already does. This section is the landing. It is a **product increment**, not a fifth probe,
and that distinction is the reason it was built rather than dispatched: the campaign has now measured both states of
`thinking` on the same 220 questions, so another run of the same two states would be the third measurement of a
two-valued switch.

#### 13.198.1 The grammar, and the three values it refuses

`DEEPSEEK_THINKING` keeps both words it ever had and gains one form:

| value | reach | readers built | artifact line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `''` (unfilled), `disabled`, `off`, `false` | every route, `disabled` | one | `/thinking=disabled` |
| `enabled`, `on`, `true` | every route, `enabled` | one | `/thinking=enabled` |
| `multi-session+temporal` (any non-empty route list) | **those** routes `enabled`, the rest `disabled` | two: the base at `disabled`, one scoped client shared by the named routes | `/thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal` |

A route list can only ever spell `enabled`. The grammar has **no form for "disabled on these, enabled elsewhere"**,
deliberately: the state that exists is the one §13.197 measured a reason for (thinking on the two routes whose block
closes with the answer instruction, off on the four that do not), and a grammar that could express the other
direction would be a way to dispatch a combination no registration names. Adding it when it is measured is one line;
un-dispatching a run is not possible at all.

Three values are refused, and each refusal was written for a mistake an operator will actually make rather than for
symmetry:

| refused | why it is the likely mistake | what the message says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a name that is not a route (`multi-session+multi-sesion`) | a run that enabled thinking on five of six routes with the sixth misspelled produces numbers consistent with six | names the offending token, and all six valid names |
| `multi-session,temporal` | the sibling reach inputs (`cortex_memory_max_turn_chars_routes`, `cortex_memory_evidence_roles_routes`) are comma-separated, so a comma is the likeliest transcription | says the separator is `+`, and that a value silently read as one route would run the treatment on a sixth of the questions it was dispatched for |
| `all` | the same two inputs use `all` for "every route", so it is the first word anyone reaches for | says every route is spelled `enabled`, and why: `all` names a reach without naming a mode |

Empty segments (`multi-session+`, `+temporal`, `a++b`) and a route named twice are refused on the same principle as
the caps' reach: dropping a segment would run the treatment on fewer routes than the value names, and printing a
duplicated route back into the artifact would make the record claim a list the run did not have.

#### 13.198.2 The base reader is `disabled`, and that is the whole treatment

The map is built on a **disabled** base, always. The four routes a route list does not name are exactly the ones that
lost nothing under `enabled` — and `IE`, which lost sixteen. A pair that built the base at `enabled` and then mapped
two routes to `enabled` would administer the treatment to all six while the artifact reported two, which is the
`thinking: enabled` arm again under a new name.

The same reasoning produces a refusal rather than a fallback in the single-reader factory. `createLlmFromEnv` now
**throws** on a route list, because its contract is one reader for every route and the only ways to honour a list
would be to pick a mode for the caller. A silent `disabled` there would let a dispatch run with the base reader while
`resolveReaderIdentity` went on naming `enabled on multi-session+temporal` — an artifact describing a configuration
the run did not administer, which is the `40698883428` failure (§13.110) on a new axis.

One client serves every named route, not one per route: two clients would be two connection pools and two usage
counters for one treatment, and the artifact's usage block would be a sum of parts that never existed.

#### 13.198.3 What is asserted, and why two of the tests read a socket

`thinking-reach.test.ts` (18 tests) covers the grammar, the identity, and the pair:

- the three refusals above, each asserting the message's *reasons* — the offender, the separator, the six names —
  because a dispatch is not repeatable for free and a message that does not state the offending input sends the
  operator back to a job log that expires;
- the reach's **order** is the operator's, not sorted: the artifact prints the value back, and a canonicalisation is
  a different claim from a record;
- every one of the six routes is accepted on its own, and the list of six is asserted against this copy — a route
  added to the product's union but missing here would be a route the arm cannot scope thinking to, silently;
- `createReadersFromEnv` builds **one** reader when the value names no routes (every archived artifact), and exactly
  two objects when it does, with the map's two entries **the same object** and the base a different one.

The last two assertions are structural, and structure is not the property the treatment depends on: a pair that
swapped base and scoped client would satisfy every one of them and buy `IE`'s sixteen questions back for nothing. So
the two clients are driven against a local HTTP server and their request bodies read: `thinking` is
`{type: 'disabled'}` on the base and `{type: 'enabled'}` on the mapped route, and a pinned `TEMPERATURE` appears on
**both** bodies — the second construction site is exactly where the temperature wrapper would be lost (§13.119).

`reader-identity.test.ts` gains three assertions rather than a file: the identity carries `thinkingRoutes: undefined`
for both shipped words (absent, not `[]`, so archived renderings stay byte-identical), a route-scoped identity renders
`/thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal/temp=default`, and an empty reach — which the parser cannot produce but a
replayed artifact could carry — renders as the plain mode instead of a trailing `on `.

The export ledger moved by two (`ThinkingReach`, `readThinkingReach`), both in `eval-harness-surface`, for the reason
`resolveTimeoutMs` is already there: a name a test imports is legitimately exported, and a barrel re-export is not a
caller the census follows.

**One defect found while moving the table, and it was not new.** `TURN_CAP_ROUTES` is an object literal, so
`name in TURN_CAP_ROUTES` is true for every inherited member as well as for the six routes. In `readRouteReach` the
effect was the silent five-of-six application its own message argues against: `toString` passed the check and was then
dropped by `ALL_TURN_CAP_ROUTES.filter(...)`, so a dispatch spelling it would have applied a cap to five routes while the
artifact recorded six. The new grammar had the same hole and would have built a map whose only entry is a key the
product can never ask for, printing `thinking=enabled on toString` as the treatment administered. Both sides now use
`Object.hasOwn`, both are tested with the four names a reviewer reaches for first, and the reach test sits beside the
rejection it belongs to rather than in a file of its own.

#### 13.198.4 What this does not do, and what the first dispatch of it will test

**No run accompanies this section.** The prediction §13.197.3 fixed is unchanged and still untouched by any
measurement:

| capability | disabled arm | enabled arm | registered prediction | rule |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `TR` | 27 | 31 | **31** | the four gained, none lost — the whole reason for the knob |
| `MR` | 23 | 24 | **24** | +1 under `enabled`; kept |
| `KU` | 29 | 31 | **29** | +2 under `enabled` was *not* predicted and is not claimed |
| `IE` | **88** | 74 | **88** | falsified if it does not return to **88 ± 2**: that would mean IE's loss was not the reader's terseness but something done to the `flat` route's prompt, and the knob is addressing the wrong layer |
| `ABS` | 29 | 28 | **29** | −1 under `enabled`; the question `6456829e_abs` that converted is the one §13.193 was built for |
| roster | 196 | 188 | **201 / 220 (91.36%)** | +5 over the better arm, +13 over the enabled one |

**Cost.** The scoped reader touches **64 of the 220 questions** (`multi-session` 32 and `temporal` 32) and only on the
feature side, because the baseline keeps `llm`. That is what makes the knob a *product* answer to the 3.58× wall clock
`§13.197` priced for the whole-run switch: it buys the two routes the measurement named and leaves the other 158
questions at the shipped reader. The artifact's `llmUsage` / `usageDelta` block puts the token bill beside the accuracy
it bought, so this run is also the first time the knob has a price rather than a wall-clock estimate.

One property of the §13.197 pair matters for how that prediction is read and was not stated there. **Both** sides of
the 220-question pair ran with `thinking: enabled` — `run-ablation.ts` builds the reference pipeline from the same
`createLlmFromEnv` — so in the enabled arm the *baseline* moved too. The feature side's per-capability counts are
attributable to the feature side alone (the two sides share no answer cache: `answerCache` is
`NaturalLanguageMemorySystem`'s, and `CortexMemory` is not given one), which is what makes the table above a
statement about the treatment. But the aggregate `196 → 188` is **not** a feature-versus-baseline delta of the shipped
configuration, and the route-scoped run is the first one in which the baseline returns to the shipped reader while
the feature side carries the treatment. That is the configuration a product ships; it is also the first dispatch that
can read the knob's own claim.

### 13.199 The first dispatch of the knob: one value against `41196801892`

§13.198 built the reach and §13.197.3 fixed what it should read. This section is the dispatch record, written before the
run so the reading cannot be chosen after the numbers arrive.

#### 13.199.1 The pair, and why it is that pair

The comparison is **`41196801892`** — the `thinking: disabled` arm of the §13.197 pair — and not the shipped 500-question
baseline. Three reasons, and the third is the one that decides it:

1. It is the same **220 questions**, so the prediction is stated in counts of the same population rather than as a share
   of a different one.
2. It is the same **configuration**: `maxPromptChars 96000`, `400:ellipsis`, `maxTurnCharsRoutes
   multi-session,temporal`, `temperature 0`, one repetition. Nothing but the reader value moves.
3. `IE`'s falsification rule is `88 ± 2` on **94 questions**. A 500-question run answers the roster question better and
   this question worse, because `IE` is 94 of 220 there and 150 of 500 — and the falsification is the part of this
   registration that can go wrong.

#### 13.199.2 The inputs, and the one value that differs

| input | `41196801892` (control) | this dispatch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thinking` | `disabled` | **`multi-session+temporal`** |
| `limit` | `220` | `220` |
| `ablation_runs` | `1` | `1` |
| `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` | `96000` | `96000` |
| `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars` | `400:ellipsis` | `400:ellipsis` |
| `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars_routes` | `multi-session,temporal` | same |
| `temperature` | `0` | `0` |
| `model` | `deepseek-chat` | same |
| everything else | the dispatch table's registered values | identical, unset overrides |

#### 13.199.3 What it must read, and what fails it

| # | prediction | fails if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **`TR` ≥ 30** — the four `enabled` gained, minus at most one question of same-prompt noise (`§13.194` measured that noise at ≥ 1 question on identical prompts) | `TR` ≤ 27, which is the control's own number: the gain did not happen |
| 2 | **`IE` ∈ [86, 90]** — the registered `88 ± 2` | outside the band: the loss was not the reader's terseness and the knob is at the wrong layer |
| 3 | `MR` ∈ [22, 26] | outside: the composite's own axis interacted, and neither is attributable |
| 4 | `KU` ∈ [28, 30], `ABS` ∈ [28, 30] | outside: the scoped reader reached routes it was not mapped to |
| 5 | **roster ≥ 197** — the `enabled` arm read 188, the disabled arm 196, and the registered prediction is 201 | ≤ 196: the knob bought nothing over the shipped reader |

Predictions 1 and 2 are the treatment's own claim and are **separate claims**: a run can satisfy one and fail the other,
and which one failed says which mechanism was wrong (§13.197.2's trade, or the route mapping).

#### 13.199.4 Three wire-level readings, which are not accuracy and are not negotiable

Accuracy can be reinterpreted; a wiring can only be right or wrong. The artifact and the log must show:

1. `memoryArmConfig.reader` carries `thinking: "enabled"` **and** `thinkingRoutes: ["multi-session", "temporal"]`. A
   record saying only `enabled` is the `40698883428` failure — an artifact describing a configuration the run did not
   administer.
2. The rendered config line contains `thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal`, because that is the line a reader of
   the Markdown sees.
3. The job log contains `Route-scoped reader: multi-session,temporal` before the first question — the pair was built, not
   merely parsed.

**And one invariant that has no tolerance:** every prompt in this run must be **byte-identical** to `41196801892`'s for
the same question. `thinking` is not an input to the prompt builder, so any prompt that moved means the wiring changed
something outside the reader — and then the roster delta is not the reader's. `tools/window-pair.mjs` reads exactly this
(`digest-equal` per capability, and the count of pairs whose prompt changed bytes at the same length).

#### 13.199.5 Why this is not the "third measurement of a two-valued switch"

Because it is not one of the two states. `disabled` and `enabled` were measured; **`enabled on two of six routes with a
disabled base** was not, and it is the only state a product can ship: it is the one that keeps the four routes that lost
nothing on the reader every archived number was produced with. A run of `enabled` again would be the third reading of the
same state, and §13.198.4 refuses it for that reason.

### 13.200 The composite arm ran at the registered budget, which is why it cannot be read

`41203245999` completed `success` in **2h04m** and its artifact says:

```
Memory arm config: maxTurnChars=400, maxPromptChars=48000, turnCutMarker=none, …
Evidence ask: operands+operand-gap
Evidence ask reached: 4 route(s) — multi-session, flat, temporal, abstention
```

Its control, `41185512391`, says `maxPromptChars=96000`, `turnCutMarker=ellipsis`, `ask=operands`. **Two fields differ
between the run and the control the prediction was pinned to**, so §13.194.4's six readings are **not read**. They are
not falsified either: nothing here tests them.

This is the `P1-budget-drift` defect (§13.192.7.3) materialising as a lost run rather than as a bookkeeping note. The
dispatch table sends `48000` and a bare `400`, because that is what §10.3 registers; every arm run since `41144910162`
has overridden both with `--set`. The composite dispatch did not, so it ran the configuration the document names — which
is, by the document's own account, **not** the configuration the campaign has been reading.

#### 13.200.1 The four arms, side by side, which is the reading this run does support

Four 500-question, four-repetition artifacts now differ in exactly one of three fields each. Per repetition, feature
side, from `tools/paired-flip.mjs`:

| run | ask | room | marker | `ABS` | `IE` | `KU` | `MR` | `TR` | roster mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `41159983913` | `operands` | 96,000 | none | 29 ×4 | 141/143/144/144 (**143.00**) | 60/59/61/61 (**60.25**) | 84/86/87/92 (**87.25**) | 105/100/104/101 (**102.50**) | **422.00** |
| `41185512391` | `operands` | 96,000 | `ellipsis` | 29 ×4 | 143/143/145/146 (**144.25**) | 61 ×4 (**61.00**) | 91/90/90/88 (**89.75**) | 102/106/103/106 (**104.25**) | **428.25** |
| `41188431321` | `operand-gap` | 96,000 | `ellipsis` | **30 ×4** | 142/141/142/140 (**141.25**) | 61/61/62/62 (**61.50**) | 42/41/40/41 (**41.00**) | 91/93/93/93 (**92.50**) | **366.25** |
| `41203245999` | `operands+operand-gap` | **48,000** | **none** | **30 ×4** | 143/140/142/143 (**142.00**) | 62/64/62/63 (**62.75**) | 92/82/86/88 (**87.00**) | 98/100/100/101 (**99.75**) | **421.50** |

Three readings come out of this table and none of them is §13.194's.

**1. The abstention gate is real at both budgets.** `ABS` reads **30/30/30/30** in the two runs whose ask carries
`operand-gap` and **29/29/29/29** in the two whose ask does not. The marker differs across those pairs, the room
differs across them, and the abstention count does not: the rule that converts fourteen of the fifteen declines into
`30/30` is doing the work, not the room. This is the one prediction of §13.194.4 that the run supports, and it
supports it against a changed budget rather than within one.

**2. Naming `operand-gap` for every route costs 62 questions, and the composite recovers all but ~7 of them.** Rows 2
and 3 are the same run configuration with one value changed: `428.25 → 366.25`. Row 4 is the composition, at a *smaller*
room and *without* the marker, and it reads `421.50`. The gap to row 2 (`−6.75`) is the same order as the two effects
that separate those rows and is not attributable without the re-run below.

**3. The `ellipsis` marker is worth about six questions and has never been measured.** Rows 1 and 2 differ in nothing
else, and read `422.00 → 428.25` (**+6.25**), with per-run rosters `419/417/425/427 → 426/429/428/430`. The two
distributions overlap on one value, so this is a **candidate finding, not an established one** — §13.175.5 priced two
dispatches of one payload at ±2.2 points, and this difference is 1.25. It is recorded because §13.188 adopted the
marker on a mechanism argument and this is the first 500-question pair that could price it at all.

#### 13.200.2 What the composite run does establish on its own

- **The ask reaches the four routes it was designed for at 500 questions**, and `promptContract`,
  `relevanceSignal`, `relevanceTopK`, `reviewPass` and the reader are byte-identical to the control's. The wiring half
  of §13.193.5 is confirmed at full N, not only in the unit test.
- **`bareRetry` reads 90 attempted, 90 answered, 100% converted**, against the control's **111 / 111 / 100%**. The
  conversion rate is therefore not the quantity that moves — it is 100% whenever the retry fires — and the reading
  that matters is the count of bare declines, which fell 111 → 90. That is consistent with §13.196 and is the first
  500-question confirmation of it.
- **Cost**: 5,624 calls, 31,326,218 prompt tokens, **80.40%** of them served from the prefix cache; the feature side
  spends 28,404,559 prompt tokens across 2,090 calls. This is the number the next dispatch is compared against.

#### 13.200.3 Registered: re-dispatch the composite at the control's configuration

The prediction is not restated; it is the one §13.194.4 already fixed. What changes is that the run must carry the two
overrides its control carried, and the record must say so before it runs:

```
python3 tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py \
  --set cortex_memory_ask=operands+operand-gap \
  --set cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars=96000 \
  --set cortex_memory_max_turn_chars=400:ellipsis
```

| field | control `41185512391` | this dispatch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cortex_memory_ask` | `operands` | **`operands+operand-gap`** |
| `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` | `96000` | `96000` |
| `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars` | `400:ellipsis` | `400:ellipsis` |
| `limit` / `ablation_runs` | 0 (= 500) / 4 | same |
| everything else | dispatch table | identical |

The six readings and their failure conditions are §13.194.4's, unchanged: `ABS` 30 in all four runs; `MR` in
`[87, 92]`; `TR` in `[99, 108]` and `IE` in `[140, 148]`; `KU` in `{61, 62}`; roster per run = the control's plus one
(`427, 430, 429, 431`, mean 429.25, band `[425, 433]`); and the mandatory `window-pair` digest check (`MR` 121/121,
`IE` 150/150, `TR` 127/127, `KU` 72/72 equal; `ABS` 30/30 different).

#### 13.200.4 The budget question this exposed, and the decision not taken here

Two facts now sit side by side and neither is a reading: the registration says **48,000 with no marker**, and the last
five arm runs say **96,000 with `ellipsis`**. §13.118.6 rejected 96,000 as a wash — a citation this section got
**wrong** on first writing, naming §13.177.5, which is `admission.ts`'s turn-id derivation and says nothing about the
budget; §13.202.1 corrects it — and §13.139 withdrew part of §13.118's mechanism. So the
campaign is running a configuration its own document rejected, and every cross-run comparison it makes inherits that.

**No adoption is recorded here.** What this section does is stop the drift from being invisible: a dispatch that omits
the overrides is now known to produce a run that cannot be paired with anything, and §13.192.7.3's first consequence
(*"an override should be recorded in §10.3's own list"*) is therefore not bookkeeping. Resolving it requires either
adopting 96,000 + `ellipsis` by registration or re-baselining the arm at 48,000, and both are product decisions with a
cost measured in runs. It is carried as an open item rather than decided in a section about the ask.

**Resolved by §13.202, which spends no run.** The question was already answered: `40698867439` against
`40722772896` is the one-variable room pair, §13.118.6 read it and declined 96,000, so 48,000 is and remains the
adopted budget. What §13.200.4 found is not an open question but a drift from a decided value, and §13.202.6 records
the drift in §10.3's own list, withdraws the re-run this section implied as already paid, and adds the instrument
that makes the next one visible before it costs two hours.

### 13.201 The knob reads 199/220, and every flip it caused is on a route the map names

`41218182053` (220 questions, one repetition, `thinking=multi-session+temporal`) completed `success` in **37 min**
against the control `41196801892` (17.8 min) and the whole-run `enabled` arm (88.5 min). All four wire readings that
§13.199.4 made non-negotiable were checked before any accuracy number was read.

#### 13.201.1 The four wire readings

| # | what it must show | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `memoryArmConfig.reader` carries the reach | `{"thinking": "enabled", "thinkingRoutes": ["multi-session", "temporal"], "temperature": 0, …}` |
| 2 | the rendered line says so | `reader=deepseek:deepseek-chat@api.deepseek.com/thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal/temp=0` |
| 3 | the pair was built, before question 1 | job log `16:08:51.862` — `Route-scoped reader: multi-session,temporal` |
| 4 | **every prompt byte-identical to the control** | `window-pair`: **220 digest-equal, 0 digest-differs, 0 unmeasured**; multiset changes 0, order changes 0 |

Reading 4 is the one that makes the rest interpretable. `thinking` is not an input to the prompt builder, so identical
prompts are the proof that the wiring changed the reader and nothing else; a prompt that moved would have made every
accuracy delta ambiguous between the reader and the prompt.

#### 13.201.2 The five accuracy readings

| # | criterion | registered | observed | verdict |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `TR` **≥ 30** | 31 | **30** | **holds** — control 27, so **+3** |
| 2 | `IE` **∈ [86, 90]** | 88 | **86** | **holds, at the lower edge** — control 88 |
| 3 | `MR` **∈ [22, 26]** | 24 | **25** | **holds** — control 23, so **+2** |
| 4 | `KU` **∈ [28, 30]**, `ABS` **∈ [28, 30]** | 29 / 29 | **29 / 29** | **holds** — both unchanged from the control |
| 5 | roster **≥ 197** | 201 | **199** | **holds** — control 196, so **+3** |

**The falsification did not fire.** §13.197.3 said a run in which `IE` does not return to `88 ± 2` would mean the
sixteen-question loss was not the reader's terseness and the knob was addressing the wrong layer. `IE` reads **86**,
which is inside the band and exactly on its edge. Sixteen questions came back as fourteen; the two that did not are on
a route the map does not touch and are discussed below.

The point prediction of 201 was **two high**, and the shortfall is legible in its components: `TR` −1, `IE` −2, `MR` +1.
The `IE` component is the informative one — those two questions are on the **unmapped** `flat` route, whose reader is
byte-identically the control's, and the prompts are identical, so the movement is the same-prompt noise floor that
§13.194 measured at ≥ 1 question on two runs of one configuration. A point prediction inside one question per capability
is not a claim this instrument can settle.

#### 13.201.3 Where the flips are, which is the stronger statistic than the net

`window-pair` reports **15 flips of 220** between the control's feature side and this run's, and their location is the
mechanism:

| capability | route mapped? | questions | flips | net |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | **yes** (`multi-session`) | 32 | **8** | **+2** |
| `TR` | **yes** (`temporal`) | 32 | **3** | **+3** |
| `IE` | no (`flat`) | 94 | 4 | −2 |
| `KU` | no (`knowledge-update`) | 32 | 0 | 0 |
| `ABS` | no (`abstention`) | 30 | 0 | 0 |

**11 of the 15 flips are on the 64 questions the map names.** Under a null in which a flip is equally likely on any
question, the probability of 11 or more of 15 landing in those 64 is **p ≈ 0.0005**. The net movement, by contrast, is
9 gained against 6 lost — a McNemar exact **p = 0.607**, i.e. **the count is not significant at this N and the location
is**. That is the correct reading of a 220-question run: an effect that concentrates where the treatment is applied is
evidence about the mechanism, and an aggregate of +3 on 220 questions is not evidence about the size.

Two routes with zero flips matter as much: `KU` and `ABS` did not move at all, which is what a map that does not name
them predicts and what a leak would have contradicted.

#### 13.201.4 What the knob costs, now measured rather than estimated

| arm | questions | calls | prompt tokens | completion tokens | cache-hit prompt | wall clock |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `disabled` (`41196801892`) | 220 | 865 | 6,327,996 | **44,668** | 6,160,303 | 17.8 min |
| **route-scoped** (`41218182053`) | 220 | 853 | 6,322,029 | **244,885** | 6,158,016 | **37 min** |
| `enabled` (`41196814139`) | 220 | 882 | 6,107,551 | **767,066** | 211,584 | 88.5 min |

Thinking is billed as completion, so the prompt column is flat across the three arms and the whole cost sits in the
completion column: the scoped arm spends **5.5×** the disabled arm's completion tokens and **32%** of the enabled arm's.
That is the answer to "what does the knob cost" in tokens rather than in wall clock — **68% of the whole-run thinking
bill is avoided while keeping the movement** — and it is the first price this switch has had that is not a stopwatch.

#### 13.201.5 What this licenses and what it does not

**Licensed:** `thinking=multi-session+temporal` is a measured configuration. Its mechanism is where the map says it is
(p ≈ 0.0005 on location), its damage is bounded (`IE` at the band's edge, `KU` and `ABS` untouched), and its cost is
known in tokens.

**Not licensed:** adopting it as the arm's default. That needs a 500-question reading against `41185512391` at the same
configuration, and it needs the budget question of §13.200.4 settled first — a 220-question, one-repetition run cannot
distinguish a +3 from a +0. And §13.197.2's trade is now *priced* rather than removed: the knob converts "TR +4 for
IE −16" into "TR +3 for IE −2", which is what a route-scoped switch is for, and it is still a trade.

**The budget question is settled by §13.202, and it unblocks this dispatch without naming a new one.** 48,000 is the
adopted budget (§13.118.6) and 96,000 is an experiment value, so the 500-question reader reading runs at **96,000 +
`ellipsis` pinned to `41185512391`** — the room is identical on both sides, which is what a reader experiment needs, and
under §13.202.6's rule it registers as an experiment that names its control rather than as a claim about the shipping
configuration. The `--config --treatment thinking` check comes before the numbers.

### 13.202 The room was decided before this section; what is new is an instrument, a bill decomposition, and a wrong citation

**Registered 2026-10-31, as an instrument and a correction, not as a dispatch.** Instrument:
`tools/readout-arm-run.py --config` (`diff_section`, `DISPATCH_FIELD_ALIASES`, `RUNTIME_CONFIG_FIELDS`),
`tools/__tests__/test_config_diff.py` (17). The measurement reads two artifacts already on disk —
`41203245999` (`maxPromptChars 48000`, `turnCutMarker none`, `ask operands+operand-gap`, mean **421.50**) and
`41185512391` (`96000`, `ellipsis`, `operands`, mean **428.25**) — and spends no run.

#### 13.202.1 §13.200.4 asked a question that was answered eighty sections earlier

§13.200.4 closed with: *"Resolving it requires either adopting 96,000 + `ellipsis` by registration or
re-baselining the arm at 48,000, and both are product decisions with a cost measured in runs."* The first half of
that sentence is false, and the campaign paid for the answer already.

`40698867439` (48,000) and `40722772896` (96,000) are a **one-variable pair**: §13.118 registered
`cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` as the only input it moved, at the same commit series. §13.118.2–.6 read it:

| statistic | 48,000 (`40698867439`) | 96,000 (`40722772896`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| roster (repetition 1 / mean of 4) | 417 | 418.00 |
| questions with **complete** gold coverage | **256** / 500 | **371** / 500 |
| mean gold coverage, `MR` / `TR` | 96.6% / 95.4% | **100.0% / 100.0%** |
| evidence as a share of the room, `MR` / `TR` | 96.2% / 98.2% | 69.9% / 69.3% |
| prompt-evidence chars, median | 46,851.5 | 92,078.5 |

§13.118.6's decision is **"Not adopted."** 48,000 remained the adopted budget, §13.82 remains its justification,
and the stated costs were 2× prompt tokens and 2.87× wall clock.

So the value the last five runs have been using was **declined by registration**, on the cleanest pair this arm
has ever produced, and §13.200.4 mistook the drift for an open question. What is genuinely open is the second
half: why five consecutive runs carry a rejected value, and what reading is legitimate in the meantime.

**One citation in §13.200.4 is wrong and is corrected here.** It reads *"§13.177.5 declined to adopt it after a
six-criterion run in which accuracy and damage failed"*. §13.177.5 is `admission.ts`'s turn-id derivation — four
FNV-1a streams, the version-8 nibble, the signed-int32 bug. The section that declined 96,000 is **§13.118.6**,
and the correction matters because §13.177.5 makes no claim about the budget at all: a reader following that
pointer would find a hash function and conclude the citation had been checked when it had not.

#### 13.202.2 What §13.118 could not see: the room is an allocation, not a clamp

§13.118 measured the median prompt length. The overlap between the two distributions is the quantity that says
*how many questions the room leaves alone*, and it was not printed.

| | 48,000 | 96,000 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `promptChars` min | 37,735 | **58,917** |
| `promptChars` median | 46,834 | 92,143 |
| `promptChars` p90 | 47,299 | 95,317 |
| `promptChars` max | 47,558 | 95,589 |
| largest prompt, as a share of its ceiling | 99.1% | 99.6% |
| questions at ≥ 97% of their own ceiling | 300 / 500 | 240 / 500 |

Every one of the 500 questions carries a prompt **above 48,000** at the larger room, so the set of questions on
which the two configurations build the same prompt is **empty**. `maxPromptChars` is not a cut that fires on the
long tail; it is the **allocation**, and doubling it re-deals the evidence on all five hundred questions. That is
consistent with §6.1.7's finding at 48,000 ("没有一道题把房间留空") and it is the stronger statement: not "the
room is spent", but "no question is unaffected by the room".

#### 13.202.3 The gold the room buys, cut by whether the delivery changed at all

The 500 questions split by whether the extra room actually put more gold turns in front of the reader:

| stratum | questions | correct at 48,000 | correct at 96,000 | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **gold turns gained** | **225** | **188** (83.6%) | **188** (83.6%) | **+0** |
| gold turns unchanged | 275 | 237 (86.2%) | 238 (86.5%) | +1 |

Turn-level recall over all five hundred: **86.5%** (6,501/7,516) → **93.7%** (7,044/7,516), i.e. +7.2 points, and
the complete-coverage count reproduces §13.118's **256 → 371** exactly — two independent pairs, different asks,
different dates, the same two numbers. That replication is what makes the coverage column a property of the room
rather than of a run.

Two hundred and twenty-five questions received strictly more gold evidence and **not one changed its verdict in
either direction**. §6.1.7's partition (by control-side coverage: 256 lost 8, 244 gained 9, net +1) and this one
(by delivery: 225 +0, 275 +1) are different cuts of the same 500, and they agree on sign and size: **the room buys
coverage, not answers.**

**What this does not claim.** The two runs differ in `ask` as well, so the zero on that stratum is the joint
effect of the room and of `operands` → `operands+operand-gap` on exactly the 225 questions where the room did
something. It is offered as a replication of a **clean** pair, not as a substitute for one — and the clean pair is
§13.202.1's.

#### 13.202.4 The bill, decomposed — which revises one half of §13.118.6's cost sentence

| | 48,000 (`41203245999`) | 96,000 (`41185512391`) | ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| calls | 5,624 | 5,566 | 0.99× |
| prompt tokens | 31,326,218 | 50,581,538 | 1.615× |
| of which served from the prefix cache | 25,186,661 (80.4%) | 44,488,008 (87.9%) | |
| **of which fresh** | **6,139,557** | **6,093,530** | **0.993×** |
| completion tokens | 317,614 | 339,501 | 1.07× |
| **prompt tokens per call** | **5,570** | **9,088** | **1.63×** |

The whole of the +19,255,320 lands in the cached column (+19,301,347, **100.2%** of it) while the fresh column
*falls* by 46,027 (−0.75%).

**That is a property of the harness before it is a property of the product**, and saying so is the difference
between a measurement and a claim: 500 prompts × 4 repetitions share one prefix, so repetitions 2–4 replay
repetition 1, and an aggregate cache share of 80.4% is what a mostly-fresh first pass plus three replayed ones
looks like. A workload that sees each prompt once would pay the increment at the input rate. The number that
survives both readings is the last row: **5,570 → 9,088 prompt tokens per call (+63%)**, which is what a request
costs whether or not anything is cached.

Where the bill goes is §13.189's instrument, and on `41188431321` it splits into exactly two sides plus a 0.50%
residual: the feature arm **94.96%** (51,126,815 prompt tokens over 2,271 calls), the reference pipeline **4.54%**
(2,443,943 over 2,633), and no judge line at all — the scorer is deterministic, so there is no third model to
optimise -- and the room, at 1.6× the whole feature bill, is the largest token lever the harness has.

So §13.118.6's *"2× prompt tokens"* is a **cached-token** statement; the resident price of the room is +63% per
call, not 2×. The other half of that sentence — **2.87× wall clock** — is untouched by any of this, and it is now
the stronger of the two cost arguments. Nothing here reverses the decision: +1 question on 500 for +63% per call
and 2.87× wall clock is a rejection at any cache rate.

#### 13.202.5 The instrument, and the pair it refuses
