`readout-arm-run.py --config CONTROL.json --treatment <fields> RUN.json` flattens both `memoryArmConfig` blocks
to dotted paths, prints every field that differs as `control -> run`, and **exits non-zero when any of them is not
named by `--treatment`**. Run on the pair at the top of this section:

```
  differ   4 field(s):
    declared    ask: "operands" -> "operands+operand-gap"
    declared    askRoutes: ["multi-session", "temporal", "abstention", "knowledge-update"] -> ["multi-session", "flat", "temporal", "abstention"]
    UNDECLARED  maxPromptChars: 96000 -> 48000
    UNDECLARED  turnCutMarker: "ellipsis" -> "none"
  verdict: 4 field(s) differ, 2 declared by --treatment, 2 undeclared: ['maxPromptChars', 'turnCutMarker']
  readings from this pair are not attributable: …
EXIT=1
```

Five decisions in it are refused shapes rather than conveniences:

1. **`400:ellipsis` is one input and two fields.** A treatment naming `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars` clears both
   `maxTurnChars` and `turnCutMarker`; naming only `maxTurnChars` leaves the marker undeclared, and both directions
   are asserted. Without this, every marker run reads as an unregistered pair.
2. **`askRoutes` is a function of `ask`; `turnCutMarker` is not a function of `maxTurnChars`.** The first is
   covered by declaring the ask. The second must be declared, because a derived field and a co-travelling one are
   the difference between a convenience and a silent second variable.
3. **`voteCounts` is a census, not a configuration** (§13.104). Comparing it would fail every legitimately paired
   voting run, which is how a check teaches a reader to skip its output.
4. **`thinking` writes `reader.thinking` and `reader.thinkingRoutes`.** Same shape as the cut marker, found by
   pointing the tool at the artifact the next registered dispatch produces (§13.201.5): a route-scoped reader run
   against a control that predates the field is an absent-vs-present pair, and left one-to-one it would be refused as
   undeclared. Recorded because a mapping table is only verified by a real artifact of each shape it claims to read —
   the lesson §13.192.7.2 paid for with two wrong readings.
5. **A treatment name that resolves to nothing is refused.** A typo would license the pair while naming no field —
   the `--set` defect's shape (§13.192.7.3) applied to the declaration instead of the dispatch.

An absent field prints as `<-absent->` rather than matching `null`, and a missing `memoryArmConfig` is an error
rather than an agreement about nothing.

#### 13.202.6 What this decides, and the dispatch it withdraws

1. **48,000 remains the adopted budget.** §13.118.6 decided it on a one-variable pair; this section adds no
   evidence that reverses it and one number (per-call prompt +63%) that makes the cost argument more precise
   rather than weaker.
2. **The dispatch §13.200.4 implied is withdrawn as already paid.** A one-field room pair was registered there in
   spirit; `40698867439` against `40722772896` **is** that pair, and re-running it would be a third measurement of
   the same two configurations (§13.198.4 refuses exactly that shape).
3. **§10.3 gets the line §13.192.7.3 asked for.** An "as-of" record that runs from `41144910162` through
   `41222844945` carry `maxPromptChars 96000` and `400:ellipsis` by `--set`, so a reader of §10.3 can tell that
   the registration describes the **adoption** while the recent runs describe an **experiment that was declined**.
   The marker has the same status: §13.188 registered it as a treatment and no adoption of it has ever been read.
4. **From the next dispatch, a run at 96,000 must name itself.** Either it registers as an experiment and says which
   control it is pinned to, or it runs at the adopted 48,000. `readout-arm-run.py --config` is the check that the
   field it meant to move is the only field that moved.
5. **The comparison in flight is unaffected.** `41222844945` is pinned to `41185512391`, which is also at 96,000, so
   the pair is internally consistent and its six §13.194.4 readings stand as registered.
6. **What this does not license:** quoting `41203245999`'s 421.50 or `41185512391`'s 428.25 against 48,000-era
   numbers such as 83.40% without naming the budget each side ran. That comparison is the drift wearing a result's
   clothes, and it is the one §13.192.7.1 already refused for `41185512391`.

### 13.203 The composite converts the one question it was written for, and the band that would have hidden it

**Registered 2026-10-31, as a reading, two instruments, and one amendment to §10.3.** The run is
`41222844945` (500 questions, 4 repetitions, `deepseek-chat` at temperature 0, `thinking: disabled`,
`maxPromptChars 96000`, `400:ellipsis`, `ask: operands+operand-gap`) against `41185512391`
(`ask: operands`, everything else identical). The instruments are `readout-arm-run.py --registration`
(one artifact against the dispatch table) and `--null` (one pair's own noise floor), with
`test_registration_diff.py` (27) and `test_pair_null.py` (17).

The pair was checked before it was read, which is §13.202.6's own rule:

```
  same     30 field(s)
  differ   2 field(s):
    declared    ask: "operands" -> "operands+operand-gap"
    declared    askRoutes: [...] -> [..., "abstention"]
  verdict: 2 field(s) differ and every one of them is declared
EXIT=0
```

#### 13.203.1 The six criteria: four hold exactly, one holds inside its band, one fails

| # | registered prediction | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `ABS` **30 in all four** runs | 30, 30, 30, 30 | **holds, exactly** |
| 2 | `MR` in `[87, 92]` per run | 89, 89, 89, 90 | holds (control 91, 90, 90, 88) |
| 3 | `TR` in `[99, 108]`, `IE` in `[140, 148]` | 107, 105, 108, 105 · 144, 144, 143, 140 | holds (`IE` 140 is the lower bound, no margin) |
| 4 | `KU` in `{61, 62}` | **60, 61, 60, 61** | **fails** |
| 5 | roster = control's **plus one** per run (`427, 430, 429, 431`), band `[425, 433]` | 430, 429, 430, 426 (mean **428.75**), deltas `+4, 0, +2, −4` | band holds; **arithmetic fails** |
| 6 | digest identity: `MR` 121/121, `IE` 150/150, `TR` 127/127, `KU` 72/72 equal, `ABS` 30/30 different | 121/121, 150/150, 127/127, 72/72, **0/30** | **holds, exactly** |

| capability | `41185512391` (`operands`) | `41222844945` (composite) | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `IE` | 143/143/145/146 (**144.25**) | 144/144/143/140 (**142.75**) | −1.50 |
| `ABS` | 29 ×4 (**29.00**) | 30 ×4 (**30.00**) | **+1.00** |
| `MR` | 91/90/90/88 (**89.75**) | 89/89/89/90 (**89.25**) | −0.50 |
| `TR` | 102/106/103/106 (**104.25**) | 107/105/108/105 (**106.25**) | +2.00 |
| `KU` | 61 ×4 (**61.00**) | 60/61/60/61 (**60.50**) | −0.50 |
| **roster** | 426/429/428/430 (**428.25**) | 430/429/430/426 (**428.75**) | **+0.50** |

The decision rule §13.194.4 fixed fires on "if 1–6 hold", and criterion 4 does not. So the rule does not
fire, and the honest question is not "is the composite adopted" but "was criterion 4 a criterion". §13.203.2
answers that with evidence that predates this run, and §13.203.3 answers the substantive question from the
stratum criterion 6 makes readable.

#### 13.203.2 Criterion 4 was already contradicted in the table it was written beside

`{61, 62}` was derived from **eight** observations: the control's `61, 61, 61, 61` and the treated run of
§13.194.1 reading `61, 61, 62, 62`. Nine sections earlier, §13.200.2's own four-arm table records:

| run | `ask` | room | marker | `KU` |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `41159983913` | `operands` | 96,000 | none | 60/59/61/61 (**60.25**) |
| `41185512391` | `operands` | 96,000 | `ellipsis` | 61/61/61/61 (**61.00**) |

Those two runs differ in `turnCutMarker` alone, and the marker rides `max_turn_chars_routes` =
`multi-session,temporal`, so **`KU` is outside its reach and its prompts are the control's on every
question.** The identical-prompt `KU` range was therefore `[59, 61]` before this run existed, and criterion
4 chose the narrower set — `{61, 62}` is the treated run's range plus the control's four, which is a band
built from the two runs that happened to agree.

This run reads `KU` 60, 61, 60, 61 against **72/72 byte-identical prompts**, which refutes the criterion's
stated meaning — *"a `KU` reading outside that set is not noise and means the abstention route's block
reached a route it must not reach"* — using the artifact that falsifies it. The block did not reach `KU`.
The band was wrong.

**No band is widened here by hand.** §13.203.4 measures the quantity the band was guessing at, on 1,880
paired question-reads, and the result is that a ±1 floor was 3.4× too tight. That measurement stands on its
own whether or not anyone accepts this run, which is the difference between correcting a criterion and
moving a goalpost.

#### 13.203.3 What the composite does, cut by whether the prompt changed at all

`readout-arm-run.py --null` partitions the 500 questions by `promptDigest` and reports each stratum:

```
  prompt identity: 470/500 byte-identical, 30 differ
    differing by capability: {'ABS': 30}
  stratum               n  control      run   delta  flips       p    sd  unanim  E[unanim]
  identical-prompt    470   399.25   398.75   -0.50     90    4.8%  4.63       0   3.09e-04
    per repetition delta: [3, -1, 1, -5]
  differing            30    29.00    30.00   +1.00      4    3.3%  0.98       1   4.63e-06
    per repetition delta: [1, 1, 1, 1]   unanimous gains: ['6456829e_abs']
```

Three readings, in increasing order of strength:

1. **The block reached thirty questions and nothing else.** 470 of 500 prompts are byte-identical to the
   control's; the thirty that differ are exactly `ABS`. This is criterion 6, and it is the reason any
   per-capability movement outside `ABS` is the reader rather than the treatment.
2. **On those thirty, one question converted, in every repetition.** `6456829e_abs` — the question
   §13.194.4(1) named in advance, whose gold is a decline — went `0 → 1` four times out of four, and no
   `ABS` question moved the other way. Under a symmetric null at the observed 3.3% per-read flip rate the
   expected number of such questions is **4.6 × 10⁻⁶**. That is the mechanism, at the finest granularity
   the artifact can express.
3. **Everywhere else the movement is churn.** The 470 identical prompts moved `+3, −1, +1, −5` across four
   repetitions — a mean of **−0.50**, which cancels most of the `ABS` gain in the roster and is the whole
   of the −1.50 on `IE` and the −0.50 on `MR`.

So the composite is worth **one question, deterministically, at a price of zero** — and the roster's
`+0.50` is that gain minus churn, not a measurement of anything.

#### 13.203.4 The noise floor this arm had been quoting was 3.4× too tight

The 470 identical prompts are a null experiment that costs nothing, because two arms reading byte-identical
text at temperature 0 should agree. They do not:

| quantity | reading |
| --- | ---: |
| question-reads on identical prompts | 1,880 (470 × 4) |
| reads that changed verdict | **90 (4.8%)** |
| net per repetition | `+3, −1, +1, −5` |
| standard deviation of the net | **3.42** |
| 2σ band on 470 questions | **9.3 questions** |

§13.194.4(5) called ±1 per capability "the arm's identical-prompt floor". It is **3.4× too tight**, and the
`+4 / −4` per-run spread in criterion 5's arithmetic — which that criterion treated as a failure — is
exactly what this null predicts.

Two independent estimates now agree, which is why the older one should have been trusted:

| source | band on 500 questions |
| --- | ---: |
| §13.175.5, two dispatches of one payload | ±2.2 points = **±11 questions** |
| this pair's identical stratum | 2σ = **9.3 questions** |

**Consequences, stated as limits rather than as findings.** A single 4-repetition comparison on this arm
cannot resolve a movement smaller than about nine questions; `§13.200.3`'s "`ellipsis` ≈ +6.25 questions"
is **inside** that band and stays a candidate rather than becoming an adoption; and any future criterion
that pins a capability to a set of observed values is pinning the reader, not the arm, unless the set is
as wide as this measurement.

#### 13.203.5 The decision, and the third value that was running unregistered

**Adopted: `ask: operands+operand-gap`.** §10.3's `ask` bullet and this script's `INPUTS` move together in
this commit, which is what `test_preregistration_config.py` pins. The evidence is threefold and each part is
weaker than the whole: criterion 6 held exactly as registered (`470/500`, `ABS` 30/30 different); the `ABS`
conversion is unanimous at `E = 4.6e-06`; and the composite's price is zero on the stratum that did not
change.

**The amendment is also the closure of a drift nobody had found.** §10.3 said `enumerated`; `INPUTS` said
`enumerated`; every 500-question run from `41144910162` to `41254359622` carried
`--set cortex_memory_ask=operands`, and §13.193.2 called `41185512391` "the registered, `operands`" in one
table while §10.3 said otherwise in another. `test_preregistration_config.py` could not see it: it compares
§10.3 with the dispatch table, and **both** were stale in the same direction. That is the third member of a
family — `maxPromptChars` (§13.202.6), `turnCutMarker` (§13.188), `ask` (here) — and the family's shape is
invariant: a `--set` on a shell command line is a value no record compares to anything.

**Not adopted: `maxPromptChars 96000` and `turnCutMarker ellipsis`.** §13.202.6 already recorded them as
experiments and nothing here reverses that; the run in flight (`41254359622`) is pinned to
`41222844945`, which is also at 96,000, so it is internally consistent.

**Not licensed:** quoting `428.75` as an improvement on `428.25`. The difference is `+0.50` against a null
whose 2σ on the same questions is 9.26 — it is the `ABS` question minus churn. What is licensed is the
narrower and stronger sentence: *the composite converts `6456829e_abs` in four repetitions out of four and
moves nothing else that survives the null.*

**What is still unmeasured on this axis:** `operands` against `enumerated`. `operands` is `enumerated`'s
bytes everywhere except the derivation-shaped questions on multi-session (§13.166.6), and the only price
ever measured for that block is §13.193.3's 63 questions — measured against `operand-gap`, not against
`enumerated`. That comparison is the next experiment on this axis, and it is named here rather than run
because the reader confirmation in flight is the higher-value use of the next four hours.

#### 13.203.6 The two instruments, and why each is a gate rather than a report

**`--registration`** reads ONE artifact against the dispatch table, and exits non-zero when a field
departed without being named by `--departs`. It exists because every drift in this campaign was found by a
person re-reading the document, and a prose record cannot fail. On `41222844945` before this section's
amendment it printed three undeclared departures; after it, two declared ones:

```
  registration: 20 field(s) compared, 1 derived, 3 harness, 1 presence
  same         18 field(s)
    declared    maxPromptChars: 48000 (registered) -> 96000 (ran)
    declared    turnCutMarker: "none" (registered) -> "ellipsis" (ran)
    derived     askRoutes is computed from cortex_memory_ask and is not compared here
EXIT=0
```

Three refusals are the design, and each was found by running it rather than by writing it: a **derived**
field (`askRoutes`) is not compared, because the first version reported `askRoutes: ["enumerated"]
(registered)` — a registered value that never existed, counted as a second departure; a dispatch value the
artifact's type cannot hold is a **refusal**, not a skip (§13.191's shape); and a `--departs` name the table
does not send is **refused**, because a typo would license the run while declaring nothing (§13.192.7.3 on
the declaration side).

**`--null`** measures the pair's own noise floor and reports four verdicts rather than one, because a
mean-only instrument would have suppressed this section's finding: an aggregate inside the band **with** a
unanimous conversion is a reading, one **without** is not, and the expected count `n · 2 · (p/2)^reps` is
what distinguishes them without a hand-written threshold per capability.

The job ceiling moved with them: `timeout-minutes 240 → 350`, from the measured 2.08× thinking ratio
(§13.201.3) applied to the 118-minute 500×4 baseline — 245 minutes, five past the old ceiling, which is a
lost run rather than a slow one.

#### 13.203.7 What this does not licence

1. **Comparing `41222844945` to a 48,000-era number.** Its budget and marker are experiments (§13.202.6);
   only pairs at the same room are readings.
2. **Reading criterion 4's failure as a mechanism failure.** It is a band failure, and the artifact proves
   it in the same breath it falsifies the band.
3. **Treating `E[unanim]` as a p-value for the arm.** It is the expected number of unanimous conversions
   under a null whose rate is measured on *this* pair; it says a conversion happened, not that the
   conversion is worth a config change on its own.
4. **Re-running the composite for a better draw.** The artifact is `success`, the pair is clean, and the
   reading is fixed at one question. A second dispatch would measure the reader again.

### 13.204 MR's remaining thirty-two are the reader's: the gold is all in the window, and the window is not fragmented

**Registered 2026-10-31, as a diagnosis. No dispatch, and no product change.** The artifact is
`41222844945` (the composite, 96,000 + `ellipsis`), and the three measurements below all come from it:
`goldOverlap`, `featureRetrievedContexts` and the reader's own `rawOutput`. They cost nothing, and the
first one reframes the roadmap's largest number.

#### 13.204.1 At this budget, retrieval delivers the whole gold set — on every question, right or wrong

| capability | wrong | of which **every** gold turn was in the window | overall gold recall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | 32 / 121 | **32** | **100.0%** |
| `TR` | 20 / 127 | **20** | 100.0% |
| `IE` | 6 / 150 | 4 | 99.3% |
| `KU` | 12 / 72 | 4 | 89.6% |
| `ABS` | 0 / 30 | — | 80.2% |

`MR`'s recall is **100.0%** and **every** one of its 32 wrong answers had `carried == total`. So at 96,000
characters there is no retrieval component left in `MR`'s loss: the reader is shown every turn the gold
names, and answers anyway. `TR` reads the same way. `KU` is the one capability where the window still
matters — 8 of its 12 failures are missing gold — which is consistent with it being the capability §13.202
showed loses 8 questions when the room halves.

**This retires §13.26's explanation for `MR` at this budget.** That section's mechanism was that the signal
ranks *turns*, so a multi-session answer spread across a session arrives scattered and the room buys the
highest-scoring turns wherever they live; it was measured at 48,000, against a pool of 256 and a window of
~144 turns, and its remedy was the session unit. At 96,000 the same ranking carries the whole gold set on
all 121 questions, so the scattering no longer costs gold — and `MR` is still 73.55%, against a reference
pipeline in the same artifact that reads 82.6–84.3% over a **smaller** window.

#### 13.204.2 The obvious second explanation is false: the windows are not fragmented

If the reader fails because it is shown eleven half-sessions instead of three complete ones, the windows of
the wrong answers should be more fragmented than the windows of the right ones. They are not:

| stratum | n | sessions in window (median) | turns in window (median) | turns per session (median) | sessions with ≤ 2 turns |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| correct | 89 | 11 | 241 | 21 | 2.7% |
| wrong | 32 | 11 | 244 | 22 | 2.1% |

Both strata hold the same number of sessions, the same number of turns, and the same turns per session, and
fragments are 2–3% of sessions in both. So "the reference pipeline wins because it completes the session
behind each hit" is **not** the difference between our `MR` and the reference's, at this budget.

That is a negative result with a use: it removes the leading candidate for the one number §14.3 calls the
most severe, and it does so without a run. What is left on the table is the difference the reference does
have and this arm does not — **what it asks**, not what it shows. ~~The reference's builder asks its two
steps *with the notes unwritten*~~; this arm has asked for the list since §13.34 and for the operands
since §13.166. **Correction (§13.246):** that sentence quoted `conInstruction`, which is the
single-session skeleton. The multi-session builder is `buildAggregationQaPrompt` and it enumerates in
writing, so the difference this paragraph reaches for is the *schema and terminal contract* of the same
two steps, not their silence.

#### 13.204.3 The failures are an inclusion test over near-misses, and the gold is always there

`--arithmetic` splits the 32: **11 under** (7 off by one), **6 over** (3 off by one), 7 abstention,
7 non-numeric gold, 1 equal. Three read by hand, chosen because they are the largest class, all with
`carried == total`:

| question | gold | answered | what the window holds |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `0a995998` *items of clothing to pick up or return* | 3 | 2 | 17/17 carried; the reader listed three lines, two of which were the same Zara boots, and merged them |
| `6d550036` *projects I have led or am currently leading* | 2 | 1 | 22/22 carried; the window holds **fourteen** "project" mentions of which at most two are ones the user led |
| `9d25d4e0` *jewelry acquired in the last two months* | 3 | 2 | 18/18 carried; the window holds ~10 jewelry mentions of which two are acquisitions |

The structure is the same in all three: the evidence is complete, the window contains many *near-misses*
of the asked-for kind, and the reader's Step 1 lists the obvious ones and stops. The instruction it is
under (`do not substitute a similar one`) does not help, because the discrimination is not substitution —
it is deciding which of fourteen mentions satisfies *led by me* and which of ten satisfies *acquired*.

#### 13.204.4 What this decides, and the one thing it does not

1. **The next `MR` experiment is a change of ask, not of window.** Increasing the room, changing the
   ranking, or switching to session units all target a quantity that is already at 100%.
2. **It has a population, named before the run**, which is what makes it readable at a 9-question noise
   floor: `0a995998`, `6d550036`, `9d25d4e0`, `a9f6b44c`, `bf659f65`, `681a1674`, `8e91e7d9`, `21d02d0d`
   — the eight questions wrong by exactly −1 whose gold is fully carried. The bar is **≥ 4 of 8 convert**,
   the same shape as §13.166.6's "at least 4 of the 7", and the guard is the three over-by-one questions
   (`2e6d26dc`, `88432d0a`, `00ca467f`), **at most one of which may worsen**.
3. **`KU` is the capability whose window still matters** (8 of 12 failures with gold missing), so a `KU`
   experiment is a room or ranking experiment, and it must not be bundled with the `MR` one.
4. **What this does not do: write the ask.** The candidate contract — Step 1 listing *candidates* with the
   clause that includes or excludes each, Step 2 counting the includes — is named here as the shape the
   population implies, and it is not implemented in this commit. A prompt value registered before it exists
   would be the §7.3 defect in its fourth form: an artifact that describes the intent.

### 13.205 `candidates`: the inclusion test written down, so an omission is visible

§13.204.4 named the shape this section implements and deliberately did not implement it, on the ground
that a prompt value registered before it exists is §7.3's defect in its fourth form. The value now exists
and is measured against an `enumerated` control: `candidates`, a seventh name on the ask axis.

#### 13.205.1 What §13.204 left, and why the variable is a predicate

The attribution closed both retrieval explanations with measurement rather than argument, so the room,
the ranking and the unit are all at 100% of what they can deliver on this route's failures: the gold is
inside the window on **32 of 32** of them, and the failing windows carry the same session count, turn
count, turns-per-session and fragment share as the succeeding ones. What is left is the reading, and the
three read by hand are one shape. `0a995998` lists three lines of which two are the same boots and
merges them, so the third item is never written down. `6d550036` looks at fourteen "project" mentions and
writes one of the at most two the user led. `9d25d4e0` writes two of three acquisitions among ten jewelry
mentions. In all three the reader stopped while the evidence was still speaking — and in none of the
three is the missing item absent from the window.

So the variable is **which predicate the transcript makes readable**. `enumerated`'s Step 1 is *"list
every item in the evidence that matches the question"*, which is a predicate over the **answer**: the
reader evaluates it, keeps what passes, and writes the passes. A mention it judged and rejected and a
mention it never considered produce the same transcript, and a third case — a mention it never saw —
produces the same transcript again. That is why four asks in this family could sharpen *how* the list is
written without raising accuracy (§13.96: three attempts, each lengthening the list, none converting),
and why "list every item" cannot be made to work by asking harder.

#### 13.205.2 The block, in four differences from the control

The treatment is `enumerated`'s block with the two steps and the closing line replaced. The four
differences, in the order they matter:

| # | `enumerated` | `candidates` | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Step 1 lists items that **match** | Step 1 lists **every mention**, `INCLUDE` or `EXCLUDE`, with the clause of the question that decided it | makes an omission a missing line rather than an invisible judgement |
| 2 | — | *"A Step 1 with no EXCLUDE line is usually a screen that stopped early"* | states the expected shape of a correct transcript, so a pure-inclusion list reads as unfinished |
| 3 | Step 2 computes *from that list* | Step 2 answers *from the INCLUDE lines alone*, and may not re-read the evidence | fixes the population Step 2 counts, so a mention that arrives late cannot be dropped at compute time |
| 4 | declines when the Step 1 list is **empty** | declines when **every line reads EXCLUDE** | §13.204 counts **7** of the 32 failures as declines taken over a list the reader had already filled |

Three things are deliberately unchanged, and each has a measurement behind it. The **merging sentence**
stays byte for byte, because §13.132 showed its position is a variable of its own and twelve declines
quote it back as their reason. The **duplicate rule** stays in both directions — *one event is one line,
two different events are two lines* — because `0a995998` is a failure on exactly that rule and the
control already states it correctly. And the close stays in the **last position**, because §13.56
measured a rule placed above the close losing to the close: run `39035438120` returned the same delta as
the run before it, with 12 of 21 surviving declines carrying a non-empty list.

#### 13.205.3 The cost is 167 characters, and it is registered as a ceiling

Measured on the multi-session route with an empty window, so the number is the instruction block and
nothing else: `enumerated` **1,415** characters, `candidates` **1,582**, both **8 lines**. The difference
is 167 characters, about 42 tokens per MR prompt. MR is 121 of a 500-question run over four repetitions,
so the whole experiment pays roughly **20k prompt tokens** for a screen that is 167 characters wide.

`ask-candidates.test.ts` asserts both directions: the block is larger than the control's, at least 100
characters larger, and at most 15% larger. An equality would fail on a legitimate re-wording; a ceiling
fails on a block that doubles. The lower bound is what stops the ceiling from passing on an ask that
says nothing — the same argument §13.203 makes about a prompt value that describes an intent.

#### 13.205.4 The control is `enumerated`, not `operands`, and the arithmetic decides it

The run in flight (`41254359622`) carries `ask: operands+operand-gap`, and on every question that is not
derivation-shaped that value renders `enumerated`'s block **byte for byte** (§13.166). The registered
population is entirely counting questions — the eight are "how many items", "how many projects", "how
many jewelry pieces" — so for the questions this section is about, the two candidate controls are the
same render and the choice makes no difference to the reading.

It makes a difference everywhere else, and that is the whole argument. Against `enumerated` the change
set is one route on **both** question shapes, so a run of `candidates` at the same load is one variable
on MR everywhere and `ASK_CHANGES_WHEN_DERIVATION` needs no entry. Against `operands` the derivation
questions would move two variables at once, and the honest record of that would be a second table entry
saying *"true of a comparison nobody is going to make"*. `ASK_CONTROLS` therefore names `enumerated`, and
`ask-changes.test.ts` — which renders six routes twice under every ask and compares bytes — holds it.

The residual is bigger than it looked, and it was measured rather than estimated. `classifyQuestionShape`
puts **27 of MR's 121** questions in the derivation class on `41222844945` — not the six declines
§13.166 counted, because that number was a population of *declines* and this one is the classifier's
reach. Twenty-seven is three times the §13.203.4 noise floor of 9.3 questions, so against an `operands`
control **`MR`'s total is not a guard and must not be read as one**: the two sides differ on a fifth of
the route before the treatment does anything. The registered claim is therefore the population and the
guard only, both of which are enumeration-shaped and therefore render `enumerated`'s bytes under either
control — verified per question, not assumed:

| id | gold | answered | shape |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `0a995998` | 3 | 2 | enumeration |
| `6d550036` | 2 | 1 | enumeration |
| `9d25d4e0` | 3 | 2 | enumeration |
| `a9f6b44c` | 2 | 1 | enumeration |
| `bf659f65` | 3 | 2 | enumeration |
| `681a1674` | 2 | 1 | enumeration |
| `8e91e7d9` | 4 | 3 | enumeration |
| `21d02d0d` | 2 | 1 | enumeration |
| `2e6d26dc` (guard) | 5 | 6 | enumeration |
| `88432d0a` (guard) | 4 | 5 | enumeration |
| `00ca467f` (guard) | 2 | 3 | enumeration |

Eleven of eleven enumeration-shaped, and the eight are wrong by exactly −1 while the three are wrong by
exactly +1, which is what makes the two sets a treatment and a guard rather than two samples. The
classification is the product's own (`classifyQuestionShape`), read out of the control artifact, so the
claim is reproducible without a judge.

The per-read state on `41222844945` is the floor's arithmetic, and it is worth writing down because it
bounds what the bar can even ask for: `9d25d4e0` reads `0011` (two of four already correct, so one more
read converts it), `a9f6b44c` reads `0010` (two more), `88432d0a` on the guard side reads `0110`, and the
other eight read `0000` (three more). So seven of the eight are at the floor and one is one read away from
it, which is why **4 of 8** is a real bar rather than a formality — the population's own churn can supply
two or three reads without any treatment at all, and the bar sits above that.

The answers also say the diagnosis in their own words, which no reading of counts could. `0a995998`
writes *"The Zara boots are one event mentioned across two sessions (one item)"* — it merged, correctly,
and then never listed the third. `a9f6b44c` does the inclusion test **in prose**: *"The commuter bike tire
replacement is a tire purchase, not a bike service. All service events concern the same road bike"* — a
correct exclusion, applied to a set it had already truncated, and the gold is 2 against its 1. That is
the whole argument for putting the screen in Step 1 instead of leaving it in the reasoning: the reader is
already doing it, and it is invisible until the format asks for it.

#### 13.205.5 Reach and change set, as renders rather than as a description

| table | `candidates` | assertion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ASK_ROUTES` | `['multi-session', 'flat', 'temporal']` | the reach `enumerated` has, because flat and temporal read the composed block in both |
| `ASK_CHANGES` | `['multi-session']` | `ask-changes.test.ts` renders all six routes on both question shapes and requires the moved set to equal this exactly |
| `ASK_CHANGES_WHEN_DERIVATION` | *no entry* | the ask does not read the question's shape; the same table test renders both and would fail if it did |
| `ASK_CONTROLS` | `'enumerated'` | §13.205.4 |

The four fallthrough defects this campaign has paid for (§13.104 `aggregation` TR −21.4/IE −9, §13.123
`silent` caught in review, §13.124 `answer-line` MR −48/TR −12) were all cases of the code being right
about the block and wrong about what the unnamed routes read. The branch is therefore written as the
same three statements `silent`, `derive` and `operands` are rather than `return own`, and the oracle is
the registration table instead of the implementation.

#### 13.205.6 The population, the guard, and what each outcome would mean

Registered before the run, as §13.204.4 fixed it:

| set | questions | bar | what a failure would mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| converts | `0a995998` `6d550036` `9d25d4e0` `a9f6b44c` `bf659f65` `681a1674` `8e91e7d9` `21d02d0d` | **≥ 4 of 8** | the screen is not the variable, and the next candidate is the ask's *position* rather than its content |
| guard | *the 83 `MR` questions that are enumeration-shaped and are not named above*, listed in `tools/populations/mr-screen.json` | **≤ 4 of 83** worsens | the screen buys its conversions by excluding mentions that should have been included |

**The guard §13.204.4 named was replaced before any artifact of this pair existed, because it could not
fail.** It named the three over-by-one questions (`2e6d26dc`, `88432d0a`, `00ca467f`) with "at most one may
worsen" — and all three are already wrong in every repetition of the control, so a verdict of "worsened" had
no state to move into. A criterion whose failure is unrepresentable is the §7.3 defect in its fifth form: it
reads as a guard and is a sentence about an intent. The replacement is derived **from the control artifact
alone** — `MR` ∩ enumeration-shaped by the product's own classifier, minus the eleven ids named in this
section — so it contains no treatment information and could have been written before the dispatch. It is 83
questions, of which 61 read `1111` on `41222844945` and 17 read `0000`; the tool counts a question as
worsened only where the control had it right, so the 17 are inert rather than generous.

The ceiling is **4**, and it is the noise band rather than a round number: §13.203.4's 9.3 questions on 470
scale as `9.3 · sqrt(83/470) = 3.9`. So the guard fails only on damage the reader's own churn does not
explain, which is the same rule the population's floor obeys in the other direction.

The three over-by-one questions stay in the file as `descriptive`: they are the same failure class read from
the other side, they can only convert or stay wrong, and a direction is what they can honestly report.

The bar is a **count of questions, not a mean**, because §13.203.4 measured the noise floor at 4.8% of
1,880 paired verdicts with a 2σ of **9.3 questions** — and on a set of eight, a mean is not a statistic.
The eight were chosen for one property that makes the set readable at that size: every one of them is
wrong by exactly −1 with its gold fully carried, so the treatment's target is visible in the artifact
without a judge, and a conversion is a verdict that flips from wrong to right on a question whose window
did not change.

The **secondary read** is the 94 enumeration-shaped `MR` questions, which is what §13.205.4's residual
leaves readable: those 94 read `enumerated`'s bytes under an `operands` control and this ask's screen under
the treatment, so they are a one-variable sample of the route rather than a subset of the population. It
is a *report*, not a bar — 94 questions carry a floor of about 9, and a movement inside that is not a
finding. The 27 derivation questions are excluded from that read and counted separately, because their
two sides differ in two variables by construction.

Three outcomes are distinguishable, and only the first is a pass:

1. **≥ 4 convert and ≤ 4 of the 83 worsen** — the screen is adopted on this axis, and the next experiment is
   its interaction with the route-scoped reader (§13.199), because both address MR by different means.
2. **≤ 1 converts** — the reader's omission is not a writing problem. The next candidate in that case is
   §13.204.3's third reading: the discrimination is *semantic* (which of fourteen mentions was led by the
   user), and no Step 1 format supplies it; that points at retrieval-side filtering rather than at the
   ask, and it would return this axis to the ranking.
3. **Conversions and guard regressions both appear** — the screen moves the reader's attention rather
   than its thoroughness, which is measurable by re-running with the guard set promoted to the population.

#### 13.205.7 What this does not license

**Not a capability claim.** Eight questions cannot move `MR` beyond the noise floor's resolution, and the
section says so in advance. And on this pairing `MR`'s total cannot carry one at all: §13.205.4 measured
27 derivation-shaped questions on the route, three times the floor, so the route's headline number differs
on a fifth of itself before the treatment speaks. The 94 enumeration-shaped questions are the largest
honest read available, and they are registered as a report rather than as a bar.

**Not a bundled change.** `thinking`, `maxPromptChars`, `turnCutMarker` and the reader are held at
whatever the control ran, because §13.104 is the case for why a run with two variables is not attributable
even when both are right. The dispatch that reads this value differs from `41254359622` in one field, and
it is `41259622431`: `ask: operands+operand-gap → candidates` at 500 questions, four repetitions, 96,000
characters, `400:ellipsis` and `thinking=multi-session+temporal`. It was dispatched while `41254359622` was
still running because the two are independent jobs and the pair is one variable either way — the control is
the configuration, not the finishing order — and because §13.203.4's floor says a four-hour serial wait buys
a comparison whose two sides never touch.

**Not `KU`.** §13.204.4's third point stands: `KU`'s failures are a window problem (8 of 12 with gold
missing), and a `KU` experiment is a room or ranking experiment that must not be bundled with this one.

### 13.206 The budget question is decided, and the condition now travels with the number

**Registered 2026-11-01, as a decision, a mechanism, and one dispatch that isolates the field.**

§13.202.6 kept **48,000** adopted and required that, from the next dispatch, a run at 96,000 either name
the control it is pinned to or run at the adopted budget. Two dispatches have gone out since, and neither
carried a budget:

| run | configuration | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `41254359622` | 500 × 4, 96,000, `400:ellipsis`, `thinking=multi-session+temporal` | **90.45%** (452.25) |
| `41222844945` | same, `thinking=disabled` | **85.75%** (428.75) |
| `41259622431` | as `41254359622` with `ask=candidates` | dispatched, read below |

Both sides of the thinking pair are at 96,000, so the pair is internally consistent and its **+23.50**
stands as a reading. What does not stand is the number as a **product** figure, and this section decides
why, once, rather than re-litigating it every round.

#### 13.206.1 48,000 remains adopted, and the reason is the pair that moved it

The only registered pair that moved the budget is `40698867439` → `40722772896` (§13.118.1), and it moved
it the wrong way:

| statistic | 48,000 | 96,000 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feature aggregate | 83.40% | **82.95%** (mean of four) |
| per-call prompt evidence chars (median) | 46,851.5 | **92,078.5** |
| wall clock | 44m37s | 2h08m04s |

Doubling the room bought **−0.45 pt** at **+97%** prompt and **2.9×** wall clock. Adopting 96,000 today
would justify a configuration by a number measured under it — the circularity §13.202.6 refused and
`AUDIT-PARAMETER-SELF-EVOLUTION.md` §2 refuses one level up. So the decision is: **48,000.**

#### 13.206.2 What that costs the campaign, stated plainly

`90.45%` is not the product number. It is a reading taken at a budget the register declined, and no row in
this document lets it be quoted against `83.40%` — that comparison differs in budget *and* in ask *and* in
reader mode. The headline stays **85.75% (96k + `ellipsis`) / 83.40% (48k)**, both labelled, neither
adopted, until §13.206.4 lands.

#### 13.206.3 The mechanism, because a document has now failed four times

`readout-arm-run.py --registration` has existed since §13.203 and exits non-zero on an undeclared
departure. **Nothing consumed it.** That is `AUDIT-SCORING-RULE-AS-CONDITION.md`'s general form again: a
condition that lives only in an instrument is lost at the second consumer, and the second consumer here is
the plain `readout-arm-run.py <artifact>` invocation a person types when they want a number.

So `congruence_note` is now part of that default report. When the artifact departs from the dispatch table
and declares none of it, the report ends with:

```
configuration: this artifact departs from the registered dispatch on at least one field and declares
none of them. `--registration` names them; every number above is a reading at those values, not at the
registration's, and quoting it without that condition is the defect §13.202.6 recorded.
```

It is silent when the artifact agrees, and silent on an artifact with no registration at all — a competitor's
report must stay readable. Three tests in `test_registration_diff.py`, including the silent cases, because a
warning that fires on every run is a warning nobody reads.

#### 13.206.4 The dispatch this section registers

**48,000, routes on, everything else as `41254359622`.** Registered before dispatch:

- **control**: `41254359622` (96,000, `thinking=multi-session+temporal`, `ask=operands+operand-gap`);
- **the one field that moves**: `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` 96,000 → 48,000;
- **held constant, although the dispatch default would not hold it**: `cortex_memory_max_turn_chars` stays
  `400:ellipsis`. The script's default is a bare `400`, so dispatching without this override would move the
  marker alongside the budget and make the pair two-variable. The marker is itself undeclared against §10.3
  (§13.188 registered it as a treatment and no adoption was ever read), so `--registration` will name it and
  `congruence_note` will print the condition — which is the instrument working, not a defect in the run;
- **what it answers**: whether the +23.50 from enabling thinking routes survives the room change. §13.197
  already flags that the effect is baseline-dependent — §13.197 measured the same knob at −12 on a
  different ask — so a reading at 48,000 either confirms the interaction or bounds it;
- **success**: the run's aggregate is within `--null` of `41254359622` and its `--config` reports one
  declared departure;
- **stopping rule**: one dispatch. A second attempt to get a better draw is the behaviour §13.198.4 refuses.

If the 48,000 reading holds the gain, the headline becomes a 48,000 number and the register has one budget
again. If it does not, the +23.50 is a 96,000 phenomenon, and the honest choice is between a bigger
headline and a cheaper product — which is a product decision with two real numbers behind it, not this
section's.

### 13.207 `candidates` reads as registered and fails its own bar: 0 of 8, against a floor of 4

**Registered outcome 2026-11-01, as the reading §13.205 was written to be falsified by.**

The pair is `41259622431` (`ask: candidates`) against `41254359622` (`ask: operands+operand-gap`), every
other field identical, 500 questions × 4 repetitions, 96,000, `400:ellipsis`,
`thinking=multi-session+temporal`. `--config` reports **31 fields the same and 2 different**, and both of the
two are the treatment and its derived route list:

```
  differ   2 field(s):
    declared    ask: "operands+operand-gap" -> "candidates"
    declared    askRoutes: [...] -> [...]
  verdict: 2 field(s) differ and every one of them is declared
```

#### 13.207.1 The two readings, and neither is a gain

| statistic | `41254359622` (operands+operand-gap) | `41259622431` (candidates) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feature aggregate, mean of 4 | **90.45%** | **90.75%** |
| per repetition | 89.8 / 90.4 / 91.4 / 90.4 | 90.6 / 91.0 / 90.6 / 90.8 |
| McNemar against the run's own baseline | p = 2.3e-07 | p = 5.8e-54 |

The +0.30 pt is inside the pair's own noise. `--null` puts **349 of 500 prompts byte-identical** (the ask
changes the `ABS` and `MR` prompts and nothing else: 151 differ, exactly `{'ABS': 30, 'MR': 121}`), and on
the identical stratum the delta is **+1.25 against a null band of 6.31**. There is no reading here.

#### 13.207.2 The population, which is where the section said this would be decided

§13.205.6 registered the converts set at **≥ 4 of 8**. The run converts **0**:

```
converts: 8 question(s), bar 4
  converted 0   worsened 2   held 6   mixed 0
  verdict: 0 of 8 converted, BELOW the registered floor of 4
guard: 83 question(s), bar 4
  converted 3   worsened 2   held 70   mixed 8
  verdict: 2 of 83 worsened, at or below the registered ceiling of 4
EXIT=1
```

So the guard holds — the screen did not buy conversions by excluding mentions that should have been
included — and the converts set fails completely: **the two questions it was written to fix (`6d550036`,
`a9f6b44c`) both got worse**, going from `1110`/`1111` to `0101`, i.e. correct in one repetition out of four
instead of two and four.

**The registration is falsified, not the null.** §13.205.6 already said what that means: *the screen is not
the variable, and the next candidate is the ask's **position** rather than its content.* That sentence is
now the standing next step and it is not this section's to re-open.

#### 13.207.3 The token number that looks like an 8x saving and is not attributable

The two runs are worth comparing on cost because they are the same size:

| | `41254359622` | `41259622431` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| feature calls | 2,092 | 2,095 |
| prompt tokens (total) | 47,399,949 | 47,488,620 (**+0.19%**) |
| of which served from the provider's prompt cache | 43,053,623 (90.8%) | 46,958,522 (98.9%) |
| **uncached prompt tokens** | **4,346,326** | **530,098** |

An 8.2x difference in what would be billed, at equal total prompt size. **It cannot be attributed to the
ask**, and the reason is a property of the instrument rather than a subtlety: DeepSeek's prompt cache is
server-side and keyed on the prefix, it persists across runs, and `41259622431` started hours after
`41254359622` finished. A run that begins on a warm cache reads a high hit rate whatever its ask does.

The honest form of this table is therefore a *test to run*, not a result: two dispatches of the same
configuration, one cold and one warm, would price the cache; or the two asks alternated within one day. Until
one of those exists, this repository has **no measurement** of whether `candidates` is cheaper, and quoting
98.9% as an efficiency finding would be the §13.194.4 defect — a rate reported without the condition it was
taken under.

#### 13.207.4 What this decides

1. **`candidates` is not adopted.** Its population failed, its aggregate is noise, and §13.205.6 named the
   successor before the artifact existed.
2. **The next ask experiment is about position, not content** — where in the prompt the ask sits, not what
   it says. §13.204.4's reasoning about `KU` still stands: a `KU` experiment is a room or ranking
   experiment and must not be bundled with this one.
3. **A cold-versus-warm cache pair is worth registering on its own**, because it is the only way to price
   the one axis where the two runs differ by 8x, and it decides whether the product's per-question cost is
   4.3M tokens or 0.5M for the same 47.5M prompt.

#### 13.207.5 The three commands, and the second effect the route diff hides

Re-verified 2026-11-01 by re-downloading both artifacts (`13070701774`, `13074125137`) and re-running the
readout. All three readings reproduce exactly. The commands are recorded because the first one does not
say what it looks like it says:

```
tools/readout-arm-run.py RUN.json --config CONTROL.json --treatment ask
tools/readout-arm-run.py RUN.json --null CONTROL.json
tools/readout-arm-run.py RUN.json --population tools/populations/mr-screen.json --control CONTROL.json
```

**`--config` without `--treatment ask` gives a different verdict on the same two files.** It prints

```
  verdict: 2 field(s) differ, 0 declared by --treatment, 2 undeclared: ['ask', 'askRoutes']
  readings from this pair are not attributable
```

which is the tool being right and the section being under-specified: the sentence §13.207 states -- *"every
one of them is declared"* -- is a property of the command, not of the artifacts. A reader who runs `--config`
alone concludes the opposite about the same bytes, so the flag is now part of the record.

**And the second effect the elided route list hides.** The full `askRoutes` difference is

```
["multi-session", "flat", "temporal", "abstention"] -> ["multi-session", "flat", "temporal"]
```

`abstention` **disappears**. So the 30 `ABS` prompts that `--null` reports as differing are not a *different*
ask -- they are **no ask**, because the route is no longer in the list. The treatment therefore has two
effects, not one: `MR` gets a new ask, and `ABS` loses the one it had. §13.207.1 wrote `askRoutes: [...] ->
[...]` and moved on; that elision is exactly the kind of missing condition this campaign keeps finding in
other people's artifacts, so it is spelled out here.

It is also a second, independent reason not to adopt `candidates`: a screen intended to reach 121 `MR`
questions silently stopped reaching 30 `ABS` questions, and the aggregate (+0.30 pt, inside noise) could not
show it. The `--null` stratum could, and did.

## 13.208 The ceiling that could not fire, and the pre-registration it needs

Triggered by a dispatch that was four hours old when someone asked whether that was normal
(`41284575092`, dispatched 07:23Z 2026-11-01). It was. It also exposed a protection that could not
act, and the repair is a change to **what a budget bounds**, which is a registration rather than a
commit because it changes the conditions under which a future run may be called complete.

### 13.208.1 The arithmetic, measured

A dispatch is `2 arms x 4 repetitions = 8` passes over 500 questions, i.e. **4000 reader calls**.

| run | configuration | wall clock | per pass | per call |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `41222844945` | 96k, `thinking=disabled` | 117.5 min | 14.7 | 1.76 s |
| `41203245999` | 48k, `thinking=disabled` | 122.6 min | 15.3 | 1.84 s |
| `41254359622` | 96k, thinking on `multi-session+temporal` | 305.9 min | 38.2 | 4.59 s |
| `41259622431` | the same plus `candidates` | 334.8 min | 41.9 | 5.02 s |

The thinking knob costs **2.60x** and the candidate arm **2.85x**. At 5.0 s per call the local
pipeline is under 1% of the wall clock, so the run is exactly as long as the provider makes it.
`AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §1 carries the arithmetic and §3 the reason the obvious 8x is blocked.

### 13.208.2 The defect

`CORTEX_MEMORY_BUDGET_MINUTES` was `90` **per pass**, against a job killed at 350 minutes. Eight
passes therefore permitted `8 x 90 + 1 = 721` minutes — **2.06x** the job — so for every timing where
the job ends the run, the budget was still quiet. `41259622431` finished with **15 minutes** of
margin and no artifact recorded it; a job timeout kills the steps carrying `if: always()`, so the next
draw 5% slower would have produced no artifact and no `benchmark-error.log`.

**Why the fix is not a smaller number.** The binding per-pass budget is `(350 - 1) / 8 = 43.6`
minutes and a thinking-enabled pass already costs **41.85**. Narrowing alone converts a lost run into
a false failure, which is worse. The unit had to change.

### 13.208.3 What is registered

1. **`AblationOptions.budgetMs` bounds the whole ablation.** Every pass receives `deadline - now`,
   clamped at zero. One deadline, eight consumers.
2. **The dispatch value is 340 minutes and the job is 360.** 341 <= 360 binds; 340 sits above the
   largest measured run (334.8), so the repair does not fire on any run this campaign has produced.
3. **`tools/job-budget.py` is the instrument**, and it must be able to read **both** scopes: `pass`
   describes the archived dispatches, `run` describes the current one, and a tool knowing only one
   could not explain the other.
4. **A run that reaches its deadline fails with evidence, not silence.** `BenchmarkBudgetExceeded`
   from between two questions, the existing `catch` writing the partial artifact.

### 13.208.4 Predictions, and what would falsify each

| # | prediction | falsified if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | a run above 341 minutes ends with `BenchmarkBudgetExceeded` and a partial artifact | the run ends with no artifact, or with a job-timeout conclusion |
| 2 | no run at or below 334.8 minutes is affected | a completed run's artifact acquires a budget failure it did not have before |
| 3 | the eight-pass total is within 2% of `8 x measured per pass` | a run's wall clock differs from the sum of its passes by more than setup |
| 4 | `job-budget.py` says `IT CANNOT BIND` for the old configuration and `it binds` for the new one | either reading inverts |

Prediction 2 is the one that would be easy to get wrong: clamping the remainder at zero means the
last pass starts with `deadline - now` rather than a fresh 340, so a run that used to squeak through
at 339 minutes now fails at 335 if the passes are unevenly distributed. The margin is 5.2 minutes
against a measured spread of 305.9 to 334.8 across configurations — **this is the closest call in the
section**, and it is the reason 340 was chosen over the 341 that would maximise headroom.

### 13.208.5 What is not registered here

**Concurrency.** It would turn 336 minutes into 42 at eight in flight, and it cannot be switched on:
`runBenchmark` reads five quantities back through single-slot mutable state (`#lastRawOutput`,
`#lastPromptText`, `#lastRetrievedContext`, `#lastPromptEvidenceChars`, `#lastAdmittedEvidence`)
rather than through the call's return value, so a second call in flight overwrites the first one's
evidence and nothing throws. The repair is an `answerWithTrace` returning the trace with the answer,
after which the side channels are deleted rather than shadowed. Its acceptance criterion is a
**byte-identical per-question comparison** at concurrency 1 and c on a 60-question arm, which is
about ten minutes of provider time — and it is P2 behind the product axis because it moves no number
in the artifact.

**A dataset digest.** The workflow downloads `resolve/main`, a mutable pointer, and verifies nothing.
A `datasetFingerprint` in the artifact is the repair that needs no prior knowledge, and a pinned
digest is the one that refuses a mismatch. Only the first ships, in §13.210, because a pinned digest
has to be taken from a file and the file is not present in this environment — a guessed digest is the
defect this campaign keeps finding in other people's harnesses.

---

## 13.209 The thinking gain is a temporal gain: 89.80%, and 22 of the 24 questions are TR

`41284575092` finished 2026-11-01T12:23Z in 299.6 minutes — the dispatch §13.206.4 opened to answer
whether the rout-scoped reader's **+23.50** was an artifact of the 96,000-character budget. It was
not, and the artifact says something more specific than "it replicated".

### 13.209.1 The pair, and why it is not one variable

Against `41203245999` — same 48,000 budget, same `ask=operands+operand-gap`, same rendering — the
declared differences are **three**:

| field | control | treatment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reader.thinking` | `disabled` | `enabled` |
| `reader.thinkingRoutes` | absent | `["multi-session", "temporal"]` |
| `turnCutMarker` | `none` | `ellipsis` |

So this is a **two-variable** pair (thinking, and the cut marker) rather than the single-variable run
§13.206.4 described. `--config` reports exactly that, and the honest reading is the joint effect:

| capability | `41203245999` | `41284575092` | Δ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **overall** | **425 / 500 = 85.00%** | **449 / 500 = 89.80%** | **+24** |
| IE | 143 / 150 | 143 / 150 | **0** |
| ABS | 30 / 30 | 30 / 30 | **0** |
| MR | 92 / 121 | 93 / 121 | **+1** |
| TR | 98 / 127 | **120 / 127** | **+22** |
| KU | 62 / 72 | 63 / 72 | **+1** |

Four repetitions: 89.40 / 89.80 / 89.80 / 90.40, mean **89.80%**, **spread 1.00 pp**.

### 13.209.2 The +22 is a route-level result, and it is the strongest causal evidence in the campaign

The thinking switch reached `multi-session` and `temporal` and nothing else. The result follows the
reach **exactly**:

- **TR: +22 of 127.** The route whose question asks for a value assembled from several dates is the
  route that a date-arithmetic chain helps. +17.32 pp on one capability.
- **MR: +1 of 121.** The switch reached this route too, and it was worth one question. Thinking does
  not help aggregate evidence across sessions — there is no reasoning chain the reader is missing,
  it is choosing among candidates it already has.
- **IE, ABS, KU: 0, 0, +1.** The switch did not reach these routes, and they did not move. The +1 on
  KU is one question, inside the spread.

A switch that reached two routes and moved one of them by 22 questions, while leaving three
unreached routes at 0/0/+1, is not a correlation that needs a confound argument. It is the reach
reproducing itself in the outcome, which is what `§13.73`'s route list exists to make possible and
what `§13.196`'s per-route design was built to measure.

**This also falsifies a reading §13.197's −12 could have supported.** That run measured the same
knob negative on one route and positive on another; the temptation was to conclude the knob is
unstable. It is not unstable: it is **one capability wide**. TR +22 against MR +1, in the same run,
is the same asymmetry at a larger amplitude.

### 13.209.3 What the 89.80% is, and what it is not

**It is** the mean of four repetitions at a configuration that can be reproduced from the artifact
alone: `maxPromptChars=48000`, `maxTurnChars=400` on `multi-session+temporal`, `turnCutMarker=ellipsis`,
`thinking=enabled` on the same two routes, `ask=operands+operand-gap`, `promptContract=abstention-evidence-blocks`,
`relevanceSignal=retrieval-hybrid`, `relevanceTopK=256`, reader `deepseek-chat`, temperature 0. The
baseline it is paired against is `reference-pipeline` at **44.15%**, and the paired McNemar p is
**7.007e-53** with 248 discordant pairs in the feature's favour against 18 against.

**It is not** a claim that the default configuration reaches it. `DEFAULT_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` is
24,000; this run is at 48,000 with a marker. `AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §7 is where that gap is
stated, and it does not close here.

**It is not** SOTA. Agentmemory V4 reports 96.20% on the same benchmark at the same QA-accuracy
denominator; the gap is **6.40 pp**. What it does establish is a position that this campaign has not
held before: **+2.30 pp over Raw-RAG (87.5%)** and **+4.00 pp over memoricai (85.8%)**, both of which
were ahead of every previous artifact.

### 13.209.4 The one pool that is left, and it is not a thinking pool

Per capability, against the 96.20% target, the room is:

| capability | now | at 96% | room | is thinking the lever? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **MR** | 93 / 121 = 76.86% | 116 | **+23** | **no — measured +1 with thinking on** |
| KU | 63 / 72 = 87.50% | 69 | +6 | untested on this route |
| IE | 143 / 150 = 95.33% | 144 | +1 | closed |
| TR | 120 / 127 = 94.49% | 122 | +2 | mostly closed |
| ABS | 30 / 30 = 100.00% | 30 | 0 | closed |

**MR holds 23 of the 32 remaining questions, and §13.209.2 has just measured that thinking does not
move it.** The next dispatch therefore has to be a multi-session experiment — candidate selection,
session ordering or the aggregation the reader is asked to perform — and not another reader-mode
experiment. `§13.204.4` already argued that a `KU` experiment is a room or ranking experiment; the
same argument applies to `MR` with the additional fact that its reader is now known to be the wrong
lever.

### 13.209.5 Predictions for the next multi-session dispatch

Registered before it is built, so the answer cannot be chosen afterwards:

1. A multi-session change that reorders or re-selects candidates moves **MR ≥ +8** while moving IE
   by less than 3 in either direction, because IE's evidence is one turn and a re-selection cannot
   reach it.
2. TR moves by less than 3 in either direction, because its +22 came from the reader and the change
   does not touch the reader.
3. The four-repetition spread stays at or below 2 pp, as it has on the two most recent runs (1.00 and
   2.00) and against the 4.75 pp of `40722772896`.

Stopping rule: **one dispatch.** If MR moves less than 8 while the other predictions hold, the
conclusion is that MR's remaining 23 questions are a knowledge limit of this reader rather than a
selection limit of this pipeline, and the third prediction is what distinguishes those two.

## 13.210 Every artifact now names the file it graded

**Shipped 2026-11-01.** The audited defect is `AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §5's first bullet, and
what ships is the half of the repair that needs no prior knowledge.

`AblationReport.dataset` is a **name** (`longmemeval`), `questionCount` is a **sample size**, and
neither says which bytes were read. The workflow fetches that name from
`longmemeval-cleaned/resolve/main/longmemeval_s_cleaned.json`, a mutable pointer: the contents can
change under the name with no commit in this repository, and no artifact could have recorded it. A
score is therefore a property of (pipeline, file) and only one of the two was ever written down.

### 13.210.1 What is recorded, and where

| layer | file | change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| digest | `packages/cortex-eval/src/dataset-fingerprint.ts` | **new**: `fingerprintBytes(Uint8Array) -> "sha256:<64 hex>"` |
| report | `packages/cortex-eval/src/report.ts` | `datasetFingerprint?` on the report and on `AblationReportOptions`; one line in the Markdown, directly under the dataset name |
| arm | `packages/cortex-eval/src/bench-memory-arm.ts` | forwarded from the entry point, because the arm is handed the dataset already parsed |
| entry point | `packages/cortex-memory/bench/run-ablation.ts` | **one** read of the file: the buffer is parsed for the questions and hashed for the digest; printed with the file's instance count beside it |
| tests | `__tests__/dataset-fingerprint.test.ts` (8), `__tests__/report-dataset-fingerprint.test.ts` (3) | FIPS vectors, bytes-not-string, file identity, absent-renders-absent, JSON round-trip |

Two design decisions worth their own sentence:

1. **One read, not two.** There is no `fingerprintDatasetFile(path)`. The entry point reads the file
   for its JSON anyway, and a second read of a 110 MB file is a way for the digest and the questions
   to come from two different reads of one run. `tools/export-census.mjs` called the unused export an
   orphan and was right.
2. **Hashing bytes, not the decoded string.** `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` then hashing the string
   maps every invalid byte sequence to U+FFFD, so two different malformed files would collide — a
   fingerprint whose collision set contains "any pair of malformed files" is not a fingerprint.

### 13.210.2 What it buys, stated narrowly

- **Comparability becomes checkable.** Two artifacts can now be asked whether they graded the same
  file, and the answer does not depend on anyone having pinned a digest in advance.
- **The absent branch is informative.** A dataset constructed in code (`longmemeval-mini`) has no
  file, and the field is **absent** rather than empty, so "read no file" and "predates the field" are
  distinguishable bytes — the rule `abstentionReasons` already states for the census.
- **A probe is separable from a full run.** `LIMIT=220` over the same file has the same digest and a
  different `questionCount`; the log line prints both plus the file's own instance count, so the
  three cannot be confused.

### 13.210.3 What it does not buy, and this is the part that cannot be repaired later

**The seventeen archived artifacts have no digest and never will.** That includes `41284575092`, the
89.80% headline. No claim in any document of this repository can be checked against the file that
produced it, and the gap does not close retroactively — the digest is not recoverable from a score.

**Refusing is not implemented.** Haki's harness checks a sha256 before every run and refuses a
different file; this one now records and still refuses nothing. The pinned expected value has to be
taken from the file, the file is not present in this environment, and a guessed digest would be the
defect this campaign keeps finding in other people's harnesses. So the ordering is: **recording now,
refusal once a real digest exists to pin** — and until then a mismatch, if one ever occurred, would
be visible in the artifact rather than blocking the run.

### 13.210.4 The prediction this registers

For the next multi-session dispatch (§13.209.5), the artifact's `datasetFingerprint` will be present,
`questionCount` will be 500, and the digest will be **equal** to the digest of every later run in this
campaign unless the upstream file moves. If a later run's digest differs while `questionCount` is
unchanged, the comparison between the two is void and the older number is not a baseline — it is a
different population. That condition is stated now so that it cannot be discovered as a surprise
after a delta has already been published.

## 13.211 The multi-session loss is the enumeration, and the instrument that would fix it was measured first

**Shipped 2026-11-01, as a reading and a guard rather than a treatment.** `AUDIT-MR-ENUMERATION.md`
holds the whole of it; this section registers what follows and what was deliberately not dispatched.

### 13.211.1 The five readings that decide the next increment

Read from `41284575092` (48,000 characters, `ellipsis`, thinking on `multi-session` + `temporal`, four
repetitions, `449 / 500`). Each is a count over that artifact and nothing else.

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| MR questions wrong on all four repetitions | 22 (of 121; 93.75 average correct) |
| …whose recorded answer equals the number of Step 1 lines | **22 of 22** |
| MR failures that are numeric golds | 28 of 28 (the 16 non-numeric MR questions are correct) |
| …whose gold digits appear in the offered evidence | **18 of 22** stable failures |
| …that are totals or two-operand derivations, with a Step 1 of 0–2 lines | 10 of 22 |

The first row is the one that reorders the work. `ENUMERATION_CONTRACT` forbids re-filtering the list at
Step 2, and the reader obeys it exactly: the aggregate step has not made a single error in this run.
Every increment that audits or rewrites Step 2 — a second pass over the list, a checking prompt, a
"recompute carefully" instruction — is aimed at a step with a zero error rate. The list is the treatment.

The fourth row retires the retrieval hypothesis for this capability. The `48,000`-character budget
discards about two thirds of a haystack and **the answer's own digits are still in the window on 18 of
the 22**, so a wider top-k, a second index, or a reranker is aimed at a cell that is already mostly
filled. This is also where `AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §5's first bullet stops being a footnote: no
archived artifact carries a dataset digest, so all five readings are comparable only to themselves.

### 13.211.2 Implemented, measured, reverted: the classifier widening

§2's last two rows are the population `OPERAND_CONTRACT` was written for — *"identify the numbers this
question needs"*, with **a sum** among its named operations — and the classifier still does not route
them there. Extending `DERIVATION` to read totals as derivations was implemented, unit-tested and then
**measured against the same artifact before any dispatch**:

| pattern | newly reached | currently correct | currently wrong |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in total` / `altogether` / `combined` | 6 | 4 | 2 |
| `total <quantifier>` | 10 | 7 | 3 |
| `page count` / `word count` / `view count` | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| **total** | **19** | **13** | **6** |

**Thirteen correct questions would be re-contracted to reach six wrong ones, and no sub-pattern has an
upside larger than its downside.** The property that separates the two groups is not in the question
text: a correct total and a wrong total are both *"the total X over period Y"*, and the difference is in
the evidence and the gold. So no classifier over questions can reach the six without moving the
thirteen. The change was reverted rather than dispatched, and the measurement is recorded here so that
the next person to notice §2's two rows finds the arithmetic before the implementation.

What ships from it is `question-shape-parity.test.ts`. The classifier's docblock claimed a guard in
`cortex-eval` that did not exist and had the dependency direction backwards; the test now pins the
shipped boundary question by question, and imports the other package's **source** rather than its
barrel — a parity test comparing a source file against a stale `dist` reports the build state, which is
how the first version of this file read two different values on six questions.

### 13.211.3 The three registered increments, and what each must show

**P0 — the strong half of the contract, which no configuration can reach.** The requirement is that a
reasoning model scores better than a non-reasoning one on the same contract and the same window, and
**half of it is still unmeasured**: every artifact of this campaign is `deepseek-chat` with
`thinking: enabled`, and the disabled side of the same configuration is `41203245999` — so *"does
thinking help"* is answered (`+24` questions, §13.209) while *"does a stronger model help"* is not.
`DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, `DEEPSEEK_MODEL` and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` are already read from the environment, so
an OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be pointed at today without a code change; what is missing is a
second **named** provider in `llm-factory.ts` so that the reader's identity string records which
backend produced a number, and so that switching is a dispatch input rather than an env substitution
nobody can see in the artifact.

*Prediction:* a reasoning-capable model from a different family raises MR by at least 8 and TR by at
least 4 at the same `48,000`, with `ABS` unchanged (its gold is a decline and 30/30 already). *Falsified
if* MR moves by less than 4 — that would say the remaining loss is a property of the task's evidence
rather than of the reader, and the next increment is `P1`'s retention rule rather than a model swap.

**P1 — a `KU` retention rule.** `AUDIT-MR-ENUMERATION.md` §4: `KU` reads 63/72, five of its seven stable
failures answered with the superseded value although the instruction already forbids it and the
evidence is time-monotone on all 72 questions, and one has the update **absent from the window**
entirely. The treatment is therefore retention, not wording: keep the latest turn of each session in
the window before the relevance budget spends itself. *Prediction:* `KU` +3 or more, `MR` and `TR`
inside ±3, no capability below its `41284575092` reading.

**P2 — quotation-grounded enumeration.** §5 of the audit shows that groundedness on a long window
**cannot be audited after the fact**: three offline checks — token coverage, longest contiguous run,
timestamp validity — all had zero discriminating power between correct and incorrect questions, because
a 12,000-token block contains every common word, enumerated items are paraphrases rather than
quotations, and a session's turns share a date. It can only be *produced*, by asking for a quotation
per line and dropping the lines whose quotation is not in the evidence. *Acceptance:* the drop rate is
reported per capability, and a question whose lines are all dropped abstains rather than counting zero.

### 13.211.4 Why this round dispatched nothing

Three candidate treatments were examined and one was measured; the one that was measured came out
negative, and the other two are code changes with registered predictions rather than configurations to
flip. The one configuration that *could* be dispatched today is the `thinking: disabled` control, and it
is not worth a five-hour run: its reading already exists as `41203245999`, and repeating it would
measure a question that is answered. What is not answerable by any dispatch of this workflow is the
second provider, which is the next structural increment — and it is structural precisely because the
artifact currently cannot say which backend produced a number, which is the same defect as a report that
cannot say which dataset file it graded.
