## 13.212 The reader's backend is a declaration, and the only public model-swap evidence says the effect is small

**Shipped 2026-11-01, as a code change with a registered measurement.** This section registers the
provider axis, states why the name could not take an input of its own, and **amends §13.211.3's
prediction before the run it applies to**, on evidence that did not exist when that prediction was
written. The amendment is recorded rather than silently applied, because a prediction moved after
the data is a different practice from a prediction moved before it.

### 13.212.1 What shipped

Four facts that were one fact before:

| fact | before §13.212 | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| which backend a run declared | nothing — the only provider was the default one | `providerId`: `deepseek` \| `zhipu` \| `custom` |
| which endpoint it reached | `baseUrl`, and a host-derived `provider` string | `baseUrl`, plus `endpoint`: `matches` \| `overridden` \| `none` |
| which variable held the credential | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, hardcoded | the declared provider's own variable |
| how an operator selected a backend | by substituting a key into a variable named after a different vendor | by naming it in the `model` value |

The `provider` field it replaces was **two kinds of fact in one field**: `'deepseek'` for one host —
a vendor — and `'openai-compatible'` for every other host — a protocol. Two runs could not be
compared on it, and a second vendor could only be reached by an act the artifact could not show.
`providerId` is a declaration; `endpoint` is the check on it; the host is already printed beside both.

### 13.212.2 Why the name rides `model` and not a 25th input

`benchmark-cortex-memory.yml` declares **24** `workflow_dispatch` inputs.
`tools/__tests__/test_dispatch_inputs.py::test_no_workflow_sits_at_the_input_ceiling` **fails a
workflow at 25**, so the ceiling is not GitHub's number but one below it — the headroom exists
precisely so that the next axis does not have to argue with the API at dispatch time. This is the
third time the surface has forced a state into an existing value (§13.188's turn-cap width,
§13.197.4's thinking reach), and the third time the grammar is what keeps it from becoming a
free-text field:

| `model` value | provider | model | note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-chat` | `deepseek` | `deepseek-chat` | every archived dispatch; unchanged |
| `deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro` | `deepseek` | `deepseek-v4-pro` | explicit spelling of the default |
| `zhipu:glm-4.6` | `zhipu` | `glm-4.6` | a different family |
| `zhipu:` | `zhipu` | `glm-4.6` | the provider's default; a complete request |
| `custom:qwen2.5:7b` | `custom` | `qwen2.5:7b` | first colon splits, so tags survive |
| `qwen2.5:7b` | — | — | **refused**, with the message naming `custom:qwen2.5:7b` |

The two facts are recorded together because a model id is meaningless without the endpoint that
serves it: `glm-4.6` is not a DeepSeek model and `deepseek-chat` is not a Zhipu one. An artifact that
carried the model and left the provider to be inferred from the host would be the §13.110 defect
again — the number with no record of what produced it.

**Backward compatibility is a property, not an intention.** Unprefixed values resolve to `deepseek`,
whose implied domain contains `api.deepseek.com`, so every archived configuration renders
`reader=deepseek:<model>@api.deepseek.com` — the exact bytes it rendered before. The clause
`endpoint=override` appears only when the declaration and the reach disagree, which is never true
for an archived run.

### 13.212.3 The credential defect this repairs, stated as a failure

Before this section, a Zhipu run had to put its key into `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. Two consequences, both
observable:

1. **The artifact could not say which backend answered.** The host could, incidentally, but the
   field that existed to say it returned `'openai-compatible'` — the protocol, which is true of every
   provider and therefore distinguishes none.
2. **A missing credential produced a message naming the wrong vendor.**
   `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is required for natural-language benchmark` on a run that had been dispatched
   as a Zhipu run sends the operator to look for a variable that is not the problem.

`requireKey` now reads `provider.credentialVariable`, and the refusal names it *and* the provider:
`ZHIPU_LLM_API_KEY is required for natural-language benchmark (reader provider "zhipu")`. The
association between a provider and its credential variable is a kind of fact this repository has
been bitten by twice: `ZHIPU_BASE_URL` belongs to the **embedding** factory, so the reader's Zhipu
endpoint is `ZHIPU_LLM_BASE_URL` — a shared name would have made a dispatch that moved the
embeddings silently move the reader, and the artifact would have shown two changed backends for one
intent.

### 13.212.4 The amendment to §13.211.3's prediction, and the evidence for it

§13.211.3 predicted, for this exact increment: *"a reasoning-capable model from a different family
raises MR by at least 8 and TR by at least 4 at the same 48,000, with ABS unchanged; falsified if MR
moves by less than 4."* That was written from the shape of the MR loss (§13.211.1) and **before any
public measurement of a model swap on a memory benchmark had been located**. Two now have been, and
they point the other way.

**Mem0, *Bring Your Own Key: Accuracy, Cost & Latency by Model*, 2026-10-20.** Seventeen models run
on LoCoMo's 1,540 questions with *"only the model that extracts memories changed; everything else
stayed the same"* — the same one-variable design as this increment, on the same benchmark family:

| model | accuracy | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 93.5% | most accurate tested |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 93.4% | half the price |
| GLM-5.3 Flash | **93.0%** | slowest tested (86.5 s p95) |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | **92.9%** | best value |
| GPT-6 Luna | 92.6% | |
| GPT-5 mini | 92.6% | |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | 92.3% | |
| Mem0's own default | 92.5% | the dashed line in their chart |
| GPT-4o-mini | 91.3% | |
| Mistral Nemo | 84.1% | least accurate tested |

The whole range is **9.4 points**, and it is a *price* range: the cheap end is where the loss is. The
**frontier band is 1.2 points wide** (92.3–93.5) across seven models from four vendors, and the two
families this increment compares sit **0.1 point apart** on it. A second, independent swap — Roampal's
model-swap run on a corrected LoCoMo, 20B open model against GPT-4o-mini — moves TagCascade from
74.1% to 76.6% (**+2.5**) and CE-Only from 74.4% to 75.9% (**+1.5**).

So the honest point expectation for a frontier-to-frontier swap, on this class of benchmark, is
**+1 to +3 points**, and `MR +8` is outside what any public measurement supports. §13.211.3's number
is therefore amended **before the run**, and the original is left in place above rather than edited:
a registered prediction that turned out to be too optimistic is a fact about the registration, and
deleting it would hide the one thing this document exists to show.

**The amended registration.**

- *Point expectation:* MR **+1 to +3**, TR **+1 to +3**, ABS unchanged (its gold is a decline and
  30/30 already). Outside `[−1, +4]` on MR falsifies the point expectation in the direction it lands.
- *Decision rule, which is what the run is actually for.* Three outcomes, three different next
  increments, and none of them is "run it again":

  | MR delta | reading | next increment |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | **≥ +4** | the reader *is* a live constraint at this window; the contract is saturating it | a per-reader-class contract: `model-portability.ts` already buckets readers, and the pair (reader, contract) becomes the unit rather than the reader alone |
  | within ±4 | the reader is **not** the constraint; the loss is in the list | P2's quotation-grounded enumeration (§13.211.3), with P1's retention rule unchanged |
  | **≤ −4** | the second reader is worse on *this* task | report it as a finding about LoCoMo's MR shape — 28 of 28 MR failures are numeric golds, which is an arithmetic task, not a recall one — not as a failed dispatch |

- *Also recorded, because it is the cost half of the same question and §13.211.3 did not name it:*
  **tokens per answered question**, from the artifact's own usage block (`prompt_tokens`,
  `completion_tokens`). A reasoning reader that buys +2 points for triple the completion tokens is a
  different product decision from one that buys +2 for the same tokens, and the artifact can already
  tell the two apart. Nothing here predicts which; it predicts only that the number is reported
  beside the accuracy rather than after it.

### 13.212.5 What this does not do, and why the omission is deliberate

**`thinking` is always sent, for every provider.** `buildReader` passes `{type: mode}` unconditionally,
which honours §13.197's treatment on DeepSeek and on Zhipu (GLM-4.5 and above accept the same field).
A third-party endpoint that rejects an unknown request field would fail at first call. The repair
would be a per-provider "does this endpoint accept `thinking`" declaration — a knob that could be
pointed at a combination no registration names, which is what §13.197.4 refused for the reach
grammar. It is registered here as a known limitation rather than shipped unmeasured:
`custom` is the escape hatch, and the honest statement is "this provider must speak the DeepSeek
`thinking` field", not "this provider is supported".

**The reranker keeps its own provider axis.** `CORTEX_RERANK_PROVIDER` already names three backends;
this section does not fold it into the reader's table, because the two are selected independently and
a shared declaration would make one dispatch's choice silently move the other.

**One thing it fixed as a side effect, and that would otherwise have been a silent break.**
`rerank-factory`'s `llm` backend read `DEEPSEEK_MODEL` directly as a model id. With the grammar in
place, a dispatch that selected `zhipu:glm-4.6` for the *reader* would have sent `zhipu:glm-4.6` as
a model id to the *reranker's* endpoint — a failure in a stage the dispatch never mentioned. It now
reads through `readModelSelection`, which is the one parser, and a test pins both spellings.

### 13.212.6 The probe: the axis works, and the second provider's tier does not carry this prompt

Run `41346610318`, dispatch `master` @ `b254e29`, `limit=20`, `ablation_runs=1`,
`temperature=0`, `model=zhipu:glm-4.6`, `thinking=disabled`. **Failed at 12 of 20 questions on
`LLM request failed: 429`** after the retry policy spent its five attempts. The artifact is a
progress checkpoint (`reached: 12`, `total: 20`), not a report, so it carries no `reader` line —
that line is written into the final report, which this run never produced.

**What the run did establish.** The declared provider reached the wire: `DEEPSEEK_MODEL:
zhipu:glm-4.6` is printed in the job env, the grammar maps it to `providerId: 'zhipu'` and
`baseUrl: 'https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4'` (five unit tests, including the refusal for an
unrecognised prefix), and a `429` is a provider-side rate answer rather than a credential or wiring
error — the same workflow serves 4,000-call runs against the other endpoint with the same code path.
Twelve questions were answered by a model that is not the default one, which is twelve more than any
earlier artifact in this campaign.

**What it established about the provider, which is the more useful half.** Two arms ran in the same
job, on the same endpoint, at the same time:

| arm | questions reached | wall clock | throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference-pipeline` | **20 / 20** | 193 s | **6.20 q/min** |
| `cortex-memory` | **12 / 20** (then 429) | 512 s | **1.41 q/min** |

Same endpoint, same minute, a **4.4× difference**, and the one variable is the prompt: the memory arm
sends the `48,000`-character window (≈12k tokens) and the reference pipeline does not. So the
binding constraint is **tokens per minute**, not requests per minute — the account's tier is sized
for the small prompts and is exhausted by the large ones. This run does not separate TPM from
concurrency, and the next attempt should: a probe that sends the same window at half the length
distinguishes a token budget from a slot budget.

**What that implies for the registered scale, computed rather than estimated.** The full comparison is
`500 × 4` on each side. At the measured rates: `2,000 / 6.20 = 323 min` for the pipeline side plus
`2,000 / 1.41 = 1,418 min` for the memory side, **≈ 1,741 min ≈ 29 h**, against the arm's
`CORTEX_MEMORY_BUDGET_MINUTES=340` and a 350-minute job ceiling. **The job budget is 5.1× too small
for this provider at this window.** No amount of retry tuning closes a 5× gap, which is why the next
step is capacity — a higher tier, or a second credential whose tier matches the prompt — and not a
code change.

**And that is what the declaration bought.** With §13.212 in place, a second credential is one
dispatch away: `model=custom:<id>` plus `CORTEX_READER_BASE_URL`/`CORTEX_READER_MODEL` in the job env
needs no source edit, and the artifact will name it. Before this section the same move required
editing the workflow's `env:` and putting the key into `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, which no artifact records.

**Registered consequence.** P0's measurement stays open; its blocker is now stated as a number
(5.1× the budget at 1.41 q/min) rather than as "needs a second provider". The increment that
unblocks it is either a higher TPM tier or a smaller window — and the second one changes the
treatment, so it is a different registration, not a workaround for this one.

## 13.213 The shipped default becomes the published configuration, and 96,000 is refused on its own pair

**Shipped 2026-11-02, as a code change plus a decision.** Two things happen here and they are one
thing: a library whose default is a configuration none of its published numbers were taken at is
offering a product it never measured. §13.213.2 is the pair that decides where the default goes;
§13.213.4 is the walk-back of a registered increment that a reading says was never aimed at a
mechanism.

### 13.213.1 Three numbers for one budget, and a fourth in a quotation

| where | value | what it describes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS` | **24,000** | what a caller who passes no `maxPromptChars` gets |
| the register, since §13.206 | **48,000** | what the published 89.80% was measured under |
| sixteen of seventeen archived artifacts | **48,000** or **96,000** | what the campaign actually ran |
| the dispatch input's empty default | **falls through to 24,000** | what a dispatch gets by forgetting the input |

A dispatch that leaves `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` blank does not run the configuration anyone
has read about; it runs one **no artifact in this repository was ever produced under**. That is not
a documentation defect. The next dispatch written from the register and dispatched without the input
measures a third configuration while reporting it as the second, and the difference is nine
questions on the roster (§13.82: 394 → 403).

**A number in this round's own reading was also wrong, and it is corrected here rather than
quietly.** `AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §7.2 says *"§13.82 measured 24,000 → 48,000 at MR +14pp"*.
§13.82.1 reads MR **78 → 83**, which is **+5 questions, +4.1 points**. The **+14.3pp** in that
section is the lift inside the 35 questions that crossed 85% coverage — a subgroup, not the
capability. Quoting it as MR's gain overstates the budget's value by 3.5×, which matters because the
whole of §13.213.3 is an argument about how much the budget is worth per token.

### 13.213.2 The pair that decides 96,000

`41254359622` (96,000) against `41284575092` (48,000). Both `thinking` on `multi-session+temporal`,
`ellipsis`, `ask=operands+operand-gap`, `relevanceTopK=256`, same reader, same 500 questions, four
repetitions each.

```
$ readout-arm-run.py --config <96k> --treatment cortex_memory_ask <48k>
  same     32 field(s)
  differ   1 field(s):
    UNDECLARED  maxPromptChars: 96000 -> 48000
  verdict: 1 field(s) differ, 0 declared by --treatment, 1 undeclared
```

One field. **No registration had ever named it**, which is why `--config` calls it undeclared: the
pair is clean and the *question* was never asked in writing. That is the gap this section closes.

```
$ readout-arm-run.py --null <96k> <48k>
  prompt identity: 0/500 byte-identical, 500 differ
  differing           500   452.25   449.00   -3.25    109    5.5%  5.08       5   5.51e-04
    per repetition delta: [-2, -1, 0, -10]
    unanimous gains: ['3ba21379']
    unanimous losses: ['0977f2af', '10d9b85a', 'a1cc6108', 'd24813b1']
  verdict: the aggregate (-3.25) is inside the 10.15 band, but 5 question(s) moved in every one of
           4 repetitions and the null expects 5.5e-04 of them -- the reading is those questions
```

**The mean is not the result; the five are.** The aggregate is 3.25 questions inside a 10.15-question
band, and 109 of 500 questions flipped at least once — which is churn. Five questions converted in
all four repetitions, and the null expects five in two thousand runs. The direction is 4:1 against
48,000, and the four are:

| question | capability | gold | 96,000 | 48,000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `10d9b85a` days at workshops/lectures/conferences in April | MR | `3 days` | 3 | **2** |
| `a1cc6108` how old when Alex was born | MR | `11` | 11 | **evidence dump** |
| `d24813b1` what to bake for a gathering | IE | a grounded preference | recommendation | **generic** |
| `0977f2af` gadget bought before the Air Fryer | KU | `Instant Pot` | correct | **`None`** |
| `3ba21379` which vehicle model I am working on | KU | `Ford F-150 pickup truck` | **Mustang GT350R** | correct |

Per capability, summed over four repetitions (`96k − 48k`): **MR +11, TR +6, IE −2, KU −2**. So the
budget's whole case is MR, which is the capability the campaign is behind on — and the case is four
questions, three of them "one item short".

### 13.213.3 The decision: 48,000 becomes the shipped default, 96,000 is not adopted

**What adopting 96,000 would buy:** 452.25 / 500 = **90.45%**, and the two MR questions above.

**What it would cost:** `llmUsage` moves 31.1M → 50.3M prompt tokens (**+61.7%**) for a dispatch,
8,830 tokens per call against 5,504, and 2.05× the evidence characters in every prompt a user ever
sends. The four recovered questions are ≈ **+0.8 point**, which is real, and this section does not
pretend it is zero.

**Why the answer is still no, stated as the trade it is.** The four are lost for one reason: a
specific turn fell outside a *prefix of the relevance ranking*, i.e. at the tail. Doubling the room
recovers them by carrying twice as much of everything, including the fifth and sixth hundred turns
that have never been read — 85.3% of the carried turns share no content word with their question
(§13.213.6). The same four are recoverable **by ranking**, at unchanged cost, and that is a code
increment rather than a flag. Buying them with a budget that doubles every prompt in the product
would make the cheaper repair invisible, because the symptom it treats would be gone.

So: **48,000 is the default from this commit**, and the four questions are registered as the target
of the ranking increment (§13.213.7), with the prediction that a ranking repair recovers ≥3 of 4 at
48,000's token cost.

| configuration | roster | MR | tokens per call | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24,000 | 394 | 78 | — | was the default; never an archived artifact |
| **48,000** | **449 = 89.80%** | **93** | **5,504** | **published, and the default from §13.213** |
| 96,000 | 452.25 = 90.45% | 97 | 8,830 | refused: +0.65 inside a 3.25-wide reading, for +61.7% tokens |

*MR in this table is the artifact's `featureMetrics.perCapability.correct` — one repetition. The
four-repetition sums are 375 → 386, which is where the campaign's "MR 77.5%" comes from (93.75 /
121); the two conventions differ by 0.75 of a question and the register uses the per-repetition one
because §13.82's 78 → 83 was quoted that way.*

### 13.213.4 P1 is cancelled: the KU retention rule was aimed at a mechanism the artifact does not show

`AUDIT-MR-ENUMERATION.md` §4 states the direction for `KU`: *"the turn carrying the update was
discarded by the budget … which is why it is a registered increment rather than a shipped change"*,
and §8 lists it as P1 — **keep the latest turn of every session in the window**.

The artifact says otherwise. Reading the seven `KU` questions wrong on all four repetitions of
`41284575092` against their own `promptTexts`:

| question | gold | answer | gold-bearing content in the window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mortgage pre-approval | `$400,000` | `$350,000` | **yes**, block 44, 111 days after block 4's `$350,000` |
| Instagram followers now | `1300` | `1250` | **yes**, block 48 "close to 1300", after block 17's `1250` |
| pre-1920 coins | `38` | `37` | **yes**, as `37` plus block 45 "I just added a new coin" |
| usual gym time | `6:00 pm` | `7:00 pm …` | **yes**, block 58 states `6:00 pm` |
| where the old sneakers are | `in a shoe rack in my closet` | `Under my bed` | **yes**, block 50 "storing your old sneakers in a shoe rack" |
| gym more often than before | `Yes` | prose decline | **yes** |
| gadget before the Air Fryer | `Instant Pot` | prose decline | **yes**, six mentions |

**Seven of seven carry the evidence.** The retention rule would have changed none of them: there is
no dropped update turn to retain. Three are not supersession misses at all —

- **the coins question is arithmetic across turns**: `37` stated, then "I just added a new coin" →
  `38`. No turn states 38, which is true and is not the same as "unfixable": the *derivation* is in
  the window and the reader applied neither operand to the other;
- **two are hedged or planned statements the gold treats as completed** — "I think I'm close to
  1300" and "planning to store your old sneakers in a shoe rack". A reader that prefers the explicit
  earlier value is being wrong about a gold that is itself an inference, and no retention rule
  addresses that.

So `AUDIT-MR-ENUMERATION.md` §4's mechanism sentence is corrected in place, and the P1 increment is
**withdrawn rather than postponed**: an increment aimed at a mechanism the evidence does not show is
a round bought with nothing.

### 13.213.5 What replaces it

Two candidates, both from the seven, neither dispatchable today:

1. **A delta step in the counting contract.** `ENUMERATION_CONTRACT`'s Step 2 says *"do not
   re-filter the list"*, which is right and incomplete: it should also ask whether any evidence
   sentence **adds to, removes from, or replaces** an item in the list. That is the coins question,
   and by §2's shape table it is also the MR failures whose answer is one short of the gold.
2. **A stated-uncertainty reading.** "close to 1300" and "planning to store" are not facts; a
   question that asks for the *current* value needs a rule for hedged updates. That is a wording
   change with a 2-question ceiling and no measurement design yet — written down so it is not
   rediscovered as a good idea.

### 13.213.6 What the room is actually spent on

The refusal in §13.213.3 rests on one measurement, taken from the 48,000 artifact's own `turns`
arrays — every carried turn, compared with its question after removing a stoplist:

| capability | carried turns | share sharing **no** content word with the question | share of characters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MR` | 21,237 | **91.1%** | — |
| `TR` | 22,971 | **91.2%** | — |
| `ABS` | 2,140 | 78.8% | — |
| `KU` | 4,658 | 70.1% | — |
| `IE` | 9,529 | 66.9% | — |
| **all** | **60,535** | **85.3%** | **65.5%** |

Two thirds of the characters in a prompt, and five sixths of the turns, are text that shares no word
with the question it is offered for. Some of that is paraphrase the metric cannot see, and §5 of
`AUDIT-MR-ENUMERATION.md` already established that post-hoc groundedness checks have **no
discriminating power** — so this is not a claim that the turns are worthless. It is a claim about
what the budget *buys at the margin*: when the four questions above need 48,000 more characters,
the room they are added into is two-thirds unrelated text, and the marginal character is drawn from
the tail of a ranking whose head is already mostly off-topic.

That is why the repair belongs in the ranking and not in the budget, and why the number above is
stated as a floor on the waste rather than as an estimate of it.

### 13.213.7 The ranking increment, registered

*Claim:* the four questions 48,000 loses unanimously are lost at the **tail** of the relevance
prefix, and a ranking repair reaches ≥3 of 4 at 48,000's token cost.

*Instrument:* the 48,000 artifact's own per-question windows — for each of the four, the position of
the decisive turn in the delivered order, and the overlap between that turn and the question. If the
decisive turn is delivered but ranked low, the claim's premise holds and the repair is a re-rank. If
it is **not** delivered at any rank, the premise fails and the budget was the only lever after all.

*Falsified by:* all four decisive turns already sitting in the top quartile of their windows, which
would say the ranking is not what excluded them and the 96,000 gain came from somewhere else.

**Nothing is dispatched on it this round**, and the reason is the same as §13.211.4's: the
instrument reads an artifact that already exists, so it costs nothing and does not need capacity that
§13.212.6 measured at 5.1× the run budget.

### 13.213.8 The premise, checked before it costs anything

§13.213.7 says the four are lost "at the tail of the relevance prefix" and that ranking can reach
them. That is a claim about the artifact, so it was checked against the artifact in the same round
rather than left to the next one.

**`10d9b85a`, "how many days did I spend attending workshops, lectures, and conferences in April",
gold `3 days`:**

| window | turns delivered | turns containing `lecture` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 48,000 | 167 | **none** |
| 96,000 | 232 | one, at position **158 of 232** |

The 48,000 window carries the two-day workshop (position 152 of 167) and **does not carry the
lecture at all**, so the reader can only reach `2`. The 96,000 window carries both and answers `3`.

**What that settles, and what it does not.** It settles the symptom: the loss is a **missing
decisive turn**, not a misread one, and the missing content is evidence rather than noise. It does
**not** settle the repair. The premise of a ranking fix is that the turn is inside the admitted pool
and outside the cut — and the artifact records what was delivered, not what was admitted, so this
reading cannot tell whether that turn was ranked 160th or was never a candidate. `--pool` would
answer it on an artifact produced with retrieval attribution; `41284575092` predates that field.

**So the decision in §13.213.3 is provisional, and it says so with a reversal condition rather than
a preference:**

> If the ranking instrument cannot show that the missing turn is recoverable at 48,000 — i.e. if it
> is absent from the admitted pool and not merely below the cut — then **96,000 is the only measured
> lever**, and it should be adopted on a registered prediction of `MR +4 ± 2` with the four
> questions named in advance, at +61.7% prompt tokens, rather than left refused.

That is a different statement from "96,000 is worse", and it is the one the evidence supports. It
also gives the ranking increment a deadline: it is the cheaper repair only until someone shows it
cannot reach these four.

## 13.214 The pool table's total was a clamp of the sums, and it hid the gold the room reached past the pool

### 13.214.1 What the table said, and what its own rows said

`--pool` prints where the gold went, per capability, in four columns: never surfaced, cut by the budget,
beyond the pool, delivered. Each **row** clamps two differences that point in opposite directions — below
the pool's width the room refuses gold the ranking offered (`pool - carried`), above it the room reaches
gold the ranking never offered (`carried - pool`). The rows were right. The TOTAL was computed from the
summed `pool` and `carried`, so a capability running a surplus cancelled a capability running a shortfall
**before either clamp ran**:

| artifact | rows: cut | TOTAL printed | rows: beyond | TOTAL printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `41284575092` (48,000) | **707** | 654 (−7.5%) | **53** | **0** |
| `41254359622` (96,000) | **296** | 111 (−62.5%) | **185** | **0** |

The mechanism is the campaign's own per-turn cap. MR and TR deliver **past** the pool (32 and 21 gold
turns at 48,000), because a 400-character turn fits more turns than the 256-wide pool holds; ABS, IE and
KU are cut **short** of it (178, 210, 319). Clamped after summing, the surplus eats the shortfall.

**The zero is the part that matters.** 53 and 185 gold turns arrived from outside the pool, and the table
printed `0` — and the note that keys off that column, `N gold turn(s) arrived from outside the pool`,
therefore never fired either. A false zero is worse than a missing number: it is a measurement, it is in
the artifact's own units, and it says the opposite of the data.

This is `max(0, Σ) ≠ Σ max(0, ·)`, which is the arithmetic equivalent of §12.7's shape — a value reported
one way and stored another. The fix is one line of accumulation: the clamps are applied per record, and
the TOTAL is the sum of the column above it. A test now asserts that identity for every column, so a
future column fails loudly rather than silently ceasing to add up.

### 13.214.2 The four-way account, corrected

| quantity | 48,000 | 96,000 | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gold turns the dataset names | 7,516 | 7,516 | — |
| the ranking never surfaced | 361 | 361 | — |
| **cut by the budget** | **707** | **296** | −411 |
| **beyond the pool** | **53** | **185** | +132 |
| delivered | 6,501 | 7,044 | +543 |

The room's shortfall falls by 411 and its reach past the pool rises by 132, and the two are consistent
with `delivered` rising by 543. Two readings follow that the previous table could not support:

- **the ranking's reach is constant at 361.** Buying room does not change what the ranking surfaces;
  it changes how much of it the prompt can hold. §13.213's budget decision is therefore a decision about
  allocation, not about signal;
- **132 of the 543 gold turns the bigger room bought (24.3%) came from outside the ranking's pool.** A
  third of what 96,000 buys is evidence the ranking never offered, so no re-ranking of that pool can be
  responsible for it.

### 13.214.3 What that does to the registered ranking increment

§13.213.7 registered: *the four questions 48,000 loses unanimously are lost at the **tail** of the
relevance prefix, and a ranking repair reaches ≥3 of 4 at 48,000's token cost.* Checked against the pair
in the same round, on the question whose decisive turn can be located at all:

`10d9b85a`, gold `3 days`. The 48,000 window carries 167 turns and **none** contains `lecture`; the
96,000 window carries 232 and one does, at position 158. Its `goldRanks` are
`[-1, 10, 113, 141, 86, 9, 167, 241, 209, 233, -1]` with `pool = 9` and `carried` 9 → 11. So the two gold
turns the bigger room adds are the two with rank **−1**: they are the `beyond the pool` kind, and a
re-rank of a pool they are not in **cannot reach them by construction**.

**So the premise is falsified for the mechanism §13.213.7 named.** They were not at the tail of the
prefix. They were never in it.

What survives is a different repair, and the subset relation is what makes it visible: on all four
questions the 48,000 window is a **strict subset** of the 96,000 one, so the budget only ever removes.

| question | capability | turns at 48,000 | turns at 96,000 | share kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0977f2af` | KU | 55 | 119 | 46% |
| `10d9b85a` | MR | 167 | 232 | 72% |
| `a1cc6108` | MR | 181 | 243 | 74% |
| `d24813b1` | IE | 50 | 86 | 58% |

For `10d9b85a` the decisive turn sits at chronological 158 of a 232-turn session while 48,000's room
holds 167 of that same session. **The room was large enough to hold a set containing it; the selection
did not choose it.** That is a selection defect, not an ordering defect and not a budget defect, and its
repair costs no tokens.

### 13.214.4 The counterweight, stated before it is convenient

Only one of the four is a demonstrated missing-evidence case. On the other three the decisive content is
present in **both** windows:

| question | probe | 48,000 | 96,000 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0977f2af` | `instant pot` | positions 4, 26, 27, 29 | 9, 57, 58, 60 |
| `a1cc6108` | `alex` | 50, 51 | 50, 51 |
| `d24813b1` | `bak` | 16, 19, 20, 21, 38 | 17, 23, 36, 38, 40 |

So "the four are lost to a shared coverage mechanism" is not supported even after the mechanism was
renamed. One is coverage, three are something else — and a single increment cannot be credited with all
four. Any registration that promises ≥3 of 4 has to name which three and what the mechanism is, and this
section cannot.

### 13.214.5 The increment this registers instead

*Claim:* filling each selected session by **relevance order rather than chronological order**, at the
same 48,000-character budget, keeps the decisive turn of `10d9b85a` and does not lose the ordering
questions that chronological adjacency exists for.

*Instrument:* the same pair, read with `--pool` (the four-way account above) and `--paired` (per-question
transitions), plus `--caps` for the repetition band. The anchor is named in advance: `10d9b85a` must
convert, and its 48,000 window must contain `lecture`.

*Prediction:* `MR +4 ± 2` at equal prompt tokens — the same prediction §13.213.8 registered for
96,000, which is what makes the two directly comparable: the increment is only worth doing if it buys
the same thing for nothing.

*Falsified by:* `TR` or `ABS` falling outside the noise band. Chronological adjacency is load-bearing
for "which came first" and for period arithmetic, and a relevance order that pays `MR +4` with `TR −5`
is a worse trade at zero tokens than 96,000 is at +61.7%.

*Not dispatched this round.* The instrument work above is offline; the increment needs a product change
in window assembly and a dispatch, and §13.212.6 measured the run budget at 5.1× what the capacity
allows. It is registered so the next round starts from a falsifiable claim rather than a preference.

## 13.215 The window was already filled by relevance, and one premise of the falsifier was a unit error

**Written 2026-11-02, as a correction.** §13.214.3 registered a selection repair — "fill each session
by relevance rather than chronology, at the same budget" — on the reading that `10d9b85a`'s decisive
turn sat at chronological position 158 of a 232-turn session while 48,000's room held 167 of that same
session. This section checks that reading against the artifact it came from and finds the inference
invalid, the mechanism already shipped, and the actual loss somewhere neither §13.213.7 nor §13.214.5
looked.

### 13.215.1 The premise that was already true

`memoryArmConfig` on `41284575092`, verbatim:

| field | value |
| --- | --- |
| `relevanceSignal` | `retrieval-hybrid` |
| `relevanceUnits` | **`turn`** |
| `relevanceTopK` | `256` |
| `rerank.provider` | `none` |

`relevanceUnits: "turn"` is the whole of it. `chooseEvidence` dispatches on that field —
`session` and `session-fill` take the session paths, **everything else falls through to
`selectByRelevance`**, which sorts the admitted turns by `relevanceFor` descending and carries the
largest prefix that fits. So the shipped configuration has been filling the window **by relevance and
not by chronology** since the signal was wired, and the increment §13.214.5 registered as "the next
thing to do" is the thing that was already running.

That is checkable in the product rather than argued from the config:

```ts
// prompt.ts, selectByRelevance
const ranked = plan.turns
  .map((turn, arrival) => ({ turn, arrival, relevance: validateRelevance(...) }))
  .sort((a, b) => b.relevance - a.relevance || a.arrival - b.arrival);
```

`a.arrival - b.arrival` is only a tie-break, and it is reachable only between two turns the signal
scored identically.

### 13.215.2 The evidence that settles it, and it is a shape rather than a document

A chronological fill and a relevance fill make **different predictions about which turns a bigger
room adds**, and the difference is visible in the two artifacts without any new field:

- chronological fill carries turns `0..166` of the 232, so 48,000's window is a **contiguous prefix**
  of 96,000's;
- relevance fill carries the top 167 by score, so the 65 dropped turns are **scattered across the
  whole session** — and, because cosine similarity is not correlated with arrival, the dropped set
  reaches into the first quarter.

Measured on the four questions §13.214.5 named, using `turns[].text` as identity:

| question | 48,000 turns | 96,000 turns | dropped | kept positions span | dropped in first quarter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0977f2af` | 55 | 119 | 64 | **3 … 114** | 17 |
| `10d9b85a` | 167 | 232 | 66 | **0 … 227** | **0** |
| `a1cc6108` | 181 | 243 | 64 | **0 … 235** | **0** |
| `d24813b1` | 50 | 86 | 36 | **0 … 83** | 10 |

**Not one of the four is a contiguous prefix.** For `10d9b85a` the window keeps turn 227 while
dropping 66 earlier ones, and it drops **none** of the first 58. A chronological prefix cannot do
that under any budget, because it can only ever stop.

So the question is not whether the fill was chronological. It was not. The question is what the
removed 66 turns had in common, and the answer is in the field that was already there.

### 13.215.3 Where the loss actually is, per question, in the artifact's own counts

`goldOverlap` on `10d9b85a`, both budgets:

| field | 48,000 | 96,000 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `total` (gold, after the role filter) | 11 | 11 |
| `totalAll` (gold, before it) | 22 | 22 |
| `pool` (gold the ranking surfaced) | **9** | **9** |
| `carried` (gold delivered) | **9** | **11** |
| `goldRanks` | `[-1, 10, 113, 141, 86, 9, 167, 241, 209, 233, -1]` | same |

Two readings, and the first one is the one §13.214.3 got wrong:

1. **At 48,000, all nine gold turns the ranking surfaced were delivered.** `carried == pool == 9`.
   Nothing inside the pool was cut. The budget did not remove a single ranked gold turn on this
   question.
2. **The two the wider room adds are the two `-1`s** — gold turns with no rank, because
   `goldRanks` encodes "not in the pool" as `-1`. There are 256 candidate slots and 241 is in the
   pool, so a `-1` means rank ≥ 256 or a turn the retrieval never returned at all.

So `10d9b85a` is not a question the 48,000 room answered worse than the 96,000 room **from the pool**.
It is a question whose answer needed a turn the ranking placed below 256th, and the only way it
reached the reader was leftover room after every scored turn had been carried.

**`pool` is identical at both budgets — 9 and 9.** The ranking's reach does not move with room, which
is what §13.214.2 said in aggregate (361 and 361) and what this question shows at the level of one
question's gold.

### 13.215.4 The inference error, named

§13.214.3 read:

> For `10d9b85a` the decisive turn sits at chronological 158 of a 232-turn session while 48,000's room
> holds 167 of that same session. **The room was large enough to hold a set containing it; the
> selection did not choose it.**

The first clause is right and the second does not follow. `167` is the **cardinality** of the window;
`158` is a **position in arrival order**; and the window is not a prefix of arrival order. Comparing
them assumes the very thing the rest of the section sets out to doubt.

The two numbers would settle each other only if the fill were chronological — and if it were, the
position evidence in §13.215.2 would show contiguous prefixes. It does not. So `158 < 167` says
nothing about whether turn 158 was carried, and in fact it was not, because the ranking scored it
below the 167th-best.

**This is the unit error to keep.** "The room holds N turns" and "the room holds turns 0..N−1" are
the same statement only under arrival order. Once selection is by a signal, cardinality stops being
a statement about membership, and every argument of the form "the room was big enough" has to name
which set it means.

### 13.215.5 The instrument that would have caught it in one line, and now exists

The missing fact is not the ordering — the ordering is in the config — it is **how much of the
delivered evidence the ranking had scored at all**. `goldOverlap.pool` answers that for gold turns
only; on a question whose annotation names eleven turns out of two hundred and thirty-two it is
silent about the other 221.

`windowComposition` is that field, per record:

```ts
export type WindowComposition = {
  readonly turns: number;          // delivered turns
  readonly offered: number;        // of those, how many the ranking scored
  readonly offeredChars: number;   // characters spent on scored turns
  readonly unscoredChars: number;  // characters spent on turns the ranking never saw
};
```

Its contract, which is `goldOverlap`'s one layer out:

- **absent** when no ranking was consulted (`relevanceSignal: none`), because a composition of
  `offered: 0` over a full `unscoredChars` is the shape of a ranking that failed, and it is also the
  shape of a run where none existed;
- **present and zero-turn** when the window is genuinely empty, because that is a measurement;
- the two character columns are the whole of `sum(turn.length)` and a test asserts that identity on
  every fixture, so a third column cannot be added as a silent partition — the `max(0, Σ)` failure
  §13.214 is one section older than this one.

The characters are the **turn texts**, not the rendered prompt. The prompt carries per-turn decoration
and the session note, so the denominator of `maxPromptChars` is larger; the share this prints is a
share of delivered evidence, and it is not a share of the budget.

`tools/readout-arm-run.py --composition` prints it per capability with a `TOTAL` that is the column
sum, and refuses an artifact that predates the field (`exit 2`) rather than printing a table of
zeroes. Both `41284575092` and `41254359622` are such artifacts, which is the honest state: the
instrument exists and no run has carried it yet.

### 13.215.6 What it decides, and the increment this replaces §13.214.5 with

The field measures the one thing that separates the two remaining hypotheses, and they call for
different work:

| if | then the lever is | cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unscoredChars` is a large share | **room** — the window is spent on turns no re-rank can order, and the repair is a selection that refuses the unscored tail or a pool wide enough to score it | a product change, no tokens |
| `unscoredChars` is near zero | **pool width and recall** — every character delivered was scoreable, so the only thing that can find `10d9b85a`'s two `-1`s is a ranking that surfaces them | `relevanceTopK` 256 → 512, no extra LLM tokens |

`10d9b85a`'s own `pool` count points at the second row: `carried == pool` at 48,000 means the room was
not wasted on unscored turns **for gold**, and the two gold turns the wider room bought were beyond
rank 255. But eleven gold turns is not a population, and the gold account cannot see the 221
non-gold turns at all — which is exactly why the field had to exist before the claim could be made.

*Registered:* with `windowComposition` in the artifact, `relevanceTopK` 256 → 512 at the 48,000 budget
raises `MR` by at least 3, on the mechanism that `10d9b85a`'s decisive turns move from `-1` to a rank
inside the window.

*Falsified by:* `MR` moving by less than 2, **or** `windowComposition.offered / turns` falling when
the pool widens — the second would mean the wider pool is displacing scored turns rather than adding
to them, which is a different event and not the one registered.

*Not dispatched this round.* The instrument has to be in a run before the prediction can be judged,
and §13.212.6's capacity measurement (1.41 q/min at this window on the second provider) is about the
second provider, not about this one: a DeepSeek pass at the registered configuration is 299.6 minutes
against a 340-minute budget, so the dispatch is affordable and is the first item for the next round.

### 13.215.7 What this section withdraws

- **§13.213.7**'s "the four are lost at the tail of the relevance prefix, and a ranking repair
  reaches ≥3 of 4": withdrawn. They are not at the tail of the prefix — they are outside the prefix,
  and for `10d9b85a` two of them are outside the pool.
- **§13.214.3**'s "the room was large enough; the selection did not choose it": withdrawn, with the
  unit error named in §13.215.4.
- **§13.214.5**'s registered selection increment: withdrawn. The mechanism it registers is the
  shipped one.

What survives from §13.214 is its arithmetic: 707 / 296 cut, 53 / 185 beyond, 361 reach at both
budgets, and the `max(0, Σ)` repair. Those numbers are unchanged and are what §13.215.2 reads.

## 13.216 A `429` ended a five-hour campaign run, and the ladder meant to outlast it reached 31 seconds

### 13.216.1 The run, and what it left behind

`41346610318` was a 20-question probe of this arm at commit `b254e29`. It ran 6m25s of grading,
reached question 13 of 20 on the first repetition, and stopped:

    progress: died on cortex-memory run=0 q=13/20 id=6aeb4375 at +385.2s
    LLM request failed: 429
        at OpenAICompatibleLLM.post (.../packages/cortex-ai/src/llm/openai-compatible.ts:94:13)

The artifact it uploaded holds `reached: 12` and a stack trace. Twelve graded answers, no verdict,
and — this is the part that took a second read to notice — **no number anywhere saying a rate limit
had been hit**. The counters existed: `retryStats()` in `cortex-ai` reports `attempts`, `retried`,
`rateLimited`, `retryAfterHonoured`, `calls`, `retriedCalls`, `cleanCalls`, `exhaustedCalls` and
`retryRate`, and its own docblock says a retried request "is a fact about the run and belongs in the
run's artifact". Every published artifact of this campaign was written without it. The only place it
was printed was stderr, on the failure path, in a log that expires.

### 13.216.2 The measurement: what the ladder actually reached

`DEFAULT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS` is 120 s, and its docblock states the requirement — a throttle window
measured in minutes has to be reachable. Measured against a fetch that answers `429` forever, at the
defaults:

    status 429  attempts 6  retried 5  rateLimited 6  elapsedMs 31051

Six attempts, 31,051 ms. The waits are `1+2+4+8+16 = 31 s` and the sixth attempt is already the last
one, because `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` was 5. The budget was **3.9× the ladder** and never consulted: the
ceiling could not be reached by any input, so its adequacy was a claim about code that never ran.

That is the same defect the budget was introduced to fix, one layer down. The budget replaced a
counted retry limit because "what has to be exceeded is a duration, and an attempt count implies a
different duration for every `baseDelayMs`" — and the count stayed, binding first, so the duration
the comment requires was never exceeded in any run this campaign has ever made.

### 13.216.3 What a 31-second ladder costs at this campaign's scale

The arm issues ~5,650 provider calls per 500-question dispatch and the job ceiling is 360 minutes.
Against a per-minute window, 31 s straddles at most one reset; 120 s spans two. The difference
between the two is not a delay, it is a dispatch: a run that dies at question 13 of 500 loses four
hours of grading, and the next one starts from zero because there is no resume path.

The repair is therefore not about this one probe. It is that the arm's survival probability against
its own provider was being set by a constant nobody had measured against the other constant.

### 13.216.4 The repair, in two halves, and why both are needed

**(a) The ladder must be able to spend the budget.** `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES` is now 8: the smallest
count whose geometric sum (`1+2+…+128 = 255 s`) exceeds the 120 s ceiling, so the ceiling binds and
the count does not. A caller that names a count still gets exactly that count — the defect was the
default, and `retry.test.ts` pins both halves, including the old 31 s reach as the control.

**(b) The last wait must be truncated to what remains.** With doubling, a budget is almost never
spent exactly: 40 ms then 80 ms against a 100 ms budget used to stop at 40 ms with 60% of the window
unused. The final computed backoff now waits whatever is left and the last attempt lands on the
deadline. The rule is asymmetric on purpose and the asymmetry is stated in the code: a `Retry-After`
beyond the remaining budget is **declined in full** (retrying inside a window the server just said
is closed is a request we know will be rejected), while our own estimate is truncated (it is a
guess, and the budget is its ceiling).

At the defaults this makes the reach exactly `DEFAULT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS` — asserted as an identity
(`at().at(-1) === DEFAULT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS`), not as a constant, so a future change to either number
has to keep the two consistent or fail.

### 13.216.5 The artifact: `transportRetry`

The arm's report now carries the counters, attached unconditionally rather than under
`attachLlmUsage`'s absence rule. The difference is deliberate: `llmUsage` omits the field when the
provider reported no `usage` block, because a run that called and was not priced is a real state.
The retry counters are incremented by the loop **before** the provider answers, so a graded run
cannot have zero — `calls: 0` in the artifact is a statement that the counters were not wired, and
absence is therefore unambiguously "written before the field existed".

Three readings are rendered as findings rather than left to the reader, because each implies a
different next action:

| counters | reading | next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retried: 0` | nothing was throttled; the run spent no wall clock waiting | none — the provider was healthy |
| `retried > 0, rateLimited: 0` | transport failures or `5xx`, not a rate limit | look at the network and the endpoint, not at quota |
| `rateLimited > 0` | the provider throttled; the cost is wall clock, not tokens | the next dispatch inherits it; the budget decides whether it survives |

`scope: 'process'`, `provider: 'run'`: the counters cannot be split by provider after the fact,
because both the reader and the embedding backend pass through the same loop, and an artifact that
presented the shared total as the reader's alone would be reporting a number it cannot substantiate.

### 13.216.6 What this section does not claim

- **Not** that the run would have survived. A `429` that outlasts 120 s kills the pass exactly as one
  that outlasts 31 s does. What changes is that the ladder now has the reach its own documentation
  claimed, and that the *next* failure carries the counters that decide whether the budget is the
  right number.
- **Not** that 120 s is the right ceiling for this provider. It is the registered value and the
  measurement that would replace it does not exist yet — `rateLimited` against `retriedCalls` in the
  next artifact is that measurement.
- **Not** that `DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES: 8` is an improvement on its own. Raising the count with the
  budget unbound would spend 255 s per failing call inside a 340-minute run; the count only earns its
  value together with the ceiling that now binds.

### 13.216.7 Acceptance

| # | what must be true | how it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the ladder reaches the ceiling at the defaults | `retry.test.ts`: attempt timestamps `[0, 1k, 3k, 7k, 15k, 31k, 63k, 120k]` |
| 2 | a short budget is spent exactly, not abandoned | attempt timestamps `[0, 40, 100]` against `retryBudgetMs: 100` |
| 3 | a named count still binds | `maxRetries: 5` reproduces the 31 s reach |
| 4 | a negative budget disables the ceiling | three attempts, nothing truncated |
| 5 | the artifact carries the counters, at zero too | `attachTransport` attaches with `calls: 0`; the section prints `NOT WIRED` |
| 6 | the reading matches the counters | throttled / retried-without-429 / nothing-throttled are separable in the Markdown |
| 7 | the counters describe this arm, not the process before it | `resetRetryStats()` before the passes; a seeded retry is absent from the report |
| 8 | the partition closes | `cleanCalls + retriedCalls + exhaustedCalls === calls`, flagged in the document when it does not |

*Registered for the next dispatch:* its artifact carries `transportRetry` with `calls > 0`, and the
`rateLimited` share it reports is the first measurement of this arm's throttling rate against
DeepSeek at the registered configuration.

*Falsified by:* an artifact whose `transportRetry.calls` is `0` on a run that graded answers (the
wiring is wrong, not the provider), **or** a `429` that still ends the pass after 120 s of permitted
waiting — which would make the ceiling, not the ladder, the thing to measure next.

### 13.216.8 The failure path carries the counters too, and it is the one that needed them

`13.216.5` put the counters in the **report**. Run `41346610318` did not produce a report. It
graded twelve of twenty probe questions, was rejected with `429` on the thirteenth, spent six
minutes and twenty-five seconds inside the ladder, and uploaded:

```
cortex-memory/benchmark-error.log    12 progress lines and a stack trace
cortex-memory/benchmark-*.json       absent
cortex-memory/benchmark-*.md         absent
```

`PartialAblation` carried `reached: 12`, the twelve answers, and no number saying a rate limit
had been hit. So the question the next dispatch had to be chosen on — *is this arm affordable,
or is the quota gone* — was answered eleven minutes later by a hand-run of the default
parameters. That is not a thing a pipeline can do, and it is the same asymmetry `13.216.5`
corrects one layer up: a report without counters is a gap, a **failure** without counters is
the end of a five-hour run that cannot be read.

#### Where the snapshot is taken

In `attachPartial`, the single funnel every failing run passes through — the
single-repetition wrapper, the repetition loop and the empty-measurement boundary all end
there. A snapshot taken by each caller would be a line every future caller could forget, which
is the argument that put `attachPartial` here rather than in `bench/run-ablation.ts` in the
first place. It makes the function impure, and the trade is stated in its comment: it is called
exactly once per run, at the moment of failure, and *what the transport had seen by then* is a
property of that moment rather than of the arguments. A pure signature would require every
caller to snapshot the aggregate before the throw, which cannot be done — the throw is the
event.

#### Why this funnel does not reset the aggregate, and the arm's does

The two paths want opposite things from the same counters, and the asymmetry is the design:

| path | rule | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| report (`bench-memory-arm.ts`) | `resetRetryStats()` **before** the passes | the report describes this arm; a preflight or probe that preceded it is traffic nobody can attribute |
| failure (`attachPartial`) | read **without** resetting | the retries are the failure. Resetting here would discard the exact traffic that ended the run, which is the number the next dispatch is chosen on |

`provider: 'run'` and `scope: 'process'` are the labels that keep the second row honest: the
number is everything the process had seen, and the artifact says so rather than presenting it
as one endpoint's.

#### Why it is attached at zero, and why that is not the same as absent

Same rule as the report: `calls: 0` on a partial says the counters were wired and saw no
traffic, which is what a system double produces. Absence therefore keeps its single meaning —
*this artifact was written before the field existed* — which is a different fact with a
different reading. The guard order matters as much: `measuredNothing` is decided **before** the
aggregate is read, so a run that measured nothing attaches no partial at all rather than a
record of two empty vectors with a live retry count on it (which would read as *a measurement
happened, and it was throttled*).

#### Acceptance

| # | what must be true | how it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | a failed run's partial carries the counters | `partial-ablation.test.ts`: seeded retry, then a feature-side death; `partial.transportRetry` defined |
| 2 | the number is live, not a constant zero | the same test: `attempts: 2`, `retried: 1`, `rateLimited: 1` from a seeded rejected-then-served call |
| 3 | it is labelled as the run's, not a provider's | `provider === 'run'`, `scope === 'process'` |
| 4 | zero is a reading | reset, then die: field present with `calls: 0` |
| 5 | no measurement attaches nothing at all | baseline-side death at question 0 with a live seeded retry: `partial` absent, so no counters hang on a fabricated record |
| 6 | the funnel does not reset | mutant that calls `resetRetryStats()` before the read fails row 2 (`expected +0 to be 2`) |
| 7 | dropping the attach fails the right rows | mutant that removes it fails rows 1 and 4 and leaves row 5 green — the correct pairing |

*Falsified by:* the next failing artifact whose `partial.transportRetry` is absent while its
`reached` is above zero (the wiring is wrong, not the provider), or one whose counters do not
close (`cleanCalls + retriedCalls + exhaustedCalls !== calls`) at the moment of death.

### 13.216.9 The record needs a reader, or the field is inert

`13.216.8` attached the counters to the partial. Nothing in the pipeline read them. The audit step is
handed `benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json`, which a failed run does not write, so it exited
with "file not found" while the one artifact the failure *did* leave sat beside it unread. **A field
with no reader is the same defect as no field, one commit later** — this campaign has now recorded
that shape in three consecutive rounds (the ladder nobody reached, the recording point nobody wrote,
the reader nobody called).

`tools/readout-arm-run.py --partial` opens that file. It reuses `transport_section` rather than
reimplementing it, so the throttle / retried-without-429 / clean readings cannot drift between the
report reader and this one, and it adds the extent the report reader has no way to know:

```
=== partial measurement (the run did not finish) ===
  died on: cortex-memory, repetition 0
  reached: 12 of 20 questions (60.0% of it)
  answers kept -- baseline: 20, feature: 12
  repetitions finished before it: 0 -- the failure was in the first repetition, so
  nothing earlier was lost with it
```

Run against the two archived records rather than invented fixtures, because the two shapes that matter
are both in the archives and they differ in a way no synthetic record would have suggested:

| artifact | keys | what it proves | what it does not carry |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run-41346610318` | 7, including `completed: []` | twelve of twenty graded, complete baseline | the counters (written before them) |
| `cortex-run-38941095220-partial` | 6, no `completed` | `run: 1`, so repetition 0 finished **on both sides** | its two thousand answers, and the field that would carry them |

The second one is why `completed` is optional in the reader. `reached`/`total`/`run` and the two answer
arrays are required; `completed` and `transportRetry` are not, and a reader that demanded `completed`
would reject the only failure records that exist — a check that passes on everything written after the
field and refuses the archives.

#### The four readings a partial must not offer

Each of these produces a number that looks like a measurement, so each is named as absent rather than
left to silence:

- **an accuracy** over whichever side happens to be complete — that artifact's baseline has all twenty
  answers, so scoring it alone yields a real rate belonging to no arm;
- **a delta**, which subtracts two aggregates over the same index, so a short side makes it arithmetic
  over a comparison that was never paired;
- **a per-capability table**, where an unanswered capability renders `0/0` — byte-identical to a
  measured zero;
- **an extent of zero** for a finished run, which is what a lenient reader prints when it is pointed at
  a report: the two files are distinguished and the report is refused by name.

#### The workflow takes the branch instead of failing on a missing file

The audit step now checks which file exists: a report → `--audit` as before; no report but a partial →
`--partial`, with a `::notice::` saying which branch it took; neither → `::error::` and exit 1, because
a run that left neither file left no measurement at all, which is precisely the defect `13.216.8`
exists to prevent.

#### Acceptance

| # | what must be true | how it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the extent reads as a share | `reached: 12 of 20 questions (60.0% of it)` |
| 2 | both sides' kept answers are counted | `answers kept -- baseline: 20, feature: 12` |
| 3 | the three prohibited readings are named | `ungraded`, `delta … never happened`, `0/0` |
| 4 | a complete report is refused, not read as empty | `--partial` on the synthetic report exits 2 with `this is a complete report` |
| 5 | a record without `completed` still reports finished repetitions | `run: 1` prints `1 (the ordinal says 0..0 …)` |
| 6 | a record without `completed` at `run: 0` says "not recorded" | the absent field is not printed as `0` |
| 7 | a finished repetition is listed with its pair | `run 0: 3 + 3 answers` |
| 8 | absent counters are never a zero | `not in this record … predates the field`, and no `nothing was throttled` |
| 9 | present counters use the same three readings | `throttled 80 of 180 requests`, `provider: run` |
| 10 | a corrupt block does not exit 0 | extent printed **and** exit 2 with `PRESENT AND UNREADABLE` |
| 11 | the extent cannot be a flag | `reached: true`, `-1`, `"20"`, `1.5`, non-list answers all exit 2 |
| 12 | every required key is named when missing | six params, one per key |
| 13 | `total: 0` does not divide by zero | `no questions in the dataset` |

*Falsified by:* the next failed artifact whose partial record is not read by the audit step, or one
whose printed extent disagrees with its own `reached`/`total`.

## 13.217 The 8× that is not on the table yet, and the two ways to get it

*A registered increment, not a change. Nothing is dispatched on it and nothing is implemented by it.*

### 13.217.1 What it is worth, measured against the thing that is actually blocking

`AUDIT-BENCHMARK-WALLCLOCK.md` §3 puts the arithmetic plainly: ~4,000 provider calls at ~5 s, one at a
time, is **336 minutes**; at concurrency 8 it is **42 minutes**. The registered job ceiling is 360 and
the arm's own deadline is 340, so today **one iteration is one dispatch and one dispatch is a day**.

That is not a throughput nicety. Requirement #12 — *the contract and the pipeline must support weak and
strong models, and the strong model must measurably do better* — is blocked on exactly this number:
§13.212.6 measured the second provider (`zhipu:glm-4.6`) at **5.1× the run budget, 1.41 questions per
minute**, which no ceiling can absorb. An 8× reduction does not make that provider fast; it makes the
measurement **fit**, which is the difference between a blocked requirement and a scheduled one.

So the priority of this increment is not "research comfort". It is the enabling change for a registered
contract requirement, and that is why it is written down now rather than queued behind the P2 items.

### 13.217.2 Why the obvious implementation is wrong, in one sentence

`runBenchmark` reads five quantities **after** the call that produced them, from single-slot accessors on
the system (`#lastRawOutput`, `#lastRetrievedContext`, `#lastPromptEvidenceChars`, `#lastPromptText`,
`#lastAdmittedEvidence`), so under concurrency the slot belongs to whichever call wrote it last and
question A's record can carry question B's prompt — silently, with nothing throwing.

There is a sixth reader the audit did not name, and it is the one that decides between the two designs
below: the arm wraps the system in a prototype chain and takes a **per-question census delta around each
answer** (`bench-memory-arm.ts`, §13.145.6). "Before and after one call" is the same single-slot
assumption one layer up.

### 13.217.3 Two designs, and what each one costs

| | **A. One system instance per worker** | **B. The trace becomes the return value** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| how | `c` instances built from the same config, sharing the LLM and embedding clients; a shared index queue hands each worker one question at a time | every routed method returns `Answer \| { answer, trace }`; the five slots and the census delta are replaced by a sink the call owns |
| single-slot state | correct **by construction** — no two calls share an instance | deleted rather than protected |
| census delta | preserved: each worker's wrapper brackets its own call | must move into the sink, or it breaks |
| cost | ~150 lines: a factory in the arm, a worker pool in `benchmark.ts`, index placement | ~500 lines across two packages, 239 references, and the five accessors' documentation has to move to the trace type |
| risk | state accumulated **per instance** (vote census, abstention census, any online state) is partitioned and must be summed — and the sum is only equal if nothing in the mechanism depends on seeing every earlier question | the type widens on a contract three packages implement, and the equality proof has to hold for every route |
| second provider | same | same |

**Recommendation: A, then B only if a mechanism is found that needs cross-question state.** A is ordered
first not because it is smaller but because its failure mode is checkable by the same instrument the
audit already registered: if the mechanism is per-question, the answers are byte-identical; if it is not,
they differ and the difference names the state. B's failure mode is a contract migration, whose mistakes
show up as *types* rather than as *numbers*, and this campaign's whole discipline is that a wrong number
is the expensive kind.

### 13.217.4 The acceptance criterion, unchanged from the audit

*Claim:* at the same configuration, a 60-question arm answers **byte-identically** at concurrency 1 and
concurrency `c`.

*Instrument:* the twin-run digest — the per-question answer vector and the per-question prompt bytes,
placed by **question index, never by completion order**. Aggregation order is part of the measurement:
summing in completion order produces last-digit differences that propagate through tie-breaking, which is
the rule `commonPrefixByPass` already follows by comparing bytes rather than hashes.

*Falsified by:* any question whose answer or prompt differs between the two runs, which names the state
that is shared. That is a **finding about the mechanism**, not a failure of the harness, and it is the
first thing this instrument is for.

*Cost:* ~10 minutes per arm at concurrency 1, ~2 at concurrency 8.

### 13.217.5 What is explicitly not registered

- **Not** that 8 is the right width. It is the audit's example. The width this arm can sustain is a
  function of the provider's refusal rate, which is what `transportRetry.rateLimited` now measures — and
  a run that raises concurrency into a `429` wall will report it rather than hide it.
- **Not** that concurrency is free of scoring consequences. A timeout is a scoring policy: the same
  answers under a longer queue are scored the same, which is why the digest compares answers and not
  elapsed time.
- **Not** that the default changes before the proof lands. Default stays 1 until the 60-question twin run
  is green; the flag exists, the default does not move.

## 13.218 The 429 that was never sent

*Dispatch `41393748964` finished after 267 minutes with `failure`. What it recorded, and what it
did not, is the subject of this section.*

### 13.218.1 Two readings that could not both be true

The artifact's tail:

```
=== transport retry accounting (process-wide) ===
{"attempts":2892,"retried":0,"rateLimited":0,"retryAfterHonoured":0,
 "calls":2892,"retriedCalls":0,"cleanCalls":2892,"exhaustedCalls":0,"retryRate":0}
progress: died on cortex-memory run=1 q=350/500 id=gpt4_2f56ae70 at +3242.8s

LLM request failed: 429
```

Read plainly, the counters say **the provider never throttled anything**: 2,892 calls, every one
served on its first attempt, zero `429`s, nothing retried. The line below says a `429` killed the
run. One of the two has to be wrong.

Neither is. `attempts === calls === 2892` means no call in that process ever made a second request,
and `rateLimited === 0` means no attempt was answered `429`. So the status in the last line was
never received. It was **manufactured one layer down**:

```ts
// retry.ts, before this round
return withResponse(resFromLastAttempt ?? new Response(null, { status: 429 }), stats);
```

A transport failure carries no response, so the retry ladder had nothing to return — and invented a
`429` "so the caller still has an HTTP status to act on". The caller printed it. The record now
blames the provider's rate limiter for a fault that happened on the wire.

### 13.218.2 Reproduced, not inferred

Three fixtures against the built package, each one line of code away from the real path:

| fixture | what was returned | counters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| transport failure, budget already spent | `new Response(null, {status: 429})` → `LLM request failed: 429 ` | `attempts 1, retried 0, rateLimited 0, cleanCalls 1` |
| `429` + `Retry-After: 200`, budget 120 s | the real `429`, immediately | `attempts 1, retried 0, rateLimited 1, cleanCalls 1` |
| `429`, no header, default budget | after 8 attempts / 120 s | `attempts 8, retried 7, rateLimited 8, retriedCalls 1` |

The first row is byte-identical to the production message (`429`, empty status text, no body) and
to the production counters. **That is the proof**: the run died of a fabricated status, and the two
"contradictory" readings are the same event seen from both ends.

### 13.218.3 Three defects, one chain

**(a) A fabricated status.** `429` is the strongest signal a provider can send about quota. Printing
it for a stall sends the next dispatch to look at rate limits. There was nothing to see there.

**(b) A refusal counted as a clean call.** `cleanCalls` is documented as *"calls that completed
without a single retry"*, and a call answered `429` and then declined a retry did not complete. It
landed there anyway, so the artifact's most reassuring number (2,892 calls served first time) was
describing a process that was ending. The class that was missing is the one that names it.

**(c) The budget could not fund a single retry in thinking mode.** The budget is measured from the
first attempt; the per-attempt deadline in thinking mode is `300 s` (`THINKING_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the
budget is `120 s`. So **one full-length attempt spends the entire allowance**, and the ladder is
unreachable by construction — the same shape as §13.216's count defect, one parameter over. Measured:
the failing attempt took 133.8 s (last progress line `+3109 s`, death at `+3242.8 s`), which is
exactly "long enough to eat the budget, short enough to be a stall".

### 13.218.4 The fixes

| where | change | why there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `retry.ts` | the no-response refusal **rethrows the transport error** with `retryExhausted` attached | there is no status to report; the transport error is the only thing this layer can substantiate |
| `retry.ts` | `RetryRefusal` travels on the outcome: `attempts-exhausted` / `budget-exhausted` / `retry-after-beyond-budget`, with `retryAfterMs` and `remainingMs` | the three call for different work and are indistinguishable in a status code |
| `retry.ts` | `refusedCalls` is a **fourth call class** | a refusal is not a completion, and the partition has to put it somewhere |
| `retry.ts` | a call that never got an answer is counted in `exhaustedCalls` **only** | it used to be counted in both `exhaustedCalls` and `retriedCalls`, which broke the identity the counters are checked against |
| `openai-compatible.ts` | `retryBudgetMs` forwarded; refusal named in the message | `41393748964` printed a status and stopped, and every reader drew the wrong conclusion from it |
| `llm-factory.ts` | `resolveRetryBudgetMs` = `THINKING_TIMEOUT_MS + DEFAULT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS` | the budget and the attempt deadline are one decision, and the composition is the only place that can hold the invariant |

The partition is now `cleanCalls + retriedCalls + exhaustedCalls + refusedCalls === calls`, asserted
in `cortex-ai` and re-checked by both readers — the report (four terms) and `--transport`
(four terms when the artifact carries the field, three when it predates it, because an artifact
cannot fail an identity written after it).

### 13.218.5 What the run actually held, and threw away

`completed` carries **one full repetition**: 500 baseline answers and 500 feature answers, paired.
The run then died 349 questions into repetition 1. Every graded answer of repetition 0 was in the
artifact, and no report exists to score it — the pipeline writes `completed` and nothing reads it.

That is now the fourth instance of the same shape in this campaign, and it is registered here rather
than fixed here: **a record with no scorer**.

### 13.218.6 What this withdraws

The pending P1 was *"if the run still dies on `429`, re-time the ceiling by the `rateLimited`
reading"*. It is **withdrawn**: the reading it would have been timed on was false. There was no
throttling to measure. Re-tuning the budget against a fabricated status would have produced a
longer ladder for a fault the ladder cannot fix.

### 13.218.7 Acceptance

| # | what must be true | how it is checked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | no fabricated status exists | `retry.test.ts`: transport failure + spent budget **rejects** with the original message (`socket hang up`) |
| 2 | the cause survives the rethrow | the same test asserts `retryExhausted.cause` and `.attempts` |
| 3 | a refusal is not a clean call | `Retry-After: 3600` → `refusedCalls 1`, `cleanCalls 0`, `rateLimited 1` |
| 4 | the reason is named, with both numbers | `it('counts it as refused and reports why')`: `retry-after-beyond-budget`, `retryAfterMs 3_600_000`, `remainingMs 120_000` |
| 5 | the count running out is a different reason | `maxRetries: 0` on a `503` → `attempts-exhausted`, `rateLimited 0` |
| 6 | the four classes close | mixed aggregate of five calls: 1 clean + 2 retried + 1 exhausted + 1 refused = 5 |
| 7 | an exhausted call is in exactly one class | the test that used to assert the double count now asserts `retriedCalls 0`, `retried 5` |
| 8 | the LLM message names the refusal | `llm.test.ts`: `not retried (retry-after-beyond-budget)`, `the provider asked for 3600 s` |
| 9 | the adapter forwards the budget | 80 ms budget + 1 s backoff → exactly 2 requests, `budget-exhausted` |
| 10 | thinking mode's budget can fund a retry | `resolveRetryBudgetMs > resolveTimeoutMs`, asserted as an inequality |
| 11 | the report renders the fourth class | `transport-transport.test.ts`: table row + `1 calls were refused without a retry` |
| 12 | the fourth class is silent at zero | control test: no `refused without a retry` on a clean run |
| 13 | the reader tolerates the field's absence | `predates` printed, no partition warning |
| 14 | a modern artifact is checked against four terms | `NOT A PARTITION: 90 + 5 + 0 + 1 != 100` |
| 15 | a legacy artifact is checked against three | the pre-existing test still passes its `90 + 5 + 0 != 100` assertion |

*Falsified by:* the next failing artifact whose log says `429` while its counters say
`rateLimited 0` — that pair is now impossible without a fabricated status, so its reappearance means
the fabrication is back.

### 13.218.8 The mutations, and which row each one breaks

Three mutants, each applied to the source, run, and reverted. A test that cannot fail is a comment.

| mutant | rows that fail | what that proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the fabricated `429` is put back on the no-response refusal | 1 and 2 (`rethrows the transport error…`, `spends the remaining budget on a retry…`) | the test is bound to the **rethrow**, not to the refusal object being present |
| `recordRefused` is replaced by `record` | 3 and 4 (`counts it as refused…`, `names the count running out…`) | the fourth class is a real counter, not a label |
| thinking mode's budget is set back to `DEFAULT_RETRY_BUDGET_MS` | 10 (`gives thinking mode a budget that can fund a retry…`) | the inequality is the assertion, so neither number can drift alone |

The third one is the one worth keeping: it fails with `120000 > 300000`, which is the defect stated in one line. Any future
change that widens `THINKING_TIMEOUT_MS` without touching the allowance reproduces the pre-fix condition exactly, and this
row is the only thing that would say so.

## 13.219 The dispatch that ran 89 commits behind, and did not build

*An operational finding, recorded because it cost a dispatch and would cost another.*

`master` is this repository's default branch and the ref every push lands on. `main` also existed,
84 commits behind and **diverged** by one: a single commit that master carries under a different SHA
because the two were written by different push paths.

A dispatch sent with `ref: main` therefore ran code from **eleven days ago**, and the job failed at
`Build packages` — the branch is not merely old, it does not compile. Nothing in the dispatch
response says which ref it used; the run's `head_sha` is the only place that fact appears, and it
takes a comparison against the branch list to notice it is not the commit that was just pushed.

**Repaired, not documented away:** `main` was fast-forwarded to the current `master` (`b9b75ca7`).
Its one unique commit is already on `master` as `01a0cf0c` with the same message, so nothing was
lost. The stale branch no longer exists as a trap.

**And the dispatch was reissued on `master`** — `41431790794`, head `b9b75ca7`.

The general rule this is an instance of: a dispatch names a ref, and a ref that is not the default
can be arbitrarily old. A run whose `head_sha` is not the commit you just pushed has measured
something other than your change, and that is checkable **before** the result is read rather than
after it looks strange.

*Falsified by:* any dispatch whose `head_sha` differs from the branch head at submit time.

### 13.219.1 The first CI run of the acceptance table found a test I had written wrong

`Verify` failed on `b9b75ca7`: `expected { remainingMs: 120000 } to deeply equal { remainingMs: 119999 }`.

That number is `budget - elapsed`, so **one millisecond of scheduling between two statements** moves it. I had written
`toEqual` on a clock reading and called it an acceptance row. The rule is *"the allowance was whole when the refusal was
decided"*, and the row now says that: `remainingMs` above 119,000 and below or equal to the budget.

Worth recording because of the direction of the error. The code was right and the test was wrong, and the wrongness was
**over-specification rather than looseness** — the failure mode everyone guards against is a test that passes when it
