| question | gold | list the reader printed | answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `0a995998` pick up or return clothing | 3 | blazer; Zara boots | 2 |
| `6d550036` projects led | 2 | one project | 1 |
| `gpt4_a56e767c` festivals attended | 4 | Austin; Portland; AFI Fest | 3 |
| `46a3abf7` tanks owned | 3 | community tank; friend's kid's tank | 2 |

The instrument says the evidence is there and the room is not the constraint:

| measurement | correct (n=93) | wrong (n=28) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `goldOverlap.carried / total` (median) | **12 / 12** | **16.5 / 17** |
| `promptChars` (median) | 46,272 | 46,225 |
| delivered turns (median) | 176 | 173 |
| share of turns at the 400-character cap | 9.2% | 10.7% |

Wrong questions carry **more** gold, use the **same** room, and are **not** more truncated. So the
arithmetic in §13.233.1 lands where the table says: a bigger room cannot fix a count. A keyword sweep
of all 166 delivered turns of `0a995998` finds exactly the two store errands the reader listed — the
third gold item is not textually a third errand in the window it was shown.

### 13.233.4 What is left, and the one number that points at it

`goldOverlap.goldRanks` carries `-1` for a gold turn the ranking never offered, and the pool is 256:

| MR population | n | wrong | wrong rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| at least one gold turn outside the pool | 41 | 16 | **57.1%** |
| every gold turn inside the pool | 80 | 12 | **26.9%** |

Fisher's exact two-sided **p = 0.0056** on a 30.3-point difference. A question whose gold the ranker
could not reach fails twice as often, and 41 of 121 MR questions are in that set — which makes the
pool the one MR-side quantity that is both short and measurable, and it is the only widening that
costs no prompt token: the window is fixed at 48,000 and a deeper pool changes *which* turns fill it.

## 13.234 Registration: `relevanceTopK: 512`, and what would refute the pool as MR's constraint

*One variable, one declared departure, no new field.*

| # | item | value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | treatment | `--set cortex_memory_relevance_top_k=512` |
| 2 | control | T (`41546569106`), the post-§13.232 registration, field for field |
| 3 | mechanism | `pool 256 -> 512` changes which turns the window may hold and nothing else: `relevanceSignal`, `relevanceUnits`, `maxTurnChars`, `maxPromptChars`, the contract and the reader are held |
| 4 | token cost | **zero on the prompt side** — the room is still 48,000 characters, so the same number of turns is printed; the pool is a candidate list, not a delivery |
| 5 | cost that is real | 256 extra scored candidates per question at retrieval time, and the embedding cache is keyed on the dataset rather than on K, so no new vectors are computed |

**Predictions, written before the run:**

| # | prediction | falsified by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR's correct ≥ 93 + 3 = **96 of 121** (≥ +2.5 points) | MR ≤ 94 |
| 2 | the MR gain concentrates in the 41-question outside-pool cohort: **≥ 3 of its 16 wrong convert** | ≤ 1 converts |
| 3 | `featureAggregate.avg` ≥ **91.5%** | < 90.5% |
| 4 | the four other capabilities hold inside §13.118.5's spread | any of them moving ≥ 2 points |

**What the pair cannot say**, stated now: the pool's ranks are capped at 255 in `goldRanks`, so the
artifact cannot report *how far* outside the pool a gold turn was. A conversion rate near 3 of 16 is
consistent both with "most were just past 256" and with "a fifth were reachable and the rest were not",
and the second would license 1,024 rather than 1,024-implied-by-extrapolation. If prediction 2 is met
at the lower bound, the next step is 1,024 as a second point on the same curve rather than a new
mechanism.

## 13.235 A recall metric was quoted as an accuracy target, and the ledger it belongs to

*The round's competitor re-verification (2026-11-03) found one error in this campaign's own reporting, and
the error is worth more than the numbers it corrected.*

### 13.235.1 The error

`SOTA-LANDSCAPE.md` §1 has carried the attribute since it was written: **`metric` — Recall@20 is not answer
accuracy; Supermemory 97% is recall, single-pass accuracy 85.86%.** The 2026-11-03 write-ups in the docs
repository quoted **97.0% as the highest published accuracy and as a 6.85-point target**. Both READMEs had the fact; the
sentence did not use it.

The correction, per three independent pages checked that day: Supermemory's advertised 97% is **Recall@20**,
its QA accuracy is **85.2%** (Gemini 3 Pro reader), and the same system reads 81.6% in a third-party
comparison. cortex at 90.15 is therefore **4.95 points above** it, not 6.85 below.

What the published QA field actually looks like, in the order that matters for a comparison:

| system | QA accuracy | the attribute that decides comparability |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Recallium | 98.4 | Claude Opus 5.5 reader, self-reported; 90.2 with the official GPT-4o reader on the same harness |
| agentmemory V4 | 96.2 | one deterministic run, Claude Opus 4.6 |
| Maximem Synap | 95.6 | self-reported, "checked 28 Oct 2026" |
| Agent Zero Memory | 95.6 | arXiv 2026-08; setting and judge **not named** |
| Mastra Observational Memory | 94.87 | GPT-5-mini; **84.23 with GPT-4o**, same memory |
| Hindsight | 94.6 | self-reported |
| Mem0 managed | 94.4 | GPT-5 as answer model **and** judge |
| Honcho / Zep | 90.4 / 90.2 | self-reported; Zep grades with gpt-5.4 |
| **cortex (this section's run)** | **90.15** | public prompt, official judge, 500 questions, 4 repetitions |
| RAW-RAG (naive) | 87.5 | arXiv:2610.30755 |
| memoricai | 85.8 | the reproducible comparison this campaign has been tracking |
| Supermemory | **85.2** | its 97% is Recall@20 |

### 13.235.2 The four measurements on the reader axis, and why the ledger matters more than the ranking

| experiment | change | effect |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Mastra (vendor's own ablation) | GPT-4o → GPT-5-mini, memory fixed | **+10.64** |
| Recallium (vendor's own ablation) | GPT-4o → Claude Opus 5.5, retrieval fixed | **+8.2** |
| **this repository, 2026-10-28** | `deepseek-chat` → `deepseek-v4-pro`, everything else fixed | **−7.20** |
| **this repository, `41546569106`** | thinking on two routes, prompt byte-identical | **+6.25** |

Three of the four are positive and large, one is negative and large, and the axis is the same one in all
four. So the honest reading of "we are 4.25 points behind the 94.4 band" is not "we need a bigger model" —
this repository already spent that experiment and lost 7.20 points on it. What the axis buys is **contract
compliance**: a reader that deliberates before emitting (`thinking`, +6.25) complies; a reader with more
parameters in the same family does not (i.e. does something else, and the arm's `ABS` was the only
capability that rose).

The consequence for the plan is negative and useful: **the reader axis is not a queue item.** It has been
measured in both directions on this arm, and the two directions disagree about size and sign. What remains
is the mechanism the reader is asked to execute — which is where §13.233.3 puts MR.

### 13.235.3 The rule this adds

A number may be quoted only after its four attributes have been read **in the sentence that quotes it**, not
in the file that records them. `SOTA-LANDSCAPE.md` §1 is the right place to keep them and the wrong place to
rely on: a table of attributes does not fail when a sentence ignores it, which is the same defect class as a
producer field with no reader (§13.181) and a check with no caller (§13.220). The three are one shape:
**a statement whose correctness depends on somebody remembering to consult it is not checked.**

## 13.236 One instrument reading cost the whole measurement

*Run `41585013786` is the experiment §13.234 registered. It answered all 500 questions, judged 342
of them, and then exited 1 without writing a report. Nothing was measured -- not the pool, not the
delta -- and the cause was a single provider call whose retry ladder ran out. The arithmetic of that
trade is the subject of this section, and the repair is four fields and one `catch`.*

### 13.236.1 What the run actually did, in order

| time (UTC) | event |
| --- | --- |
| 05:37:46 | job starts, `relevanceTopK=512` as the only declared departure |
| 06:34 | reference-pipeline pass begins |
| 07:25:14 | reference-pipeline `q=500/500`, +6361 s |
| 07:37:56 | cortex-memory pass begins |
| 08:29:48 | cortex-memory `q=500/500`, +3112 s |
| 08:29:48 - 08:55:16 | scoring: 342 of 928 judge verdicts produced, then one call dies |
| 08:55:26 | `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL`, exit 1, no report written |

The transport accounting at death, which is the whole story in one line:

```
{"attempts":1925,"retried":4,"rateLimited":0,"retryAfterHonoured":0,"calls":1921,
 "retriedCalls":1,"cleanCalls":1919,"exhaustedCalls":1,"refusedCalls":0}
```

**1,919 of 1,920 calls completed without a retry.** The gate §13.227 installed held: zero `429`s
across 1,925 requests, which is the first run of this campaign with no throttling at all. One call
exhausted, and it was the last one that mattered.

### 13.236.2 The trade, in the two numbers that decide it

| quantity | value |
| --- | ---: |
| verdicts the instrument owed | 928 |
| verdicts it produced | 342 |
| verdicts it failed to produce | **1** |
| share of verdicts that failed | **0.066%** |
| provider work discarded with it | 52 min of feature pass + 106 min of reference pass + 26 min of judging |
| share of the run's information discarded | **100%** |

A pass is a rate over a population. A rate over 499 of 500 is a measurement; the missing reading is
a fact to publish. The code did the opposite, and it did it at the one point where the cheapest
possible repair existed: `metrics.ts`'s scoring loop called `await scorer(q, answer)` with no
opinion about what happens if the instrument is unavailable.

### 13.236.3 The repair: three decisions, each with the alternative it rejects

| decision | chosen | rejected, and why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| where to catch | at the call site in the scoring loop | in the entry point: it cannot resume a loop it has already left, so the only thing a `try` there can do is turn a stack trace into a message -- which `bench-failure.ts` already did for three earlier runs |
| what to do with the question | score it `false`, record it | drop it: the denominator becomes 499 on this pass and 500 on the last, so two artifacts' accuracies are rates over different populations and the four-run mean mixes them. Impute the other arm: invents a reading in one arm from the other |
| how a reader learns | `AblationResult.unjudged`, both sides, plus audit check 11 | a log line: the job log expires, and this campaign has spent three runs learning that a fact which lives only in a log is not in the record |

The direction of the pessimism is chosen deliberately: an unjudged answer is not a correct answer,
so every accuracy in such an artifact is pessimistic by at most `unjudged / total` points, and the
census carries both sides so the McNemar count can be told which discordances the instrument
invented. The audit fails on any non-empty census and prints that bound, because the artifact
surviving is the point of the fix and a red gate is how a human learns to look -- not the reverse.

### 13.236.4 The second defect: the judge inherited the reader's transport

`resolveRetryBudgetMs` gives a thinking reader a 420 s ceiling because a 300 s deadline spends a
120 s one. The judge was built from the *base* reader -- `thinking: disabled` whenever the run scopes
thinking to routes -- so it inherited `60 s` per attempt and `120 s` for the whole ladder. **Two
attempts is what that pair buys**, and the ladder it nominally has is nine rungs.

A judge prompt is one question, one gold answer and one reply, and the completion is the word `yes`
or `no`. It is not a reader's turn. It now gets its own pair -- 30 s per attempt, 300 s for the
ladder, the pace inherited because the pace is the provider's window rather than the workload's --
and the pair is printed from the same constants the client is built from, with a test that fails if
one moves without the other.

### 13.236.5 The third defect: `rateLimited` had a reader that rejected its producer

`findExhaustion` accepted `rateLimited` only when it was a `boolean`. `RetryExhaustion.rateLimited`
is a **count**. The field was therefore dropped from every real exhaustion, and the retry line --
the only one that survives in `benchmark-error.log` -- never printed it. The run's own log shows the
shape: the transport block said `rateLimited: 0` and the retry line said nothing at all.

`bench-failure.test.ts` had a fixture carrying `rateLimited: true`, which is why the guard looked
tested: the fixture was written against the reader rather than against the producer, and two
agreeing half-truths cannot fail. That is the same defect class as §13.181's producer with no
reader, seen from the other end.

### 13.236.6 The fourth: an exhaustion whose duration could not be attributed

`attempts=4, retried=3, elapsedMs=134163` admits three repairs and the record could not pick one:

| reading | what it implies | where the repair would go |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one deadline reached, three fast wire faults | the deadline is too short for this workload | `resolveJudgeTransport` |
| four attempts of ~34 s against no deadline | the provider stalls; more attempts will not help | retry budget, or per-question fail-soft |
| four attempts truncated by a ceiling | the ceiling is being spent by attempts | the pair, one parameter over |

`RetryExhaustion` now carries `attemptsMs`, `timeoutMs` and `retryBudgetMs`, and `describeFailure`
prints a second line that subtracts the attempts from the elapsed to name the waiting. The next
incident is decidable from the log instead of from a paragraph of arithmetic over a value that does
not exist -- which is §13.225's lesson in a different register.

### 13.236.7 What this section does not fix, stated so it is not read as fixed

1. **The pool reading is still unmeasured.** §13.234's four predictions remain untested; the run
   that was to test them produced no artifact. They are not restated or weakened here.
2. **The reference pass is recomputed on every dispatch.** 106 of the 158 minutes of provider work
   this run lost were a memoryless baseline whose answers are a function of the dataset, the reader
   identity and the prompt contract. A persisted baseline keyed on those three would have made this
   loss 52 minutes and every future experiment 3x cheaper. Not implemented; it changes what an
   artifact means and needs its own registration.
3. **The judge's verdicts are cached in memory only.** The 342 verdicts this run computed were
   discarded with the process, and a re-dispatch recomputes them.

## 13.237 The run could not finish: a pace is a schedule, and nothing compared it to the budget

*`41625442265` spent 5h41m and produced no measurement. The reason was decided before its first
question, and it was arithmetic.*

### 13.237.1 What the log says, pass by pass

The dispatch declared one departure from the registration -- `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k=512` --
which is §13.234's treatment. It completed four passes and died inside the fifth.

| arm | run | started | duration | per question | against a 3,000 s floor |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| reference-pipeline | 0 | 11:12:50 | **6,355 s** | 12.7 s | **+3,355 s** |
| cortex-memory | 0 | 13:11:27 | 3,143 s | 6.3 s | +143 s |
| reference-pipeline | 1 | 14:29:20 | 3,325 s | 6.7 s | +325 s |
| cortex-memory | 1 | 15:25:32 | 3,126 s | 6.3 s | +126 s |
| reference-pipeline | 2 | 16:36:56 | 954 s | — | **abandoned at q=146** |

The floor is `500 questions x 6,000 ms`, because `CORTEX_LLM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` was `6000` in this run.
Four of the five rows are the floor plus a few percent, which is what a paced pass looks like: the
reader was answering in under 6 s and the gate was the only limit. The first row is not -- it took
2.02x the floor, at 51 s per request across four workers -- and the ordering is what identifies it.
It is the pass that ran between 11:12 and 12:58, and the pass that ran immediately after it was
already at the floor, so this was **not** a cold prompt cache warming up: a cache that had to warm
would have made the second pass the slow one.

### 13.237.2 The arithmetic

Eight passes at 500 questions and 6 s per request is 4,000 slots and **400 minutes of schedule**, and
the run's own ceiling was `CORTEX_MEMORY_BUDGET_MINUTES=340` inside a job killed at 360. The pace
alone exceeded the budget by an hour, before the reader's latency, before the grading, before
anything the run was trying to measure. `BenchmarkBudgetExceeded` fired at minute 341, exactly as
scheduled, and the artifact it left names the question it stopped before -- which is the difference
between this failure and the ones §13.236 was about. The protection worked. What it protected was a
run that could not succeed.

The gate is also not a per-worker delay, and the design says so in `cortex-ai/src/pacing.ts`:

> A gate hands out *slots* from one shared schedule, so the width of the pool changes how much work
> is in flight and not the rate at which it hits the provider.

So `CORTEX_MEMORY_WORKERS=4` did not buy four times the throughput, and no pool width would have.
Ninety-five percent of four of those five passes was waiting for a slot.

### 13.237.3 Where the pace came from, which is the defect underneath

The variable was measured on the **second** provider. `41553176719` and `41552258320` are the two
smokes that died at 55 of 60 questions on `429 {"code":"1302"}` with `retryAfterHonoured: 0`, and the
pace was the answer to a rate: 1.41 questions per minute is one request every 42 s. The number was
then stored as a repository variable, and the workflow read it for **every** dispatch:

```yaml
CORTEX_LLM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS: ${{ vars.CORTEX_LLM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS }}
```

The comment above that line already said the first provider needs neither. The comment was right and
the value was still applied, because a repository variable is global state that any dispatch can set
and no dispatch can see. The DeepSeek arm that produced the 90.15% headline ran **unpaced**, at 1.6 s
per question; the same arm under this gate costs three times that. Nothing in the artifact said
"this run was throttled", because a pipe is deliberately not part of the registration (§13.227) --
which is correct for the *score* and was not enough for the *cost*.

### 13.237.4 The tool that should have refused, and the sentence in it that was false

`tools/job-budget.py` exists for exactly this question and answered it wrongly, in a sentence:

> Only concurrency, or a budget on a quantity that does not multiply, moves that wall.

That is true of a run with no pace and false of this one. The tool carried two quantities -- a
per-pass cost and a per-run budget -- and both are statements about work that a pace has already
replaced with a schedule. It also had no way to be asked the question that mattered: is the run's
own ceiling *reachable*?

It has one now. `pacing_floor_minutes(questions, passes, min_interval_ms, calls_per_question)`
computes `questions x calls x passes x interval / 60,000`, takes no concurrency argument (because the
gate does not have one), and `can_complete` compares it against the **budget** rather than the job,
because a budget below the floor is not a protection but the scheduled cause of a failure. The
workflow runs it before the benchmark step and exits `3`:

```
pacing floor 400 min (500 questions x 1 call(s) x 8 passes x 6000 ms), budget 340 -> THE RUN CANNOT
FINISH: the budget fires 60 min before the last question is asked
```

Five seconds instead of five hours. The two tests that pin it are the two halves of this run: `500 x
8 x 6000 = 400` and `can_complete(..., budget_minutes=340) is False`.

### 13.237.5 The pace is now scoped to the provider it was measured on

The provider is already named in the `model` input -- `zhipu:glm-4.6` is how the second provider's
smoke selected itself -- so the pace rides that name rather than a 25th input this surface does not
have (24 of GitHub's 25):

```yaml
CORTEX_LLM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS: ${{ startsWith(inputs.model, 'zhipu:') && vars.CORTEX_LLM_MIN_INTERVAL_MS || '' }}
```

A provider's window is the provider's. The DeepSeek path keeps the rate it was measured at, which is
no rate at all, and the second provider keeps the protection that was bought for it.

### 13.237.6 What the gate does not bound, measured on the same file

The floor is a **lower** bound, and this run says by how much it can miss: the first pass was 112%
above it. The mechanism is the other half of the throughput identity -- the gate caps the rate at
which requests leave, and the provider caps the rate at which they finish; throughput is the slower
of the two. At 51 s per call across four workers the provider was the limit and the schedule had
nothing to say, which is why the same eight-pass shape took 288 minutes in `41546569106` and would
have taken 455 here. `job-budget.py` reports the floor and says it is a floor; a dispatch that wants
a ceiling has to add the measured pass, which is what `--measured-pass-minutes` is for.

### 13.237.7 The answers the dead run did record are graded, not re-measured

`Answer` is `string | null`, so `completed[]` holds the measurement itself: **two complete
repetitions of both arms, 2,000 answers**, and the channel census the process printed (structural
556, exact 485, numeric 204, judge 755 of 2,000) is reproducible from them alone. The report was
lost; the measurement was not.

`replaySystem(name, dataset, answers)` wraps a recording as a `MemorySystem`, so
`runAblationReport` -- the same function a live arm calls -- produces the same document, with the
same per-capability McNemar table, from answers that already exist. Three properties are structural
rather than promised:

1. **It is keyed by the question, not by a cursor.** A cursor returns answer `i` to question `i` and
   silently absorbs a misalignment; a map from question text to answer throws instead, and the error
   names the question that had no answer.
2. **Duplicate question text is refused at construction**, because two questions sharing a text would
   each receive whichever answer the map kept and the report would be a mixture no field announces.
3. **Each side is replayed from its own list.** The replay of the baseline cannot reach the feature's
   answers, so the one thing §13.236.7 forbade -- imputing one arm from the other -- is not available
   to it.

The alignment is checked, not assumed: `REGRADE_EXPECT_IDS` carries `<index>:<question-id>` pairs read
off the dead run's own progress lines (`q=25/500 id=95bcc1c8` -> `25:95bcc1c8`), and the job refuses
to grade if any of them does not match the file. An index means nothing without the order it was
taken in, and a dataset that had moved would otherwise produce a complete, plausible report for a
pairing nobody made.

**What a regrade is not.** It is not interpolation, and the distinction is the one §13.236.7 drew: a
missing answer is not a wrong answer. Nothing was regenerated, no unfinished pass was filled in, and
the reading covers two repetitions where the dispatch asked for four. §13.234's predictions are
stated against the *configuration*, not against a repetition count, so they can be read at two --
with the caveat, printed with the numbers, that a two-run mean has half the variance reduction of a
four-run one.

### 13.237.8 What this section does not fix

1. **The predictions are still the thing to read.** Nothing here decides them; it only makes the
   existing measurement readable. The reading lives in §13.238 and the predictions there are the ones
   §13.234 wrote, unedited.
2. **The baseline arm is recomputed on every dispatch.** This run's own numbers make the size of that
   waste precise rather than assumed: the reference pipeline cost 1.0-2.0 s per question against the
   feature's 6.8-7.7 s in `41546569106`, i.e. about **16%** of the run, not the 67% that "half of
   eight passes" implies. A persisted baseline is worth having and it is a smaller lever than it
   looked.
3. **The judge's verdicts are still cached in memory only**, and a regrade recomputes them. That is
   the price of reading a recording back, and it is 755 requests rather than 4,000.

## 13.238 The pool was not MR's constraint: `topK=512` read back from a dead run's recordings

*§13.234's four predictions, read from two repetitions recovered out of `41625442265`'s partial artifact
(§13.237.7). The predictions are the ones §13.234 wrote, unedited. One is met, one is in a dead zone the
registration did not cover, one is untested, one is met.*

### 13.238.1 The two arms, three ways

| arm | repetitions | overall | IE | MR | KU | TR | ABS |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **T** `41546569106` (`topK=256`, registered) | 4 | **90.15%** | 96.00% | 76.86% (93/121) | 86.11% | 95.28% | 100.00% |
| **512**, replayed, run 0 | 1 | 90.20% | 96.00% | 78.51% (95/121) | 86.11% | 94.49% | 100.00% |
| **512**, replayed, run 1 | 1 | 91.20% | 96.67% | 81.82% (99/121) | 86.11% | 94.49% | 100.00% |
| **512**, mean | 2 | **90.70%** | 96.34% | **80.17% (97/121)** | 86.11% | 94.49% | 100.00% |

Both arms were replayed through the same freshly constructed judge in the same job, so the paired
statistics are internally consistent; the baseline is the check that the replay is faithful.

| check | replayed | registered | drift |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| reference-pipeline overall | 44.20% (221/500, both runs) | 44.60 / 44.75 / 45.00 / 44.70 | **−0.35 to −0.80** |
| reference-pipeline MR | 84.30% (102/121) / 85.12% (103/121) | 86.78% (105/121) | −1.7 to −2.5 |
| feature abstention rate | 6.40% | 6.40% | 0.00 |

The baseline's three-question drop is the instrument, not the arm: the reference pipeline is a fixed
function of the dataset and the reader, and the only thing that changed between the two readings is a
fresh draw of judge verdicts. **So a comparison of 90.70 against 90.15 carries about half a point of
instrument drift in an unknown direction**, which is one of two reasons the number below is not
promoted.

### 13.238.2 The four predictions

| # | prediction (§13.234, verbatim) | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR's correct ≥ **96 of 121** | mean **97/121** (95, 99) | **MET** |
| 2 | the gain concentrates in the 41-question outside-pool cohort: ≥ 3 of 16 convert | **not computable from this artifact** | **UNTESTED** |
| 3 | `featureAggregate.avg` ≥ **91.5%** | **90.70%**; falsified only below 90.5 | **IN THE DEAD ZONE** |
| 4 | the four other capabilities hold inside §13.118.5's spread | IE +0.34, KU 0.00, TR −0.79, ABS 0.00 | **MET** |

Prediction 3 is the one worth naming precisely. §13.234 wrote a threshold to meet (91.5) and a
threshold to be refuted by (90.5) and left the interval between them undefined, and the reading landed
**inside that interval** at 90.70. A prediction with a dead zone cannot be read as either, and the
right response is to write down that it happened rather than to pick the nearer edge: the honest
statement is *"the pool change did not produce the 1.35 points prediction 3 asked for, and it did not
produce the −0.35 that would have refuted it either"*.

That is the registration's own defect, and it is the third of its kind in this campaign (a threshold
without a stated band, a metric read as another metric in §13.235, a fixture written against the reader
instead of the producer in §13.236.5). **The pattern is that a number is stated without the region
where it means nothing.**

### 13.238.3 What the reading decides, and what it does not

**It decides that `topK=512` is not adopted.** The reason is not that it lost; it is that the thing it
was supposed to move is inside the spread of the thing measuring it:

| quantity | value |
| --- | ---: |
| the increment being claimed | +0.55 (90.15 → 90.70) |
| the registered arm's own run-to-run spread | 1.60 (89.40, 90.15, 91.00, 90.10) |
| the 512 arm's run-to-run spread | 1.00 (90.20, 91.20) |
| the replay's instrument drift, measured on the baseline | 0.35–0.80 |

A change whose effect is smaller than the arm's own variance and comparable to the instrument's drift
is not a change this repository adopts on two repetitions. It also costs 256 extra scored candidates
per question at retrieval time, which §13.234 priced at "zero prompt tokens but not zero retrieval",
so the trade is a real cost for an unmeasurable gain.

**It does not decide prediction 2, and therefore does not license 1,024.** §13.234 said so before the
run: *"If prediction 2 is met at the lower bound, the next step is 1,024 as a second point on the same
curve rather than a new mechanism."* Prediction 2 is untestable from this artifact because the artifact
does not record which questions had their gold turn outside the 256-pool -- `goldRanks` is capped at
255, so "outside" and "at 255" are the same value. The cohort has to be recomputed against the
relevance index at both widths, which needs the embedding cache rather than another dispatch.

**And it moves the target off the pool.** MR at 256 was 76.86%, at 512 it is 80.17% on the mean, and
the baseline gets 84.30–86.78% **with no memory at all**. Doubling the candidate pool bought 2 to 3
points of a gap that is 8 to 10 points wide against a system that reads the whole history. The pool is
a second-order term here; §13.233 already located the first-order one (the count/operand judgement:
`recover` reaches only the 10 declined questions, and the 28 wrong answers are all answered-and-wrong).

### 13.238.4 What this cost, and what it would have cost

| route | wall clock | provider requests |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| re-dispatch the 8-pass arm at `topK=512`, unpaced | ~300 min | ~4,000 reader + ~750 judge |
| **regrade the recording** | **14 min** | **755 judge, 0 reader** |

The 5h41m the dead run spent was not wasted after all -- but that is a sentence about the fix, not
about the run. The run produced no report because nothing had been built to grade a recording, and the
first thing this campaign should have had was the thing that makes any run's answers survive it.

### 13.238.5 What the control's 44.20% is, and is not

Reading the replay makes one number newly legible that every prior artifact contained and none of them
explained: the `reference-pipeline` arm records **246 declines out of 500**, and scores **IE 1/150**
and **KU 1/72**. A pipeline that reads the whole history and answers two of those abilities correctly
is not "no memory"; it is a pipeline whose prompt declines on the routes where the history does not fit.

That is a property of the control, not of the treatment, and it changes what the +46-point delta means:

| reading | supported? |
| --- | --- |
| "cortex-memory is 46 points better than an agent with no memory" | **no** -- the control is not a memoryless agent, it is this product's prompt with the memory arm switched off, and on IE and KU it declines |
| "cortex-memory is 46 points better than the same product without its memory arm" | yes, and that is the ablation's actual claim |
| "MR's 76.86% is below the baseline's 84.30-86.78%" | yes, and **this is the one capability where the control is strong**, so it is the one where the comparison is informative -- which is exactly why §13.233 and §13.238.3 treat MR's gap as the campaign's real target |

The external number for "no memory at all" is not this arm; it is the full-history baseline in the
ledger (57.6%, `SOTA-LANDSCAPE`), and against *that* the margin is 32.6 points rather than 46. Both are
true statements about different controls, and the campaign's own doctrine -- "a number is only
comparable together with the conditions it was taken under" -- is what requires them to be kept apart
rather than quoted interchangeably.

This is not a defect to fix in the arm. It is a defect in how the arm's delta has been *described*, and
it is the fourth instance this round of the same pattern: a field that exists, is correct, and is read
as something it is not.

## 13.239 A character room is not a depth: the budget becomes per route, derived rather than guessed

*§13.238 closed the pool axis and handed back a target: MR's gap to its own no-memory baseline is
8 to 10 points, and doubling the candidate pool bought 2 to 3 of them. This section is the other
half of the same arithmetic, and it needed no new run to find -- every number below is recomputed
from `41546569106`'s own artifact.*

### 13.239.1 The defect, in one table

A budget of characters is converted into a **depth** by each route's own turn length, and depth is
what decides how much of the answer's evidence arrives. One room of 48,000 therefore became five
different experiments:

| route | chars per delivered turn | delivered turns | in-pool gold delivered | prompt chars (median) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `flat` (IE, 150 q) | 723 | 61 | 86.8% | 46,864 |
| `knowledge-update` (72 q) | 717 | 62 | 80.1% | 46,868 |
| `abstention` (30 q) | 596 | 72 | 69.7% | 46,471 |
| `multi-session` (MR, 121 q) | 215 | 174 | **94.8%** | 46,264 |
| `temporal` (TR, 127 q) | 205 | 179 | 92.9% | 47,149 |

The same number bought **2.9 times more ranking on `temporal` than on `flat`**, and nothing in any
artifact said so. The coverage column is `goldOverlap.goldRanks` read against
`windowComposition.turns`, i.e. the share of in-pool gold whose rank is inside the depth the run
actually delivered -- so it is a property of the **selection**, recomputable from the artifact, and
free.

### 13.239.2 The consequence, which is that the room has been in the wrong place

The room needed to deliver **all** in-pool gold, derived per route:

| route | room for 100% | what it costs against 48,000 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `multi-session` | **55,000** | **+16%** |
| `temporal` | 52,400 | +9% |
| `abstention` | 152,600 | 3.2x -- unaffordable |
| `knowledge-update` | 180,000 | 3.8x |
| `flat` | 184,400 | 3.9x |

**MR is the cheapest route to completeness in the set and the one with the largest accuracy deficit**,
and the reason is arithmetic rather than luck: its turns are 215 characters, so a turn of depth is
15% of the price of a turn of depth on `flat`. Meanwhile the last third of every room buys the last
tenth of the coverage -- `multi-session` reaches 79.0% at depth 60 (12,900 characters) and 94.8% at
174 (46,264).

### 13.239.3 Which route converts coverage into accuracy, measured

Full-coverage questions against partial ones, same artifact:

| route | full coverage | accuracy | partial coverage | accuracy | reading |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `multi-session` | 75 | **84.0%** | 46 | **65.2%** | **+18.8, 2.3 SE -- coverage converts** |
| `temporal` | 72 | 95.8% | 55 | 94.5% | +1.3, no signal |
| `flat` | 77 | 94.8% | 73 | 97.3% | **-2.5, coverage does not predict** |
| `knowledge-update` | 5 | 100.0% | 67 | 85.1% | suggestive, n=5 |
| `abstention` | 4 | 100.0% | 26 | 100.0% | the route is decided by the contract |

So the redistribution has a direction that is measured rather than chosen: **deepen
`multi-session`, fund it from `flat`.** `flat`'s split is the only one in the table where partial
coverage scores *higher* than full, and MR's is the only one where the difference survives its own
standard error.

### 13.239.4 The instrument, and why the width is derived rather than tuned

`tools/evidence-depth.py` takes an artifact and prints the coverage curve per route, the accuracy
split, and the room each route needs for a stated coverage target:

```
room needed for           85%        90%        95%        99%       100%
multi-session           18700      25600      38100      50300      55000
flat                    39100      61500     101300     164900     184400
```

It prints a room and refuses to print a score. Coverage explains part of the accuracy on one route
and none of it on another, so a tool that turned the curve into a predicted score would be asserting
the thing the campaign has to measure. What it does assert is arithmetic: the room is the smallest
depth that clears the target times the route's own measured density, searched over every integer
depth rather than over the printed grid (a grid-derived room is a room derived from the grid, and the
difference is turns of prompt no measurement asked for).

### 13.239.5 The registration

One knob, `maxPromptCharsByRoute`, dispatched through the existing budget input as
`<route>:<chars>` pairs -- it rides `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` rather than taking a 25th
dispatch input, because the workflow sits one input below GitHub's ceiling and its suite forbids the
ceiling. The two shapes cannot be confused: a scalar is digits, a map contains a colon.

| field | registered arm (`41546569106`) | this dispatch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `maxPromptChars` | 48,000 | not named -- the product default, which since §13.213 **is** 48,000 |
| `maxPromptCharsByRoute` | absent | **`multi-session:55000,flat:36200`** |
| everything else | — | unchanged, byte for byte |

**The spend, computed on the registered artifact before the run:**

| quantity | registered | this dispatch | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mean prompt chars | 46,630 | **45,629** | **-2.1%** |
| total prompt chars over 500 questions | 23.32M | 22.81M | -0.50M |
| MR depth (turns) | 174 | **256** | +47% |
| MR in-pool gold delivered | 94.8% | **100.0%** | +5.2 |
| `flat` depth | 61 | 50 | -18% |
| `flat` in-pool gold delivered | 86.8% | 84.2% | -2.6 |

This is a **redistribution, not an increase**: the mean prompt gets *shorter*. That matters for the
campaign's eighth requirement (spend less, do not do worse) and it is why the map names a route to cut
rather than only a route to deepen.

### 13.239.6 Predictions, and what each outcome means

| # | prediction | falsified by | meaning if falsified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR in-pool gold delivered >= **99.0%**, computed from this run's own `goldRanks` | < 97% | the room was not what limited delivery on MR, and the depth arithmetic in §13.239.2 is wrong about this route |
| 2 | MR correct >= **96 of 121** (the §13.234 threshold, so the two are comparable; the registered arm is 93) | <= 94 | **coverage does not convert to accuracy on MR**, so retrieval is exhausted there and the 8-to-10-point gap to the no-memory baseline is a reasoning deficit. This is the outcome that would save the campaign the most future work, and it is worth the run either way |
| 3 | `flat` >= **141 of 150** (94.0%; the registered arm is 144) | <= 139 | `flat` needs what was taken from it, and its full-versus-partial split was noise |
| 4 | overall `featureAggregate.avg` >= **90.15%** | < 90.15 | the two routes' movements cancel or the redistribution costs more than it buys |
| 5 | mean `promptChars` <= **46,630** (the registered mean) | > 46,630 | the map was dispatched with a wider global room than it was priced at, and the token claim in §13.239.5 does not hold |

Prediction 2 is the one this section is for. MR is 121 of 500 questions at 76.86%, and its
full-coverage accuracy is 84.0% -- so if coverage is the whole mechanism, the ceiling is
`(75 x 0.84 + 46 x 0.84) / 121 = 84.0%`, i.e. **MR +7.1 points and overall +1.7**. Half of that
converting is +0.85 overall, which is the difference between 90.15 and 91.00.

**Status: judged, three false** (§13.243). The first dispatch meant to answer them (`41751619617`)
left twenty-one of its twenty-two inputs blank and measured the product's configuration instead; the
second (`41773546221`) sent all twenty-two and declared one. Predictions 1, 2 and 4 are **false**,
3 and 5 are true, and prediction 2's falsification carries the meaning this paragraph pre-registered:
**coverage does not convert to accuracy on MR.**

### 13.239.7 What this section does not claim

1. **It is not a budget sweep.** That axis is retired with a measured exchange rate: 24,000 to
   48,000 bought +0.60 (§14.31), so the second half of the room converts about 0.6 accuracy points.
   This experiment holds the total *down* while moving where it is spent, which is a different claim.
2. **It does not set a per-question width.** The depth a question needs is not observable before it
   is answered, and the quantity that *is* observable is the route. A per-question policy would need a
   signal correlated with the gold depth, and `goldRanks` is an evaluation field -- using it to size
   the prompt would be reading the answer key.
3. **It says nothing about `knowledge-update` or `abstention`.** Both need 3.2-3.8x the room for
   completeness, which is unaffordable at any budget this campaign has measured, and KU's split rests
   on five questions.
4. **It does not re-derive MR's ranking.** Coverage rises because the room is deeper, not because the
   order is better: the gold's median rank inside the pool is 134 and stays 134.

## 13.240 Two retired levers were one lever, and the largest-looking lever is bounded by coverage

*Three decisions taken without a dispatch: a currency identified, an external bar adopted, and a
mechanism demoted. The third is the one that cost the most to accept, because the external evidence
for it was the strongest number in the paper.*

### 13.240.1 The exchange rate of coverage, measured twice

§13.238 retired the candidate pool (+0.55 for 2x the candidates, inside a run-to-run spread of 1.60)
and §14.31 retired the evidence room (+0.60 for 2x the characters). Both were read as separate
failures. They are the same purchase:

| lever | what it doubles | measured effect | resolution |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `relevanceTopK` 256 -> 512 | candidates scored per question | +0.55 | below the arm's own spread (1.60) |
| `maxPromptChars` 24,000 -> 48,000 | characters delivered | +0.60 | at the floor of detection |
| **depth, per route** (§13.239) | turns delivered | **null** | +14% depth, +1.6 coverage, 0 accuracy; three of five predictions false (§13.243) |

All three buy **the same quantity** -- how much of the in-pool gold is inside the delivered evidence --
and the first two priced it at roughly **0.6 accuracy points per doubling**. That is the exchange rate
this campaign has been paying for coverage without knowing it, and it is why §13.239 is written as a
*redistribution* rather than a purchase: the remaining coverage is affordable only where a route's
turns are cheap, which is an ordering rather than a price.

### 13.240.2 The external bar, and the one claim it changes

`SOTA-LANDSCAPE` has carried Raw-RAG since it was scanned; what had not been read is the paper's own
**evidence-token** measurement, which is the field that makes our context spend comparable:

| quantity | Raw-RAG (arXiv 2610.30755, Table 20) | this arm (`41546569106`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| corpus | LongMemEval, 500 questions | same |
| evidence tokens, median | **11,248.5** | **~11.7K** (46,834 characters) |
| evidence tokens, mean | 11,355.6 | — |
| reader | GPT-4.1-mini | deepseek-chat |
| accuracy | 87.53 (default), 89.93 (Qwen3 rerank) | **90.15** |

So the sentence §13.231 and §1.16 of the competitor analysis both leaned on -- "we read 1.9-3.9x what
the leaders read" -- holds **only against vendor self-reports**, none of which publishes a readable
configuration. Against the one baseline whose reader, judge, chunking and token budget are all
stated, our context is 4% larger and our accuracy is **2.6 points higher**. The claim is narrowed
rather than withdrawn, and the narrowing is recorded in both repositories.

### 13.240.3 The reranker's ceiling is the coverage deficit it repairs

Raw-RAG's own ablation is the strongest external evidence any single stage in this campaign has had:

| variant | MemoryAgentBench total | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Raw-RAG | 48.32 | — |
| **without the reranker** | **44.40** | **-3.92** (Holm-adjusted p = 0.0012) |
| + atomic fact extraction | 28.70 | -19.62 |
| + summary augmentation | 42.51 | -5.81 |
| + graph expansion | 42.54 | -5.78 |
| + turn de-duplication | 45.93 | -2.39 |

The natural reading is "add a reranker". Three facts, all local, say otherwise:

1. **This arm has measured it.** `VERDICT-B1-RERANKING`: cross-encoder reranking, run `35624110842`,
   150 questions, **+1.33 pp (131 vs 129 of 150), McNemar p = 0.7539**, verdict *inconclusive by power*.
2. **The paper's effect lives where coverage is low.** The same paper measures coverage at
   **19.07-45.29%** (MemoryAgentBench) and 35.69-76.35% (MEME) across the systems it compares; this
   arm's coverage is **84.2-100%** per route (§13.239.1). A reranker repairs one failure -- the right
   evidence is in the pool and ranked too low -- and there is far less of that failure to repair at
   nine-tenths coverage than at one-third.
3. **The power arithmetic does not close.** B1's discordant rate is 10/150 = 6.7%, so 500 questions
   give about 33 discordant pairs, and a McNemar exact test at that n needs roughly a 23/10 split to
   reach p < 0.05 -- an overall effect of about **2.6 points**. B1 measured 1.33. Re-running at 500
   questions would therefore still be underpowered; it would just cost five times as much to learn
   the same nothing.

A stage worth 3.92 points on a corpus whose coverage is a third of ours, and 1.33 on ours, is not
evidence that the stage is worth 3.92 here. **The quantity that transfers between corpora is the
coverage deficit, not the delta.**

### 13.240.4 What replaces it, and why this one is powered

The same artifact carries a row that had not been read as a lever:

| arm | reader | window | MR |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| `reference-pipeline` (this product with the memory arm off) | **the same DeepSeek** | **smaller** | **86.78%** |
| `cortex-memory` (registered) | same | retrieved | **76.86%** |

Same reader, same 500 questions, same judge, a **smaller** window, **+9.92 points**. That row excludes
three axes this campaign has spent money on -- the reader (identical), coverage (§13.239.2 prices full
coverage at about +7 and is being measured now), and the budget (the control's is smaller) -- and
leaves the **prompt shape**: the reference pipeline asks for the two steps with the notes unwritten,
while this arm has required a list since §13.34.

It is registered as stage **S8**, and unlike B1 it is powered: a 9.9-point effect on 121 questions is
well inside what a paired test resolves, and the bar is a B-grade measurement from our own artifact
rather than a C-grade one from someone else's corpus.

### 13.240.5 What this section does not do

1. **It does not remove the reranker.** The stage stays implemented and configurable; what is retired
   is the *expectation* that turning it on is worth a dispatch at 500 questions.
2. **It does not conclude that the paper is wrong.** Its claim is about its own systems on its own
   corpus, and its coverage numbers are the reason its ablation is large -- which is the reading this
   section adopts rather than disputes.
3. **It does not settle MR.** §13.239's prediction 2 and S8 both target MR and they are not rival
   explanations: depth and contract can each be worth points, and the two dispatches are ordered
   rather than exclusive.

## 13.241 Prediction 2 was computable. The regrade had thrown away the rows that answer it

*A correction to §13.238.2, and the third instance this campaign has found of the same shape: a field
that exists, is correct, and is not carried to the place where the decision is made.*

### 13.241.1 What §13.238.2 said, and what is true

§13.238.2 recorded prediction 2 as **"not computable from this artifact"** and gave the reason
"`goldRanks` caps at 255, so 'outside the pool' and 'at 255' are the same value". **The reason is
false.** `goldRanks` encodes a gold turn the ranking never surfaced as **`-1`**; `254` is a rank inside
a 256-wide pool. The two are different values in the same array, and the array is lossless about which
is which.

Recomputed from `41546569106`'s own artifact:

| scope | questions | with at least one gold never surfaced | of those, wrong |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| all capabilities | 500 | **161** | 26 |
| `multi-session` (MR) | 121 | **41** | **16** |

That is §13.234's prediction **verbatim**: *"the gain concentrates in the 41-question outside-pool
cohort: at least 3 of 16 convert"*. Both of its numbers reproduce exactly from the registered
artifact, with no new measurement. The prediction's scope is MR, and the difference between the two
rows is why scope has to be stated: over all 161 questions a different (and much easier) prediction is
being read.

### 13.241.2 What was genuinely missing, and it was one field

The *conversion* -- how many of those 16 answer correctly at `topK=512` -- needs per-question verdicts
of the 512 arm. Those existed when `41741547141` ran: it scored 2,000 answers through the same scorer.
What it wrote was five aggregate numbers per repetition:

```json
{ "run": 0, "baseline": {...}, "feature": {...}, "delta": 0.46,
  "discordant": {"baselineCorrectFeatureIncorrect": 19, "baselineIncorrectFeatureCorrect": 249},
  "mcnemarPValue": 2.66e-52 }
```

`discordant` is a **count**, not a list of ids, and `questions` was never written. So the measurement
existed for the length of one process and the report kept only its summary -- the same failure as
§13.236.7's "the measurement existed and the report did not", one level down.

### 13.241.3 The repair, in two places

| # | change | where | why there |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `pairedRows(questions)` -- id, capability, correct, `goldRanks`, `goldPool`, delivered turns, prompt chars | `cortex-eval/src/paired-readout.ts` | a projection that decides what a paired reading can see is not a bench script's business to own untested; 500 short objects per repetition against the 75 MB a full record set would carry |
| 2 | `tools/pool-cohort.py` -- reads the cohort off a live artifact and the verdicts off a regrade, with `--capability` and `--expect` as parameters | `tools/` | the cohort is a comparison, not a count: the tool prints conversion **inside** the cohort against conversion outside it, and McNemar on each |

Two properties are asserted rather than hoped for:

- **A missing row is an error, not a zero.** A question absent from the replay aborts the read, because
  a cohort read over a subset is a conversion rate for a population nobody defined.
- **A regrade written before this section is refused with its reason**, not read as an empty cohort:
  "a regrade written before §13.241 has only aggregates, and a cohort is not recoverable from an
  aggregate -- re-run the regrade with the current tool".

### 13.241.4 Why it is worth a re-regrade

The decision prediction 2 was written to licence -- `topK=1024` -- has already been declined on other
grounds (§13.238.3), so closing it changes no plan. It is worth doing anyway for one reason that has
nothing to do with the pool: **a prediction recorded as "untested" when it was computable is a false
statement in a registration**, and the campaign's whole method rests on that document being exact. The
cost of the correction is 755 judge calls and about fourteen minutes, which is the cheapest reading in
this file.

### 13.241.5 The pattern, named for the fourth time

| instance | the field | how it was lost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §13.236.5 | `rateLimited` | a fixture written against the reader (`boolean`) while the producer wrote a count |
| §13.238.2 | a stated threshold | a prediction with a dead zone between "meet" and "refute" |
| §13.240.3 | the reranker's 3.92 | a delta carried from a corpus with a third of our coverage |
| **here** | `goldRanks` | a report that kept the summary and dropped the rows |

Four instances, four different mechanisms, one sentence: **a number is usable only where it is still
attached to the thing it was measured on.** The repair in each case was to move the number to the place
the decision is made, not to measure it again.

### 13.241.6 The repair was necessary and not sufficient, and the guard said so

`41754705249` re-ran the regrade on the commit carrying `pairedRows`. Its own log:

```
Alignment: 4 index/id pair(s) confirmed against the dispatched run's progress log
Run 0: the report carried no question records, so no paired cohort can be read from it.
       This is written as null rather than as an empty list.
Run 1: the report carried no question records, so no paired cohort can be read from it.
```

So the projection is correct and the roster is still empty, because **`AblationReport.questions` is
not built by the report path at all**. It is built inside `runAblation` (`runner.ts`), after the
ablation, from `recordableTraces` -- the per-question trace objects that function holds and does not
return. `runAblationReport` consumes the ablation's *outputs*; the traces are not among them. A
regrade calls the report function directly, so it has no traces and therefore no roster.

Two readings of that, and the second is the one that matters:

1. **The null-versus-empty distinction paid for itself on its first run.** A `[]` would have read as
   "this run graded zero questions" and the absence would have been invisible for a second time --
   which is exactly the failure this section was written about. The guard turned a silent drop into a
   printed sentence, and the sentence names the consequence.

2. **The remaining fix is an API, not a projection.** The regrade needs the traces, and the only
   honest way to get them is for the ablation to return or persist them -- which is also what the
   B7 criterion and the noise model need, and both are already waiting on the same field. Until then
   prediction 2 stays **untested**, and the reason is now the true one: *the per-question traces are
   held by the runner and not returned*, not *`goldRanks` caps at 255*.

The three things this thread produced are worth keeping regardless: the cohort arithmetic (§13.241.1,
41 and 16 reproduced exactly), the tool (`tools/pool-cohort.py`, 12 tests, which reads a cohort the
moment one exists), and the guard that announced its own insufficiency in the run's log.

## 13.242 A dispatch that filled in one input and left twenty-one blank ran the product, not the arm

*§13.239 registered a redistribution and predicted five readings. The dispatch that was meant to
test it sent a budget map and nothing else, so the arm it actually measured was the **product's**
configuration — and the number that came back, 85.00%, is five points below the headline it would
have been compared against. This section is about the 87 minutes, and about why the guard that
caught it caught it too late.*

### 13.242.1 The run, and the number that would have been quoted

`41751619617`, dispatched at 01:05 with `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars=multi-session:55000,flat:36200`
and `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k=256`:

| quantity | registered arm (`41546569106`) | this run |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `featureAggregate.avg` | **90.15%** | **85.25%** (84.80 / 85.25 / 85.80) |
| first pass | 90.15% | 85.00% |
| baseline (`reference-pipeline`) | 44.20% median | 44.70% median |
| IE (150) | 96.00% | 95.33% |
| MR (121) | 76.86% (93) | **71.90% (87)** |
| KU (72) | 86.11% | 86.11% |
| TR (127) | 95.28% | **81.89%** |
| ABS (30) | 100.00% | 96.67% |
| wall clock | — | **87 minutes** |

The spend was real: 5,867 calls, 27.09M prompt tokens, 2.19M completion, 75.11% of the prompt
served from the prefix cache, zero retries, zero `429`. **Nothing failed.** The run built a
complete 500-question artifact, passed ten of eleven self-checks, and would have been quoted as
*"the redistribution costs five points"* by anyone reading the summary table — which is precisely
the wrong conclusion, because the redistribution never ran.

### 13.242.2 The blank is not the defect; the blank's meaning is

The workflow forwards `CORTEX_MEMORY_ASK` and its siblings **blank on purpose**, and that decision
is correct: if the file also wrote `route`, the default would live in two places and the two would
eventually disagree, which is the defect §13.69 was written about. So a blank input is forwarded as
an empty environment variable and the product fills in its own default.

That is exactly right for a *step* and wrong for a *dispatch input*, because the product's default
is not the registered arm. The registration fixes six of those fields to values that are **not**
their defaults — `ask=operands+operand-gap`, `relevance=retrieval-hybrid`,
`promptContract=abstention-evidence-blocks`, `maxTurnChars=400`,
`maxTurnCharsRoutes=multi-session,temporal`, `evidenceRolesRoutes=multi-session,temporal` — and a
dispatch that omits them gets none of the six.

The artifact said so, in six lines:

```
UNDECLARED  ask: "operands+operand-gap" (registered) -> "route" (ran)
UNDECLARED  evidenceRolesRoutes: ["multi-session","temporal"] -> [all six]
UNDECLARED  maxTurnChars: 400 (registered) -> <-absent-> (ran)
UNDECLARED  maxTurnCharsRoutes: ["multi-session","temporal"] -> [all six]
UNDECLARED  promptContract: "abstention-evidence-blocks" -> "abstention"
UNDECLARED  relevanceSignal: "retrieval-hybrid" -> "retrieval"
```

**The gate was right and it was 87 minutes late.** `readout-arm-run.py --registration` can only
read the artifact, and the artifact exists only after the money is spent. That is the whole of the
defect this section repairs.

### 13.242.3 Why the new gate reads the payload and not the environment

`tools/registration-preflight.py` runs before the build and compares the dispatch's **own inputs**
against `dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py`'s table (which `test_preregistration_config.py` already pins
to §10.3, so this is reading the registration rather than a fourth copy of it).

The environment would have been the obvious source and it cannot work, for the reason in §13.242.2:
a forwarded blank and an unset variable are the same string. Only `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` keeps the
difference — **a key that is absent was never asked for** — and the difference is the whole signal.

Two inputs make the case on their own:

| input | workflow fallback when blank | registered | what an environment read would report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `60` | `0` | `60`, a value, and a plausible one |
| `thinking` | `disabled` | `multi-session+temporal` | `disabled` |

A gate reading the environment would have passed a 60-question run whose thinking was off, because
both values are non-empty and both look dispatched.

### 13.242.4 Two gates, two questions, and why the counts differ

| gate | question | when | reads | answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `registration-preflight.py` | what was **asked for** | before the build | the event payload | 15 departures on this dispatch |
| `readout-arm-run.py --registration` | what **ran** | after the artifact | the artifact's `memoryArmConfig` | 6 departures on this run |

Fifteen against six is not a disagreement. The artifact comparison derives `askRoutes` from `ask`,
`evidenceRoles` from `evidenceRolesRoutes` and `maxPromptChars` from its own input, so three of the
fifteen are not separately observable; three more (`limit`, `temperature`, `model`/`thinking` at the
harness level) are harness properties the artifact does not carry as arm fields; and the rest are
the same six read through a different surface. **The input-layer count is the larger one because it
is the earlier question**, and an earlier question is worth answering on a larger set.

Neither gate replaces the other: a run that changes a value *inside* the harness passes the
preflight and is still caught by the artifact comparison, and a run that departs before it starts is
caught by the preflight in five seconds rather than caught by the other one in 87 minutes.

### 13.242.5 The declaration has two failure modes

`CORTEX_DECLARED_DEPARTURES` is written by the dispatcher, and this run declared
`cortex_memory_relevance_top_k` — a key that **did not move** (256 was sent, 256 was registered).
The gate said so:

```
declared but unchanged: ['cortex_memory_relevance_top_k'] -- the departure names a field
this run did not move, so the record describes an intention rather than what ran
```

So the list can be wrong in two directions, and both are now reported:

| shape | meaning | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a field moved and is not listed | the run is an experiment that has not said so | **fail** |
| a field is listed and did not move | the record describes an intention | pass, with the note |

The second is a pass because the dispatch itself is legal — the note is the repair. The first is a
failure because a reader who cannot tell which fields moved cannot attribute the delta.

The preflight prints the declared list **by value**, not by count, so a stale variable (left over
from a previous dispatch that this one did not write) is visible in the log rather than being
inherited silently.

### 13.242.6 What this run's reading may and may not be used for

**May:** nothing causal. Five fields moved at once (`ask`, `relevance`, `promptContract`,
`maxTurnChars`, `evidenceRolesRoutes`) and the budget was also re-narrowed, so the 5.15-point gap
cannot be split among them, and this section does not try.

**May, as arithmetic:** the per-capability column reconciles the headline exactly — the weighted sum
of the five capability deltas is **−5.00** against a −5.15 headline, and the residual is the
difference between a first pass and a four-run mean. That is an identity check, not an explanation.

**May, as the one thing worth keeping:** the direction of each capability's movement is the direction
its missing mechanism predicts. `relevance` losing its rare-keyword channel and `maxTurnChars`
losing its cap is where TR's **−13.39** should land, and TR is the route with the longest turns in
the set; `ask` losing the operands contract is where MR's **−4.96** should land, and MR is the route
whose contract exists to make it count (§13.34, §13.203). KU does not move, and KU is the route none
of the five fields targets.

**May not:** be quoted as `cortex-memory` at 85.00%. The product's default configuration is a
legitimate object of study, but it is not the registered arm and this document's headline is not it.

### 13.242.7 What is still open

1. **§13.239's five predictions are still untested.** Not falsified — *untested*, because the
   dispatch that was meant to test them did not run the registered arm. Prediction 2 (MR ≥ 96/121)
   and prediction 4 (overall ≥ 90.15%) are the two the campaign most wanted, and both are still
   owed a run.
2. ~~**`census-unit` failed on this artifact and the failure is a consequence, not a defect.**~~
   **Retracted by §13.244.** It is a defect, and the six departed fields have nothing to do with it:
   this run had `workers=4`, and the census was read off worker 0. 456 is that worker's share of four
   passes over 500 questions -- `41773546221`, which declared one departure and left nothing blank,
   came back at 488 for the same reason.
3. **Every future dispatch goes through `tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py`.** The preflight makes a
   hand-rolled dispatch *fail* rather than *lie*, which is the point, but the dispatcher is what
   sends the twenty-two inputs and writes the declaration that matches them.

## 13.243 The redistribution ran, four of its five predictions are false, and the falsification is the result

*`41773546221` is the dispatch §13.242 was written to make possible: twenty-two inputs, one declared
departure (`maxPromptChars`), the preflight green in five seconds, 87 minutes of wall clock. This
section reads it. The headline did not move. What moved is the campaign's belief about what limits
MR.*

### 13.243.1 The five predictions, judged

| # | prediction | falsified by | measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR in-pool gold delivered ≥ **99.0%** | < 97% | **96.4%** | **false** |
| 2 | MR correct ≥ **96 of 121** | ≤ 94 | **92** first pass, 93.5 mean | **false** |
| 3 | `flat` ≥ **141 of 150** | ≤ 139 | **141** | **true**, with no margin |
| 4 | overall `featureAggregate.avg` ≥ **90.15%** | < 90.15 | **88.80%** first pass, **89.75%** mean | **false** |
| 5 | mean `promptChars` ≤ **46,630** | > 46,630 | **46,125** | **true** |

Prediction 3 passing at exactly its threshold is not a pass to celebrate: `flat`'s room was cut to
36,200 and its depth fell 61 → **52**, and the three questions it cost are the three the prediction
budgeted for. The bar was set at 141 because that is what a 2.6-point coverage loss should cost, and
it cost exactly that.

### 13.243.2 Prediction 2 was the one this section was for, and it came back false

§13.239.6 wrote its own falsifier's meaning in advance:

> *coverage does not convert to accuracy on MR, so retrieval is exhausted there and the 8-to-10-point
> gap to the no-memory baseline is a reasoning deficit. This is the outcome that would save the
> campaign the most future work, and it is worth the run either way.*

That is what happened. The evidence is stronger than the headline, because the coverage split moved
in a way that makes the null a composition effect rather than a flat line:

| | registered arm (`41546569106`) | this run (`41773546221`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MR depth (turns delivered) | 174 | **198** (+14%) |
| MR in-pool gold delivered | 94.8% | **96.4%** |
| MR questions at full coverage | 75 | **82** (+7) |
| accuracy, full coverage | 84.0% | **89.0%** (+5.0) |
| accuracy, partial coverage | 65.2% | **48.7%** (−16.5) |
| accuracy, all 121 | 76.86% (93) | **76.03% (92)** |

Read the rows together and the mechanism is visible. **Seven questions moved from the partial band
into the full band, and the full band's accuracy rose five points — and the route's accuracy did not
move at all.** Two things are true at once and both matter:

1. **Full coverage is worth 89.0%**, which is three points above the reference pipeline's 86.78% on
   the same route. When the evidence is complete, this arm reads better than the pipeline it loses to.
2. **The seven questions that arrived at full coverage did not become correct.** The partial band's
   accuracy fell from 65.2 to 48.7 because the questions left in it are the harder ones, and the
   arrivals did not compensate. Coverage was not what separated them from their answers.

So the 8-to-10-point gap to the no-memory baseline is **not a retrieval-room deficit**. An arm that
delivers 96.4% of the in-pool gold on MR and still reads 76% has exhausted what this axis can buy,
and the next MR experiment has to be a reading experiment rather than a retrieval one.

### 13.243.3 Prediction 1 was false for a reason worth keeping

55,000 characters bought **198** turns, not the 256 that §13.239.2 derived from a density of 215
characters per turn, and 96.4% coverage, not 100%. The density moved: **189 characters per turn**
under the wider room.

That is not a broken derivation, it is a measured property of the selection. A wider room admits
turns that the narrower room excluded, and the marginal turn is shorter than the average one — so
the density is a function of the depth, and the linear conversion `room = target × density` holds
only inside the band where the density was measured. §13.239.4's tool searched every integer depth
precisely to avoid a grid artefact; what it could not avoid is that the density it multiplies by is
itself a function of the depth it is solving for.

**The repair is not a larger constant.** A 99% target on this route needs the density curve, not one
point of it, and §13.243.2 says the target would not have paid anyway.

### 13.243.4 The verdict: not adopted, and the reason is not the headline

| quantity | registered | this run | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `featureAggregate.avg` (4 runs) | 90.15% | 89.75% | **−0.40** |
| first pass | 90.15% | 88.80% | −1.35 |
| run-to-run range of the arm | 1.60 | **2.20** (88.80 to 91.00) | — |
| mean prompt chars | 46,630 | 46,125 | **−1.1%** |

−0.40 is **inside** the arm's own spread, so this is a null rather than a regression: the honest
statement is *"the redistribution moved nothing measurable, and three of its five predictions are
false"*, not *"it costs 0.40"*. The registration stands at 90.15% and the map is not adopted.

That distinction matters for the campaign's rule about reverting a regression on evidence. There is
no evidence of harm here — there is evidence of **no effect plus a falsified mechanism**, and the
second is the one that changes the plan.

### 13.243.5 A measurement defect this run exposed, stated with what has been ruled out

The artifact's `census-unit` check failed: **488 outcomes against 2,000 question-answers** (122 per
pass over 500 questions). The registered arm's own artifact sums to **2,000** exactly. Three things
have been ruled out rather than guessed at:

| hypothesis | how it was ruled out |
| --- | --- |
| the map changed the budget for the unnamed routes | the per-route mean `promptChars` for `abstention` (46,318), `knowledge-update` (46,575) and `temporal` (47,138) are **identical** to the registered arm's, field for field |
| the arm consulted more than once per question | `vote` passes (one consultation per question) and `recovery` reports 0 consultations |
| `maxPromptChars` defaulting to unbounded caused it | ruled out by the first row: an unbounded room that changes no prompt cannot change a counter |

What is left is the wiring — and the paragraph that followed this table in the first draft of this
section named it wrongly. It said *"122 per pass is 121 MR questions plus one, which is what a census
that only records the session route would look like"*. **That is a coincidence**, and §13.244 is the
correction: 122 is not `MR + 1`, it is `500 / 4` — worker 0's share of four workers, rounded down by
jitter. The `+1` was noise being read as a mechanism, and the reading survived review because it
explained the number.

**The abstention rate in this artifact is not quotable**, and §13.244 says why in both directions: 28
declines against a 488 denominator and 28 against 2,000 are rates that differ by a factor of four *in
the numerator as well as the denominator* — the run's real decline count is about four times 28.

### 13.243.6 What changes in the plan

1. **The evidence-room axis is closed on both ends.** Widening it (24k → 48k) bought +0.60 (§14.31);
   redistributing it bought nothing measurable and cost `flat` three questions. The exchange rate is
   the same at both ends because it is the same purchase (§13.240.1), and the purchase is finished.
2. **MR is a reading problem.** An arm at 96.4% delivered gold reading 76% has nothing left to buy on
   the retrieval side, and its full-coverage accuracy (89.0%) is the number a reading experiment has
   to move the whole route toward.
3. **The next MR experiment is §13.239's own runner-up**: the reference pipeline's ask, migrated
   whole — `identify` rather than `enumerate`, answer-only, `Answer:` prefix. It is the only
   difference left between two arms that share a reader, a dataset and a judge, and the smaller-window
   arm is 9.92 points ahead.

## 13.244 The pool gave every worker its own instance, and the arm read the census off one of them

*§13.242.7 and §13.243.5 both tried to explain a census that covered a quarter of its run, and both
were wrong. This section states the mechanism, the two artifacts it corrupts, the reading it does
**not** corrupt, and the repair — which is five lines of arithmetic and one enumeration.*

### 13.244.1 The measurement that identified it: a field that is **absent** from the older artifact

The three hypotheses this section replaces were all about the **configuration** (`ask=route`, six
undeclared fields, an unbounded `maxPromptChars`). The answer came from comparing the two artifacts'
log lines, where one field is missing from the older one:

| run | census | log line ends | questions | passes |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `41546569106` (registered) | **2,000** | `... maxPromptChars=48000` | 500 | 4 |
| `41751619617` | **456** | `... maxPromptChars=default, workers=4, minIntervalMs=none ...` | 500 | 4 |
| `41773546221` | **488** | `... maxPromptChars=default, workers=4, minIntervalMs=none ...` | 500 | 4 |

`workers=` is **absent** from the registered arm's line because that run predates §14.22's pool. The
two runs that under-report are the two that have it. And the quotient says the rest:

| run | census / passes | 500 / workers |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `41751619617` | 456 / 4 = **114** | 500 / 4 = 125 |
| `41773546221` | 488 / 4 = **122** | 500 / 4 = 125 |

114 and 122 straddle 125 because the pool claims question **indexes** atomically and workers finish at
different times, so worker 0's share is 122 on average and not exactly 125. No configuration field is
in this arithmetic; a worker count is.

### 13.244.2 The mechanism: a census is per-instance state, and a pool is per-instance by design

§14.22's pool exists because `MemorySystem` carries per-question state in single slots
(`lastRawOutput`, `lastPromptText`, …) and one instance with two calls in flight attributes one
question's prompt to another. The documented answer is **one instance per worker**:

> *So the pool hands each worker its **own instance** of the same configuration, sharing only the
> things that are stateless by design.*

Every census in the arm is instance state of exactly the same kind — `CortexMemory`'s `#reasons`,
`#recoveries`, `#bareRetries`, `#votes` are instance fields — and the arm read them off the `feature`
it was handed, which under a pool is **worker 0**:

```ts
const census = {
  ...abstentionReasonsOf(feature),   // worker 0 only
  ...recoveryOf(feature),
  ...bareRetryOf(feature),
};
```

So a four-worker run published a quarter of its questions as if it were all of them. The unit §13.107
fixed — *"the unit is the question answered"* — was still the unit; the **population** was the defect.

There was a second half, in the CLI rather than the arm:

```ts
featureFor: (worker: number) => (worker === 0 ? feature0 : buildFeature()),
```

Worker 0 reused `feature0` across all four passes, and every other worker got a **fresh instance per
pass**. So instance identity was a function of `(worker, pass)` — which means that even a reader who
knew to look could not have enumerated the set. `BenchmarkWorkerPool.systemFor` had documented the
opposite ("called at most `min(workers, questions)` times") since it was written, so this was a
contract violation that nothing tested.

### 13.244.3 What it does **not** corrupt, stated before what it does

This is the part that decides whether anything previously published has to be withdrawn, so it comes
before the repair.

| quantity | corrupted? | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| accuracy, per capability, per run | **no** | answers are merged by **index** into a pre-sized vector; `workers` changes completion order and nothing else |
| the headline `featureAggregate.avg` | **no** | same arithmetic, same answers; `benchmark-concurrency.test.ts` asserts byte-identity at 3 workers |
| census **counts** | **yes, by ≈ the worker count** | one worker's share reported as the run's |
| census **rates** | **not biased, twice the noise** | numerator and denominator are truncated by the same uniform split, so `28/488 = 5.74%` estimates the same quantity as `130/2,000 = 6.50%` — at `√4 = 2×` the standard error, because the sample is 122 per pass rather than 500 |
| per-capability attribution of a decline | **unreliable** | the split is by claim order, not by route, so a route can be entirely absent from the quarter that was counted |

That table is why the count check is the one that caught it and the rate check could not: **the rate
survives the defect approximately, and the count does not survive it at all.** `41773546221`'s
`5.74%` was within one standard error of the registered arm's `6.50%` and read as a normal run.

### 13.244.4 The repair: enumerate, fold, and refuse a partial answer

`AblationPool` gains `featureInstances()`, and `createAblationPool` is the implementation that cannot
forget it: it memoises one instance per worker (which is what `systemFor` always claimed) and hands
back the list in worker order, worker 0 first.

Three rules, each with its own reason:

1. **Fold, don't pick.** `abstentionReasonsAcross`, `recoveryAcross`, `bareRetryAcross`,
   `voteCountsAcross` sum over the enumerated instances.
2. **All or nothing.** If any instance cannot report, the field is **absent**. A sum over the subset
   that happened to answer is the truncated shape this section is about, so it cannot also be the
   shape of the repair.
3. **The vote rule belongs to the total.** "Three zeros is not a census" is true of a run, not of a
   worker: a worker that drew no voting questions legitimately reports `0/0/0`, and applying the rule
   per instance would drop that worker and then sum the rest.

And a guard that refuses rather than choosing:

```ts
function censusSourcesOf(feature: MemorySystem, pool: AblationPool | undefined): MemorySystem[] {
  if (pool === undefined) return [feature];
  const instances = [...pool.featureInstances()];
  if (!instances.includes(feature)) throw new Error(/* ... */);
  return instances;
}
```

A pool that does not enumerate the instance the arm measured has two possible readings — `feature`
alone (the defect) and the pool alone (worker 0's share silently dropped) — and both produce a number
a reader would believe. The arm stops instead.

### 13.244.5 The tests, and the readings they were written from

| # | test | red reading before the fix | file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | nine questions, two passes, three workers → census sums to **18** | **6** — one third, exactly the defect in miniature | `pool-census.test.ts` |
| 2 | the serial path still sums to **10** over five questions × two passes | passes (control) | same |
| 3 | a pool whose worker 1 has no census → field **absent**, not summed over the rest | return a zeroed census | same |
| 4 | a pool that does not enumerate the instance measured → **throws** | return worker 0's quarter | same |
| 5 | vote verdicts summed without discarding a worker that took none | — | same |
| 6 | all workers report `0/0/0` → **no** vote census | — | same |
| 7 | one instance per worker, the same one on every pass | fresh per pass | same |
| 8 | **five routes, one question each, product instance, three workers, two passes → 10** | **2** — worker 0 claimed two of the ten, `expected 2 to be 10` | `arm-census-routes.test.ts` |
| 9 | the same five routes serial → **5** | passes (control) | same |

Test 8 is the one §13.243.5 asked for in its last paragraph — *"a test that runs one question on each
of the five routes through the arm's own construction path, not through the class directly"* — and it
is the one that would have made the wrong explanation impossible: with one question per route, a
census that covers one third of them cannot be explained by "the session route counts and the others
do not", because the session route is one of the five.

`test_self_consistency_wiring.py` pinned the old function name (`voteCountsOf`) and now pins the pair
that matters — `voteCountsAcross` **and** `censusSourcesOf(feature, options.pool)` — because a fold
over `[feature]` is exactly the code that produced 488.

### 13.244.6 What this says about the method, which is the transferable part

Three plausible mechanisms were proposed for one number before the mechanism was found:

| proposed | why it was plausible | why it was wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
