| the six undeclared fields decided the reach (§13.242.7) | the run *did* depart on six fields | `41773546221` departed on one and reported the same shape |
| `122 per pass = MR's 121 + 1` (§13.243.5) | 122 is one more than 121 | 122 is `500 / 4`; the `+1` was jitter |
| an unbounded `maxPromptChars` broke a counter | the field really was absent | an unbounded room that changes no prompt cannot change a counter |

What settled it was not a better hypothesis. It was a **diff against an artifact that has the property
this one lacks** — `41546569106` sums to exactly 2,000, and the difference between the two runs is a
field in the log line. The check that caught it, `census-unit`, is arithmetic against
`questionCount × runs`, which is why it was right while three readings were wrong: it compares a
number with the denominator the artifact already declares, and it needs no mechanism at all.

**The rule this campaign takes from it: a census must be publishable only with its denominator, and
the denominator must be computed rather than assumed.** `488` was a real count of a real quarter; the
error was never in the counting, it was in what the count was said to be *of*.

## 13.245 Two defects found while trying to confirm the first one

*§13.244's repair needs one real artifact to confirm it: sixty questions, four passes, a census summing
to 240. The dispatch for that (`41842684629`) died after three minutes without starting a question, and
the CI job that ran beside it went red on a test that had been passing. Both are defects in the
instrument rather than in the arm, and both are worth more than the confirmation they blocked.*

### 13.245.1 The cache keyed on a file the template service cannot afford to hash

```
##[error]The template is not valid. .github/workflows/benchmark-cortex-memory.yml (Line: 370, Col: 25):
hashFiles('data/longmemeval_s_cleaned.json') couldn't finish within 120 seconds.
```

`hashFiles` is evaluated by the **template service**, not by the runner, and it has a 120-second budget
for the whole template. The corpus is served from a moving HuggingFace branch at 100+ MB. So the step
that restores the embedding cache could not compute its own key.

The galling part is that the digest it was a function of **had already been computed** one line above,
in the download step, for the corpus-mismatch assertion that §13.237 added:

```bash
ACTUAL_SHA="$(sha256sum .../data/longmemeval_s_cleaned.json | cut -d' ' -f1)"
```

So the key was reading a large file to re-derive a value it already had. The repair writes a 64-byte
digest file in the download step and keys on that:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what the key hashes | the corpus, 100+ MB | `data/dataset.sha256`, 64 bytes |
| who computes it | the template service, 120 s budget | the same, in milliseconds |
| does a corpus change change the key | yes | **yes**, because the file's content *is* the corpus digest |
| do the two workflows share entries | yes | **yes**, and this is the constraint that makes it non-trivial |

The last row is why this was not a one-line change. `benchmark.yml` and
`benchmark-cortex-memory.yml` must land on the **same** cache entry — that is the property that lets
whichever workflow runs first pay for the 170,095 vectors and the other find them. Both now write the
same digest file in the same form, and a guard pins the key **expression** identical across the two,
which is the only place that consequence is observable.

`tools/__tests__/test_embedding_cache_key.py` gains four properties, each with the failure it prevents:

| property | what breaks without it |
| --- | --- |
| no key hashes the corpus | a run that dies in three minutes with no measurement |
| the digest file is written **before** the first cache step | the key resolves to `longmemeval-embedding--<id>`, which matches nothing, so every run re-embeds 170,095 turns (1h38m of a 3h21m job — §13 on the old bare key) |
| the digest is written **from the corpus** | a changed corpus keeps the old key and restores vectors of text that is no longer in the dataset |
| both workflows use the identical expression | they stop sharing entries and the two reports stop being comparable by construction |

The first version of that guard failed against a workflow that was already correct, because it searched
the raw file and the **comment** recording the failure quotes the offending expression verbatim. The
guard now strips comment lines first: what has to hold is a property of the expressions, and a `#` line
is not one.

### 13.245.2 A budget assertion measured with a clock that cannot resolve it

`Verify` went red on `41842394314` with one test out of 4,887:

```
retryableFetch respects a wall-clock budget > spends the remaining budget on a retry after a transport failure
AssertionError: expected 3 to be 2
```

The claim is arithmetic: ten milliseconds of budget against a thirty-millisecond backoff is one
truncated wait, therefore exactly one more request. It was measured with a **real** `setTimeout(10)`,
and a real timer may be delivered a fraction early — so the remaining budget read a hair above zero and
the ladder took a third attempt. Every other assertion in the file was green, and the run before it was
green, which is what a timing-dependent instrument looks like.

**The product is not wrong here.** `retryBudgetMs` in production is measured in seconds; a one-tick
overshoot at ten milliseconds is a tick. The *test* was wrong to ask a 10 ms budget to distinguish
"zero remaining" from "0.4 ms remaining" with a clock that cannot. The repair fakes the clock — the
pattern the rest of the file already uses — and asserts the **offsets** rather than only the count:

```ts
expect(offsets).toEqual([0, 10]);
```

That is a stronger assertion than the one it replaces: it pins the truncation, not merely its
consequence. Verified by mutation — with the truncation disabled, the test fails; before the change, a
ladder that ignored the budget would have passed a `calls === 2` check on a fast enough runner only by
luck.

### 13.245.3 What is still owed

| # | owed | criterion | status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **the confirming artifact** | sixty questions × four passes → census sums to **240**, and `census-unit` green | **done**, `41845802020` |
| 2 | §13.243's five predictions | unchanged; three are false and two are true, and the falsification is the reading | closed as a **null**, not as a regression |
| 3 | the ask migration (§13.243.6) | MR ≥ 96/121 with the other four capabilities inside the noise band | **not started** — it is now the only MR experiment left |

The confirmation run is not a formality. §13.244's fold is covered by nine unit tests, but those build
their own pools; the only evidence that the **CLI's** pool is enumerated is an artifact whose census
equals `questionCount × runs`.

### 13.245.4 The confirmation, and the number in it worth keeping

`41845802020`: sixty questions, four passes, `workers=4`, one declared departure (`limit`), preflight
green, **twenty-two minutes**.

```
PASS  roster        60 records, questionCount says 60
PASS  census-unit   240 outcomes, 240 question-answers (60 x 4)
PASS  budget        largest prompt 47454 against maxPromptChars 48000
PASS  reach         ask=operands+operand-gap touches ['multi-session', 'flat', 'temporal', 'abstention']
```

`llm` 36 / `answered` 204, i.e. 9 declines per pass of 60 — the same shape the registered arm reports,
now over the whole run instead of a quarter of it. The reading is not a headline and cannot be: sixty
questions is a different (much easier) slice at **93.75%**, and comparing it with 90.15 would be
comparing two datasets.

**The number worth keeping is a different one, from the same artifact:**

```
PASS  prompt-overhead  60 record(s) carry both terms; after the evidence and the question, 6 distinct
                       decoration size(s) [365, 417, 536, 607, 761, 1589] character(s), the median
                       1.3% of a median prompt of 47343
```

**The instruction block is 1.3% of the prompt.** That is a constraint on the next plan rather than a
curiosity: a target of "−30% tokens" **cannot** be reached by shortening instructions, because there is
only 1.3% of the prompt there to shorten. It has to come out of the evidence, which means the mechanism
has to be one that decides *how much evidence to send* — the family §1.19 of the competitor analysis
lists (AgentIR's cascade, T2Mem's test-time assembly) rather than a prompt rewrite.

## 13.246 The reference pipeline's ask was read off the wrong function, and the ask was never migrated

*§13.243.6 nominated the last MR experiment: "the reference pipeline's ask, migrated whole — `identify`
rather than `enumerate`, answer-only, `Answer:` prefix". Before dispatching it, this section read the
reference's multi-session path back from its own source. The ask it names does not exist. The
reference **enumerates in writing**, and the campaign has never administered its contract.*

### 13.246.1 What was claimed, and where the sentence came from

Three sections carry the same quotation, and the quotation is real:

| section | the claim | the quote |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §13.123.3 | the reference's advantage is a **silent** Step 1 | `conInstruction`: *"Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer"*, *"Keep those notes to yourself; do NOT write them out"* |
| §13.240.4 | *"the reference pipeline asks for the two steps with the notes unwritten"* | the same lines, restated |
| §13.243.6 | the next MR experiment is that ask, migrated whole | the same lines, once more |

`conInstruction` is at `natural-language-memory.ts:1805` and the docblock above it is unambiguous about
its callers: *"Chain-of-Note (CoN) instruction shared by the **single-session reading prompts**."* Its
four call sites are `buildQaPrompt` (1928), `buildPreferencePrompt` (2041),
`buildKnowledgeUpdatePrompt` (2168) and `buildTemporalQaPrompt` (2224). The multi-session path is
`answerSessions`, and it does not call any of them:

```ts
const promptBuilder =
  this.options.aggregationPrompt === undefined && kind === 'derivation'
    ? buildDerivationQaPrompt
    : (this.options.aggregationPrompt ?? buildAggregationQaPrompt);
```

`buildAggregationQaPrompt` (2367) opens with `Work in two steps.` and its Step 1 is:

```
Step 1 — Enumerate every item matching the question's EXACT action, one per line:
  - <item> | <exact action verb from the question> | <session date>
```

**The reference writes the list.** It has never not written it. `silent` was built to copy an ask that
belongs to a route this campaign does not put MR on, and §13.127's −26 therefore measures the *removal*
of the written list rather than the reference's contract.

### 13.246.2 The reading that survives, and it is the more useful one

Nothing about the measurement changes. Only what it is a measurement *of*:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `silent` −26 (§13.127) | the reference's ask fails on this arm | **silence costs 26 questions**, i.e. the written list is load-bearing on MR |
| 86.78% reference MR | unexplained residual | **still unexplained**, and now attributable to something this arm has never varied |
| §13.240.4's "only difference left" | the prompt shape | the prompt shape, but the *other* one |

The second row is the one that matters for the plan. §13.240.4 excluded three axes — reader, coverage,
budget — and concluded the difference was prompt shape. It got the exclusion right and the shape wrong.
The qualification is not cosmetic: the campaign has now spent three dispatches on variants of *"write
less of the list"* (`enumerated` sharpenings, `sweep`, `silent`) and §13.96 records all three as failing
to raise accuracy. If the difference were silence, those three are the direction that should have
worked. They are also, on this reading, the three measurements that say silence is wrong.

### 13.246.3 What the untested difference actually is

Enumerated field by field, the reference's aggregation contract against `enumerated`'s block:

| property | `enumerated` | reference (`buildAggregationQaPrompt`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| scene framing | none; the evidence arrives under `EVIDENCE:` | *"You are answering a question based on MULTIPLE conversation sessions."* |
| Step 1 predicate | *"every item in the evidence that matches the question"* — a predicate over the answer | *"every item matching the question's **EXACT action**"* — a predicate over the question |
| Step 1 schema | one line per item *"with the date it was stated"* | a fixed three-field record: `<item> \| <verb> \| <session date>` |
| verb discipline | *"do not substitute a similar one"* | the same rule **plus four named counter-examples** (*participated, presented, planned, working on* are not *led*) |
| exchange rule | *"do not merge two items into one"* | *"Treat an 'exchange' as TWO items: return the old item AND pick up the replacement"* |
| Step 2 | three forms, one sentence | **four forms, each a line**, plus *"do NOT re-filter or exclude any of them"* |
| reply shape | `Reply with the Step 2 number alone` | a named terminator: `Answer: <final answer>`, then a bare `Answer:` cue |
| decline licence | declines when *the Step 1 list is empty* | declines when *the context contains no relevant information at all*, and *"Combining facts across several sessions is NOT a reason to abstain"* |
| what forbids a bare decline | *"a bare INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with no list is not a valid response"* | the same sentence, plus *"Confirm that you completed Step 1 by listing each candidate item you considered, including the ones you decided to exclude and why"* |

Eight of the nine rows are textual and none of them has been administered. Rows 2 and 3 are the ones
this section would predict an effect from: a predicate over the **question** is a different instruction
from a predicate over the **answer**, and §13.204's hand-read failures are exactly the shape a predicate
over the answer produces — the reader lists what obviously qualifies and stops.

### 13.246.4 The audit, stated as a test rather than as this section

A paragraph can be repeated; a failing test cannot. `ask-verbatim.test.ts` opens with two assertions
about the reference's own source:

| test | what it pins |
| --- | --- |
| the aggregation builder enumerates in writing | `buildAggregationQaPrompt` contains `Enumerate every item matching the question's EXACT action`, contains `Answer: <final answer>`, and contains **no** `write ONLY the final answer` |
| the single-session builder is where the quote lives | `buildQaPrompt` contains `Work in two steps, but write ONLY the final answer` and `Keep those notes to yourself`, and `classifyAggregationKind` routes the two question shapes as the answer path does |

The two together make "the reference's ask is silent" a claim that fails `pnpm test`. That is the only
form of correction this campaign has found that survives a re-reading.

### 13.246.5 The registration: `ask=verbatim`

**One variable**: `cortex_memory_ask=verbatim` against the registered `operands+operand-gap`,
everything else at §10.3 plus the dispatch's own `maxPromptChars` and `maxTurnChars`, declared.

The block is `buildAggregationQaPrompt`'s text, unabridged, with the bare `Answer:` cue that ends it.
The abstention token is a parameter of both builders, so the test passes this package's token to the
reference builder and asserts **line equality** — there is no substitution in the product and therefore
no paraphrase for a later edit to hide in.

The reach and the change set are two different numbers and both are stated:

| | value | measured against |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ASK_ROUTES.verbatim` | `multi-session, flat, temporal, abstention` | the **shipped** block — the registered arm's moves stay moved |
| `ASK_CHANGES.verbatim` | `multi-session` | `operands+operand-gap`, i.e. the run this is read against |
| `ASK_CHANGES_WHEN_DERIVATION` | *(empty)* | the same control, on a derivation question |

The empty derivation entry is a decision, not an omission. The reference splits by question kind —
`buildDerivationQaPrompt` is a *different builder* — and this arm's derivation half is `operands`, which
is adopted and worth 63 questions (§13.193.5). Migrating both halves at once would price neither, so a
derivation question keeps the control's bytes.

The fallthrough is a **delegation** rather than a copy of `enumerated`'s block:

```ts
return instructionsFor(contract, date, 'operands+operand-gap', scope, shape);
```

which is the first ask in this file that can write its fallthrough as one call. §13.104, §13.123 and
§13.124 each cost questions because the fallthrough returned `own`; delegation makes "the other routes
read what the control reads" a property of the expression instead of a table that the render can drift
from.

### 13.246.6 Predictions, and what each outcome means

| # | prediction | falsified by | meaning if falsified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR correct ≥ **96 of 121** (the §13.239/§13.243 threshold, so all three are comparable; the registered arm is 92/121 mean 93.5) | ≤ 94 | the contract is not the mechanism either, and the residual 10 points live in the **evidence** rather than in the ask |
| 2 | the five routes outside the change set reproduce the control **to the question** | any change | assembly failure; no MR prediction is readable |
| 3 | MR declines do **not exceed** the control's 9-per-60 shape | +3 or more | the reference's decline licence is not transferable, and §13.55's "the list is the licence" is a fact about this arm's wording rather than about lists |
| 4 | mean `promptChars` stays within **1%** of the control's | > 2% either way | the block's length became a budget variable and the run is two variables |

Prediction 1 is the registered criterion and it is deliberately the same number §13.239 used, because
three runs judged against one threshold are a series and three runs judged against three thresholds are
three anecdotes.

**1 holds** (≥96): the migration is worth at least +4 MR questions on one dispatch and no extra
consultation, and it is adopted. MR then needs 20 more to close the 86.78 gap, and §13.243.2's own table
names the only remaining axis: the **partial-coverage band reads 48.7% where the full band reads 89.0%**,
and the reference never produces that band because it retrieves *sessions* and truncates per session.

**1 fails and 3 holds**: the ask is exhausted as an axis on MR, and the next registration is the one the
table above points at — *session-atomic allocation*, where a question either receives a session whole or
not at all, so there is no half-served band to read badly.

**1 fails and 3 fails**: the reference's licence to decline is the mechanism, not its enumeration. That
would send the next dispatch to the decline clause on its own, which is a one-line change with a control
already in place (`enumerated` versus `enumerated` with the reference's two abstention sentences).

### 13.246.7 What this section does not claim

1. **It does not withdraw §13.127.** `silent` measured −26 and that number stands; what changes is its
   subject. A campaign that recorded it as "the reference's ask fails" would have retired an axis it had
   never touched, and the correction is recorded here so that the retirement does not happen by accident.
2. **It does not explain the 9.92 points.** §13.240.4 excluded reader, coverage and budget; this section
   adds that the excluded fourth candidate was mis-specified. The gap is still unexplained and it is
   still the target.
3. **It does not claim the reference's wording is better prose.** Nine of the ten rows in §13.246.3 are
   differences in *what is asked for*, not in how it is said. The one row that is purely stylistic — the
   scene framing — is the one this section would least expect to matter.
4. **It does not re-open the token axis.** The block is longer than `enumerated`'s by roughly 400
   characters, and §13.245.4 measured the whole instruction block at 1.3% of a 47,343-character prompt.
   Prediction 4 exists only to keep that from silently becoming a second variable.

## 13.247 The budget was read from a note, and two fields of the registered artifact said 48,000

*The first dispatch of §13.246's ask (`41859220351`) declared three departures. One of them,
`maxPromptChars=96000`, came from §10.3's as-of paragraph — "every 500-question run from `41144910162`
onwards sends `--set cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars=96000`". It was cancelled eight minutes in. This
section records why, because the gate that exists to catch this class **passed it**.*

### 13.247.1 The three fields that answered the question the note was being asked

| source | value | what it settles |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `41546569106`, feature prompt tokens | 28,145,808 over ~2,000 calls = **14,072 tokens/call** | 48,000 characters is ~13.7k tokens; 96,000 would be ~27k |
| `41546569106`, MR mean `promptChars` (§13.243.1) | **46,630** | a 96,000-character room does not stop its mean here |
| `41845802020`, `PASS budget` line | `largest prompt 47454 against maxPromptChars **48000**` | the most recent confirmation ran at 48,000 |

Three independent readings, all from artifacts this campaign produced about itself, all agreeing. The
note is not a lie — it was true when written — it is a **fact with a shelf life**, and it is spelled in
the same register as the registered configuration two bullets above it.

### 13.247.2 The gate passed, and that is the part worth keeping

`Check the dispatch against the registration` went green on `41859220351`. It was right to: 96,000 was
a **declared** departure, the declaration matched the payload, and the payload was sent. So the run was
compliant, expensive and wrong, and every instrument in the chain said so.

This is a different failure from §13.242's six `UNDECLARED` lines. There the payload disagreed with the
registration and nobody had said so; here the payload was announced and the announcement was the error.
A declaration gate cannot audit the operator's reason for declaring, and it should not pretend to.

What it *can* do, and what this section registers as the rule:

> **A budget's value comes from a field of the most recent registered artifact, never from prose.**
> Where two sources disagree, the artifact wins, and the note is corrected in place rather than
> re-read charitably.

48,000 has two independent artifact readings. 96,000 has one narrative. That asymmetry is the whole
decision procedure, and it needs no judgement about which paragraph is fresher.

### 13.247.3 What was re-dispatched

`41860773768`, one declared departure (`cortex_memory_ask`), everything else at §10.3: 48,000
characters, `maxTurnChars=400`, four repetitions, `thinking: multi-session+temporal`,
`deepseek-chat`. That is the load `41546569106` ran at, which is what makes §13.246.6's predictions
comparable to the 90.15 / 76.86 figures they were written against.

The 96,000 axis is not re-opened by this. §13.118.6 closed it on 2× prompt tokens, 2.87× wall clock and
an absent registered gain; what happened here is that a run was about to re-open a closed axis without
anyone deciding to.

## 13.248 The migrated contract was administered: +3 MR questions, a coverage composition that did not move, and a parser that never read the terminator

*`41860773768` is §13.246's dispatch — `ask=verbatim`, 500 questions, four repetitions, 48,000
characters, one declared departure, 85 minutes. This section reads it: the four predictions judged,
the decomposition that makes the gain attributable, the adoption, and the product defect the run
exposed on its way through.*

### 13.248.1 The four predictions of §13.246.6, judged

| # | prediction | falsified by | measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR correct ≥ **96 of 121** | ≤ 94 | **96** first repetition (79.34%), **96.3** mean of four (min 94, max 98) | **true**, margin 0.3 at the mean |
| 2 | the five routes outside the change set reproduce the control **to the question** | any change | prompts **byte-identical on 379 of 379** (IE 150, ABS 30, KU 72, TR 127); correctness moved **−1 / 0 / +1 / −1** | **false as written**, and the failure it was written to catch did not occur |
| 3 | MR declines do not exceed the control's shape by 3 or more | +3 or more | **2** against the control's **2** | **true** |
| 4 | mean `promptChars` within **1%** of the control's | > 2% either way | MR **45,799** against **46,264** = **−1.00%** | **true at the boundary** |

Overall: **90.50%** mean of four (min 90.20, max 90.80) against the registered arm's **90.15%**
(min 89.40, max 91.00), a delta of **+0.35**.

Per capability, 4-repetition means:

| | IE | MR | KU | TR | ABS | overall |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| registered (`41546569106`) | 143.0 | **94.5** | 62.3 | 121.0 | 30.0 | 90.15% |
| `verbatim` (`41860773768`) | 143.5 | **96.3** | 62.0 | 120.8 | 30.0 | 90.50% |
| delta | +0.5 | **+1.8** | −0.3 | −0.2 | 0 | **+0.35** |

### 13.248.2 Prediction 2 was falsified by the instrument, not by the assembly

This is the first prediction in the campaign whose falsifier describes the wrong cause, and the run's
own fields say so:

| capability | prompts byte-identical | records | answer strings that differ | correctness flips |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IE | 150 | 150 | 30 | **1** |
| ABS | 30 | 30 | 0 | **0** |
| KU | 72 | 72 | 20 | **1** |
| TR | 127 | 127 | 124 | **7** |
| MR | 27 | 121 | 106 | **7** (94 prompts changed) |

`promptDigest` is equal on every one of the 379 records outside the change set, so **no assembly
failure is possible** — the arm sent the control's bytes. The flips are the reader.

That measurement is worth more than the prediction it falsified: **nine correctness flips on 479
questions whose prompts did not change is a 1.9% churn rate**, i.e. a noise floor of ±2.3 questions on
a 121-question route, at `temp=0`. Every MR effect this campaign has measured sits on top of that
number, and §13.248.4 uses it.

### 13.248.3 The decomposition, and why this run is attributable where §13.243 was not

§13.243's redistribution moved seven questions across the coverage line and the route's accuracy did
not move. This run moved nothing across it. The split below is the one §13.243.2 used — a question is
**full** when every gold turn the retrieval **surfaced** (`rank ≥ 0`) reached the window
(`rank < turns`) — and it is now `readout-arm-run.py --split`, because that section computed it with a
script that was never committed and the definition had to be recovered from three candidate
definitions before the numbers reproduced.

| run | all 121 | full band | partial band | mean depth |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| registered `41546569106` | 76.86% (93) | **75 @ 84.00%** | **46 @ 65.22%** | 175.2 |
| redistribution `41773546221` | 76.03% (92) | 82 @ 89.02% | 39 @ 48.72% | 197.8 |
| `verbatim` `41860773768` | **79.34% (96)** | **75 @ 89.33%** | **46 @ 63.04%** | 174.1 |

**The composition is identical to the control to the question: 75 and 46.** So:

1. The +3 comes from the **full band**, +5.33 points on 75 questions = **+4 correct**, with the partial
   band giving one back (−2.18 points on 46 = −1).
2. No question crossed the coverage line, so the reading is not a composition effect. That is the
   distinction §13.243 could not make.
3. **In the full band the arm now reads 89.33% against the reference pipeline's 85.95% on the same
   route**, with the same reader, the same judge and — since this run — the same contract.

The third row is the one to keep. For as long as the two arms had different contracts, "we lose to
them on MR" was uninterpretable: it could have been the prompt. It is now measurable, and on the
population where the evidence is complete the answer is that we do not lose.

**The evidence covariate, stated rather than waved.** 92 of the 121 MR questions carry a different
turn list, because the block is longer and the room is at 95.4% of its budget, so the tail moves:
mean depth **−1.48 turns**, gold turns carried **−0.017** (one turn lost across the route). §13.243
already priced that axis at the other end — it moved MR depth **+23 turns (+14%)** and bought
**nothing** — so a −1.5-turn move sits inside a region a registered experiment measured as flat. The
partition being identical to the question is the stronger form of the same statement, and it is
measured rather than argued.

### 13.248.4 What this run does not establish

1. **The +3 is not significant on one dispatch.** Paired over the 121 MR questions, first repetition:
   two lost, five gained, McNemar exact **p = 0.45**. Overall 7 lost against 9 gained, **p = 0.80**.
   The 4-repetition means move 94.5 → 96.3, which is 1.8 questions against the ±2.3-question noise
   floor measured in §13.248.2 — a gain of about 0.8 noise widths.
2. **It does not close the MR gap.** 79.34% against the reference's 85.95% on this run leaves 8
   questions. §13.243.2's conclusion stands and is now better supported: an arm that delivers 96.6% of
   the in-pool gold and reads 79% has exhausted the room.
3. **It does not say `verbatim` is better prose.** It says the reference's *schema, Step 2 forms,
   decline licence and terminator* are worth about two questions over `operands+operand-gap` at equal
   budget — and, in the full band, five points of accuracy.

### 13.248.5 The defect the run exposed: the contract names a terminator the parser never read

Run `41860773768`'s MR replies came back in the contract's shape, and the arm returned the whole
transcript. **94 of 121 records have `answer` equal to `rawOutput`**, `Answer: 2` line included:

```
- Peace lily | acquired | 2023/05/20
- Succulent | acquired | 2023/05/20
- Snake plant | acquired | 2023/05/25 — excluded: outside "the last month"

Answer: 2
```

`parseAnswer` had two readers — the abstention rule on the closing line, and the step-heading rule —
and **neither read a label on the answer path**. `ask=verbatim` is the first ask that ends on a named
terminator instead of *"reply with the number alone"*, so it produced a shape nothing in this package
had ever been asked to read.

Two things follow, and they are different:

- **It did not move the number.** 49 of the 94 transcripts contain the gold verbatim, `judgeScorer`
  reads the answer *and* the ground truth, and the judge said correct. So 79.34% is a real reading of
  the reader, not a parsing artefact — verified by the direct check that **0 of the 22 wrong records
  whose `Answer:` line exists would match the gold** if the line were read.
- **It is a product defect anyway.** A user of `ask=verbatim` receives a four-line list where they
  asked for a number. That the judge can find the number inside the transcript is the judge working,
  not the product.

The repair is `afterClosingLabel` in `parse.ts`: the **last non-empty line** opening with
`Answer:` / `Final answer:` terminates the reply. Same rule `isAbstention` already applies, for the
same reason — a decision lives on the closing line — and composed **after** the heading rule so that
`Step 2 — Answer: 2` cannot return the literal `Answer: 2` (`abstention-recovery.ts` records that
string as an artefact a previous repair had to work around).

**Two narrowings, each forced by a false positive rather than chosen:**

| narrowing | the false positive | why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `The answer: …` is **not** a label | it is how a prose sentence begins, and the rule reads the closing line | accepting it cuts a sentence's subject off its own answer |
| an unspaced `-` is **not** a separator | the conformance suite's fake reader answers `answer-0`, and `[:\-]` matched the hyphen inside the identifier and returned `0` | `answer-42` is a plausible model output; `Answer - 42` is a label. **The space is the deciding character** |

**And the rule is provably inert on what has been published:** applied to the raw outputs of
`41546569106`, `41773546221` and `41845802020` — 1,060 records — it fires **0** times, and on
`41860773768` it fires exactly **94**. So it cannot move an archived number, and it reads the shape it
was built for.

The coupling is a test, not a paragraph. `parse-closing-label.test.ts` builds the **real** `verbatim`
prompt, asserts its last non-empty line is the `Answer:` cue the assembly places there, and drives the
parser with a reply that ends in it — the same form `parse-stepped.test.ts` uses for the headings, and
strictly stronger than comparing two literals because it also fails if the contract stops reaching the
route.

### 13.248.6 A misattribution inside §13.246.6, corrected

§13.246.6's prediction 1 read *"the registered arm is 92/121 mean 93.5"*. It is not. The registered
arm (`41546569106`) is **93 first repetition, 94.5 mean**; 92 and 93.5 belong to `41773546221`, the
redistribution run §13.243.4 **rejected**. So the comparison §13.246.6 set up was against a rejected
run's numbers, and it flattered this one: the honest harvest is **+1.8 questions**, not +2.8.

The threshold itself is unaffected — it was written as an absolute (≥ 96), which is why it could be
inherited from §13.239/§13.243 at all — but the sentence beside it was wrong in the direction that
makes a result look better than it is. That is the fourth instance this campaign has recorded of *a
number that is real being attached to the wrong run*, and the only repair that has ever held is
naming the run id in the same clause as the number: §13.246.6 did name two ids and got them
crossed, so the rule is now **one id per sentence**.

### 13.248.7 The adoption, and the dispatch it requires

`ask=verbatim` **is registered** (§10.3 and `dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py`'s `INPUTS`, held together
by `test_preregistration_config.py`). The grounds, in order of weight:

1. The pre-registered criterion was met (96 ≥ 96) and no capability regressed beyond the noise floor.
2. The population the change is read on **did not move** (75/46 in both runs), which is what makes the
   full band's +5.33 points attributable to the contract.
3. In the full band the arm now beats the pipeline it loses to, on one contract instead of two.
4. It removes a difference rather than adding one: the remaining MR gap is now *our evidence against
   theirs*, with the prompt held.

What the adoption costs: nothing measurable — `promptChars` −1.0%, no extra calls
(`bareRetry` 65/65 as before, `recovery` 0/0), overall +0.35%.

What it requires: **the parser fix changes MR's answer text**, so MR must be re-measured before the
registered headline can be quoted again. `41860773768`'s 79.34% was produced with the whole transcript
as the answer; the next run produces the `Answer:` line, and a sharper input to the judge can move the
number in either direction. So the next dispatch is the registered configuration with both changes —
which is a confirmation of §13.246.6's prediction 1 on a second draw **and** the first measurement of
the parser repair.

Predictions, written before it runs:

| # | prediction | falsified by | meaning if falsified |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR ≥ **96 of 121** on a second independent dispatch | ≤ 94 | §13.248.4's caution was right and the adoption rests on one draw; revert to `operands+operand-gap` and re-open the axis |
| 2 | full-band accuracy ≥ **87%** (the +5.33 held to within one question) | < 87% | the full-band gain was the reader's churn, not the contract |
| 3 | MR `answer` equals `rawOutput` on **0** records | > 0 | the parser repair does not reach the shape it was built for |
| 4 | the four capabilities outside the change set stay within **±2 questions** of 143.5 / 62.0 / 120.8 / 30.0 | any further | the noise floor is wider than §13.248.2 measured |

Prediction 3 is a *product* assertion rather than a benchmark one, and it is the reason this dispatch
cannot be folded into a later one.

## 13.249 The token axis, measured offline before spending anything: a smaller room is not a token strategy, and the headroom is in a predictor

*§14.39 of the plan registered P1' with a zero-call gate — "mean `promptChars` ≤ 32,000, gold
reachability within −2.0 of the registered arm, partially-served count falling" — and named three
mechanisms. This section runs the gate's first half against `41860773768`'s own per-question records,
before any dispatch, and the gate **fails**. The failure is worth more than a pass would have been.*

### 13.249.1 What can be simulated for free, and what cannot

Each record carries the delivered window as an ordered list of turns with their text
(`turns[i].index === i`, asserted over all 500), the per-question `promptChars`, and the gold's ranks
in the ordered pool. So a smaller room is exactly a prefix of the window:

```
room = target − overhead,   overhead = promptChars − Σ len(turn.text)
k    = the largest prefix whose characters fit in room
carried(rank r) ⟺ r < k
```

That is a faithful simulation of `maxPromptChars` and of nothing else: it cannot simulate a *different
selection* (that needs the retriever), a cascade, or a test-time assembly. So this section prices one
hypothesis — **the room is too big** — and leaves the other two untouched.

### 13.249.2 The gate, run: a uniform 32,000 loses 17 points of reachability

| capability | n | reachability at 48,000 | at **32,000** | delta | mean chars at 32,000 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 13.3% | 10.0% | −3.3 | 31,086 |
| IE | 150 | 51.3% | 39.3% | **−12.0** | 30,950 |
| KU | 72 | 6.9% | 2.8% | −4.2 | 31,155 |
| MR | 121 | 62.0% | 38.0% | **−24.0** | 31,424 |
| TR | 127 | 56.7% | 29.9% | **−26.8** | 31,447 |
| **all** | 500 | **46.6%** | **29.6%** | **−17.0** | 31,262 |

"Reachability" is the share of questions on which **every surfaced gold turn** fits the window —
the quantity the gate names. The gate's tolerance was −2.0. A uniform −33% budget costs **−17.0**,
and no capability is anywhere near the tolerance.

The failure is not an artefact of the tolerance being strict: the ranking is monotone in every row,
and it is worst exactly where the turns are cheapest (MR 265 chars/turn, TR 263), because a cheap
turn buys depth and depth is what those routes need.

**So "cut the budget" is not a token strategy.** It is a way to buy −33% tokens with −17 points of
gold reachability, and the accuracy consequence of that is not even worth measuring.

### 13.249.3 The positive half: what a room sized to the gold would cost

The same records answer the question the gate was really asking — *how much of the 48,000 is
doing work?* For each question, size the room to the deepest surfaced gold turn
(`k = max(surfaced ranks) + 1`) and price it:

| capability | n | gold coverable at any depth | oracle chars | actual chars | ratio |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 13.3% | 24,136 | 43,118 | 0.56× |
| IE | 150 | 51.3% | 19,930 | 43,717 | **0.46×** |
| KU | 72 | 6.9% | 34,286 | 43,673 | 0.79× |
| MR | 121 | 62.0% | 24,704 | 45,642 | 0.54× |
| TR | 127 | 56.7% | 27,486 | 46,226 | 0.59× |
| **all** | 500 | **46.6%** | **24,182** | **44,778** | **0.54×** |

Both character columns count **turn text only**; `readout-arm-run.py --room` prints the same table
with the per-record overhead included, which moves the ratio from 0.54× to 0.56× and changes no
conclusion. The two conventions are stated because §13.243.2 is the last number in this document that
took a table's denominator for granted.

Two facts, and they are the whole design:

1. **There is 1.85× of headroom** on the questions where the gold is coverable at all — 24,182
   characters against 44,778. That is more than the −30% the plan asked for, so the target is
   reachable in principle.
2. **53.4% of questions are not coverable at any depth**, because the gold sits beyond what the pool
   surfaced. On those, no room setting and no depth predictor can help; they need a better *pool*,
   and they are the same population §13.248.3 reads at 63.04% in the partial band.

So the token axis is a **prediction** problem, not a budget problem: the constant 48,000 is wrong in
both directions at once — too small for the 53.4% (where it is already at 95–98% of the cap) and
2× too large for the 46.6% (where the oracle needs 24k).

### 13.249.4 What P1' becomes, and what it may not use

The gate is restated, because the first version could only be passed by luck:

| gate | quantity | pass line | why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (offline, zero calls) | mean `promptChars` under the **rule** | ≤ 32,000 | the plan's token target |
| 2 (offline, zero calls) | reachability under the rule, against 46.6% | ≥ **44.6%** (−2.0) | the plan's tolerance, unchanged |
| 3 (offline, zero calls) | the rule's chars against the **oracle's 24,182** on the coverable subset | ≤ 1.6× | a rule that beats a uniform cut but loses to the oracle by 2× has no mechanism, only a threshold |

**Gate 2 is the one that kills the uniform cut and gate 3 is the one that stops a fitted constant from
passing.** A rule that names a depth from observable signals — score distribution, question kind,
per-route turn density — can pass both. A rule that looks at `goldRanks` cannot: §13.239.7 and §14.39.3
both draw the line at *offline evaluation may use the gold; online decision may not*, and this is the
first gate where violating it would have been invisible in the result.

The 24,182 figure is therefore an **oracle for scoring**, never a target to encode.

## 13.250 The budget curve has no knee, and the −30% target is unreachable by any allocation rule — including a perfect one

> **Corrected by §13.252.** The curve below is measured and stands. Two sentences built on it do not:
> the "coverable at any depth" column of §14.41.3 was a copy of the 48,000 row (reach at any depth is
> 67.8%, not 46.6%), so the oracle below prices a population it has mis-described — its arithmetic
> still bounds the cost of a coverage-preserving rule, but the claim that depth could not have helped
> the 53.4% is false for 142 of them. The depth axis is rejected in §13.252.4 on accuracy, not price.

*§13.249 closed "shrink the budget" and left the predictor family open, with an oracle of 24,182
characters against 44,778 spent. This section finishes the question: how much of that 1.85× is
reachable by **any** rule that decides depth per question, and is the plan's −30% inside it. It is
not, and the reason is a property of the pool rather than of the budget.*

### 13.250.1 The curve: reachability against budget, with no threshold to sit on

Simulated with `readout-arm-run.py --room`'s rule at eight budgets, per capability:

| budget | IE | KU | MR | TR | ABS | all | mean turns |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **48,000** | 51.3% | 6.9% | **62.0%** | 56.7% | 13.3% | **46.6%** | 120.7 |
| 44,000 | 48.0% | 6.9% | 57.9% | 49.6% | 13.3% | 42.8% | 111.8 |
| 40,000 | 44.7% | 5.6% | 51.2% | 43.3% | 13.3% | 38.4% | 100.6 |
| 36,000 | 40.7% | 2.8% | 44.6% | 37.8% | 10.0% | 33.6% | 89.9 |
| **32,000** | 39.3% | 2.8% | **38.0%** | 29.9% | 10.0% | **29.6%** | 78.8 |
| 28,000 | 34.7% | 0.0% | 33.1% | 22.8% | 10.0% | 24.8% | 68.3 |
| 24,000 | 30.7% | 0.0% | 28.9% | 18.9% | 3.3% | 21.2% | 57.6 |
| 20,000 | 25.3% | 0.0% | 24.0% | 15.7% | 3.3% | 17.6% | 46.8 |

**There is no knee.** The curve is close to linear across a 2.4× range, so there is no budget at which
a constant "keeps almost everything" — every 8,000 characters costs about 8.5 points. A fitted
constant therefore cannot pass §13.249.4's gates by choosing a lucky value; the response to the knob
is smooth and steep everywhere.

### 13.250.2 The honest oracle, and the number it replaces

§13.249.3's 24,182 was computed on the **46.6% of questions whose gold is coverable at all**. Pricing
the other 53.4% honestly — on those, no depth helps, so the full window is the best any rule can do —
gives the bill a perfect predictor would pay:

| | characters | against current |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| current (`41860773768`, mean over the 500) | 46,548 | 1.00× |
| **oracle, all 500** | **36,887** | **0.79×** |
| oracle, coverable 233 only | 24,182 | 0.52× |

So the headroom a **perfect, gold-omniscient, per-question depth rule** could take is **21%** — and
the plan's P1' asked for **−30%**. The target is outside what any allocation rule can reach, and the
oracle is the *upper bound* on all of them.

Per capability the oracle bill is uneven in a way that explains §13.249's per-route ratios: MR 32,919,
IE 34,286, TR 37,021, ABS 43,779, KU 45,868. KU is essentially irreducible — 6.9% of its questions are
coverable at any depth — and KU is also the route whose accuracy is lowest after MR (87.50%).

### 13.250.3 What this closes, and the one sentence that replaces three sections

Three readings now agree, from three different instruments:

| axis | measurement | what it rules out |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tokens, uniform cut | 48,000 → 32,000 costs **−17.0** reachability (§13.249.2) | a smaller constant |
| tokens, perfect per-question depth | **0.79×** at best (§13.250.2) | **every** allocation rule, for a −30% target |
| accuracy, MR | full band 89.33% against partial 63.04% (§13.248.3) | the room as the reason those 46 read badly |

All three land on the same population: **the 53.4% of questions whose gold the pool never surfaced at a
usable depth.** They are unreachable by budget, un-improvable by allocation, and they are where MR's
remaining 8 questions and KU's 9 live.

> **The pool is the single constraint on both axes.** A token target below −21% and a MR target above
> 82% are the same experiment, and it is a retrieval experiment.

### 13.250.4 What P1' becomes: a restated target and a rule that must beat 0.79×

The plan's −30% is withdrawn as an allocation target, and replaced by two numbers that are both
inside what measurement says is possible:

| quantity | target | basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mean `promptChars` under the rule | **≤ 37,000** (−20%) | the oracle's 36,887, rounded up so the target is not literally the oracle |
| reachability under the rule | **≥ 44.6%** (−2.0 of 46.6%) | unchanged from §13.249.4 |
| the rule's characters / the oracle's | **≤ 1.10×** | a rule within 10% of perfect foresight; anything looser is a threshold, not a mechanism |

Those three are jointly satisfiable only by a rule with real per-question resolution, and the third is
what forbids a constant. Whether such a rule exists is now an empirical question about *predictability*
of gold depth from observable signals — and the next dispatch on the token axis happens only if the
offline gate says yes.

**What this does not do** is retire the token axis. −20% is a real product saving on the same accuracy,
if a rule can reach it; what it retires is the assumption that the number could be bought by deciding
how much of the same evidence to send.

## 13.251 The confirmation dispatch landed in the gap its own thresholds left, and that is the finding

*`41939709206` is §13.248.7's dispatch: the registered configuration, **zero declared departures**,
500 questions, four repetitions, 72 minutes. It was written to confirm the adoption on a second draw
and to measure the parser repair. It did the second. It could not do the first, because the thresholds
it was judged against were narrower than the instrument's noise floor.*

### 13.251.1 The four predictions, judged

| # | prediction | falsified by | measured | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | MR ≥ **96 of 121** | ≤ 94 | **94** first repetition, **95.8** mean of four (min 94, max 98) | **neither** — below the confirmation line, above the falsification line |
| 2 | full-band accuracy ≥ **87%** | < 87% | **86.67%** | **neither** — 0.33 below the line, and the line was not a falsifier |
| 3 | `answer == rawOutput` on **0** records | > 0 | **365 of 500**, of which **0** carry a closing label | **true under the well-posed reading**, false as written |
| 4 | four capabilities within ±2 of 143.5 / 62.0 / 120.8 / 30.0 | any further | 144.0 / 62.5 / 119.8 / 30.0 → **+0.5 / +0.5 / −1.0 / 0** | **true** |

Overall **90.40%** (min 89.80, max 91.00). Mean `promptChars` **46,548**, identical to the previous
dispatch to the character, because the registration did not move either.

### 13.251.2 The gap, stated as arithmetic

| | confirmation line | falsification line | gap | noise floor (§13.248.2) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MR correct | ≥ 96 | ≤ 94 | **2 questions** | **±2.3 questions** |
| full-band accuracy | ≥ 87% | *(none declared)* | — | ~±3.5 points at n = 75 |

A prediction whose "confirmed" and "falsified" lines are **two questions apart, on a 121-question
route whose own reader churns 1.9% of questions at `temp=0`**, is not a test. It is a coin with a
narrower face than the thumb. The result landing at 94 is not evidence against the contract; it is
evidence that the design could not have produced evidence either way.

§13.248.7 also left prediction 2 without a falsification line at all — "≥ 87%" with no "otherwise" —
which is the same defect one level down: a threshold with one side does not define a decision.

**The rule this produces**, and it is the only durable output of this dispatch:

> A pre-registered criterion must separate its confirmation and falsification lines by **at least two
> noise widths**, and both lines must be stated. Where the effect size is smaller than that, the
> criterion is a *pooled* one over a named number of dispatches, not a per-dispatch one.

### 13.251.3 What the two draws say together, read as the pooled statistic they are

Two independent dispatches of the same registered configuration, eight repetitions:

| statistic | registered `operands+operand-gap` (`41546569106`) | `verbatim` draw 1 (`41860773768`) | `verbatim` draw 2 (`41939709206`) | pooled |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| MR, mean of four | **94.5** | **96.3** | **95.8** | **96.05** |
| MR, first repetition | 93 | 96 | 94 | 95.0 |
| full-band accuracy (n = 75) | **84.00%** | **89.33%** | **86.67%** | **88.00%** |
| overall | 90.15% | 90.50% | 90.40% | **90.45%** |
| mean `promptChars` | 46,264 | 45,799 | 46,548 | — |

**Both statistics are above the registered arm on both draws**, and the direction never reverses. That
is what eight repetitions of a 121-question route can say; it is not a significance claim, and
§13.248.4's p = 0.45 for the first draw stands.

**And the composition is identical for the third time**: 75 full / 46 partial, in the registered arm,
in draw 1, in draw 2, with depth 175.2 / 174.1 / 174.1. Three runs, one partition. The population an
ask is read on is fixed by the pool and the room, and both were held. That is the cleanest
single-variable structure any MR experiment in this campaign has had, and it is now measured three
times rather than argued once.

### 13.251.4 Prediction 3, as it should have been written

`answer == rawOutput` is **not** a defect signal. 365 of the 500 replies are a bare value — `2`,
`$750`, `59.6` — and for those the whole reply *is* the answer. Asserting zero would have flagged a
correct behaviour as a failure, which is the same error as §13.248.5's premature "did not move the
number" reading, one level up.

The property that actually holds the repair:

| reading | `41860773768` (before) | `41939709206` (after) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| replies whose last non-empty line is a closing label | 94 | 94 |
| **of those, answers still returned whole** | **8** | **0** |

So the parser now reads every terminator it is handed, and it is inert on the 365 replies that have
none. That is the product assertion, and it belongs in a test rather than in a prediction: it is now
`parse-closing-label.test.ts`'s first two cases plus the 1,060-record inertness check.

### 13.251.5 The decision: keep, and say why it is not a revert

§13.248.7's branch for a falsified prediction 1 was "revert to `operands+operand-gap` and re-open the
axis". That branch was written for a *falsification*, and the falsifier — ≤ 94 **mean** — did not
occur (95.8). Neither did the confirmation. A cheap reading would take the written branch anyway,
because the level check failed; that reading would revert a change whose two statistics are both
better on both draws, on the strength of a test that could not have said anything.

So the registration stands, on four stated grounds:

1. **Two independent draws, one direction.** MR 96.3 and 95.8 against 94.5; full band 89.33 and 86.67
   against 84.00. Neither draw reverses.
2. **The composition never moved.** 75/46 in all three runs, so the gain is reading and not
   composition — the one thing §13.243 could not establish for its own change.
3. **Nothing regressed.** Overall 90.50 and 90.40 against 90.15; the four other capabilities read
   143.5/144.0, 62.0/62.5, 120.8/119.8, 30/30 — every one inside two questions of the registered value.
4. **The product defect it exposed is fixed and proven.** 0 of 94 labelled replies return the
   transcript, and the rule is inert on 1,060 archived records.

**What would overturn it**, stated now so that the next dispatch is not another coin: a third draw on
which MR's four-repetition mean is ≤ 94 **and** the full band ≤ 84.00%. Both conditions, because one
of them alone is inside the noise.

## 13.252 The column headed "coverable at any depth" was the reach row above it, and the population it mis-filed reads 93.66%

> **Corrected by §13.253.** The partition below reads delivery off `goldRanks`, and delivery is not a
> rank: the window is not a prefix of the ranking, and unscored gold is admitted by leftover room. On
> `41860773768` that mis-files 58 questions -- 42 with nothing missing filed as depth-limited, 16
> with nothing missing filed as pool-missing. The corrected partition is 255 complete at 93.33%, 100
> room-cut at 95.00%, 0 unsurfaced and 145 undecidable at 82.07%; **MR has zero room-cut questions**,
> so the sentence below about the room mattering for 17 of them is withdrawn. The reach ceiling of
> 67.8% is unaffected: it is a statement about surfacing, which is what the rank array answers.

### 13.252.1 The defect, as arithmetic rather than as judgement

§14.41.3 printed this table, headed *"门 3：把房间按金标定尺要花多少——正面的那一半"*:

| capability | n | 任意深度下可覆盖 | oracle 字符 | 实际字符 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 13.3% | 24,136 | 43,118 |
| IE | 150 | 51.3% | 19,930 | 43,717 |
| KU | 72 | 6.9% | 34,286 | 43,673 |
| MR | 121 | 62.0% | 24,704 | 45,642 |
| TR | 127 | 56.7% | 27,486 | 46,226 |
| **全部** | 500 | **46.6%** | 24,182 | 44,778 |

Every entry of the third column is the corresponding entry of §14.42.1's **48,000-character row** —
13.3 / 51.3 / 6.9 / 62.0 / 56.7 / 46.6. Six rows out of six, to the decimal. A quantity that is a
function of depth cannot coincide with the current reach on every capability at once; the column was
the reach computed again, and the sentence built on it — *"53.4% of the questions are not coverable at
any depth"* — is false for 142 of those 267.

The corrected partition, from `readout-arm-run.py --strata` on `41860773768`:

| capability | n | exact | acc | depth-limited | acc | pool-missing | acc | reach@any-depth |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 2 | 100.00% | 14 | 100.00% | 14 | 100.00% | 53.3% |
| IE | 150 | 75 | 94.67% | 43 | 95.35% | 32 | 96.88% | 78.7% |
| KU | 72 | 5 | 100.00% | 43 | 93.02% | 24 | 75.00% | 66.7% |
| MR | 121 | 63 | 90.48% | 17 | 76.47% | 41 | 63.41% | 66.1% |
| TR | 127 | 52 | 94.23% | 25 | 100.00% | 50 | 92.00% | 60.6% |
| **全部** | 500 | **197** | **93.40%** | **142** | **93.66%** | **161** | **83.85%** | **67.8%** |

The reach ceiling with the pool held fixed is **67.8%**, not 46.6%.

### 13.252.2 The three strata, and why `-1` is not "very deep"

- **exact** — every gold turn the dataset names was surfaced (`rank >= 0`) *and* inside the window
  (`rank < turns`). No retrieval or room change can improve the evidence this reader saw.
- **depth-limited** — every gold turn was surfaced; at least one sat below the cut. Reachable by a
  deeper window with the ranking held fixed.
- **pool-missing** — at least one gold turn was never surfaced. No window reaches it.

`goldRanks` records `-1` for a gold the ranking never reached, and its magnitude carries no rank. A
record with `-1` beside a rank below the cut loses on **both** axes; it is filed under `pool` because
that is the part no room change can fix. Filing it under `depth` is what priced a ranking repair as a
room repair for three rounds.

### 13.252.3 What the correction does to the two published numbers, and what it does not

**The reach ceiling** moves 46.6% → 67.8%, which is the direction §14.42.2 said was impossible.

**The 0.79× oracle keeps its arithmetic and loses its premise.** §14.42.2 priced the 267 non-full
questions at their **current** cost, on the argument that *"on those, no depth helps, so the full
window is the best any rule can do"*. For 142 of them that sentence is false: a deeper window does
reach the gold. The number 36,887 is still the cheapest cost of a rule that **preserves the current
coverage** — the objection is not to the sum but to the reason given for it, and to what was built on
that reason.

What must not be inherited is the conclusion drawn from it: *"a perfect allocation rule cannot help, so
the 53.4% is a pool problem."* Of the 267, **142 are a room problem** — they are simply an expensive
one, since covering them costs a median of 56 more turns each. Whether that price is worth paying is a
question this artifact cannot answer (§13.252.6), but it is no longer answered by an oracle that
assumed the question away.

**What the token axis keeps.** Every −20% / −30% statement was about rules that do not lose coverage,
and for those the 36,887 lower bound stands untouched: a rule cannot spend less than the depth its
delivered evidence requires, and on the 142 the delivered evidence is what it is. So the retirement of
"shrink the budget" stands; what falls is the separate claim that depth could not have helped anyone.

### 13.252.4 The depth hypothesis dies on the accuracy of the population it would help

| stratum | n | accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| exact | 197 | **93.40%** |
| depth-limited | 142 | **93.66%** |
| pool-missing | 161 | **83.85%** |

The 142 questions a deeper window would make "full" already read **0.26 points above** the population
whose evidence is complete. Reach was never the mediating variable: those readers were missing a gold
turn that they did not need.

The exception is stated rather than smoothed: for **MR** the depth stratum reads 76.47% against
90.48% for exact, so within that route the room does matter for 17 questions. For **KU** the depth
stratum reads 93.02% on 43 questions — the room is exonerated there — while its pool stratum reads
75.00% on 24. TR's depth stratum reads 100.00% on 25.

There is a second thing this table refuses to say. The strata are **not ordered by cause**: IE's pool
stratum reads 96.88%, above its own exact stratum. "Gold the ranking missed" predicts a low reading in
MR and KU and predicts nothing in IE. Any sentence of the form "the pool is the constraint" has to
name the route it is about.

### 13.252.5 The 63.04% partial band was two populations averaged together

§13.248.3 read MR's partial band — 46 questions at 63.04% — as evidence that those questions *"lack a
boundary rather than a quantity"*. The band splits exactly:

| MR partial band | n | accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gold surfaced, below the cut | 17 | **76.47%** |
| gold never surfaced (and one below the cut) | 29 | **55.17%** |
| the published band | 46 | 63.04% |

`(17 × 76.47 + 29 × 55.17) / 46 = 63.04` — the arithmetic is the check, not the claim. The 21-point
gap inside a single published band is the reason the two repairs kept being confused: one half wants a
deeper room, the other wants a ranking that surfaces the turn at all.

### 13.252.6 The instrument gap this exposed, stated so the next run can be gated

The character price of a **deeper** window is not readable from the artifact. It carries `turns` — the
text of what was delivered — and their count; it does not carry the ranking's per-candidate character
cost, so the cost of the candidates that were cut cannot be reconstructed. `--room` prices the smaller
direction exactly for that reason, and that is the only direction the artifact fully describes.

Everything §13.250 and §14.42 said about *shrinking* the budget is therefore measured; everything said
about *growing* it, including the `extra turns` column above, is in turns, and a turn-to-character
conversion would be an estimate from a mean. An estimate was enough to reject the depth hypothesis on
accuracy (§13.252.4), which is the reading that decided it — but it is not enough to price a depth
rule, and the next run that wants to try one must record `rankingChars` per question: the ordered
candidate list's per-candidate length, so both directions become simulable.

### 13.252.7 What the next registration is, and the gates it must pass

The surviving population is the **pool-missing** one, and it is concentrated: MR 41 questions at
63.41%, KU 24 at 75.00%. For these the missing gold was never in the ranking, so a better window, a
better reader and a better ask are all out of scope by construction.

The mechanism the leading systems use on exactly these two routes is **aggregation** — a compact
per-session or per-fact view presented beside the turns, so a question whose evidence is a *set spread
across sessions* does not need one ranking hit per session (supermemory reports its LongMemEval-S
per-category recall "with aggregation" at MS 96 / KU 100 / TR 95 against full-context 44.3 / 78.2 /
45.1; Microsoft's Mnemis routes a second "System-2" pass over extracted FACTS and ENTITIES). That is a
*channel*, not a budget: it changes what the pool contains, which is the only thing this section leaves
standing.

Gates, written before the implementation, on the MR + KU pool-missing population (65 questions):

| gate | quantity | bar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (structural) | the timeline block's size on MR+KU | ≤ 6,000 chars on ≥95% of them, so it cannot be the budget by another name |
| 2 (structural) | LLM calls added per question | **0** — the block is derived verbatim from turns already retrieved |
| 3 (accuracy, merged) | MR pool stratum, three dispatches pooled | ≥ 30 of 41 correct (73.2%) against the current 26 of 41 (63.41%) |
| 4 (no regression) | IE / TR / ABS | each within ±2 questions of the registered arm |

Gate 3 is a **merged** criterion because the expected effect — 4 to 6 questions — is below two noise
widths on this route (§13.251.1's rule, ±2.3 questions at 121). Gate 2 is what stops the experiment
from becoming "call the model once more"; gate 1 is what stops it from becoming a bigger budget.

## 13.253 The three-stratum table read delivery off the rank array, and delivery is not a rank

### 13.253.1 The defect, stated as two numbers

§13.252 replaced a column that had restated the row above it with a partition -- `exact` 197,
`depth` 142, `pool` 161 -- and drew two conclusions from it. Both were computed from `goldRanks`:

```text
rank < turns    the window held this gold      (no -- it held a *turn*, and turns are not ranked)
rank < 0        the reader did not get it      (no -- leftover room can buy an unscored gold)
```

`GoldOverlap.carried` is the delivery count and it was in the same object the whole time. On
`41860773768` the two readings disagree on **58 questions**:

| reading | questions it mis-files | what the artifact says |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `rank < turns` = held | **42** | `carried == total`: every gold turn reached the reader. Filed as depth-limited, where a deeper window would allegedly help. |
| `rank < 0` = missed | **16** | `carried == total`: filed as pool-missing with nothing missing at all. |

### 13.253.2 Why the proxy is wrong twice over, and not by a little

**`turns` is not a window depth.** `WindowComposition.turns` counts every delivered turn,
including ones the ranking never scored, and the admission loop skips a turn that does not fit and
keeps scanning. So the delivered set is **not a prefix of the ranking**, and a gold at rank 210 can
be in the reader's window while a cheaper gold at rank 100 was skipped. On `41860773768`:

| question | rank 210 and 220 | delivered turns | scored among them |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| one complete record | both gold, both delivered | 181 | 156 |

The `--strata` column headed *extra turns* -- `max(rank) + 1 - turns` -- was therefore measuring a
quantity that does not exist. It has been removed rather than repaired: `rank` indexes candidates
and `turns` counts deliveries, and no arithmetic converts one into the other.

**`rank < 0` is not a miss.** `selectByRelevance` sorts descending and puts unscored turns last, and
leftover room admits them. A gold the ranking never scored is often a gold the reader read. Sixteen
questions in the pool stratum carried **all** of their gold this way.

### 13.253.3 The instrument: one predicate, and the count recomputed from it

`GoldOverlap.goldDelivered` is a `boolean[]` aligned with `goldRanks`, written by the same
membership test `carried` counts:

```ts
const carried = goldTurns.filter((gold) => retrieved.includes(gold)).length;
return { carried, total: goldTurns.length, goldDelivered: goldTurns.map((g) => retrieved.includes(g)), ... };
```

`goldDelivered.filter(Boolean).length === carried` and `goldDelivered.length === total` are
redundancies a test asserts rather than trusts, for the reason `pool` is. The field is absent on
every artifact that predates it, and absence means **not recorded**, never "nothing delivered".

### 13.253.4 The corrected partition, and the two sentences it retracts

`readout-arm-run.py --strata` on `41860773768`:

| capability | n | complete | acc | room-cut | acc | unsurfaced | acc | undecidable | acc | reach |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 2 | 100.00% | 14 | 100.00% | 0 | – | 14 | 100.00% | 53.3% |
| IE | 150 | 75 | 94.67% | 43 | 95.35% | 0 | – | 32 | 96.88% | 78.7% |
| KU | 72 | 5 | 100.00% | 43 | 93.02% | 0 | – | 24 | 75.00% | 66.7% |
| MR | 121 | 84 | 88.10% | **0** | – | 0 | – | 37 | **59.46%** | 66.1% |
| TR | 127 | 89 | 96.63% | **0** | – | 0 | – | 38 | 89.47% | 60.6% |
| **全部** | 500 | **255** | **93.33%** | **100** | **95.00%** | **0** | – | **145** | **82.07%** | 67.8% |

`complete` — every gold turn reached the reader. `room-cut` — not all arrived, but every one the
dataset names was surfaced: the only population a deeper window can change. `unsurfaced` — a gold
that did not arrive was never surfaced either. `undecidable` — the record has no `goldDelivered`, so
"the unsurfaced gold" and "the gold that did not arrive" cannot be shown to be the same turn.

**Retraction 1.** §13.252.4 said *"for MR the depth stratum reads 76.47% against 90.48% for exact,
so within that route the room does matter for 17 questions."* MR has **zero** room-cut questions.
Those 17 were questions whose gold all arrived; the rank that made them look depth-limited sat
beyond a `turns` count that was never a depth. The room does not bind on MR at all.

**Retraction 2.** §13.252.4's headline -- *"the 142 questions a deeper window would make full
already read 93.66%"* -- is replaced by a stronger statement on a population that is actually the
one a deeper window would change: **room-cut reads 95.00% against complete's 93.33%**. The
exoneration of the depth axis survives, and it now rests on the right population.

### 13.253.5 The confounder, printed beside the table it confounds

Accuracy tracks **how many gold turns the dataset names** on its own:

| gold turns | n | accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1–4 | 11 | 100.00% |
| 5–8 | 42 | 97.62% |
| 9–16 | 276 | 92.75% |
| 17+ | 171 | 84.21% |

and the four strata are not independent of it (a large gold set is likelier to lose one). So the
first table compares **populations, not treatments**. `--strata` now prints the cut:

| gold turns | complete | acc | room-cut | acc | undecidable | acc |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 9–16 | 162 | 93.83% | 38 | 97.37% | 76 | 88.16% |
| 17+ | 49 | 85.71% | 57 | 92.98% | 65 | 75.38% |

Two readings survive the cut and one does not:

- **`room-cut` > `complete` inside both buckets.** The confounder works *against* the exoneration
  (a 17+ gold set is harder and room-cut is 57 of the 17+ bucket's 171), so the conclusion is safe
  in the conservative direction.
- **`undecidable` loses 10 to 17 points inside a bucket** (88.16 against 97.37; 75.38 against
  92.98). So the 145 are genuinely worse than their gold count alone predicts, and the cause is
  what the artifact cannot say.
- **What does not survive** is any sentence of the form "the pool costs N points": the 145 mix at
  least two states and the mixture's composition is not in the artifact.

### 13.253.6 A number this settles: reach at *session* granularity is 100%

§22.18.5 and §1.22.2 recorded an incomparability: ContextStream publishes *"at least one
answer-bearing **session** reached the reader: 491/500 = 98.2%"*, while our 67.8% is turn-level and
demands **every** gold turn. The artifact can answer the coarser question directly, because
`carried >= 1` is exactly "at least one gold turn reached the reader":

| quantity | unit | this run |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| every gold turn delivered (`complete`) | turn, all | 51.0% (255/500) |
| every gold turn surfaced by the ranking | turn, all | 67.8% (339/500) |
| **at least one gold turn delivered** | **session-ish** | **100.0% (500/500)** |
| gold turns delivered, of gold turns named | turn | 86.47% (6,499/7,516) |

**Retrieval never fails completely on this benchmark for this arm.** Not one of the 500 questions
was answered without at least one of its annotated turns in front of the reader. That kills the
premise the previous round's next registration was written on -- *"a question either gets the small
piece that answers it or nothing at all"* -- and it kills it with an existing field rather than with
an experiment.

What the 145 lose is not *the* piece. It is **most of a set, or one member of a set**, and the
correct label for that is aggregation, not recall.

### 13.253.7 The next dispatch is an instrument run, not a hypothesis

Nothing in this section can be finished by argument: 145 questions are `undecidable` because the
artifact predates the field. So the next dispatch re-runs the **registered configuration
unchanged** -- same ask, same pool, same room, same reader -- for one reason: to convert
`undecidable` into the other three states. It is the only dispatch in this campaign with **no
accuracy hypothesis**, and its gates are therefore structural:

| gate | quantity | bar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (structural) | records carrying `goldDelivered` | 500/500, and `len == total` on every one |
| 2 (structural) | `sum(goldDelivered) == carried` | 500/500 -- the field and its own count agree |
| 3 (structural) | `unsurfaced` + `room-cut` == `undecidable` of `41860773768` (145) | the four columns are a partition of 500 |
| 4 (no drift) | accuracy, overall and per capability | within ±2 questions per capability of `41860773768`/`41939709206`; a movement larger than that is a defect in the instrument, not a finding |

Gate 3 is the one that makes the run worth its 85 minutes: it says the 145 are **converted**, not
merely re-counted. Gate 4 is a reproducibility check on a run that changes nothing, and it uses the
turn-level quantity rather than the aggregate because the aggregate is the number that has already
demonstrated a ±2.3-question noise floor (§13.251.1).

What the conversion buys is one sentence that cannot be written today, in whichever direction it
comes out:

- if `unsurfaced` dominates the 145, the deficit is a ranking problem and the mechanism to try is a
  better pool -- which is the aggregation channel, restated as *"the set is there and the ranking
  finds one member"*;
- if `room-cut` dominates, a deeper window becomes live again on a population that was mis-filed
  for three rounds, and §13.252.6's missing `rankingChars` becomes the field to add next.

The previous round's `rankingChars` is **deferred, not dropped**, and the reason is now measured
rather than assumed: the depth axis is exonerated on 100 room-cut questions at 95.00%, so a field
that would price a dead axis buys nothing until gate 3 says the axis is alive.

Gates 1 to 3 are read by one command, `readout-arm-run.py --instrument`, which prints the four
counts the bars are compared against and counts a **missing** field apart from a **wrong** one: on
`41860773768` the first is 500 and the second is 0, and on a record whose flags disagree with its
own `carried` they are the other way round. A gate re-typed at readback is a gate typed differently
the second time, which is how `--strata` came to be wrong in the first place.

## 13.254 A count is wrong by one when one item is missing, and "missing exactly one" is our modal state

### 13.254.1 An interaction nobody had looked for, on data already in hand

§13.253 exonerated the room by comparing strata. That comparison pools every question shape together, and
the shapes do not behave alike. Splitting the 500 by **whether the ground truth is a number** -- a
count, a sum, a duration -- against **whether every gold turn arrived**:

| | every gold delivered | some gold missing | difference |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| numeric answer | **89.77%** (88) | **78.57%** (70) | **−11.20** |
| text answer | 95.15% (165) | 89.12% (147) | −6.03 |

Inside MR the same split is **87.69% (65) against 55.56% (27), −32.13 points**. A counting question
loses three times as much from an incomplete evidence set as an extractive one, which is what the
mechanism predicts: an extractive answer survives losing a turn it did not need, and a count does not.

### 13.254.2 The number that decides the mechanism

Restricted to numeric questions with some gold missing (70), by **how many** are missing:

| gold turns missing | n | accuracy | mean gold turns named |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| exactly 1 | 19 | **52.63%** | 16.9 |
| 2 | 21 | 85.71% | 18.4 |
| 3 or more | 30 | 90.00% | 19.2 |

and inside MR, missing exactly one is **12 questions at 33.33%** -- four of twelve.

Read by the fraction delivered instead, the same non-monotonicity: `<0.7` delivered reads **100.00%**
(11), `0.7-0.9` reads 84.38% (32), `>=0.9` reads **62.96%** (27).

**Almost-complete is the worst state, and almost-complete is where this arm lives**: 86.47% of all gold
turns are delivered, so the modal question is missing one or two of fifteen.

The confound is stated rather than smoothed: a question missing three of nineteen may have a larger,
more redundant gold set than one missing one of seventeen, and the 100% at `<0.7` says those questions
are easy for a reason that has nothing to do with the fraction. What survives the confound is the
operational statement, because it is the one the arm is actually in: **the marginal value of the last
missing turn is the highest of any turn**, and a mechanism that improves the *average* delivered
fraction is not the same as one that closes the last gap.

### 13.254.3 Why this does not resurrect the room

It would be the natural reading, and it is wrong on this run's own numbers: **MR has zero room-cut
questions** (§13.253.4). Every MR question that is missing a gold turn is also missing one the ranking
never surfaced. So on the route where the effect is largest, the decisive missing turn is not one the
budget cut -- it is one the ranking never offered. A bigger room cannot buy it.

That leaves the ranking and the ask, and it makes the next mechanism's target precise: **the single
turn that changes a count**, on MR, numeric, delivered fraction `>=0.9`.

### 13.254.4 The prediction this section is staking, written before the readback

`41970746908` was dispatched before this section was written and re-runs the registered configuration
with `goldDelivered` added. Its `unsurfaced` column converts the 145 `undecidable` into the two states.
Two predictions, both falsifiable by that artifact:

1. **`unsurfaced` will dominate `room-cut` inside MR's 37** -- predicted from MR's zero room-cut and
   from the effect being concentrated in numeric questions. If MR's 37 come out mostly `room-cut`,
   §13.254.3 is wrong and the room is live again.
2. **The 19 numeric/missing-one questions will be `unsurfaced`, not `room-cut`** -- their missing turn
   is the one the ranking never offered. If they come out `room-cut`, the mechanism is a bigger room
   after all and the price in `rankingChars` becomes the next instrument.

Neither prediction changes any bar already written. They exist so that the next section has to argue
with a number rather than with a narrative.

### 13.254.5 The mechanism the numbers point at, and its gates

The leading systems' answer to "a set spread across sessions" is not a bigger pool; it is a
query-time reorganisation of the evidence that is already there. Chain on Demand (arXiv:2611.02480)
does it deterministically on an unchanged turn-level memory: allocate a fixed anchor budget by query
relevance, **lexical diversity relative to the chosen anchors** and **newly covered query terms**, then
restore each anchor's same-session neighbourhood verbatim. Turnbook's learned reranker is the same
family of move and is worth 4.8 points, with its own note that it helps most where the answer spans
sessions.

For a count over a period, that construction is the natural fit: the question's own words name the
*property*, not the *items*, so dense retrieval ranks the few statements that mention the property
highly and the rest of the set not at all. An anchor-plus-neighbourhood selection reaches the rest
because it stops asking the score to find them.

Gates, written before the implementation, on MR's numeric population with a delivered fraction
`>=0.9` (27 questions at 62.96%):

| gate | quantity | bar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (structural) | LLM calls added per question | **0** -- selection is deterministic, restoration is verbatim |
| 2 (structural) | characters added per question | ≤ **+15%** on the registered 46,631 median |
| 3 (accuracy, merged) | MR numeric `>=0.9` delivered, three dispatches pooled | ≥ **21 of 27** (77.8%) against 17 of 27 (62.96%) |
| 4 (no regression) | IE / TR / ABS / MR text answers | each within ±2 questions of the registered arm |

Gate 3 is merged for §13.251.1's reason -- 4 questions is under two noise widths at 27 -- and gate 1
is what keeps the experiment from becoming "ask the model again".

### 13.254.6 Two tools, two definitions, and the band both of them call "partial"

§13.252.5 bisected MR's published partial band into 17 questions at 76.47% and 29 at 55.17%, using
`--strata`'s strata. `--split` partitions the same band differently because its `full` test is
"every **surfaced** gold rank is below `turns`", which puts a question with a `-1` beside an
in-window rank in `full` where `--strata` files it under `undecidable`:

| definition | MR partial | of which delivered every gold turn | accuracy | of which did not | accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `--split` | 46 | **19** | **78.95%** | 27 | 51.85% |
| `--strata` | 46 | 17 | 76.47% | 29 | 55.17% |

Both close: `(19 × 78.95 + 27 × 51.85) / 46 = 63.04` and `(17 × 76.47 + 29 × 55.17) / 46 = 63.04`.
The two disagree on four questions and agree on the thing that matters: **the band's average mixes a
population that is missing nothing with one that is missing something painful.** Which tool a reader
