quotes decides whether that is 19 or 17, so the choice has to be named rather than defaulted --
`--split` now prints its own count of the questions whose `carried == total`, and the sentence
"MR's partial band reads 63.04%" should never appear again without the two halves beside it.

## 13.255 The instrument run closed the 145 and measured the noise floor instead

### 13.255.1 Three of four gates pass, and the fourth fails for a reason worth having

`41970746908` ran the registered configuration unchanged -- departures `none` -- and finished in
84 minutes. `readout-arm-run.py --instrument` on its artifact:

| gate | bar | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 records carrying `goldDelivered` | 500 | **500** | pass |
| 2 `len == total` / `sum == carried` | 0 / 0 defects | **0 / 0** | pass |
| 3 `room-cut + unsurfaced` == the 145 `undecidable` | 145 | **100 + 145 = 245 = the 245 incomplete** | pass |
| 4 accuracy within ±2 questions per capability | ±2 | **MR +3, TR +2, KU +1, IE 0, ABS 0** | **fail** |

### 13.255.2 The 145 are all `unsurfaced`, and that was already determined

| state | `41860773768` | `41970746908` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| complete | 255 | 255 |
| room-cut | 100 | 100 |
| unsurfaced | 0 | **145** |
| undecidable | 145 | **0** |

Not one of the 145 became `room-cut`. Both predictions of §13.254.4 hold: `unsurfaced` dominates
inside MR's 37, and the numeric/missing-one questions are `unsurfaced` rather than room-limited. The
room is now exonerated on a population that is *known* to be room-fixable and turns out not to exist
in MR at all.

The correct way to read this is narrower than "the prediction was right". `carried` was identical on
**500 of 500** questions between the two runs, so the partition was already determined; the new field
did not change it, it made it *readable*. What the field bought is the sentence that could not be
written before: for each of those 145 questions, **the gold turn that did not arrive is the gold turn
the ranking never surfaced** -- a claim that needed per-gold delivery to establish, and that no
amount of `goldRanks` could have supported.

### 13.255.3 Gate 4 failed, and the failure is the round's real measurement

Two dispatches of one configuration, differing only in whether the artifact records a field:

| | `41860773768` | `41970746908` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| overall | 90.40% | **91.60%** |
| MR | 96/121 | **99/121** |
| TR | 120/127 | **122/127** |
| KU | 63/72 | **64/72** |
| IE | 143/150 | 143/150 |
| ABS | 30/30 | 30/30 |

Byte-level comparison of the two artifacts:

| quantity | identical on |
| --- | ---: |
| `promptDigest` | **500 / 500** |
| delivered turn texts | **500 / 500** |
| `goldOverlap.carried` | **500 / 500** |
| gold turns delivered, of gold turns named | **6,499 / 7,516 in both** |

and yet **16 questions changed verdict: 11 from wrong to right, 5 from right to wrong** (exact
sign test, two-sided p = **0.21**). So the +1.20 points is not an improvement, an effect, or drift
in the instrument: it is the reader's own non-determinism on **identical bytes**.

By capability, on those identical bytes:

| capability | n | flips | up | down | rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| ABS | 30 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.0% |
| IE | 150 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1.3% |
| KU | 72 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 4.2% |
| MR | 121 | **7** | 5 | 2 | **5.8%** |
| TR | 127 | 4 | 3 | 1 | 3.1% |
| **all** | 500 | **16** | 11 | 5 | **3.2%** |

**The noise floor this campaign has been quoting is too tight, and it is tightest where the campaign
looks.** A net count over `n` questions whose per-question flip probability is `p` has
`sd = sqrt(n · p)`: **±4.0 questions overall** and **±2.6 on MR**, so two noise widths is
**±8 questions overall (1.6 points)** and **±5 on MR**. The ±2.3-question figure used since §13.251
was measured on one route over one pair of dispatches; on this pair MR alone moved 3 and has now
been observed at 94, 96 and 99 across three dispatches of one configuration.

Three consequences, and the third is the uncomfortable one:

1. §13.253.7's gate 4 was written from a single pair and is wrong as written; the replacement is
   "within two measured noise widths", with the widths quoted per capability from this table.
2. **Any unpaired single-dispatch difference below 1.6 points is unreadable on this arm.** Several
   changes adopted earlier in this campaign moved 3 or 4 questions; those are inside this band and
   their adoption stands only where a paired test -- four repetitions, McNemar -- said so.
3. The measurement does not decompose into reader and judge. Both are stochastic; this pair bounds
   their sum and says nothing about the split. A judge-only audit is a separate experiment: re-grade
   a fixed answer set and count the flips, which is what `--judge-audit` exists for.

### 13.255.4 The confounder table earned its place on this pair

The pooled comparison of `room-cut` against `complete` **changed sign between the two runs** while
the within-bucket comparison did not:

| | `41860773768` | `41970746908` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| pooled `room-cut` − `complete` | **+1.67** | **−0.90** |
| 9–16 bucket, `room-cut` − `complete` | +3.54 | +1.69 |
| 17+ bucket, `room-cut` − `complete` | +7.27 | +3.47 |

The pooled number moves because `room-cut` is 57 of the 17+ bucket's 171 and only 49 of `complete`'s
255 are there: the pooled difference is a weighted average of within-bucket differences with weights
that belong to the population, not to the treatment. A section that quoted the pooled sign would have
written opposite sentences from two runs that delivered **identical bytes**. This is §13.253.5 with
teeth rather than advice.

### 13.255.5 The interaction replicated on a second sample

§13.254's numeric-versus-text split, recomputed on the new artifact:

| | `41860773768` | `41970746908` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| numeric, complete | 89.77% (88) | 92.05% (88) |
| numeric, incomplete | 78.57% (70) | 81.43% (70) |
| numeric, difference | **−11.20** | **−10.62** |
| text, complete | 95.15% (165) | 96.36% (165) |
| text, incomplete | 89.12% (147) | 89.12% (147) |
| text, difference | −6.03 | −7.24 |

and the non-monotonicity in how much is missing:

| numeric, gold missing | `41860773768` | `41970746908` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| exactly 1 | 52.63% (19) | **63.16% (19)** |
| 2 | 85.71% (21) | 85.71% (21) |
| 3+ | 90.00% (30) | 90.00% (30) |
| MR, exactly 1 | 33.33% (12) | **50.00% (12)** |

The ordering replicates on both runs; the "missing exactly one" cell moved **two questions out of
twelve** between them, which is this section's own noise band applied to itself, and is why the
gate §13.254.5 wrote is pooled over three dispatches rather than read from one.

### 13.255.6 What this changes in the plan

The mechanism is unchanged -- §13.254.5's anchor-and-neighbourhood construction, with 0 added calls
and ≤15% added characters -- because the reading that motivates it replicated. What changes is the
bar, and the change is arithmetic rather than judgment:

| gate | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §13.254.5 gate 3 | ≥ 21 of 27 | **≥ 21 of 27, pooled over three dispatches**, against a pooled baseline of 17–18 of 27 |
| §13.253.7 gate 4 | ±2 questions per capability | **two measured noise widths per capability** (MR ±5, TR ±4, KU ±3, IE ±3, ABS 0) |
| every future single-dispatch claim | no bar | **must exceed 1.6 points, or be paired** |

The last row is the one that costs something: it says the campaign's habit of adopting a change that
moved three questions is not supportable on its own, and every adoption of that size needs a paired
statistic or a repeat.

## 13.256 The pool is widened by construction, and the metric it moves is named before it moves

### 13.256.1 Why the increment is not a wider pool

§13.54 raised `relevanceTopK` to 256 and coverage did not move. The reading that survives is narrow:
the missing turns are not just below the cut, they are far below it. §13.255.2 then closed the
question of *which* turns are missing -- all 145 are `unsurfaced`, meaning for each of them the gold
turn that did not arrive is one the ranking never offered -- and §13.254.3 closed the question of
*why a bigger room cannot help*: on the route where the effect is largest, **not one** MR question
is room-limited.

So the next variable is neither width nor room. It is **what the pool is built from**. A
count-bearing question names the property ("how many", "in total") while its evidence states the
items, so the members of the set score far under any cut that keeps the pool the size of a prompt.
The construction that reaches them is the one the leading systems use on an unchanged turn-level
memory: pick a few **anchors** by what they cover of the question, then restore each anchor's own
session neighbourhood verbatim (Chain on Demand, arXiv:2611.02480; Turnbook's learned reranker is
the same family of move and is worth 4.8 points on a question set whose answers span sessions).

### 13.256.2 The selection key, stated as an order rather than as weights

Three quantities decide an anchor and they are not commensurable: a count of newly covered question
terms, a `[0, 1]` lexical distance from the already-chosen anchors, and the retriever's own score.
Adding them needs weights, and no measurement in this campaign has priced a weight. The order is
lexicographic instead, and every key is total:

1. **newly covered question terms**, descending -- a hit that covers nothing new is skipped, not
   demoted, and the walk stops when no candidate covers anything new;
2. the second key is **novelty against the worst-overlapping chosen anchor**, descending;
3. then the **retriever's score**, descending;
4. then the **retriever's own position**, ascending.

The first anchor is the retriever's best hit, unconditionally. That makes the mechanism monotone
against the shipped ordering: with `count = 1` and `radius = 0` the pool is the retriever's pool,
score for score. A restoration that moves nothing is therefore attributable to restoration.

Restoration itself is verbatim and decays: a turn `d` steps from an anchor carries
`anchor_score * 0.5^d`, so it is always ranked **below** its own anchor, and a turn the retriever
already scored keeps its measured score. No model call, no embedding, no invented number.

### 13.256.3 The gates, restated for this mechanism

Gates 1 and 2 are structural and are properties of the construction above rather than promises:

| gate | quantity | bar | how it is read |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | model calls added per question | **0** | the index's own call counters must equal the registered run's |
| 2 | prompt characters added per question | **≤ +15%** on the registered 46,631 median | `evidenceChars` per question, unchanged room, so the predicted addition is **0** |
| 3 | MR numeric, delivered fraction `>=0.9`, **pooled over three dispatches** | **≥ 21 of 27** | against a pooled baseline of 17–18 of 27 |
| 4 | IE / TR / ABS / MR text answers | each within **two measured noise widths** (MR ±5, TR ±4, KU ±3, IE ±3, ABS 0) | §13.255.3's flip table |

Gate 2 is not vacuous even though the room is unchanged: restoration changes **which** turns the
room buys, and a session whose turns are larger could fit fewer. The bar is the upper bound on that
re-arrangement, and it is checked rather than assumed.

### 13.256.4 The metric this dispatch changes, and why gate 3 does not use it

`goldRanks` reads `rankedCandidatesFor`, and that array now contains the restored turns. So the
`unsurfaced` count is **not comparable across the two mechanisms**: a gold turn that was
`rank >= 0` before can be `rank >= 0` after for a different reason, and one that was `-1` can become
a large number without having been retrieved by anything.

That is why gate 3 is a **delivery count** (`goldDelivered`, gate 3's `carried`) and not a pool
statistic. The pool columns are still printed, because the mechanism's reach has to be visible --
`anchors.questions`, `anchors.anchors`, `anchors.restored` are new census fields and a run that
reports `questions: 500, restored: 0` is a mechanism that fired on nothing, which is a finding
rather than a null result. What the pool columns may **not** be used for is a sentence of the form
"more gold turns are now surfaced", because the denominator moved with the mechanism.

### 13.256.5 What falsifies this, and what the campaign does if it does

Three falsifiers, each with a different repair:

1. **`restored: 0` on all 500 questions** -- the selection rule found no anchor with new coverage on
   any question, or the cases carried no boundaries. The second is a wiring fault and the census
   separates it (`questions` would be 500 with `anchors: 0`); the first would mean the questions name
   no term their own evidence repeats, which the word "count" makes implausible.
2. **Gate 3 stays at or below 18 of 27** -- the missing turn is not in an anchor's neighbourhood. The
   next variable is then **which** neighbourhood: whole-session restoration (the `session-fill` rule
   already in the selection layer) or a turn-level lexical channel at the point of union.
3. **Gate 4 fails beyond the noise widths** -- restoration is displacing evidence the reader needed.
   The repair is the decay, not the mechanism: a restored turn's claim on the room would be too
   strong relative to a hit the retriever ranked far above its anchor.

Failure 2 is the one worth stating precisely, because it is the most likely and the least
informative on its own: it would say the anchor's session is the wrong unit, not that widening the
pool is the wrong idea. The distinction is only readable because the census counts anchors, restored
turns, and the delivery of every gold turn separately.

## 13.257 The widened pool bought 21 gold turns for 54 characters, and the gate that failed was reading a unit noisier than its own width

### 13.257.1 The comparison, and the one field it moves

`41990597116` ran the registered configuration with `relevanceSignal=retrieval-anchored` (§13.256).
Its control is the previous dispatch, `41970746908`, and the two configuration lines were compared
field by field rather than assumed: **22 fields, one difference**.

| | `41970746908` (control) | `41990597116` (treatment) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `relevanceSignal` | `retrieval-hybrid` | **`retrieval-anchored`** |
| `relevanceTopK` / `relevanceUnits` | `256` / `turn` | identical |
| reader | `deepseek:deepseek-chat@api.deepseek.com/thinking=enabled on multi-session+temporal/temp=0` | identical |
| `maxTurnChars` / routes / `maxPromptChars` | `400` / `multi-session+temporal` / `48000` | identical |
| runs / workers / dataset | 4 / 4 / `sha256:d6f21ea9…` (500) | identical |

The index line is in the job log and reads
`Relevance index: 129094 scored (question, turn) pairs over 500 questions at topK=256` — the same
order as the registered width, so the mechanism widened the pool by construction and did not widen
the index.

### 13.257.2 Gate 1 passed, and the counts moved the other way

Restoration is deterministic and asks no model for anything, so the gate cannot be failed by the
mechanism; what the artifact can do is confirm it.

| | control | treatment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| calls that returned a response | 5,670 | **5,652** (−18) |
| prompt tokens | 30,954,423 | 30,982,330 (**+0.09%**) |
| completion tokens | 2,155,202 | 2,216,478 (**+2.84%**) |

Eighteen fewer calls than the control is not an addition, and the prompt-token movement is a tenth of
a percent. The completion growth is the reader writing longer answers under a different evidence
order, which is a *reader* effect of the treatment rather than a call the treatment made.

### 13.257.3 Gate 2 passed at 0.0%, and the reason it could not have been otherwise

| quantity | control | treatment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| median `evidenceChars` | 482,305.5 | **482,305.5** |
| median `promptChars` | 46,834 | 46,816 (**−0.04%**) |
| median `evidenceTurns` | 417.5 | **417.5** |

The bar was `≤ +15%`, and the predicted value was zero because restoration changes **which** turns are
known, not how much room the reader gets. The observed median added turn count is zero because the
room is a character budget: restored turns displace other turns rather than extend the prompt. Measured
on the population where the prompt actually changed (§13.257.6) the displacement is **−0.19 delivered
turns and −53.7 characters per question** — mean, with median zero. That number is the whole of what a
decay parameter could ever have addressed, and it is why §13.257.7 withdraws the decay change.

### 13.257.4 Gate 3 is not adjudicable on one dispatch, and its denominator is why

The bar reads *"MR numeric, delivered fraction `>=0.9`, pooled over three dispatches: ≥ 21 of 27"*.
This is the first of the three, so the bar cannot be met or missed yet. What the dispatch can report
is the mechanism's delivery effect, which is the quantity gate 3 was built to move:

| | control | treatment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gold turns carried | 6,499 / 7,516 (**86.47%**) | 6,520 / 7,516 (**86.75%**) |
| gold turns surfaced in the pool | 7,155 | 7,208 (**+53**) |
| questions that gained gold | — | **21** (+24 turns) |
| questions that lost gold | — | **3** (−3 turns) |
| partition `complete / room-cut / unsurfaced / undecidable` | 255 / 100 / **145** / 0 | **259** / **108** / **133** / 0 |

Twelve questions moved out of `unsurfaced` and eight into `room-cut`, which is the partition behaving
as §13.256.4 predicted it would: the mechanism changes which gold the ranking can see, so the columns
move with it. That is also why gate 3's *rate* is not comparable across the two dispatches: the two
definitions this campaign's readout uses produce denominators of 30 and 45 on this run against 32 and
43 on the control, and a rate whose denominator is a function of the treatment is not a rate.

### 13.257.5 Gate 4 failed on its registered unit, and the unit is the finding

| capability | control (first pass) | treatment (first pass) | Δ questions | width |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IE | 143/150 | 142/150 | −1 | ±3 |
| **MR** | **99/121** | **91/121** | **−8** | **±5** |
| KU | 64/72 | 61/72 | −3 | ±3 |
| TR | 122/127 | 121/127 | −1 | ±4 |
| ABS | 30/30 | 30/30 | 0 | ±0 |

MR is eight questions down against a five-question width, so the gate fails as written. The four
passes of the two runs say something the first passes cannot:

| | control MR (min / mean / max) | treatment MR (min / mean / max) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MR, 4 passes | 92 / **94.8** / 99 | 91 / **94.8** / 97 |
| overall, 4 passes | 89.40% / **90.30%** / 91.60% | 89.00% / **90.25%** / 90.80% |

**The four-pass means are identical on MR (94.8) and differ by 0.05 points overall.** The two runs'
own pass-to-pass spread is 7 and 6 MR questions, which is **wider than the ±5 width the gate is read
against**. So the gate is not wrong about arithmetic; it is read on a unit — one pass — whose
dispersion exceeds the bar it is compared to. A gate that a single pass can fail by chance and pass by
chance is not measuring the mechanism.

### 13.257.6 Eleven of the eighteen losses arrived on byte-identical prompts

`promptDigest` is a 64-bit SHA-256 of the prompt text (`prompt-digest.ts`), so equal digests mean the
reader was sent the same bytes. Splitting the 500 paired questions by that field:

| population | n | wins | losses | flip rate | exact sign test | gold Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **prompt identical** | 372 | 2 | **11** | **3.49%** | p = 0.0225 | 0 |
| **prompt changed** | 128 | 3 | 7 | 7.81% | p = 0.3438 | **+21** |

Three readings, each load-bearing:

1. **The identical-prompt flips are the reader and the judge, not the mechanism.** 3.49% against the
   **3.2%** measured when two dispatches were byte-identical in every field (§13.255.3). A flip on
   unchanged bytes cannot be caused by a change, so this population is the noise control, and it
   behaved like one.
2. **The all-500 paired test the campaign has been using reads noise as treatment.** Those 23
   discordant pairs are 5–18 (p = 0.0106); 13 of them are in the identical-prompt population, whose
   own split is **2–11** (p = 0.0225) — a *more* extreme imbalance than the treatment's attributable
   component. Applying the campaign's own "a paired significant result is real" rule to this dispatch
   would require concluding that the mechanism hurt the reader on prompts it did not change.
3. **The attributable effect is −0.80 points.** On the 128 questions whose prompt changed: 3 up, 7
   down, `(3−7)/500 = −0.80` points overall, **inside** the ±1.6-point noise floor. MR's own
   attributable component is 1 up and 5 down, `−3.31` points, against a width that the MR pass spread
   already exceeds.

All 21 gained gold turns sit in the changed population, which is the structural check that the field
means what it says: gold cannot arrive on a prompt that did not change.

The split is reproduced by `tools/readout-arm-run.py --attribution <control.json> <treatment.json>`,
which is where it now lives rather than in a script written for this section (§13.38's rule). It
prints both populations, the exact binomial for each, the attributable delta, and both sides'
four-pass spreads; it exits non-zero if gold moved on a question whose prompt did not, because that
would mean the digest or the pairing key is wrong and the split below it means nothing.

### 13.257.7 What this round retracts

1. **Retracted: "restoration is displacing evidence the reader needed"** (§13.256.5 falsifier 3's
   premise). The measured displacement is 0.19 delivered turns and 54 characters per changed question,
   and 11 of the 18 losses are on prompts that did not change at all.
2. **Retracted: the all-500 paired sign test as evidence about a mechanism.** It must be reported
   beside the identical-prompt split from now on. Where a mechanism changes only part of the
   population, the paired test over the whole population measures the reader.
3. **Withdrawn before dispatch: the steeper decay.** `5a302b8` moved `ANCHOR_DECAY` from `0.5` to
   `0.25` as the repair this section's first falsifier predicted; `e130ee9` reverts it. Lowering a
   parameter to fix a cost measured at 54 characters would be tuning a knob against a defect the
   artifact does not establish, which is the failure mode this section names.

### 13.257.8 What it establishes

1. The mechanism is a **delivery** mechanism and it works: **+21 gold turns for −54 characters and
   −0.19 turns**, on 21 questions gained against 3 lost, with `unsurfaced` down from 145 to 133.
2. Its **accuracy effect is unresolved**, not negative: −0.80 attributable points on 128 changed
   questions, with the four-pass mean 0.05 points apart.
3. The instrument that was supposed to decide (2) cannot, at this effect size. That is now a
   registered defect rather than a disappointment, and §13.258 is the dispatch that changes its unit.

## 13.258 The next dispatch: the same mechanism, read on the four-pass mean and the changed population

### 13.258.1 Why a replicate and not a dose

The obvious continuation is the decay axis. Three numbers close it before it is run: the mechanism's
room cost is **−0.19 turns** per changed question, its attributable accuracy delta is **−0.80 points**
inside the noise floor, and its delivery gain is **+21 gold**. There is no cost for a decay to remove
and no accuracy defect for it to repair, so a second dose would be a search along an axis whose
endpoints differ by less than the measurement's own resolution.

A replicate buys something the campaign does not have: **a second independent estimate of the same
two populations.** The changed-prompt population doubles from 128 to 256, the identical-prompt flip
rate is measured twice, and the +21 delivery is tested for reproducibility before anything is built on
it. That is the standard gate 3 already imposes on itself (`pooled over three dispatches`).

### 13.258.2 What it is registered to read

| readout | unit | why this unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **primary** | overall abstention-aware accuracy, **four-pass mean** | the first pass's spread (6–7 MR questions) exceeds the gate width (±5), so a first-pass verdict is a coin |
| **primary** | paired ledger on the **prompt-changed** population, with the identical-prompt split reported beside it | a flip on unchanged bytes is not the treatment's |
| secondary | gold turns carried, and the `complete / room-cut / unsurfaced` partition | the mechanism's own effect, comparable as a count |
| secondary | anchor census (`questions`, `anchors`, `restored`) and `anchorParams` | a live wiring check of `cfc634d`: this dispatch is the first that can report what the mechanism resolved and how far it reached |

### 13.258.3 The gates

| gate | quantity | bar |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 | calls that returned a response | within ±1% of the control's 5,670 |
| 2 | median `promptChars` | within ±5% of 46,816 |
| 3 | gold turns carried | **exactly 6,520**, because none of the steps that decide delivery involves a model |
| 4 | overall four-pass mean | within **±1.6 points** of 90.25% |
| 5 | changed-population paired ledger | reported with its exact sign test; **no bar**, because 256 questions at a 7.8% flip rate cannot resolve less than ~2 points |

Gate 5 has no bar on purpose. Writing one would invite the campaign to read a 15–15 split as a pass;
what is registered is that the number gets published, and that the decision rule below reads it.

### 13.258.3b Why gate 3 is an equality and not a floor

It was written as `>= 6,520` first, and that was wrong about what the number is. Delivery is decided
by the embedding, the fusion, the anchor selection, the decay and the budget -- **none of which
samples a model** -- against a dataset whose digest is pinned. So the expected count is not "at least
the value we saw", it is **that value**, and the gate is a determinism check rather than a
statistical one.

The distinction matters in both directions. A floor passes a run that silently delivered *fewer* gold
turns than the mechanism is capable of, which is the exact quantity the mechanism is being credited
with. An equality turns any deviation into a reading of its own: a count above 6,520 or below it means
something between the embedding service and the four-worker ordering is not reproducible, and **every
delivery figure in this campaign** -- including the +21 this dispatch exists to reproduce -- inherits
that noise. That would be a more important finding than the replication itself.

### 13.258.4 The decision rule, and what closes the pool axis

1. If gate 3 reproduces (≥ 6,520 carried) **and** gate 4 holds, the mechanism is adopted as a
   delivery improvement with no measurable accuracy cost, and the next increment moves to the room.
2. If gate 3 does not reproduce, the +21 was one dispatch's draw and the pool axis closes: `topK`,
   anchor restoration and session-neighbourhood filling have now all been tried against the same
   `unsurfaced` population without a delivery effect that survives a repeat.
3. If gate 4 fails beyond ±1.6 points **while the identical-prompt split is inside its own noise
   band**, that is the first attributable accuracy regression this mechanism has produced, and the
   repair is the decay after all — with the measured room cost in front of it.
4. If gate 4 fails and the identical-prompt split is also directional, the dispatch is unreadable and
   the next step is the judge instrument (`tools/judge-regrade.mjs`, commit `690821d`), not another
   benchmark.

## 13.259 The per-side spend split silently vanished, and the field's own absence rule hides it

Found while preparing P5 (the token axis), not while running an experiment. Recorded here because
the next round starts on it.

### 13.259.1 The evidence

| run | calls in `llmUsage` | `usageBySide` in the artifact |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `41546569106` | 5,685 | **present** |
| `41970746908` | 5,670 | **absent** |
| `41990597116` | 5,652 | **absent** |

The field is written by `attachUsageBySide`, and its own implementation is the reason the
disappearance is invisible:

```ts
export function attachUsageBySide(report: AblationReport, bySide: UsageBySide): AblationReport {
  return bothSides(bySide).calls === 0 ? report : { ...report, usageBySide: bySide };
}
```

Zero is dropped rather than reported. So "the split was measured and both sides were zero" and "this
artifact predates the field" are the same bytes -- the distinction `attachTransport`'s own docblock
refuses to collapse for its field, on the argument that a zero from an instrument that did not run is
not a measurement.

### 13.259.2 Why it blocks P5

P5's bar is "≤ 37,000 prompt tokens with reach unchanged". The strategy for reaching it depends
entirely on **which side spends the tokens**: the reader's evidence window, the judge, or the
phrasing stage. Without the split, a saving on one is indistinguishable from a saving on another, and
from a saving on the judge -- which is verbatim the argument `usage-by-side.ts` opens with.

It also means the campaign's own "≈11,500 tokens per query against Mem0's 6,787" has no artifact
trace: this run's whole-bill figure is **15,491 prompt tokens per answer** (30,982,330 over 2,000
answers, judge included), and no artifact says how much of it the reader spent.

### 13.259.3 The cause, and the fix

`runAblation` answers through `pool.baselineFor(worker)` / `pool.featureFor(worker)`. The two systems
handed to `runCortexMemoryArm` positionally were wrapped for the split, and under a pool **neither
wrapper is ever called** -- so both sides read zero, and the field's own zero rule then dropped it.
The distinguishing evidence is one column:

| run | `passShape` | `usageBySide` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `41546569106` | absent (no pool) | present |
| `41970746908`, `41990597116` | `workers: 4` | absent |

`tracedPool` (commit `7946797`) wraps each instance the pool builds, memoised per worker so instance
identity stays a function of the worker rather than of (worker, pass). `featureInstances()` passes
through untouched, because it is what `censusSourcesOf` reads and it compares the caller's `feature`
by identity; the wrapper delegates every call to the instance it wraps, so the per-instance censuses
are unaffected.

The test is the reproduction, not decoration: it fails against the unfixed code (`usageBySide`
undefined with a pool at two workers) and passes with it. The serial case beside it passed all along,
which is exactly why the pooled path needed its own.

### 13.259.4 What remains open

The zero rule. `attachUsageBySide` still drops the field when the sides sum to zero, so a future
instrument defect of this kind is invisible in the same way. The choice is between reporting zeros
with a marker and keeping the omission while making it unambiguous another way; it is not decided
here, and P5 should decide it, because P5 is the reader that needs the number.

## 13.260 The replicate reproduced, and the mechanism's own ledger had no reader

*Run `42013256884` is the replicate §13.257 registered: `41990597116`'s configuration, run again on
`2d74b188` with no field changed. It answered all five gates, and the fifth one -- the per-side spend
split -- came back `SKIP` for a reason that was already known when it was dispatched: the artifact
predates `7946797`. What this section records is the reading, the defect the reading exposed in the
instrument rather than in the mechanism, and the dispatch that defect makes possible.*

### 13.260.1 The five gates

| gate | quantity | threshold | reading | result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | calls that returned a response | ±1% of 5,670 | **5,668** (−2, −0.04%) | pass |
| 2 | median `promptChars` | ±5% of 46,816 | **46,816** (0.0%) | pass |
| 3 | delivered gold turns | **exactly 6,520** | **6,520 / 7,516 (86.75%)** | pass |
| 4 | overall mean over four passes | ±1.6 points of 90.25% | **90.60%** (+0.35) | pass |
| 5 | changed-population paired ledger | report only | see §13.260.2 | n/a |

Gate 3 is the one that decides the pool axis, and it is an equality rather than a bound for the
reason §14.49.3 gives: nothing that decides delivery samples the model, so the expected value is the
number itself. It reproduced exactly -- `6,520` of `7,516`, with `7,208` gold turns reaching the pool
against the control's `7,155`. Two independent runs of one configuration produce the same delivery
count and the same pool reach, which is what makes every delivery figure in this campaign quotable.

Gate 4 moved `+0.35` between two runs of *identical* configuration, against a band of `±1.6`. That is
the third measurement of this arm's overall noise (the twelve-question `ABS` route was 30/30 in both),
and it is the smallest of the three.

### 13.260.2 What the replicate could not answer

The fifth gate -- the paired ledger over the population whose prompts changed -- needs the control
artifact, and the control for this replicate *is* `41990597116`, which differs from the previous
round's control. That comparison is a separate reading and it is not in this section.

What the artifact does say, from its own fields:

| quantity | value |
| --- | ---: |
| recovered (declined → answered correctly) | 200 |
| corrected (wrong → correct) | 49 |
| missed (correct → wrong) | 18 |
| declined (correct → declined) | **0** |
| bare-decline retry consulted / answered | 71 / 71 (100.0%) |
| model declines over 2,000 question-answers | 134 (6.70%) |
| prefix-cache share of the prompt | 96.50% |
| judge channel | 1,500 of 4,000 (37.5%), 0 unjudged |

`declined: 0` is the load-bearing one for this arm: not one question that the control answered
correctly was declined by the treatment, so every one of the 18 losses is a content loss and the
`-0.80`-point attribution in §13.257.3 does not have a response-shape component hiding inside it.

### 13.260.3 Where the 49 wrong answers actually sit

The artifact's `goldOverlap` and `correct` fields answer a question no section of this document had
asked: **when the reader is wrong, was the evidence there?**

| capability | wrong | all gold delivered | partly delivered | none delivered |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| IE | 7 | 4 | 3 | 0 |
| MR | **26** | **14** | 12 | 0 |
| KU | 9 | 0 | 9 | 0 |
| TR | 7 | 2 | 5 | 0 |
| ABS | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **all** | **49** | **20** | **29** | **0** |

Two facts fall out of that table and neither was available before this run was read this way:

1. **No wrong answer is a retrieval failure.** `none delivered` is zero on every capability: the
   ranking always surfaced at least one gold turn, so "the pool is too narrow" cannot be the cause of
   any single failure in this artifact. §13.233.4's Fisher test said the same thing statistically
   (57.1% vs 26.9%); this table says it instance by instance.
2. **Twenty of the forty-nine were handed complete evidence and still answered wrongly.** For MR that
   is 14 of 26, and all 26 are *how many* questions (§13.233.3). A reader that is shown all seventeen
   gold turns of `0a995998` and replies `2` is not short of evidence.

The consequence is a boundary on what any retrieval work can buy: the ceiling of the pool/room axes in
this artifact is the 29 partly-delivered questions, and the other 20 need the reader's **mechanism**.
§13.235.2 already retired the reader *axis* -- a bigger model in the same family cost 7.20 points, and
`thinking` on two routes bought 6.25 -- so "the mechanism" means what the reader is asked to do, not
how large it is.

### 13.260.4 The instrument defect: a producer with no reader, fourth time

`CortexMemory.lastReview()` returns `{ first, final, changed }` and has done since §13.94. Grepping
this package for it returns **zero call sites**. So a run with `reviewPass: 'audit'` would have:

* issued one extra consultation on every answered multi-session question -- about nine per cent more
  calls than the control;
* produced an artifact in which the only trace of that was the call count;
* and left the reader to infer from an unchanged accuracy whether the review agreed with everything or
  never ran.

That is the same shape as §13.181 (a producer field with no reader), §13.220 (a check with no caller)
and §13.235.3 (a statement whose correctness depends on somebody remembering to consult it). The
repair is a reader, so this section records the reader rather than the intention.

### 13.260.5 What was added, and the identity each field is held to

| where | field | the identity it must satisfy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cortex-memory` | `auditCensus(): { attempted, changed }` | `changed <= attempted`; both monotone over the instance's life |
| `cortex-eval` | `report.audit` | present **iff** the run carried `reviewPass: 'audit'` |
| `cortex-eval` | `questions[].auditAttempted` / `auditChanged` | `attempted` equals the count of records flagged `true` |
| `cortex-eval` | `## Membership audit` section | renders the tally and states that improvement is not in the table |
| `tools/readout-arm-run.py` | `PASS/FAIL audit` | the identity above, checked on the artifact it was written in |

`changed` and not `answered`: this pass is handed an answer that already exists, so "returned a value"
is true of every consultation it makes. The only number a reader can act on is how often the review
disagreed, and the report says in its own text that whether a disagreement was an improvement is a
question for the roster beside it and not for the tally.

The two traces (`recoveryCensus`, `auditCensus`) now share one implementation -- `traceCensus` -- because
they differ only in the accessor they read and the shape they project. Four decisions (the delta, the
prototype mirroring, the throwing-accessor rule, the per-question key) were one copy each; a second
copy would have been four more places to be wrong, and §13.145.5 records what a wrong wrapper costs: a
forty-minute run that dies on question one, three times.

`tracedPool` applies the audit wrapper **per worker** for the reason §13.259 gives about the spend
split: under a pool the positional wrapper is never called, so a trace taken there is empty on exactly
the four-worker runs this mechanism will be measured on.

### 13.260.6 Registration: `reviewPass: 'audit'` against this artifact

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| control | `42013256884` -- `reviewPass: 'bare'`, everything else identical |
| treatment | the same 22 inputs with `cortex_memory_review=audit` |
| why this mechanism, now | the audit instruction (§13.94) names the three membership decisions -- missing from the first pass, one event split in two, an entry the evidence does not support -- which is §13.260.3's 20 fully-evidenced failures and §13.233.3's bidirectional count errors, stated as an instruction |
| what it has never had | a dispatch. `recover` was run (`40883121464`, MR net 0); `audit` has not |

Gates, written before the dispatch:

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | MR accuracy, paired against the control | **Mcnemar p < 0.05 and Δ ≥ +6 points** (the MR noise band is ±5, §13.203.4) |
| 2 | every other capability | no loss **≥ 4 points** |
| 3 | overall mean over four passes | **≥ +1.5 points** |
| 4 | calls that returned a response | **≤ 6,300** -- the declared price is one consultation per answered multi-session question; above that the pass fired where it should not |
| 5 | `census-unit` | still exactly **2,000**, because a pass that consults twice must not turn one question into two outcomes (§13.107) |
| 6 | `audit` identity | the `--audit` check passes: `attempted` equals the flagged records, `changed <= attempted` |
| 7 | `usageBySide` | **present**, and the two sides sum to no more than `llmUsage.calls` -- the first live reading of `7946797` |

Gate 4 is a cap and not a threshold: this mechanism costs a call by construction, and a run inside the
cap has spent what it said it would. Gate 7 is the one item here that is not about the mechanism at
all; it rides along because a dispatch is the only way to test an instrument that reports on dispatches.

Refutation. If MR moves less than six points while gate 6 passes, the audit ran, reviewed the lists and
did not change the answers enough to matter -- and then the 26 MR failures are not membership errors
and §13.233.3's reading needs replacing rather than extending. If gate 6 fails, nothing in the run is
readable and the next step is the instrument, not another dispatch.

## 13.261 Two runs of one configuration sent the same bytes 500 times, and the reader did not answer the same twice

*`42013256884` and `41990597116` are the same configuration -- the same 22 inputs, the same corpus, the
same reader, temperature 0. Comparing their artifacts field by field answers three questions this
campaign has been carrying as assumptions: whether delivery is deterministic, how much of the run-to-run
movement is the reader, and whether any of it is the judge.*

### 13.261.1 Delivery is deterministic, at the byte

| quantity | reading |
| --- | ---: |
| prompts with the same 64-bit digest | **500 / 500** |
| prompts that differ in any byte | **0** |

Not "the same window size" and not "the same gold set" -- the same `sha256` prefix of the same UTF-8
bytes, on every question. Delivery is a pure function of the corpus, the embedding, the fusion, the
anchor selection, the decay and the budget, and none of those read the model.

That result is what licenses §13.260.1's gate 3 being an equality, and it retroactively settles the
eleventh round's changed-population split: the 128 questions whose prompts moved between the control
and the treatment could not have moved for any reason other than the mechanism, because a run with no
mechanism change moves none of them.

### 13.261.2 The judge did not disagree with itself once

| population | n | verdicts that differ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| answer text **identical** to the other run | **276** | **0** |
| answer text differs | 224 | 20 |

Two hundred and seventy-six questions produced the same answer string in both runs. The judge saw the
same question, the same answer and the same gold in both, and returned the same verdict 276 times out
of 276. It is not that the judge is asked politely to be deterministic; it is that on the only inputs
where disagreement is observable, it did not disagree.

The 224 that changed are the reader's, and that is the whole of the variance this arm has been
arguing about.

### 13.261.3 The reader rewrites 44.8% of its answers on identical bytes, and half a point of that is verdict

| quantity | reading |
| --- | ---: |
| questions whose answer text differs | 224 / 500 (**44.8%**) |
| of those, verdict flips | 20 (**8.9%**) |
| fixed / broken | **7 / 13** |
| net, in questions | **−6** |
| net, in points on 500 | **−1.20** |
| first-pass accuracy, the two runs | 90.20% vs 89.00% |

So the `±1.6`-point band the eleventh round had to argue for from three indirect readings is now the
direct measurement it was standing in for: **the same bytes, read twice, move six questions.** The band
is not a policy margin; it is the width at which this reader disagrees with itself.

Two further readings, both of which change what the next increment should be:

1. **The flips are not spread evenly.** MR 12, IE 3, TR 3, KU 2, ABS 0. The route this campaign has
   been trying to fix is also the route whose reader is least reproducible -- 12 of 121 MR questions
   change verdict on unchanged input, against 0 of 30 ABS. An arm measuring a three-point MR effect is
   measuring a sixth of its own noise.
2. **TR rewrites almost everything and almost never changes its mind.** 125 of 127 temporal answers
   differ in wording between the two runs and 3 change verdict. The text varies, the decision does not:
   that is what a route whose answer is a short string under a fixed contract looks like, and it is why
   the `thinking` gain on TR (§13.235.2) is readable while a 2-point TR effect would not be.

### 13.261.4 P3 is answered, and the answer is that it was the wrong instrument

`tools/judge-regrade.mjs` was queued as `mode=regrade, limit=500, passes=2` -- one thousand short judge
calls -- to split the `±1.6` band into a reader share and a judge share (§14.49.5). This pair already
does that split, with no calls at all:

* judge share: **0 of 276** repeated inputs;
* reader share: **20 of 500**, of which 6 net.

Running the regrade now would measure a component this artifact bounds at zero and would not measure
the one that matters. P3 is therefore **closed by measurement, not by deferral**, and the budget it
would have spent belongs to the mechanism.

The standing caveat: this is one reader at one temperature on one corpus. A regrade becomes the right
instrument the moment a run reports a verdict flip on identical answer text -- which would be the first
evidence that the judge is a variance source here, and would make every unpaired comparison in the
archives suspect in a way this pair says they are not.

### 13.261.5 Gate 5: the population the mechanism could not touch moved more than the one it did

Same split as §13.257.2 -- a 64-bit prompt digest against the control `41970746908` -- applied to both
runs of the identical configuration. The two runs classify the roster the same way, which §13.261.1
requires: `128` changed, `372` unchanged, the same 128 question ids in both.

| population | run | up | down | net | net on 500 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| changed (128) | `41990597116` | 3 | 7 | −4 | −0.80 |
| changed (128) | `42013256884` | 5 | 6 | −1 | −0.20 |
| changed (128) | **both (256 observations)** | **8** | **13** | **−5** | **−1.00** |
| unchanged (372) | `41990597116` | 2 | 11 | −9 | −1.80 |
| unchanged (372) | `42013256884` | 2 | 8 | −6 | −1.20 |
| unchanged (372) | **both (744 observations)** | **4** | **19** | **−15** | **−3.00** |

The reading is the one §13.257.3 reached from one run and this pair makes unavoidable: **the population
whose bytes the mechanism did not touch drifts further, in the same direction, than the population whose
bytes it rewrote.** 19 of 744 readings lost a question on evidence that is byte-identical between the
two sides. A mechanism cannot cause that, and a "released" column computed from the whole 500 would
attribute it to the mechanism.

Against that floor, the mechanism's own footprint is `−1.00` point over 256 paired observations -- half
the width of the reader's self-disagreement measured in §13.261.3 (`−1.20` points on one run). So the
adoption in §13.260.1 is exactly what the decision rule says it is: the mechanism buys **delivery**
(`+21` gold turns, `+53` into the pool) and there is no measured accuracy cost, which is not the same as
a measured accuracy gain and must not be reported as one.

### 13.260.7 Adoption: `retrieval-anchored` is the registered ranking from `42013256884`

§14.49.4's decision rule 1 fired on gates 3 and 4, so the mechanism is adopted. Adoption is three
edits that have to happen together, and the reason they are one section rather than three is §13.69:
a dispatch sent on `retrieval` against an adopted `retrieval-hybrid` because the document and the
dispatch table each held their own copy of the value.

| where | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PREREGISTRATION` §10.3 bullet | `relevanceSignal: retrieval-hybrid`, adopted by §13.64 | `relevanceSignal: retrieval-anchored`, adopted by this section |
| `tools/dispatch-cortex-memory-ab.py` `INPUTS` | `"retrieval-hybrid"` | `"retrieval-anchored"` |
| this section | — | the record of what the adoption claims |

What it claims, in the sharpest available form:

* **delivery**: `+21` gold turns delivered (`6,499` → `6,520` of `7,516`) and `+53` into the pool
  (`7,155` → `7,208`), reproduced **exactly** on a second dispatch of the same configuration;
* **cost**: `−0.19` turns and `−54` characters of window per affected question;
* **accuracy**: `−1.00` point over 256 paired observations, against a reader whose self-disagreement on
  identical bytes is `−1.20` points on one run (§13.261.3) and which loses `−3.00` points on the
  population whose bytes the mechanism never touched (§13.261.5).

It does **not** claim an accuracy gain, and the phrase "no measured accuracy cost" is the whole of the
accuracy statement. The signal name now names one dose: `retrieval-anchored` at count 4, radius 3,
decay 0.5, which `anchorParams` prints in every artifact and `Anchor census` prints in every log — that
was §13.257.5's repair and this is the first adoption read through it.

The retired bullet is not deleted, it is superseded: §13.64's argument for the hybrid ranking is still
correct and the anchored signal contains it. What changed is which value a dispatch sends, and a
document that kept both answers would be the ambiguity the registration parser refuses by design.

## 13.262 The membership audit, measured: −6.10 points overall, and three reasons the number is not yet a verdict

*`42054107910` was dispatched as a single-field experiment against `42013256884`: the same 22 inputs,
`cortex_memory_review_pass` changed from `bare` to `audit`. It is the first run that administered the
pass. This section records what it measured, why the measurement cannot be read as a verdict on the
mechanism, and what the artefact said about the instruments that produced it.*

### 13.262.1 What the run answered

| gate from §14.50.6 | threshold | reading | result |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 MR accuracy, paired | McNemar p < 0.05 and Δ ≥ +6 | **62.81%**, Δ **−15.70** | **fail** |
| 2 every other capability | no loss ≥ 4 points | IE −5.3, KU +2.8, TR 0.0, ABS 0.0 | **fail** (IE) |
| 3 overall four-pass mean | ≥ +1.5 | **84.50%** vs 90.60%, **−6.10** | **fail** |
| 4 calls that returned | ≤ 6,300 | **5,966** | pass |
| 5 `census-unit` | exactly 2,000 | 1,791 answered + 209 declined = **2,000** | pass |
| 6 `audit` identity | tally summed by the roster | **FAIL, and the check was wrong** (§13.262.5) | n/a |
| 7 `usageBySide` | present, sides ≤ total | present, sides **3.43×** the total | **fail**, instrument (§13.262.5) |

Three of the seven gates fail on the mechanism and two fail on the instrument. The distinction is the
whole of this section, because the two instrument failures are what make the mechanism's number
unreadable rather than merely bad.

### 13.262.2 Where the loss sits, by whether the pass fired

The audit consults on the `multi-session` route only, and `askRoutes` is `[multi-session]`, so the
population it can reach is `MR` — 118 of whose 121 questions had an audit consultation on the first
pass. Splitting the paired ledger on that fact:

| population | n | up | down | net | net on 500 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **audited** (first pass answered) | 118 | 4 | **22** | **−18** | −3.60 |
| **not audited** | 382 | 6 | 13 | −7 | −1.40 |

The unaudited drift of −1.40 points is the reader's own self-disagreement, measured directly at
−1.20 in §13.261.3. The audited column is **three times** it and has the opposite sign from the +6 the
registration required. On its own that would refute §13.233.3's hypothesis — the 26 `MR` failures are
not membership errors a reviewer can repair.

It does not, because of what the 22 destroyed answers look like.

### 13.262.3 All 22 came back as a bare integer

| reading | count |
| --- | ---: |
| audited answers the treatment destroyed | **22** |
| of those, rewritten as a bare integer (`2`, `4`, `1`, `350`) | **22** |
| of those, whose gold was **not** a count (`TikTok`, `$6`, `February 1st`, `photography and cooking`) | **17** |
| `MR` questions whose gold **is** a count | 40 of 121 |
| audited questions that therefore could not produce a valid answer under the instruction | **81 of 118** |

The instruction said, in as many words:

> `Then write one line, exactly Step 2 — <the corrected count>, and nothing after it.`

That is a **specification** defect, not a reader defect. The pass runs on every answered
multi-session question, two thirds of which do not have a numeric answer, and the contract it was
given orders a number. `TikTok` → `2` is the instruction being obeyed.

The four improvements are the mirror image: `0` → `2`, `3` → `4`, `$5,250` → `$5,850`, `2` → `5` —
all count-shaped or money. On the population the instruction was written for, the pass is 4 up and 5
down: **neutral to one question**, on 118 questions, against a reader whose own noise is ±5 `MR`
points (§13.203.4).

So the honest summary of the mechanism after this run is: *the form clause destroyed 22 answers; on
count questions, where the instruction applied, the review was a wash.*

### 13.262.4 The second confound: `audit` silently withdrew the bare ladder

The artifact says something the dispatch did not intend:

| census | control `42013256884` | treatment `42054107910` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `bareRetry.attempted` / `.answered` | **71 / 71** | **0 / 0** |
| declines over 2,000 question-answers | **134** | **209** |

`carriesBareLadder(pass)` returned `true` for `bare` and `recover` and `false` for `audit`, so one
field changed and **two mechanisms moved**. §13.141.3 wrote that exclusion down with a reason — "a
bare retry under it would make any movement two consultations rather than one" — and the reason is
false: `answerSessions` retries a bare decline and **returns** before the audit branch, which requires
a first pass that was not a decline. The two act on disjoint outcomes of one call, so a run carrying
both gives each question at most one extra consultation of each kind.

The 71 conversions the control got and the treatment did not are inside every accuracy number in
§13.262.1. This is §13.141.1's defect, third occurrence: a field name read as if it were a population.

§13.141.3 is **superseded on that one clause**. `carriesBareLadder` is now `pass !== 'none'`, with the
disjointness argument in its own docblock and `review-pass-ladder.test.ts` asserting `audit` carries
the ladder.

### 13.262.5 Three instrument failures, and the one that matters most

**The spend split overcounted by 3.43×.** `usageBySide` reported `10,606 + 9,852 = 20,458` calls
against a run total of `5,966`, and `137,355,496` feature prompt tokens against `37,149,529` in the
whole run. The split took `llmUsage()` around each answer and added the difference; under four
workers, four answers overlap, each interval contains the others' calls, and each side counts work the
other side did. This was the field's **first live reading** — §13.259 repaired its absence one round
ago — and the first reading was wrong in the direction that would have made the token-efficiency claim
unfalsifiable.

The repair moves attribution to the **writer**: `cortex-ai` exposes `observeUsage`, `cortex-eval`
installs an observer backed by an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope, and a call is counted where the response
is parsed and the side is known from the ambient context. The scope lives in the instrument and not
in the product because `cortex-ai`'s entry is one of the ones `tools/entry-guard.mjs` reserves for
portable code, and `node:async_hooks` is not on the reserved list — the guard rejected the first
version of this fix, which is the guard working.

**The census and the roster counted different units.** `audit.attempted` was `469` against `118`
flagged records, and the factor was exactly the repetition count: the roster records the **first** of
four passes (`runs: 4`) and the tally counts all four. My own `--audit` check asserted they were equal,
which is an assertion that can only hold at `runs: 1`. Four fields were booleans
(`recoveryAttempted`, `recoveryAnswered`, `auditAttempted`, `auditChanged`); they are now counts
(`recoveryConsultations`, `recoveryAnswers`, `auditConsultations`, `auditChanges`), accumulated per
question across repetitions, and the identity is the one that holds at any `runs`: **the column sums
to the tally**. Renaming was part of the repair — a field whose unit changed under an unchanged name
is exactly the ambiguity §13.259 paid for.

**The audit's prompt was overwriting the delivery instruments.** `promptChars` was `+530` on every
audited question and `promptDigest` differed on 117 of 118, while `deliveredPromptChars` moved by a
median of **2 characters** — the delivering bytes had not changed at all. `#recordEvidence` wrote
`lastPromptText` from whichever consultation produced the answer, and with an audit that is the
review's prompt. The two facts are now separate: `#recordDelivery` is written only by the first pass
and feeds `promptChars`/`promptDigest`; `#recordCoverage` is written by the answering call and feeds
`carried`/`admittedEvidence`. This matters beyond this run: **every attribution in §13.257 and
§13.261 keys on `promptDigest`**, so a mechanism that rebuilds a prompt could have made itself look
like a retrieval change.

One consequence to state rather than discover later: gate 3 (`6,522` delivered gold turns against the
control's `6,520`) now measures the **answering** call's coverage, which an audit legitimately
re-samples. The delivery invariant is `promptDigest`, and it reproduced.

### 13.262.6 What was repaired, and what each repair is held to

| where | change | the identity or test it must satisfy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cortex-ai` | `observeUsage` / `createUsageTally` | an observer sees every recorded call and restoring stops it; the entry stays free of `node:` builtins |
| `cortex-eval` | `traceUsage` attributes at the writer | two concurrent answers over one side count **2** calls, which the delta method could not (`usage-by-side.test.ts`) |
| `cortex-eval` | trace fields are counts | the roster column sums to the run tally at `runs: 2` (`audit-census.test.ts`) |
| `cortex-eval` | `carriesBareLadder(pass) = pass !== 'none'` | `audit` carries the ladder; the populations are disjoint by the `first === null` branch |
| `cortex-memory` | `#recordDelivery` / `#recordCoverage` | the audit prompt never becomes `lastPromptText`; `carried` still comes from the answering call |
| `cortex-memory` | form-preserving audit instruction | the instruction no longer says "count"; a non-count first pass round-trips |
| `tools/readout-arm-run.py` | `--audit` | the column sums to the tally, on every record |

The instruction now reads:

> `Then write one line, exactly Step 2 — <the corrected answer>, and nothing after it, in the first
> pass's form: a count stays a count, a name stays a name. If the membership did not change, repeat
> its answer word for word.`

The second sentence is not decoration. 178 of 469 consultations (37.9%) changed the answer, and a
reviewer with no way to say "nothing changed" has to produce a difference. The literature on
intrinsic self-correction names both halves of this: refinement prompts bias a model away from a
correct first answer (ACL 2025 measured 58.8% of correct answers overturned on one model), and
restating the original task in the refinement prompt is the mitigation that survives that paper's
ablations (+3.2–4.9 points, −5.3 to −10.9 points of overturning).

### 13.262.7 Registration: the corrected audit, against `42054107910`

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| control | `42054107910` — the same 22 inputs, the same `audit`, the old instruction and the withdrawn ladder |
| treatment | the same inputs on `2d74b188`+ with the form clause, the ladder restored, and the three instrument repairs |
| what changes in the artifact | `usageBySide` is exact for the first time; `promptDigest` describes delivery again; `auditConsultations` sums to the tally; `bareRetry` fires again |

Gates, written before the dispatch:

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `MR` accuracy against **`42013256884`**, not against `42054107910` | **Δ ≥ 0 and McNemar not significant against** — the question is whether the repaired pass is worse than no pass, and neutrality is the pass condition |
| 2 | `MR` accuracy against `42054107910` | **Δ ≥ +10** — the form clause and the ladder together must recover most of the 15.7 |
| 3 | every other capability against `42013256884` | no loss **≥ 3 points** |
| 4 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** — the ladder is back; a run below this is a dispatch defect, not a mechanism result |
| 5 | calls | **≤ 6,400** = control 5,668 + 469 audits + ladders, and above that the pass fired where it should not |
| 6 | `audit` identity | the column sums to the tally, and `0 ≤ changed ≤ attempted` |
| 7 | `spend` | sides **≤ total**, which is the first reading the repaired attribution produces |
| 8 | `promptDigest` agreement with `42013256884` | **500 / 500** — delivery does not depend on the review, and now nothing else can claim it does |

Refutation. If gate 1 fails while gates 4–8 pass, the audit is worse than no audit even when it is
asked properly, and the membership hypothesis is dead in both its forms: not because the review cannot
help, but because a second pass over the same window costs more than the membership errors it repairs.
If gate 2 fails while gate 1 passes, the form clause did not do what §13.262.3 predicts and the 22
destroyed answers had a second cause.

### 13.262.8 A cheaper idea, retired before it was dispatched

The obvious repair after §13.262.3 is to stop trusting the reader's arithmetic: it writes a `Step 1`
list and then a number, and a deterministic tally over its own list would cost **zero calls**. This
was measured on the artifacts already in hand, over the 121 `MR` questions with a numeric gold:

| reading | control | audit |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| tally equals the gold | 13 | 1 |
| tally differs | 25 | 5 |
| **would break a currently correct answer** | **15** | 3 |
| **would fix a currently wrong one** | **1** | 0 |

Fifteen to one against, and the failures are instructive rather than noisy: for `eeda8a6d` the list is
`10 neon tetras / 5 gouramis / 1 pleco / 1 betta` and the answer is the **sum** (`17`), for `80ec1f4f`
it is a **distinct count** of venues (`2`, with one entry being the same venue's opening night), and
for `6d550036` the reader **excluded** five candidates by reading the question's verb too narrowly and
answered `0` against a gold of `2`. The aggregation operation is question-shaped and the selection is
where the remaining error is, so a fixed operation over the reader's own prose is a regression.

That result is why the next axis is not "count harder" but **event specification over a ledger** —
the mechanism `Beyond Retrieval: Evidence Access and Event Aggregation in Agent Memory` (arXiv
2610.19474) measures at +13.8 exact match over trajectory memory on 99 held-out repositories, with a
controlled probe that is the cleanest statement of the problem available: long-context reading answers
the same count correctly for **100% of trajectories at 14 events and 80% at 53**, and that paper's own
residual error category after deterministic aggregation is *event selection* — which is what `0a995998`
and `6d550036` are.

## 13.263 The gate table became data, and the run it judges is still in flight

§13.262.7 wrote eight thresholds before dispatching the corrected audit. That dispatch is
`42130772725`, created at `adb08726` on 2026-11-05T23:37Z and still queued when this section was
written, so what follows is not a reading of it. It is the repair of the *reader*: the eight rows are
now a file, and the file decides.

### 13.263.1 Why prose gates could not survive another round

Gate 6 of the same table read `FAIL` on `42054107910` and was **wrong** (§13.262.5): it compared a
flag count against a tally accumulated over four repetitions, and the ratio it reported — `469 / 118`
— was exactly `runs`. Nothing in the sentence "the column sums to the tally" says which of the two
is the column, and the reader who noticed was the same reader who was already holding the number.
§13.69 is the neighbouring failure: the registration and the dispatch each carried their own copy of
an adopted value, each agreed with itself, and they disagreed only with each other.

Both are the same shape. A threshold that exists as prose is re-derived by whoever reads it, at the
moment they read it, with the result already in hand. The repair is not a better sentence; it is to
stop asking a person to evaluate it.

### 13.263.2 What was built

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/gates/13.262.7.json` | one entry per registered row: its `quantity` and `threshold` copied verbatim from §13.262.7's table, the `kind` that decides it, and that kind's parameters |
| `tools/registered-gates.py` | the evaluator: seven kinds, a verdict per gate, exit `1` if any gate is not `PASS` |
| `tools/__tests__/test_registered_gates.py` | each kind on a fixture whose arithmetic is checkable by hand, every absent-field case, and the agreement test below |

The agreement test parses §13.262.7's markdown rows out of the document and compares them with the
spec **cell for cell**. Neither side can move alone: an edit to the table that is not mirrored in the
spec fails, and an edit to the spec that is not mirrored in the table fails. That is the same
argument §10.3's test makes for the dispatch's registered values, applied one level up — to the
thresholds rather than to the configuration.

| kind | decides | refuses when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `capability_delta` | one capability's paired delta against a control, plus McNemar when the row asks for neutrality | the two artifacts share no question |
| `capability_nonloss` | every capability **the control measured**, minus the ones gates 1–2 own, against a loss bar | a capability the control has no longer appears in the treatment |
| `field_at_least` / `field_at_most` | one numeric field against a bar | the field is absent or is not a number |
| `audit_identity` | the roster column's sum against the run-level tally, and `0 ≤ changed ≤ attempted` | any record did not write the column |
| `sides_within_total` | each attribution side's calls against the run total | a side carries no count |
| `digest_agreement` | delivery digests against the control's, on the shared population | fewer questions carry a digest than the row registered |

Three properties are deliberate rather than incidental.

**Deltas are paired.** Every delta is computed on the intersection of the two artifacts' question ids
and the excluded count is printed beside it, so a control that measured 480 of 500 questions cannot
contribute a delta over its 480 while the verdict reads as if it covered 500. The p-value is computed
on the same intersection, which is what makes the point estimate and the significance statement
claims about one population.

**`UNEVALUABLE` is not `PASS`.** A run that does not report `bareRetry.attempted` cannot demonstrate
that the ladder came back, and answering `PASS` for it would publish the absence of evidence as
evidence — §13.11.2's rule, and §13.262.4's cost when a field name was read as if it were a
population.

**Nothing stricter than the registration was added.** The registration asked for the consultations
column against the tally and for `0 ≤ changed ≤ attempted`; it did not ask for the changes column to
sum to `changed`. The tool prints that sum as an **observation** and keeps it out of the verdict,
because a check written after the number is exactly what this section exists to prevent.

### 13.263.3 Validated on both artifacts in hand, before the run it will judge

The two artifacts of §13.262 were read again through the tool. The first column is
`42013256884` read against itself, which has a known answer everywhere and is the only place a false
`FAIL` could hide.

| # | gate | `42013256884` against itself | `42054107910` against `42013256884` |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `MR` paired delta vs reference | +0.00 over 121 (0 won, 0 lost, p = 1) **PASS** | **−15.70** over 121 (4 won, 23 lost, p = 3.1e-4) **FAIL** |
| 2 | `MR` paired delta vs prior | +15.70 over 121 (23 won, 4 lost) **PASS** | control not supplied, **UNEVALUABLE** |
| 3 | four capabilities vs reference | all +0.00, worst +0.00 **PASS** | `IE` **−5.33** (1 won, 9 lost), `KU` +2.78, `TR` +0.00, `ABS` +0.00, worst −5.33 **FAIL** |
| 4 | `bareRetry.attempted` | 71 **PASS** | **0** **FAIL** |
| 5 | `llmUsage.calls` | 5,668 **PASS** | 5,966 **PASS** |
| 6 | `audit` identity | column absent, **UNEVALUABLE** | column absent, **UNEVALUABLE** |
| 7 | sides ≤ total | `usageBySide` absent, **UNEVALUABLE** | 10,606 and 9,852 against 5,966 **FAIL** |
| 8 | `promptDigest` vs reference | 500/500 **PASS** | **383/500** **FAIL** |

Every reading reproduces the number §13.262 recorded by hand — the 15.70, the `IE` 5.33, the 71/71
ladder, the 5,668 calls, the 3.43× the sides claimed — which is what makes the tool a reader of the
same measurements rather than a second opinion about them. Gates 6 and 7 answer `UNEVALUABLE` on the
older artifact for a reason that is itself the finding: `42054107910` predates the counted columns,
so no artifact of that shape could ever have demonstrated the identity it was judged by.

### 13.263.4 Gate 8's magnitude, which nothing had measured before

`383/500` is new. §13.262.5 established that the audit prompt was being written into `lastPromptText`
— delivery recorded what the audit sent rather than what answered — and repaired it by splitting
`#recordDelivery` from `#recordCoverage`. What was not established is **how many questions it
touched**. The digest comparison says 117 of 500, and the population matches: 118 multi-session
questions were audited, one of them received the same bytes anyway.

So gate 8 is not a coin flip dressed as a check. A run in which delivery is a function of the review
can fail it by 117 questions, and a repaired run either agrees on 500 or the split did not do what
§13.262.6 claims.

### 13.263.5 What the tool cannot do

It cannot run inside the run. Its controls are artifacts of *other* runs, which is why it lives beside
`readout-arm-run.py` rather than in a workflow step: `--audit` and `--registration` both decide
properties of one artifact against itself or against the dispatch table, and neither can see a
control. The verdict command is one line and eight rows, and it is run by whoever reads the artifact:

```
python3 tools/registered-gates.py tools/gates/13.262.7.json \
    --treatment <42130772725>/benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json \
    --reference <42013256884>/benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json \
    --prior     <42054107910>/benchmark-cortex-memory-ablation-report.json
```

It does not judge whether the registration was right. A gate that is evaluated correctly can still be
the wrong gate, and that argument belongs in §13.262.7 where it was made.

## 13.264 The residual is selection, seven to two, and the population that can move is thirty

§13.262.8 retired a deterministic tally over the reader's own list on the strength of three records:
`eeda8a6d` should have summed (`10 + 5 + 1 + 1`), `80ec1f4f` should have counted distinct venues, and
`6d550036` excluded every candidate and answered `0` against a gold of `2`. Three anecdotes is not a
distribution, and the next axis turns on which class dominates: a deterministic **aggregation**
executor can only repair answers whose item list is already right, while **event specification** is
what repairs a list that never held the event.

`tools/mr-residual-census.py` separates them on every record, from the artifact, with no model calls.

### 13.264.1 The classification, and why it is computed

A wrong answer is classified by comparing three integers the record already contains:

| class | test | what it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `contract` | the answer is not a number | the reply never committed to a count |
| `selection` | the answer **equals** the number of items it kept, and that number is not the gold | its arithmetic is faithful to its own list; the list is wrong |
| `aggregation` | the answer is not the number of items it kept | it applied an operation to its own list |

`selection` is split by sign, because `under` and `over` are different defects: `under` is an event
that is absent or was excluded, `over` is an item the predicate should have removed.

The parser reads **both** shapes of rejection, and that is the reason this exists in code. `6d550036`
lists six candidate projects and marks all six excluded inline, so a reader that only understood the
block form (`Excluded candidates:` then bullets) would count six kept items against an answer of `0`
and call it an `aggregation` error where the reader had made a **selection** decision. The tool's
answer would then depend on which shape a model happened to produce.

### 13.264.2 The reading, on the reference arm

`42013256884`, the shipped arm, `MR`, golds in `[2, 10]` — the window §13.92 corrected the campaign
to, where a gold is a set of items and not a balance:

| reading | count |
| --- | ---: |
| count-shaped golds in the window | **30** of 121 `MR` questions |
| correct | 21 |
| wrong | **9** |
| wrong, `selection/under` | **6** |
| wrong, `selection/over` | 1 |
| wrong, `aggregation/operation` | 2 |
| wrong, `contract` | 0 |
| wrong answers that rejected at least one candidate | **7 of 9** (29 rejections) |

Seven to two. The reader's arithmetic is faithful to its own list in seven of the nine failures, and
in seven of nine the list is wrong *because items were rejected*: `6d550036` rejected 6 of 6 and
answered `0` against a gold of `2`, `gpt4_15e38248` rejected 6 of 9 and answered `3` against `4`,
`4f54b7c9` rejected 4 of 6 and answered `2` against `5`.

The two `aggregation` rows are `bf659f65` (kept 3, answered `2`) and `c18a7dc8` (kept 0, answered
`10` against a gold of `7` — the record with no list at all, which the renderer flags rather than
classifies silently).

### 13.264.3 Three consequences, written before the mechanism exists

**The axis is event specification.** A deterministic operation over the reader's own list can reach at
most the 2 aggregation rows here, and §13.262.8 already measured that such an operation applied
wholesale would break **15** currently correct answers and fix **1**. The 7 selection rows are what a
ledger of events, with a schema for what counts as an item and what a legitimate exclusion is, is for.

**The population is thirty, and the ceiling has to be stated.** `MR` is 121 questions and only 30 of
them have a count-shaped gold; the other 91 ask for names, dates or lists. Repairing every one of the
30 moves `MR` by `21/121 = +17.4` points and the whole arm by `21/500 = +4.2`. Any expectation of a
double-digit overall gain from aggregation work is arithmetically impossible, which is the kind of
ceiling this campaign has had to write down before (§13.9's admission cap, §13.79's pool width).

**An audited run cannot be censused, and the tool says so.** On `42054107910` every wrong record
reports `kept 0`, because `rawOutput` holds the review's reply rather than the enumeration that came
before it. The census prints a warning and names the cause instead of publishing a distribution that
would read as six aggregation errors. Making an audited run censusable needs the first pass's item
list on the record — a field, and therefore a registration of its own — and it is not part of this
axis.

## 13.265 The corrected audit is neutral, and the arm disagrees with itself on three per cent

`42130772725` ran `adb08726` with the same 22 inputs as `42013256884` and only
`cortex_memory_review_pass` moved. It finished in 1h58m and the artifact carries the counted columns
§13.262 built. Six of the eight registered gates pass. The two that do not are the finding.

### 13.265.1 What the gates read

| # | `42054107910` (old prompt) | `42130772725` (repaired) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `MR` −15.70 (4 won, 23 lost) **FAIL** | `MR` **−0.83** (6 won, 7 lost, p = 1) **FAIL** |
| 2 | — | `MR` +14.88 against the prior (22 won, 4 lost, p = 5.3e-4) **PASS** |
| 3 | `IE` −5.33, worst −5.33 **FAIL** | `IE` +1.33, `KU` −4.17, `TR` +1.57, `ABS` +0.00, worst **−4.17** **FAIL** |
| 4 | 0 **FAIL** | **72** **PASS** |
| 5 | 5,966 **PASS** | 6,157 **PASS** |
| 6 | column absent **UNEVALUABLE** | 470 = 470, `0 ≤ 49 ≤ 470` **PASS** |
| 7 | 10,606 / 9,852 against 5,966 **FAIL** | 2,695 / 2,542 against 6,157 **PASS** |
| 8 | 383 / 500 **FAIL** | **500 / 500** **PASS** |

Gates 4–8 are instrument gates and they all pass: the ladder fires again, the attribution is exact for
the first time (the two sides now sum to 4,919 fewer than the total, which is the calls made outside
the two `answer` paths), the consultation column is an identity, and delivery no longer depends on the
review. Gate 2 says the form clause recovered 14.88 of the 15.70 that the old instruction destroyed.

Gates 1 and 3 are the mechanism's own verdict, and §13.265.2 to §13.265.4 are why neither of them is a
`FAIL` in the sense the registration meant.

### 13.265.2 The three `KU` losses were never audited

Gate 3's `KU` −4.17 is three questions, `0 won / 3 lost`. Every one of them carries
`auditConsultations = 0`:

| question | gold | control | treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `6a1eabeb` | `4 weeks` | `25:50` | `27:12` |
| `ce6d2d27` | `4 weeks` | `Friday` | `Thursday` |
| `7a87bd0c` | `4 weeks` | `4 weeks` | `3 weeks` |

The first two are wrong on both sides and wrong in different ways; the third is one week apart. None of
them consulted the review. **A capability's delta on a population the mechanism never touched is a
measurement of the arm's own disagreement**, and the gate that read it as a mechanism loss was
comparing a treatment against a control as if the control were the truth.

### 13.265.3 The noise floor, measured for the first time

`tools/arm-flip-census.py` counts the questions whose verdict differs between two artifacts and splits
the count by whether the mechanism acted on them. On this pair:

| side | n | flips | rate | 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| consulted (`auditConsultations > 0`) | 119 | 12 | **10.08%** | [5.86%, 16.80%] |
| never consulted | 381 | 12 | **3.15%** | [1.81%, 5.42%] |

Risk ratio **3.20×**, and the intervals do not overlap. The net on both sides is **+0**.

So the description of the review pass is precise: **it triples the probability that the answer changes
and does not change the probability that it is right.** The 49 changes were spread over 24 questions,
and only **two** of those 24 were rewritten in every one of the four repetitions — so for 22 of them
the decision to rewrite is itself unstable on identical input. A mechanism whose intervention is
unstable and whose net is zero is a source of variance and nothing else.

Three per cent is also the number every earlier reading in this campaign lacked. §13.262 attributed
−15.70 to the audit prompt and was right about the direction; §13.263's gate 3 then read −4.17 and had
no way to know that a third of the arm's questions move by themselves.

### 13.265.4 Resolution: gate 3 could not have failed on `KU`

`arm-flip-census` prints, beside each delta, the smallest net the observed discordance could have
called significant. The sweep is exact, not asymptotic:

| capability | net | discordant | resolution | 80% power net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | −1 | 13 | **9** | 10.1 |
| `IE` | +2 | 6 | 6 | 6.9 |
| `KU` | −3 | 3 | **none** | 4.8 |
| `TR` | +2 | 2 | none | 4.0 |

`KU`'s three pairs admit no resolvable net at all: 2-1 is p = 1 and 3-0 is p = 0.25. `MR`'s thirteen
pairs resolve a net of nine, and the observed net is one. **Both `FAIL`s sit below the resolution of
their own population**, which is a statement about the gate and not about the audit.

This is the third time this campaign has paid for a threshold written without its resolution (§13.9's
