admission cap, §13.79's pool width, §13.262.7's `469 / 118`). The rule registered from here on is not
that such gates are excused: it is that **a gate on a delta must state the resolution it needs, and a
population whose discordance cannot reach it is registered as unevaluable from the start** — decided
by the arithmetic above, before the run.

### 13.265.5 Decision: the review pass is not shipped

The registration's own refutation clause said that if gate 1 failed while the instrument gates passed,
the audit is worse than no audit. It failed, on a net four and a half times below the resolution, with
a 3.20× volatility cost and no mean gain. The configuration default stays `reviewPass: bare`.

What that leaves behind is a measured property rather than a hunch: a second-pass reagent applied to
a five-hundred-question arm buys **+0.00** and **+6.93 points of flip rate**. Any future pass — a
re-examination, a self-consistency vote, a verifier — is now held to that number.

### 13.265.6 Four ideas refuted before any code was written

The four cheapest repairs each cost nothing to test against the artifacts in hand, and all four are
wrong:

| idea | test | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stop excluding candidates | add every excluded item back, recompute | **fix 0, break 10** — 10 currently correct answers depend on an exclusion |
| the scorer is too literal | re-grade 26 wrong `MR` answers under a lenient contract | **0 of 26** are semantically right; no format penalty exists |
| enumerate more items | listed items / gold turns, correct vs wrong | **0.24 vs 0.29** — the ratio does not separate them |
| our prompt is stricter than the reference's | read the reference's builder | it asks for *"every item matching the question's EXACT action"*, and §13.123.3 already recorded that |

The second and third matter because both were the obvious next move: a formatting clause and an
"enumerate exhaustively" clause. Neither has a population to act on.

The fourth matters most. The reference pipeline beats this arm on `MR` by 16 questions to 9, and the
temptation is to attribute that to prompt shape — but the two arms have been compared under that
attribution twice already (§13.123.3, §13.240.4) and both times the attribution was the defect.

### 13.265.7 What the `MR` failures actually are

`tools/evidence-completeness.py` splits every wrong answer by whether the gold turns reached the
window at all. `goldOverlap` was already on the record; nothing had read it this way.

| capability | n | full evidence | accuracy | partial evidence | accuracy | headroom |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | 121 | 87 | 83.9% | 34 | **64.7%** | **+6.5** |
| `KU` | 72 | 5 | 100% | 67 | 86.6% | **+9.0** |
| `TR` | 127 | 90 | 97.8% | 37 | 86.5% | **+4.2** |
| `IE` | 150 | 75 | 94.7% | 75 | 96.0% | −1.0 |
| `ABS` | 30 | 2 | 100% | 28 | 100% | +0.0 |

**No wrong answer in the whole artifact had `carried = 0`.** The gold evidence is always at least
partly there, which retires "the retrieval found nothing" as a class. What exists is a population where
**one to five** gold turns are missing, and its error rate is two to three times the complete-evidence
error rate in three of five capabilities.

`MR`'s 26 failures split **12 partial / 14 full** on that line. The 12 are retrieval-shaped; the 14 are
reasoning-shaped, and they are the population §13.264 called selection. So §13.264's conclusion —
"the axis is event specification" — was half the answer, and the half it named is the smaller one.

### 13.265.8 The retrieval never offered the turn, in 133 of 241

`pool < total` is the sharper case: those gold turns were not merely ranked low, they were never
candidates, so no ordering inside the pool could have delivered them.

**133 of the 241 partial questions are in that sub-case.** At `relevanceTopK = 256` against a haystack
of roughly five hundred turns, a gold turn ranked below the cut does not exist for any downstream
mechanism. This is the largest single measured headroom in the campaign so far — `MR` +6.5, `KU` +9.0,
`TR` +4.2 — and it is not reachable by any prompt, any exclusion predicate, or any arithmetic.

It is reachable by one number.

## 13.266 Registration: the retrieval width, against `42013256884`

The hypothesis is narrow and it is the one §13.265.8 measured: **the pool cut removes gold turns, and
the pool cut is `relevanceTopK`.** The arm has run at 256 since §13.254; the haystack is five hundred
turns; 133 questions have a gold turn outside the pool.

The diagnostic is one variable. Everything else is `42013256884`'s configuration byte for byte,
including `reviewPass: bare` — the shipped default, now that §13.265.5 retired the audit.

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| control | `42013256884` — `relevanceTopK = 256`, `retrieval-anchored`, anchors 4/3/0.5, 48,000 prompt chars |
| treatment | the same inputs with `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k=512`, so the pool is the whole haystack |
| what changes in the artifact | `goldOverlap.pool` rises toward `total`; delivery digests move, because a wider pool is a different ranking |
| what does not change | the reader's budget, its contract, its model, and every other registered input |

Gates, written before the dispatch:

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `MR` accuracy against `42013256884` | **Δ ≥ 0** — with the resolution printed beside it, and a net below that resolution reported as neutral rather than as a win |
| 2 | every other capability against `42013256884` | no loss **≥ 3 points**, and only where the discordance can resolve three |
| 3 | `MR` questions reaching every gold turn | **≥ control + 20** — the leading indicator: a null accuracy result still says whether the mechanism fired |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | **≤ 6,400** — the reader's call count must not move with the pool |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 38,000,000** against the control's 31,076,815, i.e. **+22%** — the price a wider pool is allowed to cost, and no more |
| 6 | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` | **equals 512** — a run whose departure never took measures nothing and would pass every other gate |
| 7 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** — unchanged from §13.262.7, because a dispatch that loses the ladder is broken regardless of the pool |

Refutation, and this one is symmetric. If gate 3 passes and gates 1–2 do not, the pool was not the
constraint: reach rose and accuracy did not, which localises the defect in the ranking inside the pool
or in the reader, and retires width for good. If gate 3 fails, the pool never bound, `pool < total`
means something other than the cut, and `relevance-index.ts` is where to look. Both outcomes are
readings; neither is a null.

What is deliberately not gated: the direction of `TR` and `KU`. Their headroom is larger than `MR`'s
(+4.2, +9.0), but their partial populations are 37 and 67 questions with 90% and 86.6% already
correct, so a 3-point bar on them is below the resolution §13.265.4 measured. Gating them would repeat
gate 3's defect in the same registration that corrects it.

## 13.267 Registration: the restore counterfactual, before the harness exists

`evidence-completeness` splits a capability's failures by whether the gold evidence reached the
window. It cannot say whether the ones that did not are *recoverable*: a wrong answer with one gold
turn missing may be an answer that the missing turn would have fixed, or an answer the reader would
have got wrong anyway. §13.265.7 wrote "12 partial / 14 full" as if the first group were retrieval's,
and that inference is not in the data.

The published instrument for this is per-question and paired: reinstate the question's gold evidence in
the read-time context, rerun **the same reader**, and classify by what happens.

> "We introduce the restore counterfactual, a per-question paired intervention that reinstates the
> question's gold evidence in the read-time context and reruns the same reader. Combining the change
> in correctness with whether the evidence was retained after eviction classifies each
> oracle-answerable error as recoverable, irreversible, or residual."
> — *What Eviction Destroys* (arXiv 2609.08279)

### 13.267.1 The artifact already holds almost all of it

| field | what it gives the counterfactual |
| --- | --- |
| `turns[].text` | the evidence as the reader saw it, in order |
| `goldOverlap.goldDelivered[]` | which of those turns are gold, per turn |
| `goldOverlap.goldRanks[]` | where each gold turn ranked, or outside the pool |
| `featurePromptTexts` | the exact bytes the reader was sent |

What is missing is one path: appending the undelivered gold turns to the prompt and asking again. That
is a harness route, not a benchmark arm — the population is the partial-evidence failures plus a
matched control of partial-evidence successes, which is tens of calls rather than the six thousand a
full dispatch costs.

### 13.267.2 The three classes, and what each one licenses

| class | test | what a repair would be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recoverable` | wrong, and correct once the gold turn is restored | retrieval or window: the BFR step |
| `irreversible` | the turn was never in the pool (`pool < total`), so restoring it changes nothing about what the store held | storage and eviction policy |
| `residual` | still wrong with every gold turn in front of it | the reader, and nothing upstream of it |

The distinction is the one §13.264 could not make and §13.265.7 only approximated. It also separates
the two populations `pool < total` already identified: a gold turn that was ranked below the cut is
`recoverable` by a wider pool, and one that was never a candidate is not.

### 13.267.3 The gates, and one that is about the reading rather than the mechanism

Registered before the harness exists, because a counterfactual whose pass condition is written after
the replies arrive is a counterfactual shaped to its answer.

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | `MR` partial-evidence failures that become correct under restore | **≥ 4 of 12** — a third of the population, which is the smallest share worth a mechanism |
| 2 | `MR` partial-evidence **successes** that become wrong under restore | **≤ 1 of 12** — the control: restoring evidence must not be able to break an answer that was right |
| 3 | `residual` share among restored-correct errors | **reported, not gated** — arXiv 2609.08279 measures 0.67–0.73 irreversible at an 80k budget, and a share quoted without a regime is not comparable |
| 4 | restore prompts that exceed the control's `promptChars` by more than the restored turns | **0** — the intervention is the restored text and nothing else; a prompt that grew for another reason measured a different experiment |
| 5 | `llmUsage.calls` for the whole counterfactual | **≤ 120** — 24 questions × 4 repetitions plus the retry allowance, so the instrument stays inside the price of one dispatch's rounding error |

Gate 2 is the one that makes the instrument honest. A restore that *helps* everything would be a
prompt change in disguise — the restored text would be doing work beyond restoring — and the control
population exists to catch that. It is the same argument §13.265.6 made when the re-admission
counterfactual broke ten answers: an intervention that cannot fail is not being measured.

### 13.267.4 What this does not decide

It does not choose between BFR's completion loop and a wider pool. It measures how much of the
population either could reach, which is the input to that choice and not the choice itself. The
mechanism experiment that follows will be registered against these numbers.

### 13.267.5 Amendment, written before the harness was built: the record does not hold the text

§13.267.1 said the artifact holds almost all of what the counterfactual needs. It does not, and the gap
is exact.

| block | length on `42013256884` | what it indexes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turns` | 73 | the **delivered** turns, with their text |
| `windowComposition.turns` | 73 | the same 73 |
| `goldOverlap.goldDelivered` | **12** | the **gold** turns — `total`, not the delivered ones |
| `goldOverlap.goldRanks` | **12** | the same 12, by rank in the scored pool |

So on the first partial-evidence record, `e47becba` has `total = 12`, `pool = 8`, `carried = 4` and
**seventy-three delivered turns of which four are gold**. The eight gold turns that were not delivered
have no text anywhere on the record: `turns` holds what the reader saw, and the four of the eight that
were offered-but-dropped were dropped by the budget after being scored, so their text left with them.

That is the same class of defect as §13.265.7's, one level down. There, `pool < total` could not be
distinguished from `carried < total` by rank alone and the census said so. Here, **the counterfactual
cannot be run at all**, because restoring a turn requires knowing what it said.

The repair is one field, and it is cheap:

```
goldTurns: string[]   // the text of every gold turn, delivered or not, in goldRanks order
```

Twelve turns at the 400-character cut is under 5 KB per record and ~2.4 MB on a 500-question artifact,
which is a rounding error against the 23 MB the artifact already carries. Two consequences follow, and
both are registered:

**The next dispatch after §13.266 must carry the field before any restore experiment can run.** A run
that measured the counterfactual from today's artifact would have to re-derive the missing text from
the dataset, and a counterfactual whose intervention is reconstructed outside the artifact is a
different experiment from one whose intervention is on the record.

**`goldTurns` is a delivery-independent record, so it is a privacy surface.** The artifact already
carries `turns`, so the marginal exposure is limited to the gold turns that were *not* delivered —
which is to say, exposure grows exactly where the diagnostic is most needed. That trade is worth
stating rather than discovering later: the artifact is a research record, not a product surface, and
§13.267.3's gates do not reach it.

Until the field exists, §13.265.7's "12 partial / 14 full" stays an **inference** and not a
measurement, and the tracking report says so in those words.

### 13.267.6 The field now exists, and what it cost

`goldTurns` is on the record as of this commit. `goldOverlapOf` already received the gold turn texts —
it needed them for the `retrieved.includes(gold)` membership test that `carried` is counted from — so
the change is a projection and not a new measurement, which is also why it cannot disagree with
`goldDelivered`: both are the same list walked twice.

The fourteen existing `toEqual` assertions in `question-record.test.ts` were extended rather than
loosened. A test that had been changed to `objectContaining` would have let the field vanish again
without a failure, and the field is the whole of the restore counterfactual's input.

One new assertion is the one worth naming: a gold turn **that was not delivered** has its text on the
record, in `total` order alongside `goldDelivered` and `goldRanks`, so index `i` means the same gold
turn in all three. That is the property §13.267.5 was written for, and it is now pinned by a test
rather than by a paragraph.

## 13.268 Result: the width is free, the pool is not the constraint, and the audit was publishing a zero

`42161343457` (`c1f8fb85`, `relevance_top_k = 512`) landed and was read against `42013256884` on the
seven gates §13.266 registered before the dispatch.

| # | quantity | reading | verdict |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `MR` accuracy | 78.51% → 79.34% (+0.83 over 121; 7 won, 6 lost; p = 1) | **PASS** |
| 2 | every other capability | `ABS` 100.00 → 100.00 (0/0); `IE` 95.33 → 95.33 (2/2); `KU` 87.50 → 86.11 (2/3); `TR` 94.49 → 94.49 (3/3) — worst −1.39 against a bar of 3 | **PASS** |
| 3 | `MR` questions reaching every gold turn | 89/121 against 87/121 (**+2**; bar: ≥ +20) | **FAIL** |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | 5,671 (bar: ≤ 6,400) | **PASS** |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | 31,047,070 (bar: ≤ 38,000,000) | **PASS** |
| 6 | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` | 512 (registered: 512) | **PASS** |
| 7 | `bareRetry.attempted` | 68 (bar: ≥ 60) | **PASS** |

Six pass and gate 3 fails, which is the outcome §13.266 called "the pool never bound" — and the
sentence it wrote for that case, "`relevance-index.ts` is where to look", turns out to be wrong. The
pool bound, it was emptied, and the constraint moved rather than disappeared.

### 13.268.1 The gold was partitioned, and the partition moved instead of shrinking

`goldOverlap.goldRanks` and `goldDelivered` are indexed by the same gold turns, so each of the 7,516
gold turns on the 500 questions is in exactly one of three states per run. Counted on both artifacts:

| where the gold went | `42013256884` (k=256) | `42161343457` (k=512) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| reached the reader | 6,476 | 6,522 |
| the ranking never surfaced it (`rank = −1`) | **264** | **2** |
| the ranking surfaced it and the budget did not buy it | 732 | **992** |
| arrived from outside the pool, which is the §13.214 regime | 44 | 0 |

Widening the pool did exactly what §13.265.8 predicted, and the effect is almost total: the ranking
went from missing 264 gold turns to missing 2. **Every one of those 262 rescued turns was then cut by
the budget** — the cut count rose by 260, from 732 to 992, and the net arrival rose by 46.

This is the cleanest single-variable result the campaign has. The signal problem and the allocation
problem are not two descriptions of one defect: they are two defects, the first is now closed, and
closing it converted itself into the second at a one-to-one rate. Any future claim that "retrieval
cannot find the evidence" has to be measured against this run, where it can no longer be said.

It also retires §13.265.8. That section's "133 of 241 partial questions have a gold turn that never
entered the pool" was true at k=256 and is 2 at k=512. The 133 were the pool cut, exactly as
registered; the reason widening it did not raise accuracy is not that the reading was wrong but that
the budget stood directly behind it.

### 13.268.2 Width is free, which is a second finding and not a footnote

The treatment issued 5,671 calls against the control's 5,668, and **31,047,070 prompt tokens against
31,076,815** — 29,745 fewer, with twice the pool. The registered ceiling allowed +22%; the run spent
−0.1%.

The reason is the one §13.230.2 got wrong once and this artifact settles: the offer is not the
delivery. On a partial `MR` question the admitted offer is `evidenceChars = 64,665` and the delivered
evidence is `promptChars = 45,741`, inside a whole prompt of `deliveredPromptChars = 47,786` against a
48,000 cap. The pool can grow all it likes; the delivered bytes are fixed by the budget, and the
ranking only decides *which* bytes they are.

So the width axis is closed on cost as well as on effect: it cannot be blamed for tokens, and it did
not buy accuracy. It is nonetheless the right platform to leave the arm on for the next axis, because
it is the only configuration in which the ranking's own misses are 2 instead of 264 — a selection
experiment run at k=256 would be measuring the pool and calling it selection. That is a change of
default, and defaults are not changed by a failed gate, so §13.269 registers it rather than assuming
it.

### 13.268.3 The budget is not one turn short; it is 2.1 to 6 times short

`tools/evidence-depth.py` turns `goldRanks` into a coverage-versus-depth curve for depths the run did
not use, because the curve is a property of the selection and costs no call. On `42161343457`:

| route | delivered depth | chars/turn | coverage at that depth | room for 95% | room for 99% | multiple of 48,000 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| multi-session | 175 | 254 | 90.8% | 63,700 | 100,000 | **2.1×** |
| temporal | 182 | 250 | 88.0% | 70,500 | 104,900 | **2.2×** |
| knowledge-update | 62 | 717 | 78.3% | 143,400 | 239,500 | **5.0×** |
| flat | 61 | 723 | 84.7% | 152,600 | 290,000 | **6.0×** |
| abstention | 72 | 596 | 66.4% | 178,900 | 250,400 | **5.2×** |

The missing gold is not sitting just below the cut. At `multi-session` — the capability with the
largest headroom and the most partial failures — the last nine points of coverage are 2.1 times the
current budget away, and on `flat` they are six times away. A reordering that promotes the next few
turns cannot reach them, because there is no "next few": the curve is shallow past the cut by
construction.

Combined with §13.268.1 this closes the second axis too. Buying the budget would take prompt tokens
from 31.0M to somewhere between 65M and 190M. The registered ceiling for a diagnostic was +22%. There
is no version of this that is affordable, and no version of it that is measured.

### 13.268.4 What is left to measure, and why nothing else is worth measuring first

Two axes are now closed by measurement — the pool is empty of misses, the budget is 2.1× to 6× short
— and neither closure says anything about whether the gold would have helped. That question is the
one §13.267 registered the instrument for, and it is now the only question standing between this
campaign and a defensible next step:

- if restored gold converts wrong answers to right ones at a high rate, the axis is evidence
  **density** — packing more of the offer into 48,000 characters — and the budget stands still;
- if it converts at a low rate, the reader cannot use evidence it is given, and every axis that moves
  evidence is worthless until that is fixed.

The prior for the second is not zero. §13.265.6 measured a manipulation on this population that fixed
**0** and broke **10**, and `accFull = 90.6%` against `accPart = 66.7%` on `multi-session` is a
difference between two populations rather than a effect of adding a turn.

### 13.268.5 The arm audit failed the run, and it was right

`42161343457`'s benchmark job exited 1 on check 7b:

```text
FAIL  audit   reviewPass=bare, so neither a tally nor a per-question count may be published
              -- a zeroed census here would claim a mechanism that never ran
```

The artifact carried `audit: { attempted: 0, changed: 0 }` and `auditConsultations: 0` with
`auditChanges: 0` on all 500 records, under `memoryArmConfig.reviewPass: "bare"`. The check is correct
and the product was wrong.

The cause is one line of intent that the code did not honour. `CortexMemory.auditCensus()` returned
`{ attempted: 0, changed: 0 }` unconditionally, and both readers — `auditOf` for the run-level tally
and `traceCensus` for the per-question delta — faithfully recorded what it said. A test already
existed for this and asserted the zero, with the justification written into its comment:

> Zeroed rather than absent on the product side, because the product always carries the accessor; the
> artifact omits the field, and that omission is what says "this build has no audit".

**The artifact did not omit the field.** The test's fixture had no accessor at all, which is a shape
the product never has, so the assertion passed against a system nobody ships. That is the fifth
instance of the shape §13.181 named — a producer field with no reader — arriving this time as a test
whose fixture diverged from the product.

The repair makes absence a property of the mechanism, because the mechanism is the only thing that
knows: `auditCensus()` now returns `null` unless `reviewPass === 'audit'`. A configured pass that
declined every list still reports `{ attempted: 0, changed: 0 }`, because that is a measurement. Three
tests hold it:

- `review-pass.test.ts` — a bare build reports `null`, and the same file's decline case still reports
  a genuine zero;
- `audit-census.test.ts` — a system whose census answers `null` publishes neither the tally nor the
  per-question pair, which is the fixture shape the product actually has;
- the existing no-accessor test stands, now as the second of three distinct shapes rather than as the
  only one.

`traceCensus` also grew an explicit `reading === null` branch. It already took that path by way of a
`TypeError` caught by the fault handler, which is a behaviour nobody reading the function could see,
and "the product said it has no mechanism" is not a fault.

### 13.268.6 The gate table was data that nothing validated

The seven-gate readout died on `KeyError: 'max_loss_points'` before printing anything, because
`tools/gates/13.266.json` said `at_most_loss_points`. The implementation and its sibling table
`13.262.7.json` both say `max_loss_points`; one of the two files was wrong and the suite could not
tell, because the consistency test compares the `quantity` and `threshold` cells against the
document's table and those cells were right.

A registration is data, and a table whose only failure mode is a crash halfway through a readout has
not been validated — a typo that the kind *ignores* would have been worse, setting no bar and printing
a pass.

`registered-gates.py` now carries `GATE_SCHEMA`, beside `KINDS`: the required keys and the permitted
extra keys per kind, with `GATE_COMMON` for the printed cells and the documentation cells. A gate now
fails as a malformed table — exit 2, naming the key, before any artifact is loaded — and the suite
holds `GATE_SCHEMA` and `KINDS` to the same key set so a kind cannot be added without one. Six tests
cover it, including the exact spelling that broke this readout and the case of an unknown key, which
is the same defect arriving silently.

### 13.268.7 What this round did not do

The restore counterfactual did not run, and the reason is mechanical rather than a choice: `goldTurns`
landed in `3f6eeed1`, and `42161343457` was produced at `c1f8fb85`, before it. The artifact carries
`goldOverlap` with `carried`, `total`, `pool`, `goldRanks` and `goldDelivered`, and no text.

A first draft of the room calculation in §13.268.3 was computed against this artifact and reported
every partial question as reachable under a perfect selector, because `sum(len(t) for t in goldTurns)`
over an absent field is zero and the sum then compared only the overhead against the cap. The reading
was wrong in the one direction that matters — it said the budget was ample when the budget is the
binding constraint — and it was wrong for the fourth time in this campaign for the same reason.

`tools/gold-room.py` is that draft made into an instrument, and its first property is the refusal:
run against `42161343457` it exits 2 and names all five hundred records rather than printing a table.
Three more refusals are tested beside it — a gold list shorter than `total`, a record with no
`deliveredPromptChars − promptChars` pair to measure the overhead from, and an artifact with no
`maxPromptChars` to price against — because each of them, left to arithmetic, would have produced a
number that reads as a finding.

The arithmetic itself is `sum(len(gold turn)) + (deliveredPromptChars − promptChars)` against the
budget, where the second term is the overhead **measured on that same record** rather than estimated.
Both readings of the character cap are printed: `goldTurns` holds uncapped text while the delivery was
capped at `maxTurnChars`, so the uncapped sum over-states the cost and a question it calls fitting
certainly fits. The conservative column decides; the capped one is labelled a judgement.

## 13.269 Registration: the re-instrumentation run, at the shipped configuration

The next dispatch is not a hypothesis about accuracy. It exists to produce one artifact that the arm
audit accepts and that carries the field the next two instruments need, at the configuration the
product actually ships.

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| configuration | the registered default, unchanged: `reviewPass = bare`, `relevanceTopK = 256`, 48,000 prompt chars, anchors 4/3/0.5 |
| control | `42013256884`, which is the same configuration |
| what changes in the artifact | `audit` and the per-record audit pair are **absent**, and `goldOverlap.goldTurns` is present on every record with gold |
| what this is not | a test of any mechanism. No mechanism moves, so a delta here is the noise floor, and it is reported as one |

Gates, written before the dispatch:

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **all twelve checks pass**, including 7b — the run that this registration exists to make green |
| 2 | `MR` accuracy against `42013256884` | **Δ ≥ −3 points**, and the net reported beside its resolution. The bar is a null, not a win: nothing was supposed to move |
| 3 | every other capability against `42013256884` | no loss **≥ 3 points** |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | **≤ 5,900** against 5,668 — a shape change must not cost a call |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 32,000,000** against 31,076,815, i.e. **+3%** — an absent field and a present one are the whole of the difference |
| 6 | `goldOverlap.goldTurns` | **present with `length === total` on every record that names gold**, and absent on the records that do not. This is the field the room calculation and the restore counterfactual both read, and a zero-length list would make the first of them report every question reachable |
| 7 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

Refutation is asymmetric and both directions are readings. If gate 1 fails, the absence repair is
wrong and the shape has to be re-derived from the failing check rather than from the intent. If gates
2–5 fail, the shape change is not inert: an absent `audit` block is not supposed to cost anything, and
a run that loses accuracy to it has found a consumer of the field that nobody documented.

The two instruments this artifact unblocks, and the order they run in:

1. **the room calculation** — for each partial question, `sum(len(goldTurns)) + overhead` against
   `maxPromptChars`, where `overhead` is the measured `deliveredPromptChars − promptChars` on that
   same record rather than an estimate. It converts §13.268.3's curve into a count: how many of the
   partial questions could a perfect selector have completed inside 48,000 characters.
2. **the restore counterfactual** of §13.267 — the 12 partial failures plus 12 matched controls, the
   same reader, the gold turns appended verbatim, the outcome classified recoverable, irreversible or
   residual. Under 120 calls, which is one fiftieth of a dispatch.

## 13.270 The restore population, chosen before any answer exists

§13.267 registered the counterfactual and §13.267.5 found it blocked on one field. The field landed.
The remaining risk is not the classification -- that is arithmetic once the answers exist -- but the
**population**, because choosing it after seeing which questions convert is selection on the outcome
and no result it produced could be believed.

`tools/restore-population.py` produces the list from the artifact alone, before any call, and prints
the rule that produced it.

### 13.270.1 The rule, and the number that chose between two rules

Pairs are matched on `missing = total - carried`, the size of the intervention, because both sides of a
pair have to receive the same intervention for the control to price that intervention. `total` is
minimised inside the stratum rather than demanded, and ties break on `questionId` so two runs of the
tool produce one population.

The first version matched on `total` exactly. Against `42161343457` it produced **3 pairs and 7
unmatched failures**: gold counts on that run run from 10 to 30 while partial successes cluster at the
small end, so a rule that reads as conservative on paper discards seventy per cent of the population --
including the questions that failed hardest.

Matching on `missing` produces **8 pairs and 2 unmatched** on the same artifact:

| | count |
| --- | ---: |
| `MR` partial failures | 10 |
| `MR` partial successes | 22 |
| pairs | **8** |
| unmatched failures | 2 (`1a8a66a6` missing 6, `gpt4_ab202e7f` missing 5) |

Sixteen questions at two arms is **32 calls**, against the 120 §13.267 budgeted.

The yield is a design fact and not an outcome: it was read from the artifact's counts before any
restore ran, and no question's answer entered the choice. That is what makes it legitimate to prefer
one rule over another -- and it is written down because a rule changed after the answers existed would
not be.

### 13.270.2 What the population says before anything is spent

All ten `MR` partial failures on `42161343457` carry `all_offered: true` -- every gold turn reached the
ranking. That is §13.268.1 seen from the other side: at k=512 the ranking is no longer what removes
evidence, so a restore counterfactual run on this artifact measures **allocation and nothing else**.
Had the population contained questions whose gold never entered the pool, the same classification
would have conflated two mechanisms.

That is also why the tool records `all_offered` per record and prints it: the day the column stops
being all true, the population has changed meaning and the classification needs a fourth class.

### 13.270.3 What is deliberately not in this step

No prompt is assembled and no call is issued. Building the reinstated prompt is a separate step, and
keeping the selection reviewable on its own is the point: a list of sixteen question ids can be read
and disagreed with in a way a table of conversion rates cannot.

## 13.271 The residual is one gold turn, at rank 382, and the budget delivers 175

§13.268.3 priced the budget with a curve and §13.268.1 partitioned the gold. Neither says what a single
partial question is missing, and the answer decides which repair is even expressible.

On `42161343457`'s 32 partial `MR` questions, counted from `goldRanks` and `goldDelivered` alone:

| how many gold turns the question is missing | questions |
| --- | ---: |
| 1 | **21** |
| 2 | 5 |
| 3 | 3 |
| 4 | 1 |
| 5 | 1 |
| 6 | 1 |

And where those 55 missing turns sit in the ranking:

| | value |
| --- | ---: |
| median rank of a missing turn | **382** |
| median turns delivered on those questions | **175** |
| lowest rank among them | 275 |
| never surfaced (`rank = −1`) | **1** of 55 |

So the deficit is not diffuse. Two thirds of the partial questions are missing **exactly one** gold
turn, and that turn sits about **207 positions below the cut**. The ranking is not failing to find the
evidence -- it delivered between 17 and 29 of the 9 to 30 gold turns each question names. It is failing
to put **one** of them inside the depth the budget buys.

### 13.271.1 The number that constrains the counterfactual, and it is not the failure count

Of those 32 partial questions, **22 are answered correctly anyway** and 10 are not. So the base rate of
"a missing gold turn did not prevent a correct answer" on this population is **68.8%**.

That is the prior §13.267's instrument has to beat. A restore that fixed every one of the ten failures
would move `MR` from 79.34% to 87.60% -- **+8.26 points, 10 of 121**, which is just above the 9-question
resolution §13.268 reports. A restore that converts half moves it 4.1 points, which is below it. The
counterfactual is therefore correctly sized: it can distinguish "the evidence matters" from "it does
not" only if the conversion rate is high, and if the rate is low the answer is that the axis is dead
rather than underpowered.

### 13.271.2 Why a set-level objective is the only repair this shape admits

Put beside §13.268.3, this closes an argument that neither instrument makes alone:

* the gold for one question costs **tens of turns**, not hundreds -- a selector that knew which turns
  were gold would fit them inside 48,000 characters with room to spare, so the budget is not what
  makes the delivery impossible;
* but **no prefix** of the ranking reaches them, because the last one sits at rank 382 while the
  budget buys 175.

A prefix cannot be repaired by widening it (2.1x to 6.0x, §13.268.3) and cannot be repaired by
reordering it either, unless the reordering is allowed to **skip** -- an item-level objective that
takes the top `k` by relevance has no term that says "this question's need is not yet covered". That
is the shift arXiv 2610.09348 names, and the reason its FCA-based sufficient-subset step exists rather
than a better scorer.

Which is testable here without adopting anything: a set-level objective's ceiling on this population
is "does every question's gold fit", and `tools/gold-room.py` computes exactly that once `goldTurns`
is on the artifact. §13.269 is the run that puts it there.

## 13.272 Result: seven of seven, the audit is silent, and the room calculation names its own population

`42177443765` (`5492088d`, the registered default) landed and passed every gate §13.269 registered
before the dispatch:

| # | quantity | reading | verdict |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | every check passes | **PASS** |
| 2 | `MR` against `42013256884` | 78.51% → 80.17% (+1.65 over 121; 5 won, 3 lost; p = 0.73) | **PASS** |
| 3 | every other capability | `ABS` 0/0, `IE` 1/1, `KU` 0 won 1 lost (−1.39), `TR` 3 won 1 lost (+1.57) — worst −1.39 against a bar of 3 | **PASS** |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | 5,690 (bar: ≤ 5,900) | **PASS** |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | 31,103,964 (bar: ≤ 32,000,000) | **PASS** |
| 6 | `goldOverlap.goldTurns` | 500 of 500 records, **7,516 turns recorded** | **PASS** |
| 7 | `bareRetry.attempted` | 75 (bar: ≥ 60) | **PASS** |

The shape change is inert as registered. Total accuracy reads 90.80% (454/500) against the control's
90.20%, which is +0.6 points on a population where the resolution is nine questions; `MR` moved +1.65
with a discordance of 8, and p = 0.73 says the move is indistinguishable from the floor. The three
fields that were supposed to disappear did: `audit` is absent from the report, and **0 of 500 records**
carry `auditConsultations` or `auditChanges`.

`goldTurns` adds 7,516 turns and 5.5 MB to an 81 MB artifact -- 6.8%, against §13.267.5's estimate of
"under 5 KB per record and ~2.4 MB". The estimate was low by a factor of two and the reason is
ordinary: a gold turn renders at the full turn length, not at the 400-character render cap, and the
estimate used the cap.

### 13.272.1 The room calculation's first real reading, and the half of it that is empty

`tools/gold-room.py` on this artifact:

| capability | n | full | partial | had the choice | fits | room |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ABS` | 30 | 2 | 28 | 14 | **14** | 0 |
| `IE` | 150 | 75 | 75 | 49 | **49** | 0 |
| `KU` | 72 | 5 | 67 | 45 | **45** | 0 |
| `MR` | 121 | 87 | 34 | **0** | 0 | 0 |
| `TR` | 127 | 90 | 37 | **0** | 0 | 0 |

Two statements, and they are different:

**For `ABS`, `IE` and `KU` the answer is unambiguous: every partial question whose missing gold the
ranking actually surfaced would have fitted inside 48,000 characters, all 108 of them.** Zero are
limited by room. On those three capabilities the budget is not the constraint and never was; the
selector is, entirely.

**For `MR` and `TR` the column is zero because the population is zero, not because the answer is
no.** At `top_k = 256` not one partial question in either capability has all of its *missing* gold
inside the ranking -- which is §13.268.1's 264 never-surfaced turns seen per question. The room
question cannot be asked of a selector that was never offered the choice.

So the room axis is answered for three capabilities and blocked for the two that matter, and what
blocks it is exactly one variable: the pool width. §13.268.1 measured that widening it to 512 takes
never-surfaced from 264 to 2. §13.272.2 is why that run could not answer this question.

### 13.272.2 No artifact has both halves, and that is what fixes the next dispatch

The room calculation needs two things from two different runs:

| what it needs | which artifact has it |
| --- | --- |
| `goldTurns` on every record | `42177443765` -- the run at `5492088d`, `top_k = 256` |
| the missing gold inside the ranking | `42161343457` -- the run at `c1f8fb85`, `top_k = 512` |

Neither has both, and `42161343457` cannot be recomputed: it predates the field by one commit. So the
next dispatch is not a new hypothesis. It is `top_k = 512` at HEAD, and it exists to make one table
computable for `MR` and `TR`.

### 13.272.3 The instrument had the defect it was built to refuse, one level down

The first version of `gold-room.py` required **every** gold turn to be inside the pool before it would
call a question one where "the selector had the choice". On this artifact that produced the table
above's zeros, and the zeros are what exposed it: `MR` and `TR` reporting *no candidates at all* while
`ABS` reported 14 of 28.

The condition is wrong, and wrong in the direction that empties a population silently. The room
calculation asks what a selector could have done differently, and the only turns it could have treated
differently are the **missing** ones -- a gold turn that arrived is not a turn anybody chose against. A
question naming thirty gold turns essentially never has all thirty inside a 256-deep ranking, so the
strict condition was not a filter, it was a guarantee of zero.

§13.268.7 records the same failure one level up: an absent list summed to zero and every question
looked reachable. That was a refusal problem. This is a **scope** problem -- the tool refused correctly
and then asked the wrong question -- and it is the more dangerous of the two, because the output was
well formed, plausible, and empty only in the rows that mattered.

Three tests hold the corrected condition: a delivered gold outside the pool must not disqualify its
question, a missing gold outside the pool must, and a `goldDelivered` list whose length disagrees with
`total` is refused rather than truncated.

### 13.272.4 The restore population on the new artifact, with the characters in it

`tools/restore-population.py` on `42177443765`: **12 partial failures, 22 partial successes, 11 pairs,
1 unmatched.**

| | range over the 22 questions |
| --- | --- |
| characters the intervention adds | **158 - 1,195** |
| as a share of the 48,000-character budget | **0.33% - 2.49%** |

That is the number the restore counterfactual needed and could not have: reinstating a question's
missing gold costs at most 1,195 characters, which is 2.5% of the budget. There is no version of this
intervention that is expensive, and no version where the budget is what stops it.

Twelve failures against twenty-two successes restates §13.271.1 on a second run and does not confirm
it: that section read 22 of 32 (**68.8%**) on the k=512 artifact and this one reads 22 of 34
(**64.7%**), because the two runs have different partial populations. The instrument's prior is
therefore a band rather than a point -- roughly two thirds of partial-evidence `MR` questions are
answered correctly anyway -- and it is still the thing the counterfactual has to beat.

## 13.273 Registration: the width again, at HEAD, to make one table computable

This dispatch has no accuracy hypothesis. §13.272.1 answered the room question for `ABS`, `IE` and
`KU` and could not ask it of `MR` or `TR`, and §13.272.2 named why: the field and the width live in
different artifacts and one of the two cannot be recomputed.

So the run is `top_k = 512` at HEAD, and its gates are about the artifact rather than about the
mechanism. That distinction is the whole of the registration: none of these numbers is supposed to
move, and a run that moved one would have found something nobody registered.

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| configuration | §13.269's configuration with `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k = 512` |
| control | `42177443765` — the same tree, the same reader, the same budget, `top_k = 256` |
| what changes | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` and the ranking that follows from it |
| what this is not | a test that width buys accuracy. §13.268 closed that: +0.83 points against a resolution of 9 |

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **all twelve checks pass** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` | **equals 512** — a departure that did not take measures nothing |
| 3 | `goldOverlap.goldTurns` | **present with `length === total` on every record that names gold** |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | **≤ 5,900** against 5,690 — a wider pool must not cost a call |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 32,000,000** against 31,103,964, i.e. **+2.9%**. §13.268.2 measured −0.1% for the same change at `c1f8fb85`, so the bar is slack on purpose: it is set to catch a regime change, not to price this one |
| 6 | `MR` accuracy against `42177443765` | **Δ ≥ −3 points**, with the resolution printed. The bar is a null |
| 7 | every other capability against `42177443765` | no loss **≥ 3 points** |
| 8 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

What the run is for, stated so that a reader can hold it to this and nothing else:

- `gold-room` becomes answerable for `MR` and `TR`, which is the population §13.271 measured as missing
  one gold turn at median rank 382;
- `restore-population`'s pairs become pairs whose missing gold is inside the ranking, which is the
  condition §13.272.3 corrected the tool to require.

Refutation: if gate 1 or 3 fails the artifact is not a reading and the cause is in the writer, not the
arm. If gates 4–7 fail the wider pool costs something it did not cost at `c1f8fb85`, which would make
§13.268.2's "width is free" a reading about one tree rather than about the change.

### 13.273.1 Dispatch record

Dispatched against `1369fb8f` with one declared departure, `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k`, run
`42190193540`. The departure is the registration: `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` reads 512 on the
artifact and gate 2 fails if it does not, which is the check §13.262.7 introduced after a dispatch that
silently did not take.

## 13.274 Reading: seven of eight, the room is zero everywhere, and the residual is selection

The run landed. `42190193540` is `top_k = 512` at `1369fb8f`, and the reference is `42177443765` at
`5492088d` with `top_k = 256`.

### 13.274.1 The comparison is clean, and that is the first thing to establish

`git diff --stat 5492088d..1369fb8f` touches **six files, none of them under `packages/`** -- the
pre-registration, the two new tools, their tests and the gate table. Nothing in the pipeline moved
between the two runs, so this is the first width comparison in the campaign whose only difference is
the width. §13.268 compared two trees; this compares one.

| # | quantity | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | every check passes | **PASS** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceTopK` | 512, as registered | **PASS** |
| 3 | `goldOverlap.goldTurns` | 500 of 500 records, 7,516 turns | **PASS** |
| 4 | `llmUsage.calls` | 5,650 against a bar of 5,900 | **PASS** |
| 5 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | 31,010,483 against 31,103,964 — **−0.3%** | **PASS** |
| 6 | `MR` against `42177443765` | 80.17% → **76.03%**, **−4.13** over 121, 2 won 7 lost, p = 0.1797 | **FAIL** |
| 7 | every other capability | `ABS` ±0, `IE` ±0, `KU` +1.39, `TR` −0.79 — worst −0.79 | **PASS** |
| 8 | `bareRetry.attempted` | 67 against a bar of 60 | **PASS** |

Gate 6 was registered as a null with a three-point tolerance and the reading is 4.13. The gate did
what it was written to do: it refused to let "the width is free" stand on a run that moved the number
it was supposed to leave alone.

### 13.274.2 What the failure means, and what it does not

Five questions net, seven lost to two won, on a p of 0.18 -- inside the resolution the campaign has
measured for this dataset (§13.268.6: nine questions). So the honest reading is not "the width hurts".
It is that **the width has now been measured twice at fixed code and the two readings point in
opposite directions**: +0.83 at `c1f8fb85`'s comparison, −4.13 here, and the discordant pairs pooled
(7 won, 10 lost) give p ≈ 0.63. Neither is a signal.

That changes what the width *is*. It was registered in §13.273 as a run to make a table computable, and
that is precisely what it turned out to be: the cost is 0.3% of the prompt tokens and the accuracy
effect is noise in both directions, so what the run bought was not points. It bought §13.274.3.

The one claim that does change: "width is free" (§13.268.2) is a claim about **tokens**, and this gate
is the record that says so. Any future reading of that phrase as "free in accuracy" is refuted here.

### 13.274.3 The room table, complete: nothing fails for lack of room

`tools/gold-room.py` on the k=512 artifact. `offered` means the ranking surfaced every *missing* gold
turn, so a selector had the choice; `fits` means the gold plus the record's measured overhead is inside
48,000 characters.

| capability | n | full | partial | offered | fits | **room** |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ABS` | 30 | 2 | 28 | 27 | 25 | **2** |
| `IE` | 150 | 75 | 75 | 75 | 75 | **0** |
| `KU` | 72 | 5 | 67 | 67 | 67 | **0** |
| `MR` | 121 | 89 | **32** | **31** | **31** | **0** |
| `TR` | 127 | 93 | **34** | **34** | **34** | **0** |

The two rows that were blank in §13.272.2 are the two that mattered, and both come back **zero**:
every partial-`MR` question but one has its missing gold inside the 512-turn ranking, and every one of
those fits inside the budget. `TR` is unanimous -- 34 of 34 offered, 34 of 34 fit.

So the budget axis closes on **both** of its arguments, and they were different arguments:

- §13.268.3's coverage-versus-depth curve priced it in turns, and 99% coverage costs 2.1× to 6.0×
  the budget -- unpayable at 31M → 65–190M tokens;
- this table prices it in **characters**, and says the turns are already affordable; the budget is not
  what stopped them.

A failure that is neither out of room nor out of pool is a failure of **order**. That is now the only
mechanism the residual can be attributed to, and it is what makes the next experiment the next
experiment rather than a hypothesis.

The two `ABS` rows that do not fit are the abstention questions whose gold is the evidence that
nothing was said -- they are not the population any selector can repair, and they are reported rather
than counted as reachable.

### 13.274.4 The restore population on the wider pool

`tools/restore-population.py` on `42190193540`: **12 partial failures, 20 partial successes, 10 pairs,
2 unmatched.** Every row reports `offered = True` -- on this artifact the missing gold is inside the
ranking for both sides of every pair, which is the condition §13.272.3 corrected the tool to require
and the first time it has held.

The two unmatched failures are the largest interventions -- six and five missing turns -- and they are
not dropped: §13.267.5's plan carries them, unpaired.

## 13.275 Registration: the restore counterfactual, before the harness ran

§13.267 registered the instrument and its gates; this registers the **run**, with the population now
known and the harness now written. The gates below are §13.267.3's, restated with the numbers this
artifact supplies, plus three instrument gates that the harness made necessary.

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| population | `42190193540`'s 12 partial-`MR` failures and their 10 matched controls — **22 questions** |
| intervention | each question's missing gold turns, inserted above the `QUESTION:` line |
| injection point | the reader (`LLM`), decorated — the product is not modified and does not know |
| reader | `deepseek-chat`, thinking on `multi-session+temporal`, temperature 0 — the source run's identity |
| repetitions | 4 per question per side, the arm's scale |

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | failures correct under restore | **≥ 4 of 12** |
| 2 | controls wrong under restore | **≤ 1 of 10** |
| 3 | `residual` share among the failures | **reported, not gated** |
| 4 | prompts grown by other than the restored text | **0** |
| 5 | reader calls | **≤ 400** |
| 6 | `memoryArmConfig` fields that moved from the source run | **0** |
| 7 | planned questions never asked | **0** |
| 8 | calls that matched no planned question | **0** |

### 13.275.1 The amendment to gate 5, written before the run

§13.267.3 registered `≤ 120` calls as "24 questions × 4 repetitions plus the retry allowance". That
arithmetic assumes **one side**. The harness that was built runs the arm as it exists, and the arm's
pair is the feature against the reference pipeline in one `runAblationReport` call -- so 22 questions ×
4 repetitions × 2 sides is 176 answers before the judge, and 120 is not reachable by any faithful
implementation.

The number is therefore **400**, and the reason it is stated here rather than discovered later is that
a ceiling adjusted after the replies arrive is a ceiling chosen by them. The spare 224 is the judge's
share and the retry ladder's, and it is deliberately loose: this gate exists to catch a run that
restored into five hundred questions, not to ration a run of twenty-two.

The alternative -- teaching the arm to run one side -- was refused. The baseline side is waste here,
and it is waste that buys the thing the whole campaign insists on: one `runAblationReport` call, one
process, one clock, and an artifact whose two sides are the same measurement.

### 13.275.2 The two outcomes, and why both sides are a majority of four

`42190193540` answered every question four times, and `questions[].correct` is **one** of them -- on
that artifact it disagrees with the fourth pass on **14 questions**. So a population split on that
field is a population split on a draw.

Both sides are therefore read the same way, and the rule is written before the run: **a question is
correct when at least three of its four passes were**. The plan's `recordedOutcome` is the single-pass
field the population was drawn on; `tools/restore-classify.py` counts the disagreements between the two
and prints them rather than reconciling them, because a large count is a fact about the instrument that
the classification cannot repair.

### 13.275.3 Three instrument gates, and the two defects they were written after

Gates 6–8 are not about the mechanism. They exist because building the harness produced two defects of
the class this campaign keeps finding, and neither would have thrown:

1. **the workflow keyed the cache on a digest it never wrote.** `restore-counterfactual.yml` read
   `hashFiles('data/dataset.sha256')` and no step wrote that file, so the key resolved to the empty
   hash and the restore would have missed every entry the main benchmark wrote -- re-embedding 5,000
   turns while reporting a cache miss as an ordinary event. `tools/__tests__/test_embedding_cache_key.py`
   caught it before any dispatch, which is the second time that guard has paid for itself.
2. **the question line can be truncated.** `prompt.ts` truncates the `QUESTION: <question>` line when
   the evidence leaves it no room, and those are exactly the questions whose windows are full -- the
   population this instrument exists for. An equality-only match would have reported them unmatched,
   and gate 8 would have failed on the run rather than on the code. The matcher now accepts a unique
   prefix of at least 24 characters and refuses an ambiguous one instead of choosing.

Gate 6 is the third: the workflow writes the arm's configuration **out by hand** rather than
translating the source artifact's `memoryArmConfig` back into `CORTEX_MEMORY_*` variables. Generating
it would make the two runs agree by construction and would put a second, unreviewed definition of the
mapping in the tree. Writing it out means it can be wrong -- so it is **checked**, field for field,
before any number is classified. A duplicated value that is verified is a checkpoint; one that is
generated is a second source of truth.

### 13.275.4 Refutation

Gate 1 failing is the interesting outcome and not a disappointment: if four of twelve failures do not
convert with the missing evidence in front of them, the residual is the **reader**, and every remaining
retrieval axis in this campaign is dead -- which is worth knowing at the price of 176 answers. Gate 2
failing would mean restoring evidence breaks answers that were right, and would make the intervention
unsafe in a way no classification could repair. Gates 6–8 failing mean the run is not the experiment,
and the cause is in the harness.

## 13.276 Reading: eight of eight, and the ceiling the counterfactual puts on every retrieval axis

`42219514040` ran the counterfactual §13.275 registered: 22 questions from `42190193540` -- 12
partial-evidence `MR` failures and their 10 matched controls -- each re-asked four times with its
missing gold turns reinstated above the `QUESTION:` line.

### 13.276.1 The gates

| # | quantity | reading | threshold | verdict |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | failures correct under restore | **4 of 12** | ≥ 4 | **PASS** |
| 2 | controls wrong under restore | **1 of 10** | ≤ 1 | **PASS** |
| 3 | residual share among the failures | **0.67** | reported | — |
| 4 | prompts grown by other than the restored text | **0** | 0 | **PASS** |
| 5 | reader calls (decorated side) | **88** | ≤ 400 | **PASS** |
| 6 | `memoryArmConfig` fields that moved | **0** | 0 | **PASS** |
| 7 | planned questions never asked | **0** | 0 | **PASS** |
| 8 | calls matching no planned question | **0** | 0 | **PASS** |

Gate 1 passes on the nose and gate 2 on the nose. Gate 4 is the one that says the experiment is the
experiment: every prompt grew by exactly `calls × restoredChars`, so nothing but the intervention
touched the bytes the reader was sent. Gate 6 says the restore run reproduced `42190193540`'s
configuration field for field, which is the checkpoint the hand-written workflow needed.

Gate 5 reads 88 rather than 176 because the ledger decorates **one side**. The arm's baseline side ran
unadorned, as §13.275.1 said it would.

### 13.276.2 The two strata are softer than they were drawn, and by exactly two questions

The classifier reads both sides as a majority of four passes and reports where that disagrees with the
single-pass field the population was drawn on. It disagrees twice:

| question | plan's `recordedOutcome` | four-pass majority | what it means |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gpt4_2ba83207` | incorrect | **correct** | it was never a failure |
| `3a704032` | correct | **incorrect** | it was never a control |

So the conservative tabulation, which is the one the classifier's own rule implies, is:

| | as registered (`recordedOutcome`) | corrected by the four-pass majority |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| genuine failures | 12 | **11** |
| converted by restore | 4 | **3** |
| residual | 8 (0.67) | **8 (0.73)** |
| genuine controls | 10 | **9** |
| broken by restore | 1 | **0** |

Both are reported because they answer different questions: the registration asked whether four of the
twelve it drew would convert, and four did. The correction asks whether four of the *actual* failures
converted, and three did -- 27%, below the third the registration called "the smallest share worth a
mechanism".

The corrected control column is the better news and it is not a rescue: the one question the registered
gate counted as broken was already wrong in the source. **Restoring evidence broke nothing.**

### 13.276.3 The residual share is 0.67–0.73, which is the published number

*What Eviction Destroys* (arXiv 2609.08279) measures the irreversible share of oracle-answerable errors
at **0.67–0.73** on an 80k budget. This run measures **0.67 by the registered strata and 0.73 by the
corrected ones** -- on a different corpus, a different reader and a different budget.

That agreement is worth more than the point estimate: it says the instrument is measuring the thing
the literature measures, and it means the number is not an artifact of how this population was drawn.
Two thirds of partial-evidence failures are **not** repaired by the evidence they were missing.

### 13.276.4 The ceiling this puts on every retrieval axis

`MR` had 29 failures at `top_k = 512` (121 questions, 92 correct on the single pass). Twelve of them
had incomplete evidence; **seventeen had every gold turn delivered and were still wrong**.

| population | count | what could fix it | ceiling on `MR` |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| incomplete evidence, repaired by restore | **4** | selection | **+3.31 points** |
| incomplete evidence, not repaired | 8 | nothing upstream | 0 |
| complete evidence, still wrong | **17** | the reader, and only the reader | **+14.05 points** |

A perfect selector -- one that delivered every missing gold turn to every question that had one --
would recover at most the 12 partial questions, and this experiment says four of those actually
convert. **+4 questions is +3.31 points on `MR`.** The gap to the reference pipeline is 6 to 11.5
questions depending on which aggregate is read (§13.276.5).

So **selection cannot close the gap on its own**, and that is a quantitative statement rather than an
opinion: the mechanism that was the only remaining candidate on the retrieval side is worth at most a
third of the distance.

The 17 questions are the find. `MR` is not a retrieval problem at two thirds of its failures; it is a
reading problem, and the reference pipeline -- the same DeepSeek reader, the same 500 questions, the
same judge, a **smaller** window -- reads 85.33% to 85.95% on the same capability. Whatever it is doing
that this arm is not, it is doing it in the prompt.

### 13.276.5 The two aggregates, stated so that nobody has to guess which one a number came from

| run | `top_k` | cortex `MR`, ablation average | reference `MR`, ablation average | single-pass readings the gate table uses |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `42177443765` | 256 | **79.34%** (96.0/121) | 85.33% (103.25/121) | 80.17% → reference 84.30% |
| `42190193540` | 512 | **76.45%** (92.5/121) | 85.95% (104.0/121) | 76.03% |

The gate table compares `questions[].correct` -- one pass -- on both sides, which is what makes its
delta paired. The ablation averages are means over four passes and are the better estimate of the
capability, but they are not paired question-by-question and so are not what a McNemar test can use.
The campaign has quoted both; this table is the record of which is which, and the earlier "84.30%" is
the single-pass reading of the same capability that reads 85.33% by average.

The gap is therefore **5.99 points (7.25 questions) at `top_k = 256` and 9.50 points (11.5 questions)
at `top_k = 512`** by the averages, or -4.13 to -8.27 points by the single-pass readings. Neither
version is closable by selection alone.

### 13.276.6 Refutation, and what each outcome licensed

| outcome | reading | what it licensed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gate 1 fails | evidence does not convert | every retrieval axis dead; go to the reader |
| gate 1 passes, gate 2 fails | evidence converts and also breaks | the intervention is unsafe; the classification is unusable |
| both pass, conversion low | this | selection is worth ≤ +3.31 points; the reader is worth +14.05 |
| both pass, conversion high | not observed | set-level selection as the next mechanism |

What happened is the third row, and it is the informative one. The next experiment is not the
set-level selector -- it would be buying a third of the distance at the price of a mechanism -- it is
the prompt contract, and §13.246 already names what to compare: the reference's multi-session builder
enumerates under a fixed `item | verb | session date` schema, states the arithmetic in Step 2, and
terminates on an `Answer:` cue. This arm renders a different schema, a different Step 2 and no
terminator, on the same reader, and loses 6 to 9.5 points for it.

## 13.277 Registration: the contract, ported whole, as the next single-variable experiment

> **Superseded by §13.278 before dispatch.** This registration was written from §13.246's audit row,
> which described the arm as it stood before §13.248 adopted `ask=verbatim`. The contract it names is
> already this arm's, and the render recorded in §13.278.1 says so. The section is kept rather than
> deleted because the reasoning about *which* three properties matter is still the right reasoning --
> it was aimed at a prompt that no longer exists. §13.279 registers what replaced it.

§13.276.6 named where the gap is and what to compare. This registers the comparison.

### 13.277.1 The three differences, and why the whole contract rather than one of them

`acceptance.ts`'s S8 row already carries the audit: the reference pipeline's multi-session builder
enumerates under a fixed `item | verb | session date` schema, states the arithmetic of Step 2 in the
question's own terms, and terminates on `Answer: <final answer>`; this arm renders a different schema,
a different Step 2 and no terminator.

Porting one of the three would be a smaller experiment and a worse one. The three are not independent
knobs -- the schema is what makes the enumeration checkable, Step 2 is what turns a list into an
answer, and the terminator is what tells the reader the list is finished. A run that ported the
terminator alone would answer "does the terminator help" and leave the other two unmeasured, and this
campaign has spent enough runs on single knobs with sub-resolution effects.

So the treatment is the **whole instruction set**, and the registration is a single variable:
`memoryArmConfig.promptContract`.

### 13.277.2 What changes, and what deliberately does not

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| treatment | a new contract name that renders the multi-session route under the reference's instruction set |
| control | `42177443765` — same tree family, same reader, same budget, `promptContract = abstention-evidence-blocks`, `top_k = 256` |
| unchanged | reader, temperature, thinking routes, embedding, budget (48,000 / 400), ranking signal and width, all five gates of §10.3 |
| reach | **multi-session only.** Every other route renders exactly what it renders today, so `IE`, `KU`, `TR` and `ABS` are the internal control |

The reach is the design. If `MR` moves and the other four do not, the difference is the contract and
nothing else; if the other four move too, the contract leaked out of the route it was written for and
the run measures a different question than the one registered.

### 13.277.3 The gates

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **every check passes** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | **equals the new name** — a departure that did not take measures nothing |
| 3 | `MR` accuracy against `42177443765` | **Δ ≥ +3 points** with the resolution printed |
| 4 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` against `42177443765` | **no loss ≥ 3 points** — the internal control for the reach |
| 5 | `llmUsage.calls` | **≤ 5,900** against 5,690 |
| 6 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 34,000,000** against 31,103,964, **+9.3%**. The reference's instruction block is longer than this arm's, so the bar allows for it; a run above the bar is a contract that costs more than the instruction it adds |
| 7 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

Gate 3's bar is **+3**, well below the 9.5-point gap, and deliberately so: the gap is measured against a
pipeline that differs in more than the prompt (its window is composed differently and its session
grouping is its own), so the contract is only part of it. A run that moves `MR` by 3 or more has shown
the contract is load-bearing; how much of the gap it explains is then a second subtraction, not this
gate.

### 13.277.4 Refutation

- **`MR` does not move.** The contract is not the difference. The next candidate is the **window
  composition** -- what the reference puts in its smaller window and this arm does not -- and the
  experiment for that is a per-record diff of the two prompts on the same question, which costs no
  provider call at all.
- **`MR` moves and another capability moves too.** The contract leaked out of its route, and the run
  answers a question nobody registered. The cause is in the rendering switch, not in the contract.
- **`MR` moves by more than 9.5 points.** Then the arm beats the reference on its own contract, which
  would mean the reference's advantage was never the contract and the two are not comparable in the way
  §13.276.5 says. That is the outcome that would require re-deriving the whole comparison.

### 13.277.5 What this does not decide

It does not test multi-step retrieval (MemCog's family). §13.276.6 says so explicitly, and the reason is
mechanical rather than a priority: a second and third retrieval step changes the arm's structure -- it
needs an intermediate answer before the next query exists -- and folding it into this run would make one
artifact carry two treatments. It is the experiment after this one if this one lands.

## 13.278 The next experiment was registered against a prompt this arm no longer renders

§13.277 registers "the contract, ported whole". At HEAD that contract is already ported, and the
sentence naming it as missing is §13.246's audit row quoted without the adoption that superseded it.
This section records the contradiction, the render that settles it, and the four censuses the
archived artifacts could already answer -- run because the registration had to be checked before it
was dispatched rather than after.

### 13.278.1 The contradiction, and the render that decides it

§13.276.6 and §13.277.1 both say:

> this arm renders a different schema, a different Step 2 and no terminator

That was true when §13.246 wrote it. It stopped being true at §13.248.7, which **adopted**
`ask=verbatim`: the reference pipeline's `buildAggregationQaPrompt`, line for line, held to line
equality by `ask-verbatim.test.ts`, which renders the reference builder out of `cortex-eval` and
compares it against this package's constant.

The artifact says so in its own configuration. `42177443765` records:

```json
"ask": "verbatim", "askRoutes": ["multi-session", "flat", "temporal", "abstention"]
```

And a render at HEAD, with the control arm's options (`ask=verbatim`, `rendering=sourced`,
`maxChars=48000`), carries all three of the properties §13.277 registers as missing:

| property §13.277 registers as absent | marker in the rendered prompt | present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the fixed `item \| verb \| session date` schema | `<item> \| <exact action verb from the question>` | **yes** |
| Step 2's arithmetic in the question's own terms | `how many hours/days/weeks/months in total` | **yes** |
| the `Answer: <final answer>` terminator | the prompt's last non-empty line is `Answer:` | **yes** |

So dispatching §13.277 as written would have re-administered `41860773768` and cost a full dispatch
-- roughly **5,690 reader calls, 31.1M prompt tokens and 85 minutes** -- to re-measure a treatment
already measured at **+1.8 questions with the gap intact** (§13.248.4).

### 13.278.2 How the sentence survived four sections, and the rule it adds

The chain is short and worth writing down, because it is a new failure mode rather than a new
instance of an old one:

| section | what it did | what it left behind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| §13.246 | audited the difference between the two pipelines | a row stating the three properties are missing |
| §13.248 | migrated the block, measured +1.8, **adopted** it | the row is now historical |
| §13.276 | read the eight gates of the restore counterfactual | quoted §13.246's row in §13.276.6, unqualified |
| §13.277 | registered the next experiment from that quote | a treatment that no longer exists |

Every number in the chain is correct. Nothing was mismeasured, mis-transcribed or mis-attributed to
another run, which is what makes it different from the four "a real number attached to the wrong
run" defects §13.248.6 catalogued. It is a **stale premise**: a sentence that was true at the
revision it was written against and was never re-read after the section that answered it.

The rule this adds is one line, and it is a rule about reading rather than about writing: **an audit
row is a claim about a revision, and an adoption section supersedes it; a later section may quote an
audit row only with the adopting section's id in the same sentence.** §13.248.6 already forced
"one id per sentence" for numbers. This is the same discipline applied to *states*: the id that
matters is the one where the state last changed, not the one where it was first described.

The correction is cheap and it is applied here rather than in a rewrite: §13.277 is **superseded**,
not deleted, and `acceptance.ts`'s S8 row -- the artefact this section was reading -- carries a
sentence saying which section closed it. A row that quietly changed its mind would leave the next
reader to repeat exactly this.

### 13.278.3 What the archived artifacts can already answer, measured before spending anything

Four censuses over `42177443765` (`top_k=256`) and `42190193540` (`top_k=512`). All four cost zero
provider calls: they read `ablation.featurePromptTexts` -- the exact prompts sent -- and the
per-question records.

**(a) The residual is reading, not retrieval, and by a wider margin than §13.276.4 could see.**

| population (`MR`, `42190193540`) | count |
| --- | ---: |
| failures | 29 |
| ...whose gold value is a substring of the delivered prompt | **24** |
| ...whose gold value is absent from the prompt | 5 |

§13.276.4 said 17 of 29 failures had "every gold turn delivered", measured against the dataset's
gold-turn annotation. This says 24 of 29 have the *value itself* in the bytes the reader read, which
is a stronger statement about a larger population: on the failure set, delivery is not the problem
for four fifths of it.

**(b) The derivation-shaped questions are not the weak population.** §13.277 would have inherited
the assumption that they are, because the reference routes them to a different builder
(`buildDerivationQaPrompt`) and this arm does not:

| `MR` by question shape | `42177443765` | `42190193540` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| derivation (27 questions) | **24/27 = 88.89%** | 23/27 = 85.19% |
| enumeration (94 questions) | **73/94 = 77.66%** | 69/94 = 73.40% |

The `operands` block this arm adopted for derivation questions (§13.166, §13.193) is **11.2 points
better** than its enumeration block on the same run. Porting the reference's derivation builder is
therefore aiming at the arm's best-performing population: even a flawless port buys at most three
questions, and the evidence says there are none to buy. That experiment is retired before it was
registered.

**(c) The provenance prefix is 14% of the window, and it is not the mechanism.**

| quantity (`MR`) | median |
| --- | ---: |
| turns in the delivered prompt | 175 |
| session headers | 45 |
| characters spent on `N. [uuid] ` prefixes | 6,650 |
| prompt characters | 47,859 |
| provenance share of the prompt | **14.0%** |

Every turn carries a 36-character memory id because the sourced rendering does. At 175 turns that
is 6,650 characters -- about 25 turns' worth of room -- spent on provenance nothing in the reader's
answer uses. It is a real cost and it has never been registered as a variable, but the census says
it is not what the failures are made of: accuracy does not fall as the window fills (the four
turn-count quartiles read 0.63 / 0.80 / 0.73 / 0.87 on `42190193540`), and the per-turn 400-character
cap -- the other silent filter in the same rendering -- removes the gold value on exactly **one**
question of 121, which that question answered correctly anyway.

**(d) Width is not free on `MR`, and the paired test says so.** §13.268 read the 256 → 512 widening
as free on the aggregate (p = 0.18) and §13.276.5 recorded `MR` falling 79.34% → 76.45% without a
paired test. The artifacts carry one:

| comparison | `b+f-` | `b-f+` | exact McNemar |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR`, arm vs reference, `42177443765` (`k=256`) | 13 | 8 | p = 0.383 |
| `MR`, arm vs reference, `42190193540` (`k=512`) | **18** | **7** | **p = 0.043** |

And the direction is not only "the reference is better at 512". Seven questions flipped correct →
wrong against two the other way, and one of them (`1a8a66a6`) lost gold coverage while the pool was
being *widened*: 22/22 → 16/22. A wider candidate pool changed which turns the ranker delivered.
That is a ranking-stability question rather than a budget one, and it is the only paired-significant
effect this round found.

### 13.278.4 What that changes about the order of work

1. **The contract port is retired**, and §13.277 with it. It was measured in §13.248 and adopted.
2. **The derivation port is retired** before being registered: census (b) prices it at ≤ 3 questions
   aimed at the arm's strongest population.
3. **The turn cap and the provenance prefix are not the mechanism**: census (c) prices the cap at
   one question and shows no size-accuracy relation.
4. **Order is the one prompt-side difference left** that has never been measured, and it is now the
   only difference between this arm's multi-session prompt and the reference's that is not the
   evidence itself. §13.279 registers it.
5. **Ranking stability under pool width** is entered as the next candidate behind it, with census
   (d) as its evidence and `1a8a66a6` as its worked example.

## 13.279 Registration: the assembly order, against `42177443765`

§13.278.4 leaves one prompt-side difference unmeasured. This registers it.

### 13.279.1 The one difference, and why it is an order rather than a rewrite

§13.246 closed its migration with a paragraph naming what it deliberately did not port:

> The reference emits its instruction block *above* the context and ends the prompt with `Answer:`.
> This arm's assembly puts the instruction block last.

That sentence has been in the document since §13.246 and has never been a variable. The reference's
multi-session prompt is `[instruction][context][question][Answer:]`; this arm's is
`[evidence][note][question][instruction]`, whose last line is also `Answer:` -- the cue arrives at
the end in both, but in this arm it arrives after ~2,000 characters of instruction rather than
immediately after the question.

The treatment moves the block above the evidence and re-attaches the cue after the question. **The
two prompts' segments are the same strings**: `prompt-assembly.test.ts` splits both on `\n\n` and
asserts the multisets are equal at three budgets, so the treatment cannot have changed a word
without failing a test. A rewrite would have been a second variable; a permutation is not.

### 13.279.2 What changes, and what deliberately does not

| item | value |
| --- | --- |
| treatment | `promptContract = evidence-blocks-instruction-first` |
| what the contract names | the control's sourced rendering **plus** `assembly = instruction-first` |
| control | `42177443765` -- same tree family, same reader, `top_k=256`, `ask=verbatim`, `maxChars=48,000` |
| unchanged | reader, temperature, thinking routes, embedding, budget, ranking signal and width, the derived builder on derivation questions, all five gates of §10.3 |
| reach | **multi-session only.** `buildSessionPrompt` is the only builder that takes `PromptOptions.assembly`; `buildPrompt` does not carry the option, so `IE`, `KU`, `TR` and `ABS` are the internal control |

### 13.279.3 The gates

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **every check passes** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | **`evidence-blocks-instruction-first`** |
| 3 | `memoryArmConfig.promptAssembly` | **`instruction-first`** |
| 4 | `memoryArmConfig.assemblyRoutes` | **`["multi-session"]`** |
| 5 | `MR` accuracy against `42177443765` | **Δ ≥ +3 points** with the resolution printed |
| 6 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` against `42177443765` | **no loss ≥ 3 points** |
| 7 | `promptDigest` on the 379 non-MR questions | **identical to the control's, 379 of 379** |
| 8 | `llmUsage.calls` | **≤ 5,900** against 5,690 |
