| 9 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 32,000,000** against 31,103,964, **+2.9%** |
| 10 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

Rows 2 to 4 are one gate in the reasoning and three in the table, because the treatment is an order
and an order leaves **no trace** in the prompt's length, its segment set or its token count: a run
that named the contract and whose builder ignored it would produce a prompt with the same characters
as the control and every other config field agreeing. The name is the only field that can say the
run asked; `assemblyRoutes` is the only field that can say the asking arrived.

Gate 7 is the strongest statement of the reach the campaign has yet had in a gate table: a digest
equality on every question outside the changed route says the treatment did not leak, without
reading a single answer. It is decided by `registered-gates.py`'s `digest_agreement` kind, which
gained the `excluding` key for this registration -- the kind could previously only ask "did any
prompt move", which is what a treatment is for on its own route. Gate 9's bar is tighter than
§13.277's because a permutation has no reason to cost tokens at all -- the block is the same text,
and the cue moves 2,000 characters closer to the question rather than further away. A run above
+2.9% would mean the assembly is not the permutation the test asserts it is.

The table above is the prose; `tools/gates/13.279.json` is the machine-readable copy the readout is
decided from, and the two are numbered identically **and agree cell for cell** -- a test reads this
document and asserts it, so neither can be edited alone. What the spec does not carry is the reason
a bar sits where it does; that is this section's prose, and §13.279.6 records why the split is
enforced rather than merely intended.

### 13.279.4 Refutation

- **`MR` moves by less than 3.** Order is not the difference either, and the remaining prompt-side
  differences are exhausted: the block, its rendering and its position are all the reference's. The
  next candidate is then 13.278.4's item 5 -- ranking stability under pool width -- and the
  experiment is the same question diffed across the two pool widths, which costs no call.
- **`MR` moves and gates 4 or 5 fail.** The order leaked out of its route. The cause is in the
  resolution path (`ASSEMBLY_BY_CONTRACT` through `#promptOptions`), not in the assembly.
- **Gate 7 fails.** The treatment is not a permutation in the assembled prompt even though it is in
  the builder, which would mean the budget path re-spends room differently under the new order. That
  is a defect in this increment and it would be repaired before the result is read.
- **`MR` moves by more than 9.5 points.** The arm beats the reference on the reference's own order,
  which would mean the reference's advantage was its evidence after all and the comparison in
  §13.276.5 has to be re-derived for a third time.

### 13.279.5 What this does not decide

It does not test multi-step retrieval (MemCog's family) and does not test a second reader. §13.277.5
said the same, and the reason has not changed: both change the arm's structure rather than a field,
and one artifact may carry one treatment.

### 13.279.6 The dry run, and the two defects the machine copy had

The readout is decided from `tools/gates/13.279.json`, so the copy was dry-run before the artifact
exists. It failed twice, and both failures were in the instrument rather than the registration.

**The table reader could not see this table.** `RegistrationAgreementTest._rows`, which binds a
spec to its section, ended the section at the *first* following heading of any level. Every
registration in this campaign states its gates under `### x.y.3 The gates`, so the span was the
preamble and the table parsed to zero rows. It surfaced as `KeyError: 1` -- the correct, loud
failure -- but the reason it had never surfaced before is worth stating: the reader was written
against `13.266`, whose table sits directly under its `##` heading, and it had never been asked to
read the house shape. The fix is the span rule, not a special case: subsections whose title starts
with the registration's own number belong to it, and the span ends at the first heading that does
not. Every registered spec was re-read under the new rule and every one of them parses (13.262.7
eight rows, 13.266 seven, 13.269 seven, 13.273 eight, 13.275 eight, 13.277 seven, 13.279 ten).

**Six thresholds were two copies, not one.** The spec's `threshold` cells carried the bar *and* the
reason it was set there (`**Δ ≥ +3 points**, with the resolution printed. The bar is well below the
9.5-point gap on purpose...`), while the document's cell carried the bar alone. That is exactly the
divergence the cell-for-cell test exists to refuse: two texts that agree today and are edited
separately tomorrow. The bars now live in the spec's `threshold` and the reasons stay in this
section's prose, which is where they already were -- the spec is the number, the section is the
argument.

**The dry run also priced the denominator.** Feeding `42177443765` as both sides makes gate 7 read
`379/379 agree`: 500 questions, 121 of them `MR`, and the exclusion removes exactly the 121. So the
registered `379` is not an estimate -- it is what the reader computes from the exclusion, and a
treatment artifact that lost any of the remaining questions would fail on the denominator rather
than pass on a smaller population. The same run reads gates 2, 5 as **FAIL** (the reference's own
contract is the old name, and its `MR` does not improve on itself) and 3, 4 as **UNEVALUABLE**
(`promptAssembly` and `assemblyRoutes` are absent from the reference artifact, which is the point of
adding them). Six of ten gates decided against an artifact that is not the treatment, with the four
undecided ones being the four that name fields the treatment introduces: the table does not pass by
default.

## 13.280 The delivered set is not stable under pool width, and `MR` loses exactly there

§13.278.3 (d) found the width's paired cost on `MR` (7 down / 2 up, exact McNemar p = 0.039) and one
worked example where gold coverage *fell* while the pool was being widened. This section measures
that population over all 500 questions and asks the code what could produce it. No provider call.

### 13.280.1 The census: 63 questions delivered a different gold set under a one-parameter change

`42177443765` (`top_k=256`) and `42190193540` (`top_k=512`) differ in one dispatch input. Same
budget, same ranking signal, same reader, same corpus.

| | count |
| --- | ---: |
| questions whose `goldOverlap.carried` differs between the two runs | **63** (12.6%) |
| ...coverage **fell** | 28 |
| ...coverage **rose** | 35 |
| fell, and flipped correct -> wrong | **5** |
| fell, and flipped wrong -> correct | 0 |
| rose, and flipped wrong -> correct | 1 |
| rose, and flipped correct -> wrong | 0 |

The asymmetry is the finding. Losing coverage cost five questions and bought none; gaining coverage
bought one and cost none. A wider candidate list is supposed to be a superset operation, and on this
arm it is not.

### 13.280.2 It is not a difficulty artefact: the gap survives stratification

Movers are enriched for `MR` and `TR`, which are also the harder capabilities, so the aggregate
difference is confounded. Within capability:

| capability | delivered set moved | delivered set stable |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | **15/25 = 60.0%** | 77/96 = 80.2% |
| `TR` | 28/31 = 90.3% | 93/96 = 96.9% |
| `IE` | 5/5 = 100.0% | 138/145 = 95.2% |
| `KU` | 1/2 | 62/70 = 88.6% |

And it is not a size effect: the movers' median gold set is **12** turns and their median prompt is
**47,049** characters, against the stable population's **12** and **46,813**.

On `MR` the difference is **20.2 points**: a question whose delivered evidence changed under a
pool-only edit is four times likelier to be wrong than one whose did not.

### 13.280.3 What in the code can do that

The registered ranking is `retrieval-anchored`, and its pool is not the retriever's list. It is
`retrieved ∪ restored`, where restored turns are the session neighbourhoods of up to four **anchors**
whose choice scans the whole retrieved list:

```ts
function selectAnchors(question, hits, count = ANCHOR_COUNT): number[] {
  ...
  for (let position = 0; position < hits.length; position += 1) {   // <- the pool's length
```

A candidate that covers two question terms the chosen anchors have not yet named beats one that
covers one, whatever their ranks. So a hit beyond position 256 that covers more of the question can
take an anchor slot that a narrower pool gave to a different hit — and the neighbourhood restored
around the first is not restored around the second.

**What it takes for that to reach the delivered window.** Three properties of this arm, each of which
a fixture can omit and then report the opposite conclusion:

| property | why the head cannot move without it |
| --- | --- |
| scores are reciprocal-rank (`1/(60+rank)`, the arm's fusion output) | a restored turn scores `0.5 x anchor`; on a cosine-like band (`1 - rank/1000`) that is below every hit, so restoration can only reach the tail |
| the corpus is far larger than the pool, so a neighbourhood usually holds unscored turns | on a dense pool every neighbour is already a hit, `scores.has(text)` skips it, and restoration adds nothing |
| one candidate past the narrow cut covers **two** question terms | a candidate that merely *adds* an anchor cannot move the head; the head moves when it **displaces** one |

With all three, at window 73 out of a 256-wide pool: anchors `[alpha beta top, gamma here, delta
here]` narrow and `[alpha beta top, gamma delta together]` wide, restored turns 15 vs 9, and the
delivered window loses **4** turns and gains **4** -- the `d = 1` neighbours of the two displaced
anchors go, and four mid-rank hits take their places. That is the shape §13.280.1 measured on the
artifacts (one sampled question: 2 narrow-only, 4 wide-only, 73 vs 75 delivered), reproduced on a
fixture with no provider and no corpus.

The third property is the correction this note makes to the mechanism as first stated: §13.280.3
demonstrated that the anchor *set* changes, which is necessary and not sufficient. What moves the
delivered set is that the walk's `fresh`-count-first rule lets a worse-ranked hit **take a slot from
a better-ranked one**, and the displaced anchor's neighbourhood is what leaves the window.

The consequence is a statement about the mechanism rather than about this run: **under
`retrieval-anchored`, `topK` is not a width parameter. It is a parameter of the mechanism.** Two runs
that differ only in `topK` differ in the anchor set, the restored set, and therefore the pool.

### 13.280.4 What that does to the archived readings, including one this campaign has been quoting

Every topK comparison on this arm was made under this signal, `41990597116` and `42013256884`
included. Each of them moved the width *and* the anchor set, which is two variables where the
registration named one. The readings are not wrong — they are readings of "this mechanism instance
versus that one" — but they cannot be cited as "wider is free" or "wider costs four points", and
§13.268's dismissal and §13.278.3 (d)'s cost both need that sentence beside them.

### 13.280.5 The invariant, and why it is the next experiment behind §13.279

The property a pool owes its caller is **monotonicity**: widening the candidate list may add
evidence and may never remove any. It is checkable without a provider and without a run — build the
pool at two widths over one corpus and assert containment — and it fails today by construction,
because the anchor walk reads `hits.length`.

Two repairs are expressible, and they are different experiments rather than one:

1. **Pin the anchor head.** Choose anchors from a fixed prefix (`min(hits.length, 256)`), so the
   anchor set is a function of the question and the retrieval, not of the pool's width. Restoration
   then becomes monotone by construction and the width becomes a width again. What that buys and
   what it does not: the anchors and every restored turn become identical, and the two pools then
   differ only by hits ranked below every hit of the narrow pool. Those can still **outrank the
   deepest restored turns** (`0.5 x anchor` from a deep anchor is below the pool's floor), so the
   invariant is exact for any budget whose cut lies above the narrow pool's last hit -- which
   includes the registered one (73 delivered of a 256-wide pool) -- and approximate below it. The
   repair owes a test at the registered shape, not a claim about every budget.
2. **Union the pools.** Build the pool at the registered width and at the widest supported one and
   take the union. Monotone by construction as well, at the cost of a second retrieval pass -- and
   not the same experiment: a union keeps the wider pool's extra anchors *in addition*, so it
   delivers the displaced anchor's neighbourhood rather than the displacing one's. On the fixture
   that is 15 restored turns instead of 9, which is more evidence and a different prompt.

The two are not equally cheap and they do not point the same way: (1) is free and buys the invariant
at the registered shape, while (2) spends a second retrieval pass to *keep* the evidence that (1)
gives up. What the fixture cannot say is which is better on `MR`, and that is the only thing worth
spending a run on.

Both were registered here as *candidates*. Repair one turned out not to need a run at all: it is a
defect fix whose acceptance criterion is an equality the archived artifacts already establish, and
§13.280.6 lands it with a proof and the test the entry above asks for. Repair two stays an
experiment, and it stays behind §13.279 -- which is still in flight, and a second treatment in the
same artifact would make its `MR` delta unattributable.

### 13.280.6 Repair one is a defect fix with a proof, and it costs no run

The paragraph above registered both repairs as candidates awaiting §13.279. Working out what repair
one *costs* to verify shows that it is not an experiment at all, and that its two controls are
already in hand.

**The proof is an inequality the artifacts already satisfy.** With the anchor walk bounded by a
constant, the anchors and every restored turn are identical at both widths. The two pools then differ
only by hits ranked below every hit of the narrow pool. A delivered window is a prefix of the pool's
order, so provided its length is at most the narrow pool's width, nothing in it can come from the
added region and nothing in it can leave. The lengths are in the two artifacts:

| | `42177443765` (`top_k = 256`) | `42190193540` (`top_k = 512`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| delivered turns, median | 129 | 129 |
| delivered turns, **max** | **232** | **238** |
| questions delivering more than 256 | **0** | **0** |

So for all 500 questions the window is narrower than the narrow pool, and nothing the anchor walk
chooses can be pushed out of it by a wider pool. That is why repair one needs no dispatch: its
acceptance criterion is an **equality**, not a level -- on the pool. §13.280.8 restricts what the
equality covers: delivery draws turns the ranking never scored on 243 of 500 questions, and that
dependence on width survives this repair.

**The defect is sharper than "the set reorders".** The invariance test was written before the fix and
five of its six assertions failed; the one that matters most is containment. Pre-fix, the wide pool
did **not** contain the narrow pool: the displaced anchor's restored turns were simply gone. Widening
the candidate list could *remove* evidence, which is the monotonicity violation in its strongest
form, and it is the sentence §13.275's restore counterfactual and §13.254.5's "widening by
construction" both assumed away.

**What landing it changes, and what it does not.** `selectAnchors` gains `ANCHOR_SCAN_TURNS = 256`,
which is where `min(hits.length, 256)` lands at the registered width, and `terms` is still built for
the whole pool because the comparator reads only chosen anchors. At `top_k = 256` the bound is a
no-op by definition, so no archived artifact's reading moves and §13.279's in-flight treatment is
untouched. At `top_k = 512` the run that would have been dispatched to test the repair is replaced by
`anchor-width-invariance.test.ts`, whose fixture keeps the three properties that make the defect
visible -- reciprocal-rank scores, a corpus far larger than the pool, and a displacing candidate that
names two question terms -- and which fails against the old code for exactly the reason §13.280.3
gives.

Repair two is still an experiment, and its question is now different from repair one's: not "should
the pool be stable" (it must be, and it is) but "should the neighbourhood the wider pool found be
kept or dropped". That one costs a second retrieval pass and buys 6 restored turns on the fixture,
and it stays behind §13.279.

### 13.280.7 The prediction this makes, so the repair can be refuted

A repair that removes a cause makes a statement about every reading that cause produced. Three are
on record and all three are falsifiable without a new treatment, by the next run at `top_k = 512`:

| reading under the old bound | what the repair predicts at `top_k = 512` |
| --- | --- |
| `MR` ablation average 79.34% at 256, **76.45%** at 512 (§13.276.5) | within noise of the 256 figure: the width cost was the anchor walk, and the walk no longer reads the width |
| paired `MR` 7 down / 2 up across the widths, exact McNemar **p = 0.039** (§13.278.3 d) | sign test no longer rejects: the discordant pairs were the displaced anchors |
| 63 of 500 questions delivering a different gold set, 28 down / 35 up (§13.280.1) | **31 to 0** among the 257 questions that delivered no unscored turn; the other 243 are out of scope for this repair (§13.280.8) |

The third is an equality on the population the repair covers. §13.280.8 restricts it: the repair makes the
*pool* width-invariant, and 243 of the 500 questions deliver turns the pool never scored, which is a second
width dependence this increment does not touch. The first two carry the
noise floor this campaign has measured twice (**3.2%** on byte-identical dispatches, **3.49%** on
the round-ten pair), so a 512 run that lands within about three points of 79.3% is consistent with
the prediction and a run that reproduces 76.45% refutes it.

None of this needs a dispatch of its own. It is what the next 512 run means, whichever experiment
that run is.

## 13.281 The room is exhausted, so the anchor-budget question is a substitution question

> **Read with §13.283.** Every number below is taken at the `sourced` rendering, where 13.83% of a
> multi-session prompt is source id. §13.283 withholds it and predicts ~24 more turns per `MR` question
> for the same room, so the arithmetic here describes the room *before* that change. The conclusion --
> that a larger anchor budget substitutes rather than adds -- survives only if gate 8 of that
> registration fails to move coverage; if it moves, this section is the pre-treatment reading rather
> than the current one.

SOTA-LANDSCAPE §12 ends with "raise `ANCHOR_COUNT` toward 60 and price the room first". Pricing it is a
read of an artifact, and the answer closes the experiment as it was stated.

| | `42177443765`, 500 questions |
| --- | ---: |
| `deliveredPromptChars`, minimum | 38,292 |
| **median** | **47,761** |
| p90 | 47,953 |
| **maximum** | **47,999** |
| `maxPromptChars` | **48,000** |

Half the questions sit **239 characters** below the cap -- about half of one turn at `maxTurnChars =
400` -- and the largest is one character under it. The prompt is not nearly full on the questions
where room would help; it is full, which is the same finding §13.274.3 reached from the other
direction ("nothing fails for lack of room" was about gold availability, and this is about the
budget that would carry it).

So a larger anchor budget cannot add evidence. Every restored turn that enters the window does so by
outranking a hit that was already there, and `0.5 x anchor` puts it mid-pack rather than at the tail
-- it evicts a mid-ranked *retrieved* turn, not the weakest one. The experiment is therefore not "does
more restoration help" but **"is a restored neighbour better evidence than the retrieved turn it
displaces"**, and it has a shape that can be checked before it is dispatched:

- delivered turn count should stay where it is (median 129) and `deliveredPromptChars` should stay at
  the cap -- if either moves, the run did not test substitution;
- `windowComposition.offered` should rise toward `windowComposition.turns`, because the turns that
  enter are restored and a restored turn is by construction in the pool -- it reads 73 of 73 on the
  sampled question above, so the field is already near its ceiling and the prediction is that it
  stays there while the *composition* underneath it changes;
- the displaced turns are identifiable: they are the hits whose text is in `42177443765`'s delivered
  set and not in the treatment's, and their retrieval rank is known from the treatment's own pool.

That last line is why this cannot be answered by the width experiment or by anything else in flight:
it needs a treatment artifact, and it needs the ordering question stated first. It also re-prices
CoD's 60 anchors: their configuration carries an evidence budget of about 200 delivered turns and
restores up to 240 candidates into it, which is the same substitution at a larger scale, not a
larger prompt.

What this does **not** say is that the anchor budget is right at 4. It says the budget is not the
binding constraint on evidence *quantity*, and that the honest version of the comparison is about
rank -- which is the same axis §13.280.6 just repaired.

### 13.280.8 The pin's equality is a pool equality, and the delivery has a second width dependence

§13.280.6 said the delivered prompt becomes byte-identical across widths, and §13.280.7 put "0 of
500" in a prediction table. Both were too strong, and the artifact says so in a field the argument had
not read: `windowComposition.offered`, the count of delivered turns the ranking scored.

| reading | 256 | 512 | cross-run |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| questions delivering at least one turn the ranking never scored | **243 / 500** | **0 / 500** | -- |
| questions whose **delivered text set** differs across the two runs | -- | -- | **274 / 500** |
| ...of those, with no unscored turn at 256 | -- | -- | **31** |
| ...of those, with at least one | -- | -- | **243** |
| questions whose `goldOverlap.carried` differs | -- | -- | 63 |
| ...of those, in the padded population | -- | -- | **55** (30.6 expected by chance) |

Two populations, and the pin addresses one of them.

**All 243 questions that delivered an unscored turn at `top_k = 256` deliver a different set at 512**,
because at 512 the ranking scores turns it previously did not -- the delivery is not a prefix of the
pool (it draws session neighbours the ranker never saw), so widening the pool reclassifies those
neighbours and can reorder them. The anchor walk does not enter that at all. **Among the 257 questions
with no unscored turn, 31 (12.1%) changed**, and that population is the one §13.280.3's mechanism can
explain and §13.280.6's repair addresses.

So the claim the repair supports is: *the pool's anchors, restored turns and order prefix become
width-invariant*, which is what `anchor-width-invariance.test.ts` asserts and what the inequality in
§13.280.6 proves. The prompt-level equality needs a second property this increment does not provide:
delivery as a function of the pool. §13.280.7's third row is withdrawn to the number it can carry --
**31 to 0 among the unpadded, with the 243 out of scope** -- and the gold-level 63 can only be
attributed to the mechanism up to its **8** members that had no padding at 256.

This is the same defect the round began with, one layer down: a claim that a repair removes a cause,
written before the artifact was asked which population the cause covered. It is corrected here rather
than at the readout because the readout would have blamed the repair.

## 13.282 Reading: nine of ten, the order is not the difference, and the prompt side is exhausted

Artifact `42237543941`, 500 questions, 121 of them multi-session. Reference `42177443765`.

| # | quantity | reading | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | every check passes | **PASS** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | `evidence-blocks-instruction-first` | **PASS** |
| 3 | `memoryArmConfig.promptAssembly` | `instruction-first` | **PASS** |
| 4 | `memoryArmConfig.assemblyRoutes` | `['multi-session']` | **PASS** |
| 5 | `MR` against `42177443765` | 80.17% -> **77.69%** (-2.48 over 121; **1 won, 4 lost**; p = 0.375) | **FAIL** |
| 6 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` against it | IE -2.67 (1 won, 5 lost), KU **+2.78** (3 won, 1 lost), TR -1.57 (0 won, 2 lost), ABS 0.00 | **PASS** |
| 7 | `promptDigest` on the 379 non-`MR` questions | **379/379** agree | **PASS** |
| 8 | `llmUsage.calls` | 5,622 against 5,690 | **PASS** |
| 9 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | 30,991,956 against 31,103,964 (**-0.36%**) | **PASS** |
| 10 | `bareRetry.attempted` | 74 | **PASS** |

### 13.282.1 The instrument did exactly what it was built to do

**All 121 multi-session digests changed and none of the other 379 did.** That is the route scope of
the treatment measured on the delivered bytes: 121/121 inside, 0/379 outside, and the two fields this
increment added -- `promptAssembly` and `assemblyRoutes` -- are the reason the artifact can say the
run *asked* for the order and that the asking arrived. Gate 7 is what turns the ablation from an
average into a reach statement, and it is the first gate in this campaign decided entirely on prompt
bytes.

The permutation also cost nothing measurable: calls 5,690 -> 5,622, prompt tokens -0.36%, and
`deliveredPromptChars` unchanged at a median of 47,761 -- the same text, in a different order.

### 13.282.2 What the failure means

§13.279.4's first refutation branch, verbatim: *"`MR` moves by less than 3. Order is not the
difference either, and the remaining prompt-side differences are exhausted."* The move is -2.48 with
**1 win and 4 losses** -- indistinguishable from noise on 121 questions (p = 0.375) and, if anything,
pointing the wrong way. The four-pass averages say the same thing more quietly: feature 79.34% ->
77.48%, reference 85.33% -> 85.12% on the same artifact, so the arm-versus-reference gap widens from
-5.99 to **-7.64** points and the reference is stable through the change.

That is the third prompt-side lever to come back null, and the pattern is now a finding rather than a
run of bad luck:

| lever | dispatch | `MR` |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| the evidence contract, ported whole (§13.248) | `41860773768` | +1.8 questions |
| anchor restoration as a mechanism, first dispatch (§13.257) | `41990597116` | 5 won / 18 lost |
| the assembly order (§13.279) | `42237543941` | **1 won / 4 lost** |

Three mechanisms aimed at the presentation side, three results inside the noise band -- the third
one with a paired count that points the wrong way. What they share is that each changed *how the same
evidence is presented* (the restoration row changed where the pool stops, but its prompt delta was 54
characters out of 46,816); none changed *which evidence the reader gets*. The gap is therefore not in
the prompt's shape, and the campaign can stop looking there.

### 13.282.3 What this closes, and what it does not

**Closed: the prompt-side lever list.** Every degree of freedom this campaign enumerated on the
presentation side has now been measured -- the contract, the ask, the rendering, the order -- and the
best of them is worth +1.8 questions with a null on the last two. §13.277.2's "what deliberately does
not change" list was the last one; it is empty now.

**Not closed, and now the whole remaining argument:**

| axis | state |
| --- | --- |
| ranking stability under pool width | **repaired this round** (§13.280.6), prediction pending a 512 run (§13.280.8) |
| the room itself | **13.83% of every multi-session prompt is a source id**, and the reference pays none of it; §13.283 withholds it and reaches the coverage shortfall it was hiding |
| anchor budget 4 against CoD's 60 | measured as a **substitution** question, not a room question (§13.281) -- and that measurement is now read against a room §13.283 enlarges |
| multi-step retrieval (MemCog family) | not started; §13.278.4's item 3 |
| a second provider | not started |

The reading also settles the order of those four by elimination rather than by preference: three of
them change which evidence arrives, and the one that has just failed changed only how it is
presented.

**Cost of the negative:** 5,622 model calls and 30.99M prompt tokens. That is what a decisive
refutation costs on this arm, and it is worth stating beside the result -- the campaign spent the same
order of magnitude to find out that the order is not the difference, which is cheaper than the two
further levers it would otherwise have been stacked behind.

## 13.283 The room is spent on a source id the reader never cites

Every multi-session prompt this arm has ever sent carries, in front of each turn, a bracketed 36-character
identifier followed by a space -- 38 characters. It is the `sourced` rendering, and it exists for a stated
reason (§12.5): a bare number is a position rather than an identity, so two turns from one session would
otherwise be indistinguishable from two turns from two sessions. That reason was measured and refuted as an
*answer-quality* claim in §12.10 (dispatch `37827496757`, `MR` 0/17 with the rendering on all six routes),
but the rendering stayed on, and the cost of keeping it has never been measured at all.

This registration measures it, and the census is a read of `42237543941`:

| | `MR` | `TR` | `IE` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| marker share of the delivered prompt, median | **13.83%** | **14.51%** | 5.95% |
| characters, at the observed prompt sizes | ~6,650 of 48,000 | ~6,900 | ~2,900 |
| turns the freed characters buy, median | **24.4** | 26.2 | 3.1 |
| answers that reproduce an identifier | **0 / 121** | **0 / 127** | 2 / 150 |

The reader cites a source id in **4 of 500** answers and never on the two routes that pay the most for it.
It names a `Session N` header -- which `buildSessionPrompt` writes unconditionally, and which costs about
eleven characters once per session instead of 38 per turn -- in **31 of 500**. So on this arm the id is a
per-turn copy of a per-session fact, the boundary it was introduced to draw is already drawn, and the room
it occupies is the room §13.281 found to be the binding constraint: the median question sits **239
characters** below the 48,000 cap.

**The reference pipeline pays none of it.** Its aggregation prompt renders session blocks and carries no
per-turn marker at all, so on the axis where this arm trails by 7.64 points (§13.282.2) it has been comparing
a pipeline that spends its whole room on evidence against one that spends a seventh of it on provenance.

**And it does so at less than half the room, which is the part that has to be written down before the
readout rather than after it.** `NaturalLanguageMemorySystem` is constructed by the arm with `embedding`,
`llm`, `enableAbstention` and the two caches -- no budget options -- so `answerSessions` runs at the defaults:
**2,000 characters per session, 20,000 for the whole aggregation context**, against this arm's 48,000. It
reaches 85.95% on `MR` with 41% of our evidence room, at a coarser grain, with no per-turn cap.

So the tax this registration removes is real and this treatment is free evidence for the same money, but it
**cannot explain the gap**: a pipeline with 2.4x the room does not lose by 7.64 points because of a 13.8%
overhead inside it. What the two configurations differ in is **shape** -- 20,000 characters of
session-complete evidence against 48,000 characters of turn-scattered fragments cut at 400 each. That is
§13.34's reading of the same artifact and SeCom's finding (arXiv:2502.05589) arrived at from the other side,
and it is what §13.283.6 registers next. The correction matters because the tempting read of this whole round
is "we were paying a tax and now we are not", which would close the gap in a document and not in a run.

### 13.283.1 What the treatment is, and the two things held fixed

`promptContract: evidence-blocks-unsourced` -- the §13.279 instruction block, the §13.279
`instruction-first` assembly, and `rendering: numbered` instead of `sourced`.

Both fixed properties are held by construction rather than by intent, which is what makes this one variable:

- **the instruction text** is `CONTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS['evidence-blocks-instruction-first']` returned by
  reference, so there is one function and a later edit moves both sides;
- **the order** is `ASSEMBLY_BY_CONTRACT['evidence-blocks-unsourced'] = 'instruction-first'`, and a test
  asserts the two entries are the same value rather than asserting a literal.

`evidence-unsourced.test.ts` pins three further properties: that the first `\n\n`-separated segment is
byte-identical under both renderings, that the `Session N` header and the turn's own date survive, and --
the one that matters -- that the treatment **cannot remove a turn the control delivered**.

### 13.283.2 The containment, and why no per-question exception is needed

`fitToBudget` takes the largest prefix of one relevance order whose rendering fits. Making each item
cheaper therefore admits a weakly **longer prefix of the same order**: the delivered set under the
unsourced rendering contains the control's, question by question. That is not a hope about averages, it is
a property of a prefix, and it is what makes the safety claim gatable per question instead of only in the
mean (gate 7).

The arithmetic that predicts a *gain* is the same census read forward. On `MR`, 34 questions fall short of
their gold set by 53 turns in total, and every one of the 34 is short by fewer turns than the 24.4 the freed
characters buy; on `TR`, 37 questions and 64 turns, again all within reach. The estimate is necessary rather
than sufficient -- it says the room exists, not that the next turns in the rank order are the missing gold
ones -- which is exactly why gate 8 asks for **+20 of 500** against an arithmetic ceiling of 109 and not for
the ceiling.

**A refinement read off the same field, and it changes what the prediction means.** On `MR` the delivered
count already **exceeds** the ranked pool -- 1,779 gold turns delivered against 1,753 that the ranking
surfaced -- so this route's recall is produced by restoration rather than by ranking depth. Every one of the
53 missing turns carries `goldRanks = -1`, the marker for "the ranking never surfaced it": they are not
candidates a wider `top_k` would find, they are neighbours of an anchor that sits below the character cut.
The freed room therefore acts on precisely the population the deficit is in, and a run that answered this by
widening the pool would be answering a different question.

The same records give the retrieval-side quantity `LongMemEval` scores and publishes, so the arm can be
compared on it: **gold-turn recall**, the fraction of the labelled evidence turns that reached the prompt.
It has never been printed for this arm, and it is the number the coverage gap actually moves:

| | `IE` | `MR` | `KU` | `TR` | `ABS` | all |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| gold turns carried | 1,437/1,709 | **1,779/1,832** | 1,313/1,688 | 1,551/1,615 | 440/672 | 6,520/7,516 |
| recall | 84.08% | **97.11%** | 77.78% | 96.04% | 65.48% | **86.75%** |
| questions delivering every gold turn | 75/150 | 87/121 | 5/72 | 90/127 | 2/30 | 259/500 |

`MR`'s recall is already 97.11%, which is why the gain this registration predicts is not "more evidence in
general" but **the last 2.9%**: 53 turns spread over 34 questions, each of which is a counting question whose
answer is one short. `KU` is the mirror image and worth stating so nobody reads recall as accuracy -- 77.78%
recall against 88.9% accuracy, because a knowledge-update question needs the latest value and not the set.

### 13.283.3 The gates

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **every check passes** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | **`evidence-blocks-unsourced`** |
| 3 | `memoryArmConfig.promptAssembly` | **`instruction-first`** |
| 4 | per-turn source markers across the 500 delivered prompts | **0** |
| 5 | `MR` accuracy against `42237543941` | **Δ ≥ +3 points** with the resolution printed |
| 6 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` against `42237543941` | **no loss ≥ 3 points** |
| 7 | `goldOverlap.carried`, question by question | **no question carries fewer gold turns than the control** |
| 8 | questions delivering every gold turn | **≥ 279** against 259 |
| 9 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 31,400,000** against 30,991,956, **+1.3%** |
| 10 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

Gate 4 is the one this table is built around. Every other row can be satisfied by a run that changed
nothing: gate 2 is a config field, gate 5 a score, and gate 5 would pass on a mechanism improvement that
had nothing to do with the marker. Gate 4 reads the **bytes**: 500 prompts, zero bracketed identifiers,
decided by `source_marker_absence` -- a kind added for this registration, because the existing kinds decide
either on scores (`capability_delta`) or on digests (`digest_agreement`), and a digest equality cannot say
*which* bytes left.

Gate 7 is the second new kind, `coverage_monotone`, and it exists because the safety argument is
per-question. A mean would pass on a run that gained fifty questions and damaged twenty, which for a
resource change is the one outcome that would make gate 5's gain unattributable.

Gate 9's bar is **+1.3%** rather than the **-0.36%** §13.279 measured. The room is the same size and every
prompt stays inside it, so a rise can only come from the reader's own output on a longer evidence block;
a run above +1.3% would mean the prompts grew, which the rendering change cannot do -- every turn
contributes strictly fewer characters.

### 13.283.4 What would refute it

Three branches, and each names the increment that follows rather than a retry:

1. **`MR` moves by less than 3 points.** Coverage was not the mechanism either, and the id was not the
   constraint -- which would leave the reference's 8-point lead attributable to its session-level
   retrieval (§13.34's reading) rather than to the prompt's composition. The next increment is then
   `relevanceUnits: session-fill` **on the anchored signal**, which has never been run: §13.34 retired it
   under `retrieval-hybrid`, where every session in the pool was admitted anyway.
2. **`MR` gains but a capability loses 3 points.** The marker was load-bearing somewhere: the follow-up is
   to restore it at **session scope** (`Session 3 [id]`), which costs 1/38th of the room and separates
   "provenance" from "per-turn position" as explanations.
3. **Any question carries fewer gold turns** (gate 7). The containment argument in §13.283.2 is then wrong
   at artifact scale, which would mean the budget is not the prefix the proof assumes -- and the width
   repair in §13.280.6 rests on the same assumption, so that would be the more important finding.

### 13.283.5 What this does not decide

- **The anchor budget** (§13.281). More anchors can only substitute for retrieved turns, and this
  registration changes how much room there is to substitute into -- so it must be read first.
- **The 512-width verification** (§13.280.7). Its three predictions stand, and this run is at `top_k = 256`
  with the repaired bound, so it neither tests them nor disturbs them.
- **Multi-step retrieval** (MemCog's family). It changes what is retrieved rather than how it is rendered,
  and it is the axis §13.282.3 leaves standing.
- **A second provider.** Nothing here touches the reader.

### 13.283.6 The comparison this treatment does not fix, and the increment it points at

The reference arm is constructed with no budget options (`run-ablation.ts`), so it runs at
`DEFAULT_MAX_AGGREGATION_CHARS = 20,000` and `DEFAULT_MAX_SESSION_CHARS = 2,000`, and it delivers **whole
sessions** joined by `\n\n` with no numbering, no dates and no per-turn cap. This arm runs at 48,000 with
400-character turns.

| | `reference-pipeline` | `cortex-memory` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| room | **20,000** chars | **48,000** chars |
| unit | session, whole | turn, with a score and a neighbourhood |
| per-item cut | 2,000 chars per **session** | 400 chars per **turn** |
| per-turn markers | none | 13.83% of the prompt, until this registration |
| `MR` | **85.95%** | 77.69% |

More room, finer grain, five times as many cuts, and 7.64 points lower. The order of the next two
experiments follows without another census: **shape before size**, and the shape that wins is the one the
competitor with less room is using.

**§13.284 (candidate, not dispatched).** The reference's **shape** at this arm's registered room:
`relevanceUnits: session-fill` on the anchored signal, `maxPromptChars` and the per-turn cap untouched.
One variable, and `chooseEvidence` already dispatches on it for any signal (`sessionOf` is the only
precondition), so the dispatch is a value rather than a code change -- unlike §13.34, where the same value
was read under `retrieval-hybrid` and the pool admitted every session anyway.

Predictions, each checkable from the artifact: `MR` at least level with §13.283's reading; gold-turn recall
on `MR` no lower than 97.11%, because `session-fill` allocates whole sessions and skips the ones that do not
fit; and `windowComposition.turns` **down**, since a session costs what it costs.

**And the room may not need to be 20,000 at all.** `usageBySide` on `42237543941` reads **977 prompt tokens
per call on the reference side against 13,570 on ours** -- a 14x difference, against a 20,000-character cap
the reference never approaches. Converting at this arm's own measured 0.297 tokens per character, the
reference's answering prompt is of order **3,300 characters**, i.e. a sixteenth of ours. So `maxPromptChars`
on the multi-session route is a **sweep** rather than a value: the shape may be worth more at 8,000 than at
20,000, and the artifact can decide it. §13.285 is written as one value because a registration needs one, and
4,000 is the number the observed usage suggests -- but the honest form of the question is "how small can the
room be before session-shaped evidence stops fitting", and that is what the sweep answers.

**§13.285 (candidate, after §13.284).** The reference's **room**: `maxPromptChars` 20,000 and no per-turn cap
on the multi-session route, at whatever unit §13.284 leaves in place. This is the increment that is expected
to **save** tokens and gain points at once -- about 58% less prefill on `MR` -- and it is deliberately second,
because a room change and a unit change in one run would make neither attributable, and the campaign has paid
for that lesson four times (§13.104, §13.124, §13.279, §13.282).

Both stay behind §13.283 for the same reason: if its coverage gate moves, the room is not the constraint at
48,000 and §13.285 becomes a sharper test than it is today; if it does not, the constraint is the unit and
§13.284 is the one to read.

## 13.286 The competitor's selection, read from its source, and the unit that reading implies

Until this iteration the Chain on Demand comparison in this document cited a paper. The repository it
belongs to is public (`github.com/Renkiroo/chainondemand`, linked from the paper's own abstract), and
reading it changes two things: what its pipeline actually does at each step, and — separately — what one of
our own archived conclusions was actually about.

### 13.286.1 What the code does, step by step

The main entry (`cod/run_cod.py:150`) is four calls, and every parameter is a CLI default rather than a
tuned value: `--pool-k 200`, `--final-k 60`, `lambda_div=0.06`, `beta_ent=0.10`, `expand_window=2`.

| Step | Code | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pool | `store.search_memory(cid, question, 200)` | dense top-200 from raw utterances; no session pre-selection |
| seeds | `select_greedy_unprotected` (`cod/selector.py`) | 60 picks, each scored `dense + 0.06·(1 − max Jaccard to S) + 0.10·(uncovered query terms this hit covers)`, **recomputed after every pick** |
| restoration | `expand_seeds` → `store.expand_context(±2)` (`cod/expand.py`, `cod/store.py:161`) | each seed's same-session neighbours, `index ± 2`, **clamped to that session** — `entries` is filtered to `entry_position(id)[0] == target_session` before the slice, so a window cannot cross a boundary |
| assembly | `merge_evidence(seeds, expanded)` (`cod/controller.py:50`) | seeds in **score order** first, then each seed's window in arrival order; deduped by id; **never re-sorted globally** |
| answer | `ANSWER_USER_PROMPT` (`cod/prompts.py`) | one line per utterance, `timestamp speaker: utterance`, no ids, no numbering, plus "resolve relative dates against the utterance timestamp" and an explicit premise-mismatch instruction |

Two mechanisms in the file are **not** used by the main entry and should not be cited as if they were:
`select_with_seed_protection` (replace a dense top-k seed only when a later candidate outscores it) and
`select_seeds_rescue` (keep `core_k`, then take `rescue_k` from a **mid-rank window** `[lo, hi]`, skipping
the ranks immediately below the core — [11, 30] in their smoke test). The rescue rule is the more
interesting of the two: it encodes the claim that the hits just under a cut are near-duplicates of the ones
above it, so the informative candidates sit further down. It is a *cheaper* answer to the same problem this
section is about, and it is worth a dispatch of its own after §13.286 is read.

So the shape is: **bounded anchor set + local restoration**, with the budget spent on *anchors* and the
neighbourhoods arriving for free. Ours, until now, has been: budget spent on *ranked turns*, prefix rule,
neighbourhoods either unranked (invisible to the cut) or admitted to the pool where they compete on a
decayed fraction of their anchor's score (§13.257, which lost eight MR questions to displacement).

### 13.286.2 The defect this wiring found, and what it invalidates

While adding the fourth unit to the forwarding chain, `run-ablation.ts` was found to forward **one** of the
three units that existed:

```ts
...(armOptions.relevanceUnits === 'session' ? { relevanceUnits: 'session' as const } : {}),
```

`session-fill` was accepted by the arm's parser, projected into the artifact's configuration line as
`relevanceUnits=session-fill`, and then **never passed to the product** — the run executed the `turn` unit.
The single construction site (`run-ablation.ts:610`) and the single forwarding line make this exhaustive: no
other path could have reached `CortexMemoryOptions.relevanceUnits`.

**What this does not invalidate.** `session` was forwarded, so §13.27's dispatch of it measured what it
says it measured, and §13.282.3's reading of `38753835652` — whole sessions, MR 12.40% against the turn
unit's 42.15% — stands. The claim that a session unit loses is unaffected.

**What it does invalidate.** §13.32's dispatch `38828538851` and §13.34's reading of it. That section's
finding — "`session-fill` spends the room and changes nothing" — is a sentence about the **turn** unit, and
the tell is in §13.34's own table: the treated arm agrees with the turn arm to within one question on MR and
three across the other four capabilities. A configuration whose whole claim is "the same ranking, a repaired
search" agreeing with the control exactly is the signature of the control. `session-fill` is therefore
**unrun**, not negative, and the candidate §13.284 stays open — with the caveat that its own prediction
(watch `MR`'s room usage) can no longer be read from an existing artifact.

**The repair, and why it is compile-time.** A test cannot see this class of failure: `bench/**` is excluded
from coverage, and the failure is an **omission** — a value nobody wrote a line for. The forwarding is now a
table typed `Record<RelevanceUnits, RelevanceUnits | undefined>`, so a fifth unit added to the product's
union fails to compile until the table names it. Injected for proof: adding `| 'injected'` to
`RelevanceUnits` and rebuilding produces

```
bench/run-ablation.ts(248,7): error TS2741: Property 'injected' is missing in type
'{ turn: undefined; session: "session"; 'session-fill': "session-fill"; 'anchor-window': "anchor-window"; }'
but required in type 'Record<RelevanceUnits, RelevanceUnits | undefined>'.
```

The resolver additionally refuses a name the table does not contain, because an index miss returns
`undefined` and would reproduce the same silent fall-through one layer down.

### 13.286.3 The unit neither existing unit could be

| unit | what the room buys | why it cannot answer §13.283's residue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `turn` | the highest-scoring turns, wherever they live | the missing MR turns have `goldRanks = -1`; no width of a ranked prefix reaches them |
| `session` | every turn of a session, prefix rule | one gold turn costs a whole session — MR's median gold session is 24 turns against a room of about 23, so the first session over the line ends the pass (§13.27, measured, lost) |
| `session-fill` | the same, skipping sessions that do not fit | still buys whole sessions, so it pays for 24 turns to read 3 (unrun — see above) |
| **`anchor-window`** | **an anchor and its `±window` same-session neighbours, indivisibly** | the neighbours are bought *with* the anchor, so they are never ranked and cannot displace anything |

`relevanceUnits: 'anchor-window'`, `windowRadius` defaulting to **2** — the reference's frozen
`expand_window`. Three properties are what make it a unit and not a heuristic:

1. **Radius 0 is the control.** With `windowRadius: 0` every neighbourhood is its anchor, the ladder has one
   rung, and the walk visits the same anchors the prefix rule keeps in the same order — so the delivered set
   is the turn unit's, character for character. Asserted as an equality against `relevanceUnits: 'turn'`
   rather than against the implementation's own arithmetic, which is what makes the radius the only variable
   in a dispatch of this unit.
2. **The ladder shrinks the window, never the anchor.** A window is several turns, so a strict prefix pass
   over windows would end the pass with **no evidence at all** the first time one did not fit. The pass tries
   `radius`, then `radius − 1`, … then the anchor alone, and stops only when the anchor itself does not fit.
   The last rung is the turn unit's own decision, so under a tight budget this unit can never carry less than
   the turn unit would — asserted as a for-all over a 30-point budget sweep.
3. **The neighbourhood is session-local by construction.** The per-session arrival index makes a window a
   slice, so it cannot wrap from a session's last turn into the next session's first — the boundary the
   session routes exist to respect, and the one a naive `arrival ± radius` would cross, since the flat list
   is the concatenation.

Presentation stays chronological. This is the one place the reference disagrees with us and we are not
following it: CoD prints anchors in score order and restores windows after them, relying on a timestamp on
every line. Ours prints arrival order, because a log in rank order makes relative-time and
knowledge-update questions unanswerable — the rule `selectSession` already records, and TR is 96.04% on the
arrival-order prompt.

### 13.286.4 Verification

`packages/cortex-memory/src/__tests__/anchor-window.test.ts`, twelve tests, no mocks:

- the control leaves `a3`'s neighbours behind under the same budget, and a **band assertion** pins the
  fixture at four to seven carried turns so a change to the instruction block fails by naming the budget
  rather than by looking like a selection bug;
- radius 0 equals the turn unit exactly; radius 2 completes `a1..a5`; `a0` and `a6` stay out (the radius is
  bounded, so a window that ignored it and took the session would fail); the default is 2;
- the window clamps at both ends of a session and never reaches into the next one (B's turns score nothing
  in that fixture, so their absence is evidence of the clamp rather than of the ranking);
- the anti-starvation for-all, the budget ceiling at radii `0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 50`, and rejection of
  `−1, 1.5, NaN, Infinity`;
- `windowRadius` is inert on the other three units, which is what lets a dispatch of it stay single-variable.

The arm-side guard fired on cue: adding `'anchor-window'` to the product's union failed
`bench-memory-arm.test.ts`'s both-directions table comparison (`expected [ 'session', 'session-fill', 'turn' ]
to deeply equal [ 'anchor-window', 'session', … ]`) until `RELEVANCE_UNITS` named it.

### 13.286.5 What it is registered to move, once §13.283 has been read

Not dispatched this iteration: `42310779222` is still running, and a second variable in flight would make
neither attributable. The registration, written now so that it cannot be fitted to the result:

| Field | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cortex_memory_relevance_units` | **`anchor-window`** | the variable — now actually forwarded |
| `cortex_memory_relevance` | `retrieval` | held at §13.283's value; the anchored signal is *not* used, because pool-side restoration is the mechanism §13.257 refuted |
| everything else | §13.283's values | held |

Predictions, in reading order:

1. **MR gold-turn recall does not fall below 97.11%.** The mechanism buys the residents of turns that already
   scored, so it can only add to the delivered gold set at a fixed room — if recall falls, the ladder is
   trading anchors for neighbours and the trade is wrong at 48,000 characters.
2. **MR accuracy rises**, because §13.283.1's arithmetic says all 53 missing MR turns sit inside the room a
   13.83% tax was consuming (upper bound +109 fully-covered questions).
3. **The number of sessions the prompt shows falls sharply on MR, while the carried turn count
   stays near the room's capacity.** Measured on `42237543941`: MR delivers a median of **173 turns
   over 44 sessions — 3.9 turns per session, 252 characters per turn** — i.e. it already touches
   roughly every session and reads each to about a quarter. A five-turn window per anchor is most of
   a short session, so the same room must buy **fewer, deeper** sessions. If the session count does
   not fall, or the carried count falls with it, the pass is not pricing shared neighbours once and
   the room is being spent on the accounting rather than on evidence.
4. **`TR` and `KU` do not move more than three points either way**, since both are already above 96% on
   recall and neither's residue is a neighbour.

Refutation: if the carried count falls, accuracy is flat and recall is flat, then the neighbours were not the
constraint and §13.283.6's "shape before size" ordering is wrong — the next variable would be the reader, not
the selection. If recall rises and accuracy does not, the ceiling is downstream of the window and the second
provider (§13.282.3's last item) is the increment.

### 13.286.6 The counterfactual the existing artifact can already answer, and the risk it names

No new run is needed to ask where the missing gold turns live relative to what the prompt showed.
`42237543941` records, per question, the full delivered roster (`turns`), the gold set, and
`goldDelivered` per gold turn. Grouping both by the rendered timestamp — which this corpus stamps once
per session, so it is the session key, and the grouping is an **inference from the prompt bytes** rather
than from the harness's `string[][]` (that corpus is not reachable from this sandbox: the Hugging Face
host is blocked, so the exact ±2 distance is left to the dispatch) — gives:

| | value |
| --- | ---: |
| gold turns not delivered (all 500 questions) | **996** |
| …whose **session the prompt already showed** | **985 (98.9%)** |
| delivered turns in that session, p25 / p50 / p75 | **4 / 6 / 8** |
| of the 996, on `MR` | 53, **all 53 in a shown session** |

So the missing evidence is not in unseen sessions. It is in sessions the reader was already reading and
did not finish — which is what §13.283 inferred from `goldRanks = -1` and what this measures directly.
The `session` unit could not fix that (it pays 24 turns for 3, and lost); a window around the anchors that
session already supplied is the cheaper way to finish it.

**And the risk, stated before the run rather than after it.** The same measurement says MR's prompt
currently shows a median of **44 sessions** — very close to the number of sessions the corpus gives those
questions at all. So the arm is not failing to find the right sessions; it is reading every session it
could reach to a quarter. A deeper unit must therefore **give up breadth to buy depth**, and the
prediction that accuracy follows is the same claim §13.26 measured (accuracy rising 14.3 → 66.7% across
coverage bands). If a five-turn window makes MR *worse*, it is because these questions need one turn from
many sessions rather than several turns from one — and that would refute §13.283.6's "shape before size"
ordering, not merely this parameter. A result that reversed it would be the most informative outcome
available, which is why the registration states it in this direction rather than as a hope.

## 13.287 Reading: eight of ten, the id was 22% of the tokens, and eleven MR questions became complete without one of them changing

`42310779222` ran §13.283's treatment — the same instruction, the same order, no per-turn source id —
against `42237543941`, which drew the id on the same six routes.

### 13.287.1 The gates

| # | quantity | reading | threshold | verdict |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **`reach` failed**: four ask routes, none reported rendered | every check passes | **FAIL** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | `evidence-blocks-unsourced` | the same | **PASS** |
| 3 | `memoryArmConfig.promptAssembly` | `instruction-first` | the same | **PASS** |
| 4 | per-turn source markers across 500 prompts | **0 of 500**, 0 markers in total | 0 | **PASS** |
| 5 | `MR` accuracy | 77.69% → **77.69%** (+0.00; 6 won, 6 lost; p = 1) | Δ ≥ +3 points | **FAIL** |
| 6 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` | IE 92.67→94.67 (+2.00), TR 94.49→95.28 (+0.79), KU 0, ABS 0 | no loss ≥ 3 | **PASS** |
| 7 | `goldOverlap.carried`, per question | **500 of 500** carry at least as many gold turns | none fewer | **PASS** |
| 8 | questions delivering every gold turn | **285 of 500** against 259 (+26) | ≥ 279 | **PASS** |
| 9 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **27,308,598** against 30,991,956 | ≤ 31,400,000 | **PASS** |
| 10 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **71** | ≥ 60 | **PASS** |

Gate 1 failed, and the failure was ours rather than the run's: `RENDERING_ROUTES['evidence-blocks-unsourced']`
was `[]`, which is the *baseline's* answer — "this contract administers no rendering" — and no other
contract's. §13.287.5 records the repair and the test that would have caught it for free.

Gate 5 is the negative, and it is the informative one.

### 13.287.2 The tax was 9.91% of the characters and 22.41% of the tokens

The id is 38 characters plus a space, drawn once per delivered turn. Across the 500 reference prompts
that is **60,312 markers and 2,352,168 characters**, 9.91% of 23,723,712. The prompt sizes are otherwise
identical — mean 47,447 characters before, 47,430 after — because the prefix rule reinvests every freed
character, which is the inclusion property §13.283.3 proved and gate 7 confirmed per question.

What is *not* identical is what the tokens say:

| | reference | treatment | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| feature-side prompt tokens | 28,149,919 | **24,209,976** | **−14.00%** |
| feature-side calls | 2,074 | 2,071 | — |
| prompt tokens per call | 13,573 | **11,690** | **−13.9%** |
| characters per prompt | 47,447 | 47,430 | −0.04% |

Two numbers cannot both be right unless the *density* changed, and it did. Taking the treatment's rate as
the pure-evidence rate (0.2464 tokens per character), the reference's excess over it is 1,883 tokens
per prompt, carried by 4,703 characters of id — **0.6466 tokens per character, 2.62× the density of the
evidence the id displaced**. Excluding the displaced evidence, the id is **22.41% of the prompt's token
cost while being 9.91% of its characters**.

That is the first finding of this round and it is a defect in the *instrument*: this arm denominates its
budget in **characters**, so the number of tokens a prompt costs depends on what is rendered into it, and
a 38-character marker that costs 2.6× the tokens of 38 characters of prose makes the budget report a
full prompt while buying 14% less of everything else. §13.283 called it a 13.83% tax because it measured
characters; in tokens it was 22.41%.

### 13.287.3 The coverage rose and the answers did not move

The freed room admitted evidence, and it admitted the right evidence:

| | reference | treatment |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| gold turns carried, all 500 | 6,434 | **6,520** |
| questions delivering every gold turn | 259 | **285** |
| — of which `MR` | 87 | **98** |
| — of which `TR` | 90 | **104** |
| — of which `KU` | 5 | 6 |

`MR` gained **eleven** complete questions and lost none. Then:

| question | was it right? |
| --- | --- |
| the eleven newly complete `MR` questions | **9 were already correct, 2 were already wrong — none flipped** |

Eleven questions went from "the reader was missing evidence" to "the reader had all of it", and the
verdict changed zero times. The six `MR` flips this run does have (6 won, 6 lost, p = 1) are elsewhere
and cancel.

### 13.287.4 The decomposition, and the number that bounds the next axis

Classifying every `MR` record by whether the prompt delivered all of its gold turns:

| | n | correct | accuracy | 95% Wilson |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `MR`, every gold turn delivered | 98 | 80 | **81.63%** | [72.82, 88.05] |
| `MR`, at least one gold turn missing | 23 | 14 | **60.87%** | [40.79, 77.84] |
| `MR`, all | 121 | 94 | 77.69% | [69.48, 84.19] |

So **18 of `MR`'s 27 errors are questions whose prompt held every gold turn**, and the coverage-bound
remainder is 9. That is the same split §13.276 measured from the other direction — restoring the missing
turns converted 3 of 12 failures, a residual of 0.73 — arrived at without spending a call.

Two consequences, stated as arithmetic rather than as opinion:

1. **Perfection of coverage is worth at most 5 points on `MR`.** If every one of the 23 partial questions
   were made complete and answered at the complete population's rate, `MR` would read 81.63%; the
   interval's top is 88.05%, so a coverage-only world is not *excluded* from reaching CoD's 86.6%, but
   the point estimate leaves 5.0 points unexplained and the interval leaves it unresolved rather than
   closed. What is excluded is the stronger claim that coverage is the mechanism: eleven questions
   gained completeness here and none changed.
2. **The reference's 7.43-point `MR` lead is not significant on 121 questions.** 18 discordant pairs one
   way against 9 the other is McNemar p = 0.122, in the same artifact that reports the delta. The lead is
   real in the direction it points and is worth chasing; it is not a resolved measurement, and treating
   it as one would be the error §13.261.3 exists to prevent.

### 13.287.5 The defect the audit found, and the test that would have found it for free

`RENDERING_ROUTES['evidence-blocks-unsourced']` was written as `[]` on the reading that the field means
"which routes draw a **sourced** rendering" — for this contract, none. The field does not mean that. Its
own docblock says otherwise two paragraphs above the entry: *"The baseline contract reaches nothing: it
administers no rendering, so reporting it as covering routes would claim a treatment the control arm did
not receive."* Every other contract is administered on every route, because `instructionsFor` begins with
`const own = CONTRACT_INSTRUCTIONS[contract](date)` and returns it wherever an ask does not override —
with `ask=verbatim` that is all six.

The consequence was a false claim in the one direction that matters: the artifact read as §12.8's defect
(a contract named, four of five capabilities never reached) when the run had administered it everywhere.
The audit caught it. **The audit was right and the artifact was wrong**, and the entry is now the six
routes with the mistake written into the comment rather than deleted.

`rendering-reach.test.ts` (5 tests) is the check that costs a second instead of a run. It asserts the
**relations** the wrong value violated rather than a literal list, because a literal would have been
edited in the same commit as the mistake:

| assertion | what it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `[]` for exactly one contract, and it is `abstention` | the baseline's answer is the baseline's alone |
| every other contract reports the identical six | the block is a fallthrough, so a subset is impossible |
| `assemblyRoutes ⊆ renderingRoutes` | **the invariant `42310779222` violated** |
| the four `verbatim` routes are rendered by every non-control contract | no contract can be dispatched under the shipped ask and leave one unrendered |
| `assemblyRoutes` non-empty ⟺ `promptAssembly` present | a reach the artifact cannot name |

Injected for proof: restoring `[]` fails **four of the five**.

### 13.287.6 What this round did not do, and what it costs

- **No dispatch.** `42310779222` was the only run in flight; §13.288 registers the next one below.
- **The `session-fill` unit still has no reading.** §13.286.2 found it never reached the product; the
  forwarding is repaired and the unit is now dispatchable, which is what §13.288 spends its run on.
- **The token axis has no instrument yet.** The finding in §13.287.2 is that the budget's unit is wrong,
  not that the budget is too large. A token-denominated room is a product change with its own design
  question (which tokeniser, and what to do when the reader changes), and it is not attempted here.

## 13.288 Registration: the unit that never ran, against the run that removed the id

§13.286.2 found `session-fill` never reached the product. §13.287 then measured the prompt side from
every other angle available and closed them: order (no), the id (a cost win and an accuracy null), room
content (285 of 500 questions now hold every gold turn, and eleven newly-complete `MR` questions changed
zero verdicts). What is left is **what the room is spent on**, and there is exactly one value of that
axis with no reading at all.

### 13.288.1 The variable, and what it is not

| | value | note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cortex_memory_relevance_units` | **`session-fill`** | the variable |
| `cortex_memory_relevance` | `retrieval-anchored` | held at §13.260.7's adoption |
| `cortex_memory_relevance_top_k` | `256` | held |
| `cortex_memory_max_prompt_chars` | `48000` | held — **this is why the dispatch is single-variable** |
| `cortex_memory_prompt_contract` | `evidence-blocks-unsourced` | held at §13.283's value |
| `cortex_memory_ask` | `verbatim` | held at §13.248's adoption |
| everything else | as `42310779222` | the registration matches it field for field |

The unit is unchanged since §13.31: whole sessions ordered by their best-scoring turn, and a session that
does not fit is **skipped** rather than ending the pass. §13.27's rule stopped at the first rejection and
left half the room unread; that is the one thing this value is not.

**What it must not be reported as.** The reference pipeline leads this arm by 7.43 points on `MR` with
the same reader on the same dataset, and its evidence is *sessions, truncated to 2,000 characters each,
20,000 in total*. This dispatch buys the **session unit at this arm's own room**, not the reference's
shape: no per-session cap exists here, and the room stays at 48,000. So a gain here is evidence for the
unit; it is not a replication of the reference, and a null is not a refutation of the reference's shape.
The two-knob replication (per-session cap plus the 20,000 room) is a separate registration that only
becomes worth writing if this one moves.

### 13.288.2 The eleven gates

`tools/gates/13.288.json`, control `42310779222`. Every gate is an invariant of a legitimate run, and the
two that can distinguish a null result from a missing treatment are gates 3 and 4.

| # | quantity | threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the artifact's own audit | **every check passes** |
| 2 | `memoryArmConfig.relevanceUnits` | **`session-fill`** |
| 3 | `MR` deliveries whose prompt bytes differ from `42310779222` | **≥ 110 of 121** — the value reached the product, which is the check `38828538851` failed |
| 4 | the four capabilities outside the unit's reach | **379 of 379 agree** — a unit that leaked past `multi-session` would make every judgment about it a judgment about two changes |
| 5 | `memoryArmConfig.promptContract` | **held at §13.283's value** |
| 6 | per-turn source markers across the 500 delivered prompts | **0** — §13.287.2's saving is only attributable if it is still withheld |
| 7 | `MR` accuracy against `42310779222` | **Δ ≥ +3 points** with the resolution printed |
| 8 | `IE`, `KU`, `TR`, `ABS` against `42310779222` | **no loss ≥ 3 points** |
| 9 | `MR` questions delivering every gold turn, against 98 | **no fewer than 98** — buying whole sessions must not deliver less of the gold set than fragments did |
| 10 | `llmUsage.promptTokens` | **≤ 33,000,000** against 27,308,598 — the unit may cost up to 20% more, and a run that costs more than that is buying depth it is not reporting |
| 11 | `bareRetry.attempted` | **≥ 60** |

Gate 3's bar is 110 rather than 121 because a unit that delivers the same set for a question whose gold
sits entirely in one session is a legitimate no-op on that question; the bar says "essentially every `MR`
prompt changed", which no run that failed to forward the value can satisfy.

### 13.288.3 Predictions, in reading order

1. **`MR` prompts show far fewer sessions and about as many turns.** Today `MR` shows a median of **45**
   sessions at 3.9 turns each — the breadth is already saturated against a haystack of 45-52 sessions, so
   the only direction left is depth. A median above 30 sessions means the unit did not change the shape,
   and gate 3 would have to have passed some other way.
2. **`MR` gold coverage rises, and §13.287.4 says what that is worth.** Complete sessions should carry
   more gold; the arithmetic from the last round caps the accuracy reward of coverage alone at about five
   points. If coverage rises and accuracy does not, the session unit is the third shape that changes what
   the reader sees without changing what it concludes — and the axis closes with it.
3. **`TR` does not move.** It shows 45 date-stamped sessions in its prompt too, but it is built by
   `#promptWithDate` from a flat turn list, so `sessionOf` is absent and the unit cannot reach it. A `TR`
   movement of more than three points is evidence that the unit reaches further than the single call site
   says it does, which would be the more important finding.
4. **Tokens stay within 20% of the control.** Whole sessions carry the same evidence with fewer per-turn
   decorations, so the plausible direction is *down*.

### 13.288.4 Refutation

- **`MR` flat, coverage flat, sessions unchanged.** The unit did not change the shape and gate 3 will have
  been satisfied by something else; the next check is the agent-side read of `featurePromptTexts`, which
  records the delivered bytes.
- **`MR` falls.** Depth bought at the cost of breadth is wrong at 48,000, and the reading is that these
  questions need one turn from many sessions — which refutes §13.286.5's "shape before size" ordering and
  makes the per-session cap the next variable rather than the room.
- **`MR` rises with coverage flat.** The unit is doing something other than delivering gold: the session
  boundary itself is information (the reference's contract says *"based on MULTIPLE conversation
  sessions"* and its Step 1 asks for a `<session date>` per item). That would make §13.286's
  `anchor-window` a different experiment than the one registered, and the registration for it would be
  rewritten before dispatch rather than after.

### 13.288.5 Amendment, written before the artifact exists: the prediction above was wrong about depth

`42328499107` was dispatched at `b299fdd2` and is running. Before any answer record exists, the
arithmetic below shows prediction 1 in §13.288.3 was stated backwards, and it is corrected here rather
than after the reading — the point of writing predictions first is that a correction has a timestamp.

**The measurement, on `42310779222`'s own artifact, no calls spent.** `ablation.featureRetrievedContexts`
holds the turns the reader was shown, and the rendered timestamp groups them into sessions:

| | `MR`, median |
| --- | ---: |
| sessions in the retrieved context | **45** |
| turns in the retrieved context | **199** |
| delivered turns (`turns`) | **189** |
| turns the plan held (`evidenceTurns`) | **243** |
| rendered size of the whole context, at `maxTurnChars=400` | **44,753 chars** |
| rendered size of one session | **956 chars** |

So the room is **48,000 and the whole pool renders to 44,753**. `session-fill` will therefore admit
roughly 44 of 45 sessions and deliver about 194 turns, against the `turn` unit's 189 — *more* turns, not
fewer, and not fewer sessions either.

**What the dispatch therefore tests, stated correctly.** Not "depth against breadth". It tests whether a
session that is **complete** reads differently from a session that is 78% complete: the turn unit spends
the room on the 189 highest-scoring turns of the 243 the plan held, which cuts each session's tail; the
session unit spends it on whole sessions and skips the one that does not fit. The reference pipeline's
advantage, if it is the session boundary rather than the volume, has to show up under exactly this
comparison.

**The refutation branch this makes sharper, not weaker.** If `MR` is flat with 44 complete sessions
against 45 partial ones, then fragmentation at this granularity is not the mechanism, and the reference's
7.43 points must come from something the room cannot express — its 2,000-character truncation, which
*deliberately* keeps sessions partial but bounded, or its `parseAggregationAnswer`, or the critique pass
it does not enable. That is a different and more useful question than the one §13.288.4 was written for,
and §13.288.4's third branch already anticipated the shape of it.

**What is unchanged.** Gates 1–11 stand as registered: the unit either reaches the prompts (gate 3), stays
inside `multi-session` (gate 4), and moves `MR` without costing the other four (gates 7, 8), or it does
not. Only prediction 1's mechanism sentence is withdrawn.

### 13.288.6 The room binds by 86% on the flat routes and by 18% on `MR`, and the first draft of this section had it backwards

This section was first written from a comparison of `promptChars` against the rendered size of
`ablation.featureRetrievedContexts`, which appeared to show the whole context inside the prompt on every
route. That comparison is circular: the field records the turns that were **delivered**, so "the prompt is
the context plus the instruction block" is arithmetic rather than evidence. The informative comparison is
the plan the evidence bound held against what the render actually carried:

| capability | turns the plan held (`evidenceTurns`) | delivered (`turns`) | cut | `promptChars` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `MR` | 243 | **199** | **18.1%** | 45,838 |
| `TR` | 242 | 205 | 15.3% | 47,158 |
| `IE` | 495 | **64** | **87.2%** | 46,710 |
| `KU` | 488 | 67 | 86.3% | 46,878 |
| `ABS` | 506 | 76 | 85.1% | 46,722 |

Both medians, from `42310779222`. Three readings, and the third changes what the next registration should
be:

1. **`MR` and `TR` are evidence-rich; the flat routes are evidence-starved.** The two session routes carry
   four fifths of the turns their plan held, because `maxTurnChars=400` shrinks each turn to about 230
   characters and 199 of them fit. The three flat routes carry **13-15%** of theirs, because their turns
   are uncapped and average 722 characters. So "the room is not binding" is true of `MR` and false of
   `IE`, and a single sentence about "the room" across this arm is a sentence about five different
   regimes.
2. **Therefore the reference pipeline's 7.43-point `MR` lead cannot be an evidence-volume effect.** We
   hand `MR` 45,838 characters against its 20,000-odd, and 199 turns against its roughly ten sessions
   times twelve. It wins by giving less.
3. **The one allocation the arm has never had is the reference's per-session cap.** Our sessions reach
   the reader at about 956 rendered characters each across 44 of 45 of them; the reference truncates each
   session to 2,000 and stops at 20,000, i.e. ten sessions. That is not "less evidence" so much as
   "contiguous evidence": 2,000 characters of one conversation read as a conversation, and 956 characters
   of it read as an excerpt. §13.288.5 already narrowed this run to *completeness at fixed volume*; the
   registration that follows it must vary the **allocation per session**, which is the one knob this arm
   does not have at all.

What is unchanged: `42328499107` tests whether a complete session reads differently from a 78%-complete
one, and its refutation branch ("fragmentation at this granularity is not the mechanism") is now the
branch most likely to fire, because 956 characters per session is not enough for a session to read as one.

### 13.289 The reader is shown 45 conversations of five turns each, and the twenty-seven failures are all one item short

A zero-cost reading of `42310779222`, taken while `42328499107` runs. It exists because §13.288.6 priced
the next variable from a number (`956 characters per session`) that had been carried in prose across
several sections and never derived from the artifact. It is derived now, and the derivation changes what
§13.288 is a test of.

#### 13.289.1 Where the shape comes from, and why not from the fields that look like they already have it

`evidenceTurns`, `turns` and `windowComposition` describe the **plan**: the roster the arm built, the
count it believed it carried, the room it believed it spent. The reader was handed a string. Between
those two sit a renderer, a character budget, a per-turn cap and an ordering stage, and §13.283's defect
lived in exactly that gap — a table that stated one thing while the dispatch did another.

So the shape is parsed out of `ablation.featurePromptTexts`, and the parser is checked rather than
trusted: its turn count is compared against `windowComposition.turns` on every record, and it agrees on
**121 of 121** `MR` records. `tools/delivered-shape.py` is the tool, `test_delivered_shape.py` is its
test, and the check is the reason the first draft of the parser is in that test file as a named defect:
keyed on `^\d+\. ` it counts the assistant's own numbered lists as turns and reports 155 turns per
question where the artifact records 199.

#### 13.289.2 The shape

| quantity | median | note |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| sessions per question | **45** | mean 44.94, min 36, max 52 |
| turns per question | **199** | equals `windowComposition.turns` on 121 of 121 |
